  Files: `bless.ts`, `medium.ts` (`BAKE_WAVELENGTHS_NM`), `channels.ts`, `channels.json`,
  `channels.test.ts`, `apps/hyperion/vitest.config.mts`, the tool and its script, `NOTICE`.
  Tests:
  - the refit starts from (620, 540, 445) and does not worsen the recorded objective;
  - at Earth the fitted triple beats 680/550/440 at a sun zenith of 85°.
- **R08.T4.b Curves of growth.** `absorbers.ts`: `absorberCurve(absorber, spectrum)` computes T_c(u)
  per absorber and channel for one sun, for an `AbsorberSpec` keyed by species string
  (decision-composition §1.9), weighted by the signed c̄_c·S, clamped to [10⁻⁶, 1] and
  non-increasing in u (Design note 5, ruled 2026-10-10), on σ's own grid of 1 nm or finer, with S
  interpolated from the sun's 15 `bake_spectrum` bin averages. It runs in the optics worker at
  arrival, once per sun. `absorberBinCurves(absorber, spectrum)` gives the same sun's curve in
  each of the 15 bake bins, weighted by S over the bin alone, for the spectral bakes and the
  reference's 15-wavelength runs (Design note 5). The reduced cross-sections, ozone binned to 1 nm and
  methane's σ at its three temperatures interpolated onto a uniform grid of 0.25 nm or finer
  (below), are written to `absorbers/crossSections.json` by the same reduction step (T4.a's Node
  tool, since a renderer test fetches and reads no raw file). Ozone's 1 nm bins are centred, on
  [λ − 0.5, λ + 0.5) nm (`decisions-r05.md` item 2), unlike R05's three upward 10 nm bins, which
  R05 keeps for parity with Bruneton and sebh.
  - Sources: ozone from Serdyuchenko et al. 2014 (AMT 7, 625; the articles CC BY 3.0, the data
    page's terms unstated). Methane from Karkoschka and Tomasko 2010 (Icarus 205, 674), as NASA's
    Planetary Spectrum Generator converts them to cross-sections at 100, 198 and 296 K:
    <https://psg.gsfc.nasa.gov/data/linelists/xuv/data/ch4.txt>, SHA-256
    `cf7f7195a9ceadad1480b436d1657b722d1bb6264a603618faead3dd8aa4a3ef`, fetched 2026-10-09, 4,949
    points to 0.836 µm, with no terms stated. Elsevier's supplementary Table 4 is not an input: its
    table is images, and Elsevier reserves text and data mining on it.
  - Only the reduced values are committed, with attribution in `NOTICE`'s Data section. The raw
    files are fetched with their checksums and never committed.
    - Ozone: the reduced 1 nm table (ruled 2026-10-02, `decisions-r05.md` item 4).
    - Methane (ruled 2026-10-09, `decision-r08-licences.md` row 1): σ at the three temperatures
      over 380–800 nm, interpolated onto the tool's own uniform grid of 0.25 nm or finer, so that
      no band-model value is averaged.
    - T4.b's science check (ruled 2026-10-10, `decision-r08-t4b-t12c.md`).
      - _Sources._ Table 4's caption, read in Elsevier's supplementary file and not used as an
        input, and Collins et al. 2018 (Sci. Adv. 4, eaas9593, Methods Eqs. 1–5, open access),
        which restate K&T's equations. No open copy of the paper was found.
      - _PSG's columns_ are Table 4's coefficients "for the limit of infinite pressure", on air
        wavelengths. They equal the band parameters of Irwin's AOPP k-tables, which the caption
        names, to a unit of their last digit. No value below K&T's first row, 400 nm, is used,
        so no MPI-Mainz value enters.
      - _The finite-pressure correction, Eqs. 2–4, is not built._
        - It is a Goody random band of Voigt lines, τ = 2kw ∫₀^∞ V ÷ [1 + kw(δ/α_D0)V ÷ √T] dx,
          with y = (α_L0/α_D0)(P/P0)(√T0 ÷ T)[q + (1 − q) ÷ SFB], α_L0/α_D0 = 150 K^½ (the
          caption) and SFB 1.4. δ/α_D0 is Table 4's last column, which PSG's file omits.
        - e^(−ku) at infinite pressure is a stated approximation. Measured with Irwin's δ/α_D0 at
          100 K, the correction would raise the red channel's transmittance by at most 1.4% at
          1 atm through 30 km-amagat, 4.4% at 0.3 atm and 11.5% at 0.1 atm. A body's methane
          lies chiefly at 0.5 bar and deeper.
        - NEMESIS's `tkark.f` takes 125 for the 150; that is recorded, not followed.
      - _Eq. 8_ is Lagrange's quadratic in ln k through the three temperatures, z = (T − 198) ÷ 98:
        ln k(T) = ½z(z − 1) ln k₁₀₀ + (1 − z²) ln k₁₉₈ + ½z(z + 1) ln k₂₉₆.
        - It is used in place of linear-in-σ, from which it differs by at most 0.7% in channel T
          through 10 km-amagat.
        - The caption gives it "for other temperatures", and the k-tables it names span 50–300 K,
          so the result is `measured` over 50–300 K.
        - Beyond that range the nearest end's value is held and is `estimated`. Methane above
          300 K is R08.T4.f's.
        - A row with a zero at any of the three temperatures is linear in k.
    - Karkoschka 1998 (PDS GBAT_0001, DOI 10.17189/2bp8-k793, CC0) is the open fallback and a
      cross-check. It has no temperature dependence, so using it is a recorded deviation.
  - Absorbers whose ratios hold constant with height share one curve of growth:
    σ_mix(λ) = Σ xᵢσᵢ(λ) is exact for them. So Design note 8's five stored columns count distinct
    vertical profiles, not species, and do not cap the composition. A listed absorber with no
    cross-sections draws nothing and is reported for `atmosphereApproximate`. Past five profiles,
    after H₂O's two continuum pairs share one column (R08.T4.d), the five of greatest optical depth
    are kept. A profile's depth is the largest over the three channels of
    −ln[Σ w_c e^(−Σᵢ Uᵢσᵢ) ÷ Σ w_c] for its vertical column, under an equal-energy spectrum, with
    w_c = max(c̄_c, 0) on σ's grid over the bake range. Equal depths keep the earlier listed, and the
    kept profiles take their columns in the order listed. Every species of a dropped profile draws
    nothing and is reported `noColumnFree` for `atmosphereApproximate` (decided 2026-10-10,
    `decision-r08-cmf-licence.md`).

  Tests:
  - a flat spectrum's curve is e^(−σu);
  - every T_c lies in [10⁻⁶, 1] and is non-increasing in u, for a 2,500 K and a 30,000 K Planck
    sun; where the clamp and the running minimum act is recorded per channel (blue above 1; the
    floor on red or green, whichever leaves Rec. 709 first, and on the other where it follows;
    red's running minimum, for ozone from up to 0.125 decade before its gamut exit), and every
    node at the floor has a negative signed sum;
  - two suns of different temperature give different curves, and the same sun the same curve;
  - the sun's colour through 0.1–10 × a reference column matches the spectral result to
    Δu′v′ ≤ 0.002, for the Sun and for a 6,500 K Planck spectrum (measured 0.0012 at most):
    - the reference columns are 300 DU of ozone at 233 K, and 3 km-amagat of methane at 100
      and 296 K (about an ice giant's column a bar above its deck; Titan's is 2–3);
    - the 2,500 K and 30,000 K Planck suns, ozone to 30 × and methane to 300 km-amagat, and
      each curve's gamut exit are recorded in `absorbers/curves.json`, checked unchanged;
  - the 15 bins' curves, reduced on storage, give the same colours within Δu′v′ ≤ 0.003
    (measured 0.0026 at most), and a flat spectrum's bin curve is the bin's mean of e^(−σu);
  - 300 DU of ozone gives a green-channel Chappuis optical depth of 0.02–0.04;
  - the bless check fails on a changed table and names the command;
  - two absorbers on one profile give one curve equal to the curve of their mixed cross-section;
    six absorbers on five profiles fit the five columns. Six profiles keep the five of greatest
    optical depth, whether the least is listed first or sixth, and report the dropped one's
    species `noColumnFree`. Two profiles of equal depth keep the earlier listed.

- **R08.T4.c Continua, pairs and Thomson scattering** (decision-composition;
  `decision-r08-t4b-t12c.md`, follow-ups 2 and 3). After T4.b. `absorbers.ts` and `absorbers/`:
  - **Pair absorbers.**
    - A pair spec has σ in m⁵ a molecule pair, over the pair column u = ∫ n_A n_B ds
      (x_A x_B n_s² ∫ρ² ds for two well-mixed gases).
    - It sits on a vertical profile of its own, the product of its members' number densities,
      and takes one of Design note 8's stored columns.
    - `absorberSpecs` forms each pair from its members' layers (R08.T10.a's rule), and a pair
      with an absent member is not formed.

    The pairs:
    - O₂–O₂ collision-induced absorption (its bands near 380, 446, 477, 532, 577 and 630 nm),
      from HITRAN's CIA file (Karman et al. 2019), measured over the file's temperatures
      (223–287 K, or colder if a set holds it), held and `estimated` beyond;
    - O₂–N₂ in the A band, over 733–760 nm, from HITRAN2024's O₂–N₂ file (Tran et al. 2006),
      not its O₂–air file, which would count O₂–O₂'s A band twice;
    - O₂–CO₂ in the A band, over 733–760 nm, from HITRAN2024's `O2-CO2_2024.cia`
      (Vangvichith et al. 2009). It and O₂–N₂ are measured at 296 K and held, `estimated`,
      beyond it;
    - H₂–He from HITRAN's CIA files where they reach 380–760 nm. HITRAN's 950–1,175 K sets are
      skipped where they break the temperature trend (its 925 K set holds to it), recorded, and
      σ is interpolated in ln σ.
    - H₂–H₂ from Borysow 2002's tables (A&A 390, 779; 60–1,000 K, to 607 nm at 60–350 K and
      589 nm above) and Borysow, Jørgensen and Fu 2001's (1,000–7,000 K, to 501 nm), as reduced
      values with citation (`decision-r08-cmf-licence.md` §8). Hydrogen is in thermal
      equilibrium, ln σ is linear in T, and σ is 0 where the tables end, a stated approximation;
    - H⁻'s free–free absorption, per H atom and electron, John 1988's closed form;
    - e⁻–H₂ and e⁻–He free–free (H₂⁻ from Bell 1980's table, He⁻ from John 1994's table), each
      checked at fetch; a pair whose source is not lawful is pending with its bound;

  - **Continua per species:**
    - H⁻'s bound–free, per H⁻ (John 1988);
    - SO₂'s near-ultraviolet tail over 380–420 nm, from the MPI-Mainz atlas (its CC BY 4.0
      snapshot where it holds the data).
  - **Thomson scattering by e⁻:** `thomsonTerm`, a `MediumTerm` on e⁻'s layer.
    - It has σ_T = 6.652 × 10⁻²⁹ m² (CODATA 2018) in every channel, no absorption, and
      Rayleigh's phase at ρ = 0.
    - R08.T10.a builds it from the record.
  - **Stated transparency and pending absorbers** (`decision-r08-t4b-t12c.md`, follow-up 3).
    - `NO_VISIBLE_ABSORPTION` holds only what no column can make visible, each with its reason:
      He (`bandsOutsideRange`, below 5,000 K: its levels start 19.8 eV up), e⁻
      (`noBoundStates`), and N₂ (`bandsOutsideRange`, below 1,800 K; above it, its first
      positive bands are R08.T4.f's). CO₂, by the same check, is pending: HITRAN2024 holds its
      bands over 565–737 nm (`decision-r08-t4b-t12c.md`, follow-ups 4 and 5).
    - `PENDING_ABSORBERS` names each absorber-flagged species whose data are still to be built,
      with its task and its 1 nm cell-mean cross-sections over 380–760 nm at its source's
      temperature nodes, marked measured or estimated.
      - CO, CO₂, N₂O, HCN, H₂'s quadrupole lines, C₂H₂, C₂H₄, C₂H₆, PH₃ and CH₃OH are
        R08.T4.d's.
      - O, and He above 5,000 K, are R08.T4.e's.
      - H₂S, SiO, hot CO, N₂O and HCN, and N₂ above 1,800 K are R08.T4.f's.
      - Mg⁺, from 2,570 K (its 448.1 nm line, 8.86 eV up), and H₂⁻'s free–free (`H2+e-`, while
        Bell 1980's table is not obtained, its values estimated), are R08.T4.e's.
      - K's resonance doublet's far wing is R08.T4.e's as the pairs `K+H2` and `K+He`, per
        (atom, perturber) pair, `estimated`, beside K's own lines per atom (follow-up 5).
      - ExoMol-derived bounds go in `absorbers/exomol/bounds.json`.
      - CO's ExoMol Li2015 bands from 8–0 up are dropped, recorded: they break the overtone
        ladder's monotone decline. Their bound is the ladder below HITRAN2024's 7–0.
    - R08.T10.a applies them at each body's own column, channel by channel (follow-up 4).
  - Each source's licence is checked at its fetch under `decision-r08-licences.md`'s rule.
  - Tests:
    - H⁻'s bound–free equals John 1988's tabulated values, and its free–free Bell and
      Berrington 1987's (J. Phys. B 20, 801), at three wavelengths and two temperatures. John's
      Table 1 is a factor of 10 off in free–free, recorded;
    - Earth's vertical O₂–O₂ optical depth at 477 nm lies in 0.004–0.012
      (∫ n_O₂² dz ≈ 1.2 × 10⁴³ cm⁻⁵);
    - a pair's column equals an `f64` quadrature of n_A n_B to 10⁻⁹, and a pair with an absent
      member is not formed;
    - e⁻'s term scatters n_e σ_T in every channel, absorbs nothing, with ρ = 0;
    - every T_c lies in [10⁻⁶, 1] and is non-increasing in u, for a 2,500 K and a 30,000 K sun,
      with each absorber's clamp places recorded;
    - every absorber-flagged row of `substances.json` has cross-sections, a `PENDING_ABSORBERS`
      entry with its cell means, or a `NO_VISIBLE_ABSORPTION` entry.
  - Acceptance: `pnpm --filter hyperion exec vitest run view/atmosphere/absorbers`.

- **R08.T4.d Lines at temperate temperatures** (follow-ups 2 and 3). After T4.c and R08.T6.c,
  whose read it widens. These are molecular lines too narrow for a 1 nm σ: at 1 bar an O₂ or H₂O
  line is about 0.003 nm wide.
  - **The species:**
    - O₂'s B band (686–695 nm), its γ band (628–634 nm), the head of its A band (759–760 nm;
      the rest lies outside the range), and the weaker bands HITRAN holds in the range;
    - H₂O's visible bands (near 590, 650 and 700–735 nm), from HITRAN, over 150–500 K;
    - H₂O's continuum over 380–760 nm, as T4.c's pairs in `crossSections.json`: the self part as
      `H2O+H2O`, and the foreign part as H₂O with each other gas (`decision-r08-t4d-kdist.md`
      §6). MT_CKD is not an input in any form: AER grants it "for scientific and research
      purposes only".
      - From 567 nm it is the Clough–Kneizys–Davies (CKD) continuum as LOWTRAN 7 tabulates it
        (Kneizys et al. 1988, AFGL-TR-88-0177; the formulation in LOWTRAN 6's AFGL-TR-83-0187,
        Eqs. 22–24), from `lowtran7.f`'s `SF296`, `SF260` and `BFH2O`:
        <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/space-physics/lowtran/5b8d38714b204eaa12595f5f15e2babec1dbdfb5/src/lowtran/fortran/lowtran7.f>,
        SHA-256 `25e83d94e24bb8acc3242dfd3b97e0bd8ca8ffceff9ec6dce1f5a37c9c5459ac`.
      - Its 10 cm⁻¹ values are reduced to 1 nm cell means with the radiation term
        ν tanh(hcν/2kT). With N₂ and O₂ over 260–296 K it is `measured`: a published model
        within its range, checked against the visible measurements (Risks).
      - Below 567 nm, where CKD's line list ends, the continuum is CKD's ratio to HITRAN2024's
        lines, `estimated`. Each line contributes its Lorentz wing beyond 25 cm⁻¹ plus its
        pedestal, summed over lines within 1,000 cm⁻¹, with γ_air for the foreign part and γ_self
        for the self part. The ratio is taken over CKD's 567–600 nm cells (about 5.9 foreign and
        9.9 self), and is recorded.
      - The self part is a power law in T through CKD's 260 and 296 K values in each cell. The
        foreign part is held at 296 K, as CKD prescribes. Outside 260–296 K both are
        `estimated`, and beyond 150–500 K they are held.
      - With N₂ and O₂, and with any other gases together up to 2% of the foreign molecules
        (Earth's Ar 0.93% among them), the foreign part is `measured` as air. Beyond that, the
        excess share is `estimated`, the air value scaled by each gas's broadening ratio r
        (below) (`decision-r08-t4d-kdist-chain.md` §15).
      - The source is LOWTRAN, a US Air Force program "approved for public release; distribution
        unlimited" whose code states no terms. The values are reduced, with citation, and the raw
        file is not committed;
    - NH₃'s 552 and 648 nm bands: R08.T4.g, split out (its 243.7M transitions need their own
      reduction). Until then NH₃ is a `PENDING_ABSORBERS` entry naming R08.T4.g, so that
      R08.T10.a's margin labels any body that needs it;
    - CO₂'s bands over 565–737 nm (HITRAN2024, 1,204 lines; measured at 200, 296 and 500 K;
      τ ≈ 0.7 at 716 nm through Venus's vertical column);
    - Karman et al. 2018's computed A- and B-band collision-induced sets at 206–346 K (Nature
      Chem. 10, 549; HITRAN's alternate files), in place of R08.T4.c's single-temperature A
      and B bands, for each pair they cover: `measured` over 206–346 K, held and `estimated`
      beyond.
    - CO's 7–0 band (691–700 nm, HITRAN2024), its higher overtones bounded by the ladder;
    - N₂O's HITRAN2024 bands (713–754 nm). Its TYM part is R08.T4.g's, split out with NH₃: below
      714 nm, and TYM's bands that HITRAN2024 lacks over 714–760 nm. Until then it is a
      `PENDING_ABSORBERS` entry naming R08.T4.g, bounded by TYM's 296 K cell means below
      714 nm, and by their excess over HITRAN2024's, cell by cell, over 714–760 nm;
    - HCN from HITRAN2024 (to 568.6 nm), with ExoMol's list beyond if it reaches the range;
    - H₂'s quadrupole lines (HITRAN2024; 4–0 S(1) at 636.95 nm among them);
    - C₂H₂, C₂H₄, C₂H₆, PH₃ and CH₃OH:
      - first from the measured visible overtone band intensities the literature publishes, each
        intensity over its band width a measured bound, with a band-model shape `estimated`;
      - else from a stated overtone-ladder estimate anchored on the strongest catalogued band, at
        a factor of 10 a quantum, `estimated`;
      - both labelled under Design note 12's τ rule unless negligible on the body (R08.T10.a);
  - **The machinery:**
    - A k-distribution per 1 nm cell on a grid of pressure and temperature, reduced offline from
      the line lists with Voigt profiles (by R08.T4.a's tool, or a `hyperion-fit` task if its
      cost needs one). The line-by-line grid is a quarter of the cell's narrowest Voigt
      half-width or finer (`decision-r08-t4d-kdist.md`).
      - **g-points** are shared by all of a cell's nodes (2-point Gauss–Legendre intervals by
        bisection), so that k is interpolated at fixed g.
      - **Pressure** runs on the broadening-equivalent pressure (below) at 4 nodes a decade from
        10 Pa to 1 MPa and 8 a decade from 1 to 10 MPa, with one more node at 13.3 MPa, only to
        centre the read's stencil (`estimated`). Alternate nodes below 1 MPa may be dropped
        wherever the between-node test still passes with the rows at 4 a decade, recorded.
      - **Temperature** runs at nodes 50 K apart over each species' range, refined to 25 K and
        then 12.5 K in any interval where the between-node test fails. An interval still failing
        at 12.5 K is recorded (cell, T, p, u, error), and the species is `estimated` between
        those two nodes.
      - **Interpolation** is cubic (4-point Lagrange) in T on ln k at fixed g, once per body at
        the profile's temperature. Linear interpolation is not used: it is 4–8 times worse at
        these nodes.
      - **Storage** is 16-bit ln k, code 0 for k = 0, with a per-file offset and step, in
        little-endian binary files with a short header, committed as binary, each under the
        500 kB hook. The optics worker loads each species' files lazily through Vite's `?url`
        (as the height worker loads its wasm), never the render thread's bundle. Tests read them
        as `?inline` assets (`assetsInclude`). Failing either path, base64 JSON, recorded.
      - A cell whose largest k times the gated column is ≤ 0.02 at every node is stored as its
        mean σ alone (G = 1). No cell is dropped.
      - T4.d's committed binary is recorded. Past 40 MB, alternate nodes below 1 MPa are dropped
        where the between-node test still passes on rows at 4 a decade (rows there then cubic in
        ln p from the stored nodes), and this is recorded. From R08.T4.e on, the economies and cap
        are decision-r08-t4ef-storage's.
    - **Each species' range.**
      - Its temperatures run from where its saturated column is negligible to its line list's
        limit (HITRAN's 500 K, C2018's 300 K). Negligible means R08.T10.a's Δ_c under 10⁻³ at
        k = 100, for a pure gas at saturation over 40 p_sat ÷ (m g) at g = 0.5 m s⁻²: H₂O from
        150 K. A gas that does not condense there runs to the coldest atmosphere it can be a gas
        in.
      - Its pressures are not cut per species, since the axis is the broadening pressure, which
        any trace gas can see.
      - Below 10 Pa the 10 Pa table is held. It stays `measured` by a recorded check at 1 Pa,
        over columns to 40 p ÷ (m g) at g = 0.5 m s⁻².
      - Above 10 MPa, and outside a species' temperatures, the nearest node is held and
        `estimated` (`decision-r08-t4b-t12c.md`, follow-up 5). R08.T10.a decides the label.
    - **The line shape.**
      - One shape at every pressure, so that the tables are smooth in p
        (`decision-r08-t4d-kdist-chain.md`). No cut-off grows with p, since a reach that grows
        switches on a distant band's wing between two nodes.
      - Every species without a published far-wing shape takes Voigt within 25 cm⁻¹ of each
        line centre, with no pedestal.
      - CO₂ takes Voigt × χ(|ν − ν₀|), each line's wing being Σ_j x_j r_j χ_j ÷ Σ_j x_j r_j over
        its broadeners.
        - The two sets are SpeCT's ν3-band CO₂–CO₂ and CO₂–N₂ χ (Chaverot et al. 2025, A&A 702,
          A137; CC BY 4.0), applied to the visible bands as SpeCT applies them beyond
          4,300 cm⁻¹ (`decision-r08-t4d-kdist-chain.md` §§12–13). N₂, O₂, Ar and air take
          CO₂–N₂'s χ, and so does any other broadener, `estimated`.
          - Wherever χ ≠ 1 they take SpeCT's Eq. 11 shape: the profile times the quantum
            asymmetry factor x ÷ (1 − e^(−x)), x = c₂(ν − ν₀) ÷ T, with its detailed-balance
            term, against which χ is defined.
          - CO₂–CO₂: σ 3, 50 and 220 cm⁻¹; B₁ = 0.055 − 0.11 e^(−0.008 T),
            B₂ = 0.021 + 0.08 e^(−0.0095 T), B₃ = 0.01. It is held outside 218–751 K, SpeCT's fit
            temperatures.
          - CO₂–N₂: σ 3, 10 and 70 cm⁻¹; B₁ = 0.416 − 0.354 e^(−0.00386 T),
            B₂ = 0.00167 + 0.0421 e^(−0.00248 T), B₃ = 0.019. Table 2 prints 0.0167, a misprint
            corrected from SpeCT's own code (spect-public commit e7c4579c08, `fcts.f90`),
            recorded. It is held below 295 K and above 773 K, unless a test against Cousin et
            al. 1985's 193–238 K measurements moves the low hold.
          - The table flags each node whose χ is held. R08.T10.a decides on the body's own column
            whether the hold is visible (`decision-r08-t4d-kdist-chain.md` §14). The reduction
            itself marks no held node `estimated`.
          - The science check's residuals against SpeCT's lab compilation
            (10.5281/zenodo.15564294) are recorded both ways: CO₂–CO₂ +0.04 (rms 0.11) against
            PH89's −0.71 (rms 1.10), and CO₂–N₂ tied within the lab sets' own 0.15–0.45
            disagreement.
        - Each cell stores the two sets on shared g-points, mixed at arrival as
          σ(g) = w σ_self(g) + (1 − w) σ_N₂(g), with w = x_CO₂ r_self ÷ Σ_j x_j r_j.
        - The reach is fixed where χ < 10⁻³ at every temperature the tables use, 293 cm⁻¹ over
          100–500 K as the reduction computes it, the coefficients being held beyond.
        - Outside its source's stated temperatures each set's coefficients are held and
          `estimated` (outside the temperatures of the measurements each set is fitted to, as
          the science check records them). None is clamped.
        - The coefficients are reduced values with citation, read from carriers that are
          finding aids (decision-composition item 17). Failing a lawful source, CO₂ takes the
          25 cm⁻¹ cut-off, recorded.
      - A node is `estimated` where the cell's S-weighted Lorentz half-width γ_L exceeds
        0.25 cm⁻¹, since the far wing's shape is not measured in the visible. Each node records
        two shares of a Lorentz line: beyond 25 cm⁻¹, 2 γ_L ÷ (25π), the most a far wing would
        add; and 3–25 cm⁻¹ from the centre, (2/π)[arctan(25/γ_L) − arctan(3/γ_L)], which a
        sub-Lorentzian wing would reduce. A species whose own χ is published, found at fetch,
        takes it as CO₂ does.
      - H₂O instead takes its continuum's convention at every pressure: Voigt within 25 cm⁻¹ less
        the line's pedestal (its Lorentz value at 25 cm⁻¹), with no widening, the continuum
        carrying the rest. CKD's continuum, like MT_CKD's, contains the pedestal, since FASCODE's
        line function subtracts each line's value at its 25 cm⁻¹ bound. H₂O's nodes are
        `estimated` where γ_L > 2.5 cm⁻¹.
      - Line mixing in O₂'s A-band head and Dicke narrowing of H₂'s lines are recorded, not
        modelled.
    - **The broadener.** The tables are air-broadened. A body's broadening-equivalent pressure
      is p_eff = p Σ_j x_j r_j, with r_j = Σ S γ_j ÷ Σ S γ_air over the species' lines that
      HITRAN2024 gives γ_j for. r_self comes from γ_self, and N₂, O₂ and Ar are taken as air. A
      gas with no HITRAN width is taken as air, at any share: `estimated` where it has a permanent
      dipole of at least H₂S's (`DIPOLAR_BROADENERS`) or the table has two variants, and otherwise
      weighed by R08.T10.c's effect bound. A table with no γ_self takes its own species likewise,
      by the entry under its own key where it lists one (H's); a neutral atom with neither is
      `estimated`, its resonance lines' self-broadening being tens of times its H₂ width
      (R08.T10.d). Each broadener takes its own
      HITRAN2024 temperature exponent where given (n_air otherwise), through
      p_eff = p Σ_j x_j r_j (296 ÷ T)^(n_j − n_air) at the profile's temperature.
    - Each sun's curve is Σ_cells c̄ S Σ_g w_g e^(−k_g u): signed by cell and positive within
      it (correlated-k; Lacis and Oinas 1991, JGR 96, 9027).
    - An absorber-weighted (Curtis–Godson) pressure per path sits beside the profile's
      temperature. It is carried as a stored pressure-weighted column, or derived from the bulk
      column for a well-mixed gas, packed as one `rgba16float` table a κ slice, whose channel 0
      holds the bulk's pressure-weighted column (serving every well-mixed line slot) and whose
      channels 1–3 hold up to three other line slots' own, with a second table only past three
      (§15). The curves become T_c(u, p̄), p̄ weighted by the local p_eff:
      - one row a stored pressure node over the pressures the body's tables see (to the surface,
        or to the deck's for a `cloudDeck` body), and one more each side for the read. Each row
        is computed at arrival at the profile's temperature, its exponentials shared by every
        sun, channel and bake bin, and the arrival time is recorded beside `BAKE_CEILING_S`.
        Line arrival (line specs and every sun's curves) is a budget line of its own in R08.T11,
        held to 5 s a world on the UHD 620 host, not sharing `BAKE_CEILING_S`. A thick world's
        arrival latency, curves plus bake, is recorded. The curves are split by cell across the
        optics workers, the brightest sun's first. A cell whose largest k times 10³ U is ≤ 0.02
        may take its mean (§15);
      - read in the kernels and the twin by 4-point Lagrange in ln p̄, its weights from the rows'
        own ln p̄ (the spacing halves at 1 MPa), on the stored depth τ = −ln T_c, with p̄ held at
        10 MPa above it, linear in u, unclamped between rows (at high pressure T at fixed u is not
        monotone in p), then with τ clamped to [0, −ln 10⁻⁶]. If R08.T11's benchmark finds this
        read over the low setting's per-frame figure, the fallback is a linear read of τ on rows
        at twice the stored density, made by the same cubic;
      - the curves texture's bytes are counted in Design note 11's per-planet row: about 0.59 MB
        for Earth in `rgba32float` at four suns. It may move to `rgba16float` (Design note 8's
        10⁻³τ) where a body would pass 2 MB.
    - T4.d states Design note 8's column budget for Earth: O₃, O₂'s lines, O₂–O₂, H₂O's lines
      and H₂O's continuum, five.
      - H₂O's self and foreign continua are two pair profiles. Where a body's profiles would
        exceed five, they share one column before T4.b's ranking applies. The lesser by T4.b's
        depth adds its σ to the greater's at the ratio of their vertical pair columns. This is
        exact vertically, and its slant-path error is recorded. On Earth the self part folds into
        the foreign part, about 20% low at grazing incidence from the ground (about 5 × 10⁻⁴ of
        red).
      - T4.d also widens T6.c's read sites in the twin and the kernels.
  - Tests:
    - against an `f64` line-by-line reference from the same lines and continuum, with O₂ and
      H₂O in one spectrum: Earth's O₂ B band and H₂O's 590, 650 and 720 nm bands, through 1–38
      air masses, from the ground and from 3 km. Channel T within 2 × 10⁻³, and the colour
      within Δu′v′ 0.0005;
    - the Curtis–Godson error on slant paths is recorded;
    - each cell's k-distribution reproduces its line-by-line curve of growth to 10⁻³ in T at
      every stored node. Through the client's whole chain (the cubic in T at arrival, the rows,
      the kernels' read of τ in ln p̄) it does so to 2 × 10⁻³ midway between rows, midway
      between temperature nodes, and at both at once, at `measured` and `estimated` nodes
      alike.
      - The columns stop at 400 p_eff ÷ (m g) at g = 0.5 m s⁻², m the species' molecular mass.
        That is the most a tangent path on any generated body holds, about 57 s² m⁻¹ at worst
        against the cap's 80, times 2.5 for the broadening axis (He's least ratio, 0.40) and a
        fourfold spare.
        They stop too at u_R(λ) = −ln 10⁻⁶ ÷ σ_R,He(λ), helium's Rayleigh cross-section at the
        cell (5.1 × 10²⁸ cm⁻² at 380 nm, 8.3 × 10²⁹ at 760 nm) (Mansfield and Peck 1969,
        extrapolated below 480 nm and checked there against Kurucz 1970's helium after Dalgarno
        1962, to 0.33%). Any straight path holding more
        lies under the curves' 10⁻⁶ floor by Rayleigh scattering alone, since helium scatters
        least of any bulk gas. From R08.T4.g on, the between-node test's columns also stop at the
        species' own Rayleigh column, −ln 10⁻⁶ ÷ σ_R,s(λ), with σ_R,s from `rayleigh.ts` for a
        `measured` gas (helium's otherwise). The node tier, the bisection, G = 1 and the 16-bit
        test keep the columns above. T4.d's tables were gated on helium's cap alone, recorded.
      - For a condensing species at a temperature where it condenses, they stop at
        400 p_sat(T) ÷ (m g) where that is lower: ten times its saturated column, for
        supersaturation. p_sat is cited per species: Murphy and Koop 2005 for H₂O, Span and
        Wagner 1996 for CO₂, Fray and Schmitt 2009 (PSS 57, 2053) for the other ices, or a
        derivation from the triple point, recorded. N₂O, which condenses below 309.52 K, takes
        it from R08.T4.g on.
      - Errors beyond either cap are recorded, not gated.
      - The reduction tests every cell and records each species' worst node and worst midpoint.
      - Vitest repeats the test for O₂'s 687 and 760 nm cells and H₂O's 500, 592, 650 and
        719 nm cells, at three node pressures and three midpoints, against committed
        line-by-line curves;
    - the 16-bit tables' curves equal the reduction's `f64` curves within 2 × 10⁻⁴;
    - every G = 1 cell's curve equals its line-by-line curve within the node tier at every node,
      and the bytes of each species are recorded beside the projection;
    - outside a species' range the nearest node is held and `estimated`. Below 10 Pa the hold
      stays `measured`, by its recorded 1 Pa check;
    - H₂O's curve on a CO₂ background, from HITRAN2024's γ_CO2 line by line, against the same
      curve at p_eff: the error is recorded;
    - the continuum's cell means equal LOWTRAN 7's tables, with the radiation term, at three
      wavenumbers and both of the self part's temperatures;
    - their 12,850–16,000 cm⁻¹ mean equals RRTMG_SW's band-24 CKD_2.4 coefficients, weighted by
      its 16 g-weights, within 1%: self 1.178 × 10⁻²⁵ and foreign 1.388 × 10⁻²⁶ cm² at 296 K
      and the reference density (`data/rrtmg_sw.nc` at `286e84ed`, SHA-256
      `6bbdcaf3339d98b6da64980677b8f72332d128cc9576fae301cca852c97de717`; AER, BSD-3);
    - below 567 nm the continuum equals the recorded ratio times the lines' Lorentz wing and
      pedestal, and is `estimated`;
    - the lines' pedestal is removed exactly where the continuum is drawn;
    - Earth's six profiles fold the self continuum into the foreign's column, exactly for the
      vertical column, and the grazing error is recorded;
    - every read of the curves texture has τ in [0, −ln 10⁻⁶], so T in [10⁻⁶, 1], and the
      largest fall of a read's τ along u is recorded;
    - a band-edge cell (O₂'s 633, 692 and 749 nm) passes the between-node test at 0.13–7.5 MPa,
      and CO₂'s 716 nm cell does so with its χ;
    - CO₂'s fixed-g mix against line by line, through the client chain at 0.1, 1 and 9 MPa and
      every temperature node and midpoint, at w = 0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 0.95. Each cell's
      sidecar records u_mix(w, T), the least column over the tested pressures at which the mix
      errs past 2 × 10⁻³ ("none" within the cap), at each tested temperature, nodes and midpoints
      alike. Samples inside the table's `estimated` temperature intervals set none (§17). The mix
      is recorded, not gated (`decision-r08-t4d-kdist-chain.md` §16). Each χ set's coefficients
      reproduce the source record's values;
    - with T4.c's O₂–O₂, an Earth-like body draws O₂, H₂O's lines and H₂O's continuum, and
      clears `ATMOSPHERE: APPROXIMATE` for O₂, H₂O's lines and H₂O's continuum from 567 nm.
      H₂O's continuum below 567 nm, `estimated`, keeps the label on Earth under R08.T10.a, and
      is negligible on a Mars-class body. Earth's real air (0.93% Ar) clears the H₂O
      continuum's label (§15);
    - every T_c lies in [10⁻⁶, 1] and is non-increasing in u.
  - Acceptance: `pnpm --filter hyperion exec vitest run view/atmosphere/absorbers` and
    `just test-render`.

- **R08.T4.e Atomic and ionic lines** (follow-ups 2 and 3; science-r08-unowned-absorbers). After
  T4.d, on its machinery.
  - **Populations and data.**
    - Boltzmann level populations at the profile's temperature, with Barklem and Collet 2016's
      partition functions (A&A 588, A96), cited.
    - Each species' column is the record's: ionisation is the generator's.
    - Line data from R. L. Kurucz's line lists (`gf<ZZII>.all`, one a spectrum, by URL and SHA-256),
      reduced to the lines and quantities this task uses in `absorbers/lines/<species>.json`, one
      file a spectrum, each line keeping Kurucz's reference code; no raw file is committed. NIST's
      ASD (SRD 78, all rights reserved) is a finding aid and a cross-check only: at most a few
      values per species asserted in tests, with ASD cited (`decision-r08-cmf-licence.md` §7).
    - Broadening by Barklem et al.'s ABO theory where tabulated, Unsöld's van der Waals
      otherwise, and Stark broadening for Balmer.
    - Each source is checked at fetch.
    - **The reference column** for its line list and for T4.c's third reason
      (science-r08-unowned-absorbers): the stage's vertical column above 0.1 bar at g = 10 m s⁻²,
      doubled for the mean slant path. It is taken at solar abundances, with every atom of the
      element free (no molecules, no condensate), split among its stages by Saha, at Saha
      equilibrium, at the stage's most favourable temperature in 2,000–4,600 K.

      Each drawn species takes every line in 380–760 nm, and within 20 nm outside it for its wings,
      whose equivalent width there is at least 10⁻³ nm.

    - **Range** (decision-r08-t4ef-storage §3): `Na` and `K` 500–5,000 K, every other atom and
      every ion 1,000–5,000 K, on R08.T4.f's temperature ladder. Below a floor the first node is
      held, `estimated`; above 5,000 K the 5,000 K node. A stage under the third reason's 10⁻³ at
      the reference column up to a node is stated none below it (`belowK`), its table starting
      there.
    - **Columns:** T4.d's caps (400 p_eff ÷ (m g) at g = 0.5 m s⁻², helium's Rayleigh column),
      not a multiple of the reference column.
    - **Lines in the tables:** every line of the spectrum's list over 360–780 nm. The reference
      column's 10⁻³ nm selection serves the third reason only.
  - **The lines:**
    - Na D (589.0 and 589.6 nm), and K's resonance doublet (766.5 and 769.9 nm, outside the
      range, whose broadened blue wing enters it), with Allard et al.'s pressure-broadened
      profiles for H₂ and He perturbers;
    - **Na I's and K I's other lines:** Na I's 2.10 eV subordinate lines (568.3, 568.8, 615.4,
      616.1, 497.9 and 498.3 nm), and K I's second resonance doublet (404.4 and 404.7 nm);
    - **Ca I:** 422.7 nm, its 1.88–1.90 eV lines (428–431, 442–446, 612–616 and 643–647 nm), and its
      657.3 nm intercombination line;
    - **Cr I:** 425.4, 427.5 and 429.0 nm, and the 520.5, 520.6 and 520.8 nm triplet;
    - **Si I:** 390.6 nm;
    - **Mg I:** the b triplet (516.7, 517.3 and 518.4 nm) and the 382.9, 383.2 and 383.8 nm triplet,
      both from 2.71 eV. Its resonance line at 285.2 nm lies outside the range;
    - **Al I:** 394.4 and 396.2 nm;
    - **Mn I:** 403.1, 403.3 and 403.4 nm, and its 2.1–2.3 eV lines;
    - **V I:** its lines, strongest at 437.9, 438.5, 439.0, 411.2 and 384.1 nm;
    - **Ni I:** its lines, strongest at 385.8, 380.7 and 547.7 nm;
    - **Zn I:** 468.0, 472.2 and 481.1 nm (4.0 eV) and 636.2 nm;
    - **Ti I and Fe I:** their lines in the range;
    - **H I:** the Balmer lines in local thermodynamic equilibrium, from Hα 656.3 nm to the series'
      members above 380 nm. A non-LTE thermosphere is not modelled, which is recorded. H's
      bound–free absorption from n ≥ 3 is stated negligible beside H⁻ below 5,000 K;
    - **The ions,** once P14.T49.b's rows exist:
      - Ca II's H and K (393.4 and 396.8 nm);
      - Fe II's lines (492.4, 501.8 and 516.9 nm strongest);
      - Ti II's;
      - V II's (387–404 nm);
      - Cr II's (455.9 and 458.8 nm and others, from 3.9–4.1 eV);
      - Mn II's (412.8 and 420.5 nm, and 432–440 nm).

      Mg II, Si II, Al II, Ni II, Na II, K II and Zn II are R08.T4.h's stated none (or pending, as
      its record says), by the third reason below. Mg II's 448.1 nm line (8.86 eV up, reaching
      τ 10⁻³ at 10³ km-amagat near 2,570 K) is pending in T4.c as built (follow-up 5), and stays
      pending, its line drawn here, unless Kurucz's full list confirms its share under the third
      reason's 10⁻³;

    - [Fe II]'s forbidden lines from Deb and Hibbert 2011 (A&A 536, A74; CDS J/A+A/536/A74);
    - Na D's and K's far wings as pairs with H₂ and He, from Allard et al.'s profiles over
      their density-linear range, beside each doublet's own profile per atom;
    - O I's forbidden lines [O I] 630.0 and 636.4 nm (Kurucz's `gf0800.all`), and He I's lines in
      the range for profiles above 5,000 K;
  - **Stated transparency, the third reason** (science-r08-unowned-absorbers). T4.c built two
    reasons for a band absorber: its catalogued bands lie outside the range
    (`bandsOutsideRange`), or its strongest catalogued band in or nearest the range, extrapolated
    up the overtone ladder at a factor of at least 10 a quantum, stays under τ 10⁻³ in every 1 nm
    cell at 10³ km-amagat (`underOvertoneBound`), with e⁻'s `noBoundStates`. Its
    `NO_VISIBLE_ABSORPTION` gains a third, for an atom or ion: its catalogued lines in the range
    take under 10⁻³ of every bake bin's light (a summed equivalent width under 0.0253 nm a bin) at
    the reference column. Expected at build for the line species, each confirmed on Kurucz's full
    list:
    - `Mg+` (448.1 nm, 8.86 eV up): 7 × 10⁻⁴;
    - `Si+` (from 6.86 and 8.12 eV): 5 × 10⁻⁴;
    - `Ni+` (forbidden lines only on NIST's list; Kurucz's holds 6,560 (R08.T4.h)): 1.5 × 10⁻⁴;
    - `Al+`: 5 × 10⁻⁶;
    - `Na+` and `K+`: no line from below 20 eV; `Zn+`: Kurucz none in the range, ASD's three
      3d¹⁰4p–3d⁹4s² lines from 6.0 eV with no A (R08.T4.h).
  - Tests:
    - Na D's depth monotone in column;
    - a class IV giant's (900–1,500 K) geometric albedo under 0.1 at 550 nm (Sudarsky et al.
      2000's Bond albedo for class IV is 0.03, Table 1a);
    - each line's equivalent width against an `f64` line-by-line reference, within 1% over
      three columns;
    - every T_c lies in [10⁻⁶, 1] and is non-increasing in u;
    - each drawn species' largest bake-bin share at the reference column is recorded beside
      science-r08-unowned-absorbers' estimate, and the stated-none ions stay under 10⁻³ on Kurucz's
      full lists.
  - Acceptance: `pnpm --filter hyperion exec vitest run view/atmosphere/absorbers`.

- **R08.T4.f ExoMol's hot molecules** (follow-ups 2 and 3; decision-composition §5). After T4.d, on
  its machinery, for 500–4,000 K, and for H₂S at every temperature its list covers, from 296 K.
  - **Its bytes** (decision-r08-t4ef-storage §1). R08's line tables live in plain git under a cap
    of 150 MB over `absorbers/kDistributions/`, `absorbers/exomol/kDistributions/` and
    `absorbers/lines/`: T4.e within 60 MB, T4.f within what remains.
    - Hot tables take a temperature ladder (50 K steps to 1,000 K, 100 K to 2,000 K, 200 K
      beyond, each failing interval bisected twice) and each species' own range.
    - Alternate pressure nodes below 1 MPa are dropped where the between-node test passes on
      rows kept at 4 a decade (the rows the standard 30 pressures).
    - A raised first pressure node is allowed where its hold passes the 1 Pa check generalised.
    - Each task projects its bytes first. T4.f defers N₂, SiO, HCN and then H₂S above 500 K to
      their pending entries while over. Otherwise "main" rules.
  - **Where the data go.** `absorbers/exomol/<species>.json`, under CC BY-SA 4.0, with a sibling
    licence note and a `NOTICE` entry offering the adapted files under CC BY-SA 4.0. Never inside
    `crossSections.json` or code.
  - **The species:**
    - TiO (McKemmish et al. 2019, Toto) and VO (ExoMol's HyVO list, cited at fetch);
    - FeH's F⁴Δ–X⁴Δ bands below 760 nm (MoLLIST, Dulick et al. 2003, as ExoMol carries it);
    - hot H₂O (POKAZATEL, Polyansky et al. 2018), handing over from R08.T4.d's HITRAN at a
      recorded temperature where the two agree;
    - H₂S's visible overtones (AYT2, Azzam et al. 2016), from 296 K;
    - hot NH₃ from ExoMol's CoYuTe (Coles, Yurchenko and Tennyson 2019), which reaches 500 nm,
      over its coverage, with C2018 below 500 nm held at its temperature, `estimated`, deferred
      (decision-r08-t4ef-storage §5.4): held at C2018's 300 K with its pending entry;
    - CH₄ above 300 K, where an open line list reaches 380–760 nm. As known when ruled, none
      does: HITEMP 2020's CH₄ stops at 746 nm. Failing one, CH₄ is held at Eq. 8's 300 K
      value, `estimated`;
    - SiO's A–X hot bands (ExoMol's SiOUVenIR), which reach the range above about 1,000 K;
    - N₂'s first positive (B–A) bands above 1,800 K, from its metastable A state 6.17 eV up, as
      an LTE band model (Huber and Herzberg's constants), `estimated`;
    - hot CO and HCN (HITEMP or ExoMol, checked at fetch), handing over from R08.T4.d's HITRAN
      at recorded temperatures;
    - hot N₂O: not drawn. No plan-14 rule makes it above 500 K. Its table is held above 500 K,
      and its pending entry stays;
    - CO₂ above HITRAN's 500 K, considering ExoMol's UCL-4000 list (Yurchenko et al. 2020,
      MNRAS 496, 5282, to 20,000 cm⁻¹), checked at fetch. Venus's lowest 30 km or so, above
      500 K in VIRA (Seiff et al. 1985), is held at HITRAN's 500 K node and `estimated` until
      then;
    - any molecule P14.T52.a lists with a visible band system (AlO's B–X near 450–540 nm, CaH's,
      MgH's), from ExoMol or MoLLIST, checked at fetch. T52.a's other molecules are T4.c's stated
      none (science-r08-unowned-absorbers); of these only HCl applies, drawn in R08.T4.h.
  - Tests:
    - each reduced k-distribution passes R08.T4.d's node and between-node tests;
    - every T_c lies in [10⁻⁶, 1] and is non-increasing in u, for a 2,500 K and a 30,000 K sun;
    - the M-dwarf limitation (TiO in both the star and the planet) is recorded.
  - Acceptance: `pnpm --filter hyperion exec vitest run view/atmosphere/absorbers`.

- **R08.T4.g ExoMol's temperate lines: NH₃ (C2018) and N₂O (TYM)** (split from
  R08.T4.d, 2026-10-12). After T4.d, on its machinery.
  - **NH₃.** Its 552 and 648 nm bands from ExoMol's C2018 list (Coles et al. 2018, CC BY-SA 4.0),
    in `absorbers/exomol/` with a sibling licence note and a `NOTICE` entry, over C2018's
    temperatures (to 300 K), from where NH₃'s saturated column is negligible.
    - Its 243.7M transitions over 13,000–20,000 cm⁻¹ are reduced by super-lines: each node's line
      intensities binned on a grid finer than a tenth of the narrowest Voigt half-width, and the
      bins convolved with the Voigt profile by FFT, within 25 cm⁻¹ of each line as T4.d's shape.
    - Q(T) is summed from the states file, since ExoMol's `.pf` fetch returns 404.
    - C2018 gives no air widths. They are estimated from ExoMol's defaults (0.053 cm⁻¹ bar⁻¹,
      0.0537 cm⁻¹ atm⁻¹, n = 0.5) and its H₂ and He `.broad` files, by J where those give them, and the lines'
      broadening is `estimated`.
  - **N₂O from TYM.** ExoMol's TYM list (Yurchenko et al. 2024, Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc.,
    DOI 10.1093/mnras/stae2201; CC BY-SA 4.0), whose 1.36 billion transitions reach 20,000 cm⁻¹,
    by the same super-line/FFT reduction, in `absorbers/exomol/`
    (`decision-r08-t4d-kdist-chain.md` §11).
    - Below 714 nm, every TYM band.
    - Over 714–760 nm, each cell takes HITRAN2024's bands (T4.d's) and TYM's bands that
      HITRAN2024 lacks, each band from one list only.
    - Bands match by vibrational assignment and isotopologue (upper and lower v₁ v₂ l₂ v₃),
      checked by band centre and by 296 K band strength within a factor of 3, with the
      tolerances recorded. A matched TYM band is filtered from the states file before binning,
      and a doubtful match keeps HITRAN's, recorded.
    - Every cell holding TYM-derived lines moves to `absorbers/exomol/`.
    - TYM's lines inside HITRAN-held bands under HITRAN's intensity cut-off are left out. At
      296 K that cut-off bounds them, and above it follow-up 5's k = 100 does, until R08.T4.f.
    - Tests: over 714–760 nm, each cell's mean equals HITRAN2024's plus its added TYM bands', to
      10⁻⁹. No band appears from both lists.
  - **The machinery and tests** are T4.d's: the same nodes, refinement, interpolation, storage,
    chain, column caps and read (`decision-r08-t4d-kdist.md`, `decision-r08-t4d-kdist-chain.md`),
    and T4.d's node and between-node tests, the 16-bit test and the 1 Pa check. N₂O takes the
    condensing cap, and the between-node test stops at each species' own Rayleigh column as well.
  - **The pending entries.** NH₃'s and N₂O's `PENDING_ABSORBERS` entries (R08.T4.g) go, and
    their bounds with them, once the tables are committed.
  - Acceptance: `pnpm --filter hyperion exec vitest run view/atmosphere/absorbers`.

- **R08.T4.h The fifteen rows' answers** (split from R08.T4.e and T4.f, 2026-10-16; decision-r08-t4ef-storage and its addendum of 2026-10-19). After R08.T19; before P14.T54.a's bless.
  - The third reason (T4.e's "Stated transparency, the third reason") and T4.e's reference column, built in `src/tools/` for T4.e to reuse.
  - Stated nones for `Na+`, `Al+`, `Si+`, `K+`, `Ni+` and `Zn+` on Kurucz's full lists (Zn⁺'s on the lines NIST ASD lists, Kurucz holding none in the range), and Mg⁺'s check. An ion reaching 10⁻³ by 4,600 K is pending instead. Each stated none is pending from its `belowK` (4,600 or 5,000 K), as He's is.
  - Interim pending entries with T4.c's cell means for `Al`, `V`, `Mn`, `Ni`, `Zn`, `V+`, `Cr+` and `Mn+`, which T4.e's tables replace. The atomic and ionic entries it adds go in `absorbers/atomicBounds.json`.
  - HCl from HITRAN2024 on T4.d's machinery, to 500 K, with a science check of its 5–0 to 8–0 bands, failing which (or past its 2 MB budget) a pending entry with its cell means (science-r08-unowned-absorbers, erratum 2026-10-16).
  - A parity test holding the fifteen keys to condition 2.
  - Acceptance: `pnpm --filter hyperion exec vitest run view/atmosphere/absorbers view/atmosphere/parity`.

Acceptance: `pnpm --filter hyperion exec vitest run view/atmosphere/absorbers view/atmosphere/channels`.

### R08.T5 Aerosols

- **R08.T5.a Mie for a sphere.** `mie.ts` follows Wiscombe 1980's structure (Appl. Opt. 19, 1505):
  - N_stop = x + 4.05x^(1/3) + 2;
  - ψ_n and χ_n by upward recurrence;
  - D_n(mx) by downward recurrence started from Lentz 1976's continued fraction, or at
    n ≥ |mx| + 4.05|mx|^(1/3) + 16. The code says why BHMIE's start is not enough.

  Tests:
  - Wiscombe's published cases as miepython tabulates them (MIT), to 10⁻⁶, omitting
    m = 1.5 − i, x = 100, which miepython itself relaxes;
  - Bohren and Huffman's m = 1.55 case (Q_ext 3.10543, Q_back 2.92534, g 0.63314);
  - the Rayleigh limit;
  - Q_abs = 0 for a non-absorbing sphere to 10⁻¹²;
  - the phase normalisation to 10⁻⁹, on a Gauss–Legendre grid of more than N_stop nodes.

  The research timing (4.8–6.3 ms for x = 10³ at 256 angles) was taken under load and is re-measured
  here on a quiet machine. Acceptance: `pnpm --filter hyperion exec vitest run view/atmosphere/mie`.

- **R08.T5.b Size distributions and materials.**
  - `sizeDistribution.ts`: Gauss–Legendre in ln r over ±4σ, doubled until the phase integral and
    ⟨cos θ⟩ change by under 10⁻⁴, typically 200–500 nodes.
  - `materials/`: one refractive-index file per material, keyed by plan 14's material key
    (P14.T49.b; `H2O`, `NH3`, `CH4`, `CO2`, `H2SO4`, `NH4SH`, `Fe`, `soot`, `tholin`, `mars_dust`,
    and the silicates by species, `MgSiO3` and `Mg2SiO4`). Each file's header carries:
    - its paper and its source;
    - its licence basis (decision-composition §5);
    - its `provenance`: `measured`, `derived` (CO₂ ice's fit) or `standIn`;
    - its phase, its temperature and its shape class.

    `standIn` is general, NH₄SH's mechanism for any material without a measured visible index: a
    named analogue's file, or a constant index with its citation, under Design note 12's
    `ATMOSPHERE: APPROXIMATE` while the mode lies under less than
    `CLOUD_DECK_SPLIT_OPTICAL_DEPTH` at 550 nm. An unknown key (a newer server's) takes the generic
    stand-in, a non-absorbing sphere of real index 1.5 (a stated convention), under the same label.
    The files are also P14.T49.e's inputs: the sim's mass extinction is computed from them, so a
    changed file moves generated output. The first files, with their papers and CC0 or MIT copies:
    water (Hale and Querry 1973), ice (Warren and Brandt 2008), NH₃ ice (Martonchik et al. 1984),
    CH₄ (Martonchik and Orton 1994), silicates (Dorschner et al. 1995), soot, iron.

  - Ruled 2026-10-09 (`decision-r08-licences.md` rows 2–5). Each file is reduced by T4.a's Node
    tool from a source fetched by URL and SHA-256 and never committed. Its header carries:
    - its paper, its source, the checksum and the date fetched;
    - "reduced values; the source states no terms".

    The citation goes in `NOTICE`'s Data section. The files:
    - **H₂SO₄**, 75 and 84.5 wt% at 300 K, from Palmer and Williams 1975 (Appl. Opt. 14, 208) as
      ARIA distributes them:
      - `https://eodg.atm.ox.ac.uk/ARIA/data_files/Acids/Sulphuric/70%25_to_79%25/Sulphuric_acid_75%25_300K_(Palmer_and_Williams_1975)/original/H2SO4_75%25_300K_R_Palmer_1975.ri`
        (SHA-256 `ca84ce9a373bf9d0356dbbeeb59d61f771bf9d14667cecb3206f8a3cdac954fe`);
      - the `80%25_to_100%25/…84.5%25…` file
        (`6ae3eceb2c3895ec367f9b86e8e082445f1473413d224c2b625d85baaf452dc3`).

      In the visible they give n only, at 359.7, 408.2, 449.4, 555.6 and 701.8 nm, with k `NaN`.
      The file states how k is set there, and checks n against Hansen and Hovenier 1974's
      1.44 ± 0.015 at 550 nm.

    - **Mars dust** from Wolff et al. 2009 (JGR 114, E00D04): NASA Ames's
      `Dust_Refractive_Indicies.txt`, as kept at
      `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sukritranjan/ranjanwordsworthsasselov2017b/1e67a4819255ff907df2a97eb8cecd9eee32c928/Raw_Data/ComplexRefractionIndices/Dust_Refractive_Indicies.txt`
      (SHA-256 `bf6069ad22fbfbbef7bf957d386a8177647c87fd98ed6574b5c5f8d6c8016769`). The
      repository's MIT licence covers its code, not these data. The dust's literature
      single-scattering albedo and phase function follow the same rule: values with citation, no
      figure or file copied.
    - **Tholin** from Khare et al. 1984 (Icarus 60, 127), as HITRAN2024's aerosol compilation
      distributes it, inside <https://hitran.org/data/Aerosols/Aerosols-2024/hitran_ri.tar>
      (207,422,976 bytes). Its SHA-256 is recorded at the first fetch. Only Khare's ASCII file is
      read, and none of the archive's code is run. He et al. 2022 (PSJ 3, 25; CC BY 4.0) is the open
      alternative, and T5.b's science check picks between them.
    - **NH₄SH** has no measured visible optical constants (Howett et al. 2007 cover 1,300–12,000
      cm⁻¹).
      - Its stand-in is non-absorbing, with a Lorentz–Lorenz index (ruled 2026-10-10,
        science-r08-nonspherical.md §3.1).
        - The molar refraction is NH₃'s plus H₂S's from their measured dispersions (`rayleigh.ts`'s
          Cuthbertson rows), times 1.027, ammonium chloride's ionic increment (re-derived
          2026-10-10 from NH₃ and HCl in the same Cuthbertson paper, once NH₃'s formula was read at
          its theoretic density: Risks, "Deviations in T3.b's follow-up, as built"; then from
          NH₄Cl's X-ray cell and measured dispersion: "Deviations in T3.b's second follow-up, as
          built").
        - The density is 1.1717 g cm⁻³, from West 1934's cell (COD 1010249). The ruling's 1.1715
          is the entry's rounded cell volume; n differs by about 3 × 10⁻⁴.
        - The result is 1.674 at 380 nm, 1.638 at 550 nm and 1.623 at 780 nm, within +0.081 and
          −0.022 for an increment from 0 to +12%. The ruling's 1.685, 1.648 and 1.632 took NH₃ at
          the real gas's Z.
        - It replaces the earlier 1.80, which Sromovsky et al. 2017 state without a source and
          which would need a 22% larger molar refraction.
        - It is named `standIn` in its file.
      - A body whose medium shows an NH₄SH mode carries `ATMOSPHERE: APPROXIMATE` (Design note 12).
      - No NH₄SH case is committed or gated.
    - **CO₂ ice**, a derived file rather than a reduction of a fetched data file: no data file
      exists, and refractiveindex.info, NASA's OCdb and ARIA hold none over 0.3–1 µm
      (`science-r08-sulphur-co2ice.md`, 2026-10-09).
      - The real index is n(λ) = 1.3994 + 0.004312 µm² ÷ λ², a two-term Cauchy fit to Warren 1986's
        Table I over 0.30–1.10 µm (Appl. Opt. 25, 2650, pp. 2663–2667).
        - Warren's index comes from Kramers–Kronig, "accurate to ±0.05", and the fit departs from
          it by under 0.001.
        - The fit was made by the science agent from the author's copy:
          `https://atmos.uw.edu/~sgw/PAPERS/1986_CO2ice_mcx.pdf`, SHA-256
          `55873a3bcb4820867112c1243b4f583fa311f995d9a56f3db26f635664a7b485`, fetched 2026-10-09.
      - The imaginary index is k = αλ ÷ 4π with α = 10⁻² m⁻¹, Hansen 2005's estimated visible
        absorption (JGR 110, E11003), below that paper's detection limit over 0.25–1.0 µm.
        Warren's Egan–Spagnolo k, about 10³ larger, is the stated upper bound.
      - The header carries both papers, the fit and its residual. It reads: "derived values: Optica
        holds Warren's article under its pre-2017 agreement (reuse by permission only, text and
        data mining reserved; its copyright page, 2026-10-09), and AGU's terms for Hansen 2005
        could not be read; the data are the authors' (decision-r08-licences.md)". Its citation goes
        in `NOTICE`'s Data section.
      - No table of Warren's is committed.
      - Its shape class is crystal (T24.c), so Mie supplies cross-sections only.

  - Until the H₂SO₄ file lands, the Venus mode-2 test below takes the single index n = 1.44 at
    550 nm that Hansen and Hovenier 1974 publish.
  - The non-spherical materials' phase functions and matrices are R08.T5.c's
    (science-r08-nonspherical.md).

  Tests:
  - the distribution reproduces r_eff and v_eff to 10⁻⁴;
  - every file covers 380–780 nm;
  - a narrow distribution equals the single sphere;
  - a mode's table carries its scattering matrix (a₁ = a₂ and a₃ = a₄ for spheres, b₁ and b₂,
    from S₁ and S₂ in T5.a's convention). A sphere of x = 10⁻³ reproduces Hansen and Travis
    1974's Rayleigh matrix (eq. 2.15, δ = 0) to 10⁻⁶. The single-scattering degree of
    polarisation is −b₁ ÷ a₁;
  - Venus's mode-2 droplets (r_eff 1.05 µm, v_eff 0.07, n ≈ 1.44 at 550 nm; Hansen and
    Hovenier 1974) give g within that paper's figure;
  - an NH₄SH mode with less than `CLOUD_DECK_SPLIT_OPTICAL_DEPTH` above it gives
    `atmosphereApproximate`, and one beneath a τ 30 deck does not;
  - CO₂ ice's real index is 1.413 ± 0.001 at 553 nm and 1.404 ± 0.001 at 1,000 nm (Warren 1986,
    Table I, asserted values);
  - its k lies between 0 and 2.2 × 10⁻⁶ over 380–780 nm;
  - a 2 µm sphere's single-scattering albedo at 550 nm exceeds 0.9999;
  - an unknown material key gives the generic stand-in and `atmosphereApproximate`;
  - once P14.T49.b's rows exist, every file's key is a row of `substances.json` (R08.T19 checks
    it).

- **The follow-up to R08.T5.b: two rulings on its files** (science-r08-nonspherical.md §3,
  2026-10-10).
  - NH₄SH: the tool computes the stand-in's n(λ) from the formula in §3.1 on the file's grid,
    replacing `NH4SH_STAND_IN_N`. The file's `standIn`, which the operator reads under the label,
    states the estimate, its three indices and its band. Its `source` states the inputs (the two
    Cuthbertson dispersions, West 1934's cell via COD 1010249, NH₄Cl's increment), the NH₃-ice
    check, the basis for k = 0 and the withdrawn 1.80 (science-r08-mmf.md §4.8). `provenance`
    stays `standIn`, and the label is unchanged.
  - Mars dust: the values are unchanged, and the 321 nm row stays the 380–440 nm anchor. The
    file's reduction text no longer counts the 263 nm row as used. It states that the two
    ultraviolet rows are part of Wolff's distributed compilation, separately retrieved (k to
    three figures), presumably Wolff et al. 2010's MARCI values (Icarus 208, 143), unconfirmed.
  - Tests:
    - NH₄SH's n is 1.648 ± 0.001 at 550 nm and falls monotonically from 380 to 780 nm, with
      k = 0 (replacing the 1.80 test). _Superseded 2026-10-10:_ 1.638 ± 0.001, with NH₃ at its
      theoretic density and the increment re-derived (Risks, "Deviations in T3.b's follow-up, as
      built" and "Deviations in T3.b's second follow-up, as built");
    - Mars dust's k at 380 nm lies above its 440 nm value (0.00767) and at or below the
      log-linear extrapolation of its 440–500 nm rows (0.0107).
  - Acceptance: `pnpm --filter hyperion exec vitest run view/atmosphere/materials`.

- **R08.T5.c Aggregates, non-spherical grains and phase tables.** Each non-spherical class gets
  optics from a published model (science-r08-nonspherical.md, 2026-10-10), and every mode gets
  its √θ phase tables.
  - _Aggregates._ `aggregate.ts` implements Tazaki and Tanaka 2018's MMF with D_f ≤ 2.5. It gates by
    Design note 6 on their (9), Δφ = max(2x₀|m − 1|, 2kR_c|m_MG − 1|), as optool computes it
    (`mmfPhaseBasis`; ruled 2026-10-10, science-r08-mmf.md, which leaves no choice of rule):
    - Δφ < 1 and |m − 1| < 2: the MMF table and matrix, a `model`;
    - Δφ ≥ 1 with 2kR_c|m_MG − 1| < 1: the same table and matrix, optool's `-mmfss` result, an
      `analogue`;
    - 2kR_c|m_MG − 1| < 1 with |m − 1| ≥ 2 (Tazaki and Tanaka's (7)): the same, an `analogue`;
    - 2kR_c|m_MG − 1| ≥ 1: its opacities, with a Henyey–Greenstein phase from its MMF asymmetry, a
      `fallback` with no matrix.

    An aggregate's matrix is kept only if it agrees with optool's elements to their stated tolerance
    (`-mmfss`'s past the gate); otherwise `matrix` is `undefined`, a total depolariser, flagged in
    the code (Design note 10).

  - _Non-spherical minerals_ (`nonSphericalMineral`: dust, the silicates and T5.d's condensates)
    take TAMUdust2020's ensemble of 20 irregular hexahedra (Saito, Yang, Ding and Liu 2021,
    J. Atmos. Sci. 78, 2089) at sphericity 0.71. That is the best fit to three Martian dust
    analogues' measured matrices (Martikainen et al. 2025, MNRAS 537, 1489).
    - Source: the data kernels, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.4711247, v1.0.0, CC BY 4.0,
      `TAMUdust2020-DataKernels-v1.0-20210422.tar.gz` (7,939,243,504 bytes, MD5
      `ff4abf3ee2919494d47679ffc4cba817`; its SHA-256 recorded at the first fetch). The archive's
      GPL-3.0 Fortran is read for the kernels' record layout only, and none of it is ported or
      committed.
    - Ranges, in the kernels' size parameter x = 2πD ÷ λ (D the maximum dimension; the v1.1.0
      README and the code, superseding v1.0's πD ÷ λ):
      - the shortwave kernel: x ≤ 11,800, n 1.37–1.70, k 10⁻⁴–0.1;
      - the longwave kernel: x ≤ 1,470, n 0.4–3.2, k 10⁻³–4.

      Both tabulate in (x, m), so either serves the visible wherever m lies inside it. Below a
      kernel's smallest x, the volume-equivalent sphere's Mie.

    - Below a kernel's k floor, the floor's matrix and C_sca, with absorption scaled by k ÷ k_floor,
      while the floor's own ω at that size is at least 0.99. Beyond that the mode is an `analogue`,
      or a `fallback` above n 1.70.
    - Liquid iron is a `sphere` (Mie). Solid iron takes the longwave kernel. The mode's
      `form.phase` chooses: iron condenses as a liquid deeper than about 0.7 bar at solar
      metallicity (Visscher, Lodders and Fegley 2010, eq. 2; melting point 1,809 K).
  - _Crystals_ (`crystal`).
    - Water ice takes Yang et al. 2013's aggregate of eight hexagonal columns, severely roughened
      (σ = 0.5), in version 2 (Bi and Yang 2017). That is the MODIS Collection 6 habit, and the best
      fit to in-situ angular scattering at 532 and 804 nm (Järvinen et al. 2018, ACP 18, 15767).
    - Source: Zenodo record 5348402, CC BY 4.0, `Data_0.2_15.25.tar.gz` (27,420,579,422 bytes, MD5
      `2fb9bbab2c2c735a869c863a680e2f70`), of which only `8_columns/Rough050/` is extracted. Its
      crystals are 2–10,000 µm in maximum dimension. Below 2 µm, the equal volume-to-area sphere's
      Mie, labelled when that tail carries more than 10% of the mode's C_sca at 550 nm.
    - The other ices (NH₃, CH₄, CO₂, NH₄SH, and T5.d's H₂S, N₂ and CO) have no published visible
      phase function. They take water ice's table at their own size parameter as a named
      `analogue`, with Mie's cross-sections and ω for their own index. Its g bias by van
      Diedenhoven et al. 2014's eq. (16) (NH₃ −0.056, CO₂ −0.048, CH₄ −0.007) is recorded in
      Risks.
    - A `crystal` that is not an ice takes the hexahedra.
  - _The reduction._ A Node tool on T5.b's pattern (`src/tools/nonSpherical.ts`,
    `scripts/nonSpherical.mjs`) reads the unpacked kernels by offset from an untracked directory,
    inside the capped scope's 3 GB.
    - It writes `materials/phase/<file>.json` for each material file the kernels cover: C_ext,
      C_sca, V and A, and C_sca × a₁, a₂, a₃, a₄, b₁ and b₂, per wavelength node and size node,
      on a reduced angle grid.
    - Wavelength nodes are chosen so that n moves by under 0.01 and k by under a factor of 1.26
      (the shortwave kernel's own k step) between nodes. Each file stays under 400 kB.
    - b₂ takes the sign that reproduces the laboratory F₃₄ (test below), in T5.b's convention.
    - Each header carries the source, DOI, checksum and date, "adapted from CC BY 4.0 data", the
      model and its sphericity or habit.
    - `NOTICE` gains the "Data" and "Test data" entries drafted in science-r08-nonspherical.md §4.
  - `nonSphericalModeOptics(mode, λ, mu?)` integrates the mode's distribution over the table's
    nodes, in the volume-to-area radius r = 3V ÷ 4A, and returns `ModeOptics` with its matrix.
    A is the orientation-averaged projected area, S ÷ 4 for a convex particle. A mode's r_eff and
    v_eff are Hansen and Travis's cross-section-weighted moments of r, so r_eff = (3 ÷ 4)⟨V⟩ ÷ ⟨A⟩
    for every shape class: a sphere's radius, and Yang et al. 2013's D_eff ÷ 2 for ice. A size cited
    from visible or near-infrared scattering (the sky near a sun, a phase function, an extinction
    spectrum) is converted at equal projected area, which fixes the forward lobe and the
    geometric-optics extinction: r = Ψ^(3/2) r_A with Ψ the mode's sphericity (0.71 for the
    hexahedra), where r_A = r_S for a surface-equivalent size and r_V ÷ √Ψ_source for a
    volume-equivalent one. v_eff is unchanged. Only a size fixed by mass or by absorption alone
    converts at equal V/A (science-r08-mmf.md §3).
  - _Basis and label._ `ModeOptics` gains `phaseBasis`:
    - `model`: Mie for spheres, MMF inside Δφ < 1 with |m − 1| < 2 (Tazaki and Tanaka's (9) and
      (7)) at any D_f the inventory allows (1 < D_f ≤ 2.5; `decision-r08-aerosol-labels.md`
      item 1), a kernel inside its ranges, Yang et al. for water ice;
    - `analogue`: the k-floor rule exceeded, another ice on water's table, the small-crystal
      tail, an aggregate past (9) whose own term 2kR_c|m_MG − 1| is below 1, or an aggregate
      monomer past (7);
    - `fallback`: the Henyey–Greenstein phase below.

    Two labelling questions were signed off 2026-10-10 (`signoff-2.md` item 5;
    science-r08-nonspherical.md §5, items 1 and 2) and are built as `aerosol.ts`'s
    `MODEL_RESIDUALS_LABEL` and `SMALL_BIAS_ANALOGUES` (`decision-r08-aerosol-labels.md` item 2):
    - a validated model with known residuals is `model` and unlabelled, as Mie is for spheres,
      with its residuals recorded in Risks (the hexahedra run 20–37% low at side and back angles);
    - every analogue is labelled, CH₄ ice's included, though its estimated Δg is only −0.007,
      with no exemption by estimated bias.

    An `analogue` or `fallback` mode with less than `CLOUD_DECK_SPLIT_OPTICAL_DEPTH` above it at
    550 nm gives `atmosphereApproximate` (Design note 12).

  - _The fallback_ stays only for an aggregate whose own term 2kR_c|m_MG − 1| is at least 1 and for
    a non-spherical mineral outside
    both kernels: n above 1.70 with k under 10⁻³ beyond the floor rule (larger Al₂O₃, TiO₂,
    CaTiO₃ and ZnS grains). It is a Henyey–Greenstein phase from Mie's g, with Mie's ω and no
    matrix.
    - Small grains of such a mineral take the sphere's own Mie table and matrix instead, still a
      `fallback`. That applies below the effective size parameter at which the shortwave kernel's
      hexahedra and spheres agree to 5% in a₁, which the builder measures at n = 1.6 and records.
      As x → 0 every compact shape tends to the dipole phase function, (3 ÷ 4)(1 + cos²θ), while
      Henyey–Greenstein tends to isotropic, a factor of 2 wrong at 90° against forward
      (science-r08-nonspherical.md §2.5, adopted).
  - Beside them go the √θ phase tables per channel (`PHASE_TABLE_U`), with the matrix elements
    where the model gives them, and the delta-M truncated series with its fraction, for the bakes
    only (Design note 6).
  - _A follow-up, once both R08.T4.a and T5.c have landed_ ("main", 2026-10-10): T4.a fitted the
    channels with Mars dust under T5.b's provisional Henyey–Greenstein phase, so `channels.ts`'s
    `marsFitAir` moves to the hexahedra table (at r_eff 0.8974 µm, science-r08-mmf.md §3) and
    `channels.json` is blessed again before R08.T6.d, through T4.a's bless step (`test/bless.ts`,
    `spectralColour.ts`). The triple and residuals before and after are recorded in Risks. It is
    its own small commit, not T5.c's.
  - Tests (asserted values cited to science-r08-nonspherical.md §2):
    - optool fixtures for a Titan-like aggregate (monomer 0.05 µm, about 3,000 monomers, D_f = 2;
      Tomasko et al. 2008), generated offline and committed, to their stated tolerance, with
      `-mmfss` at the wavelengths past the gate (380 and 440 nm);
    - the Titan-like aggregate's Δφ is 1.09, 0.80 and 0.54 (± 0.01) at 380, 550 and 780 nm, and its
      aggregate term 0.92, 0.67 and 0.45. It is a `model` at 550 and 780 nm, and an `analogue` at
      380 nm whose table and matrix are optool's `-mmfss`. A compact large aggregate whose own term
      exceeds 1 is a Henyey–Greenstein `fallback`;
    - the reduction (the tool's test, on committed raw-kernel fixtures): a test distribution over
      a reduced table matches the same integral over the kernel's nodes to 1% in a₁ at every table
      angle and to 0.002 in g and ω;
    - fidelity: MGS-1 M (n 1.50, k 4.33 × 10⁻⁴, its tabulated size distribution
      `size_MGS1M_6.txt`, a test-only distribution in its own projected-area-equivalent radius,
      mapped onto the kernel by each node's own A, sphericity 0.71) at 650 nm gives
      Martikainen et al. 2025's g 0.7111 ± 0.005 and ω 0.9905 ± 0.002;
    - against that sample's measured matrix at 640 nm (Martikainen et al. 2024, ApJS 273, 28):
      - a₁ ÷ a₁(30°) within 40% of 0.141, 0.105, 0.099 and 0.119 at 90°, 120°, 150° and 170°;
      - −b₁ ÷ a₁ positive at 90° (0.147) and negative at 165° (−0.039);
      - a₂ ÷ a₁ at 170° within 0.15 of 0.54 (measured 0.556 at 169° and 0.520 at 171°);
      - b₂ ÷ a₁ at 90° of the sign of F₃₄ ÷ F₁₁ (+0.137);

      spheres of its distribution give 0.081, 0.041, 0.101 and 0.304, and fail;

    - Mars dust (the `mars_dust` file; gamma r_eff 0.8974 µm, v_eff 0.3, which is Wolff et al.
      2009's surface-equivalent r_eff of 1.5 µm at equal projected area, × 0.71^(3/2);
      science-r08-mmf.md §3) at 650 nm:
      - g within 0.673 ± 0.081, and a₁(150°) ÷ a₁(90°) within 0.5–0.85 (Chen-Chen, Pérez-Hoyos
        and Sánchez-Lavega 2019, Icarus 330, 16: MSL's sky, 0.71);
      - ω within 0.975 ± 0.015 (Wolff et al. 2009's, as Chen-Chen et al. take it);
      - its forward lobe: the resolved a₁'s half-width at half maximum (without `forwardPeak`) at
        645 and 434 nm within 15% of Mie spheres of the same distribution in r_A (gamma r_eff
        1.5 µm, v_eff 0.3, on the file's index, by T5.b's Mie; the ruling's proxy gives 4.04° and
        2.72°). At r_eff 1.2247 µm it fails, about 27% narrow (32% as built: T5.c's record);
    - enstatite at 520 nm (Frattin et al. 2019, MNRAS 484, 2198; ruled 2026-10-10,
      science-r08-nonspherical.md §7):
      - the particle takes the sample's own composition, Mg₀.₈₅Fe₀.₀₈Si₀.₉₉O₃ (its §4.1.2), as
        Dorschner et al. 1995's pyroxene glasses give it: 1.594 + 4.5 × 10⁻⁴i, linear in n and
        log-linear in k between Mg₀.₉₅ (1.588 + 2.9 × 10⁻⁴i) and Mg₀.₈₀ (1.612 + 1.7 × 10⁻³i). This
        index is test-only, and the MgSiO₃ file stays iron-free;
      - its sizes are `size_enstatite.txt`'s MIE section (r_eff 3.71 µm, v_eff 3.14; the paper's
        Tables 3 and 4), with r read as the volume-equivalent radius (its §4.3.2) and mapped by the
        table's own r_VA ÷ r_V, cut at 290 µm. The FRAUNHOFER section is not used;
      - a₁(170°) ÷ a₁(90°) lies within 0.5–1.2 (measured 0.77);
      - −b₁ ÷ a₁ is positive at 90° (measured +0.108 ± 0.003);
      - a₁ ÷ a₁(30°) lies within a factor of 2 of the measured 0.149, 0.110, 0.102 and 0.115 at
        90°, 120°, 150° and 170°. The test also asserts that spheres of the same table, and
        Henyey–Greenstein at the mode's g, each fail that bound at one angle or more;
      - the residual at each angle is recorded in the as-built notes, beside its value with the
        iron-free index, with the projected-area reading and with sphericity 0.695.
    - the k-floor rule: at n = 1.6 on the shortwave kernel, a₁ at k 10⁻³ and at 10⁻⁴ differ by
      under 2% wherever ω at 10⁻³ is at least 0.99;
    - the small-grain rule: the size parameter it starts below is recorded, and a fallback-class
      mode below it carries the sphere's Mie matrix and is still a `fallback`;
    - water ice (gamma r_eff 30 µm, v_eff 0.1):
      - g = 0.750 ± 0.010 at 532 nm and 0.754 ± 0.010 at 780 nm (Järvinen et al. 2018);
      - no local maximum of a₁ between 15° and 50°;
    - labels:
      - an NH₃-ice mode is an `analogue` and a 3 µm TiO₂ mode a `fallback`, each giving
        `atmosphereApproximate` under the τ rule;
      - a Mars dust mode and a water-ice mode do not;
    - tables integrate to 1 to 10⁻⁶, and the truncated series plus its fraction reproduces the
      full integral and asymmetry.

Acceptance for T5.b and T5.c:
`pnpm --filter hyperion exec vitest run view/atmosphere/sizeDistribution view/atmosphere/aggregate view/atmosphere/nonSpherical view/atmosphere/materials view/atmosphere/aerosol src/tools/nonSpherical`.

- **R08.T5.d The registry's condensates and hazes** (decision-composition). After T5.b and T5.c,
  and before galaxy plan 14's P14.T49.e, which reads these files.
  - Index files, by T5.b's rules, for KCl, NaCl, ZnS, Na₂S, MnS, Cr, FeS, MgSiO₃, Mg₂SiO₄, SiO₂,
    Al₂O₃, CaTiO₃, TiO₂, graphite, S₈, H₂S ice, N₂ ice, CO ice, the chromophore (Braude et al.
    2020's retrieved absorption, reduced) and the ice giants' haze (Irwin et al. 2022), and
    `acid_uv_absorber` (below), each from its primary measurement.
    - `acid_uv_absorber` (science-r08-unowned-absorbers): `H2SO4`'s 75 wt% index, with
      k = k_H₂SO₄ + k_UA. Its `provenance` is `standIn`.
      - k_UA = k₃₆₅ e^(−(λ − 365 nm)/L) over 360–500 nm, times (550 − λ) ÷ 50 nm over 500–550 nm,
        and 0 from 550 nm.
      - The a-priori values are k₃₆₅ = 1.2 × 10⁻³ and L = 26.9 nm, the bound from Spacek et al.
        2026's 1278 and under-54 cm⁻¹ at 375 and 455 nm. R08.T5.e refits them.
      - The file covers 360–780 nm, so that T5.e can fit at 365 nm.
      - Its shape class is sphere, and its phase basis is Mie, a `model`.
      - Its stand-in text: "an empirical absorber: H₂SO₄ droplets with an unidentified ultraviolet
        absorber, whose k is fitted to Venus's albedo spectrum (candidates FeCl₃, S₂O/OSSO, Sₓ,
        organics)".
  - Kitzmann and Heng 2018's compilation (LX-MIE's `compilation/`, GPL-3.0 repository, no
    separate data terms) is the finding aid. Each primary is fetched from its own distribution
    where one exists. Where the compilation is the only machine-readable copy, its values are
    reduced to 380–780 nm on the file's grid and cited to both the primary and Kitzmann and Heng.
    No compilation file, and none of LX-MIE's code, is committed (decision-composition §5).
  - A material without visible data takes a stated stand-in.
  - Every `nonSphericalMineral` or `crystal` file takes its phase basis by T5.c's rules, decided
    from its own index and recorded in its phase file or header:
    - a reduced TAMUdust2020 table where a kernel covers it (KCl, NaCl and SiO₂ in the shortwave
      kernel by the k-floor rule; Cr, FeS and graphite in the longwave);
    - the floor rule, then the fallback, for transparent grains above n 1.70 (Al₂O₃, TiO₂,
      CaTiO₃, ZnS, Na₂S, MnS and S₈);
    - water ice's table as the named analogue for H₂S, N₂ and CO ice.
  - Any registry material a dust can be made of (P14.T24.c) needs a file or a stand-in. Leads for
    the lithologies (science-r08-nonspherical.md §2.1, unverified): Pollack, Toon and Khare 1973
    for basalt and other rocks, and Martikainen et al. 2023 (ApJS 268, 47, CC BY 4.0) for the
    Mars simulants.
  - Tests:
    - every file covers 380–780 nm and names its provenance;
    - every aerosol-material row of `substances.json` has a file or a stated stand-in;
    - every `nonSphericalMineral` or `crystal` file has a phase table, a named analogue or the
      stated fallback;
    - a 1 µm forsterite sphere's single-scattering albedo at 550 nm lies above 0.99, and an iron
      sphere's lies below a forsterite sphere's of the same size (Mie on the files);
    - a solid-iron grain's a₂ ÷ a₁ at 170° lies below 0.95;
    - a Venus-class deck whose mode 2 is `acid_uv_absorber` gives `atmosphereApproximate` for it,
      and its k is 0 from 550 nm.
  - Acceptance: `pnpm --filter hyperion exec vitest run view/atmosphere/materials view/atmosphere/nonSpherical`.

- **R08.T5.g The liquids' optical constants** (briefed 2026-10-14; client data only, no
  GENERATOR_VERSION bump). After T5.d. The surface payload's palette gains a liquid record for
  R11's water and lakes: n and absorption at each of the 15 bake bins (380–760 nm), plus
  scattering. R08's material files stay the one source of liquids' n and k.
  - _Water._ `water.json`'s k over 380–727.5 nm becomes Pope and Fry 1997's (Appl. Opt. 36, 8710),
    from its open distribution, with Hale and Querry 1973's kept above 727.5 nm and Mason, Cone and
    Fry 2016 (Appl. Opt. 55, 7163) recorded as a cross-check below 550 nm. The file's header names
    the change and the factor by which the blue fell (Hale and Querry's k is about 5 times Pope and
    Fry's at 440 nm). n stays Hale and Querry's unless a better open n exists over 380–780 nm,
    which is recorded. Pure water, not seawater: a scattering column, if the file gains one, takes
    pure water's (Zhang, Hu and He 2009, Opt. Express 17, 5698, at S = 0, or Morel's pure-water
    column), and any seawater variant is recorded apart.
  - _New liquid files_, where open measured visible constants exist, each `measured` or `derived`
    with its basis, by T5.b–T5.d's format and rules (the per-file grid, provenance and stand-in
    fields, licences and `NOTICE`, the reduction tool):
    - liquid ethane (Titan's seas): the search recorded if nothing is measured, as `sulphur.json`
      records its own; a Lorentz–Lorenz n of about 1.40 at 94 K, with absorption absent;
    - liquid N₂;
    - liquid NH₃;
    - seawater, with Quan and Fry 1995's n;
    - molten sulphur's absorption edge, with Meyer 1976 (Chem. Rev. 76, 367) as the finding aid.
  - _The fitted table._ `water.json`'s dataset hash changes, so the fit tool marks
    `condensate_extinction` stale. It is not refitted here; a desktop lane refits it with no bump.
  - Tests: each new file parses; water's k at 440 nm lies within 10% of Pope and Fry's; the parity
    check, if one lists material keys, covers the new liquid keys.
  - Acceptance: `pnpm --filter hyperion exec vitest run src/renderer/src/view/atmosphere/materials`.

- **R08.T5.h Water's index and absorption, and liquid ethane's measured level** (briefed
  2026-10-15, decision-r08-t5g; client data, `variantWords` and tests only, no GENERATOR_VERSION
  bump, no contract change). After T5.g, and before P14.T49.h, whose palette reads `water.json`'s n
  with the oracle "IAPWS R9-97 within 5 × 10⁻⁴". It corrects T5.g's liquid files with better
  sources and takes up three of T5.g's deferred findings: _Water's n_, _Pope and Fry below 420 nm_
  and _Water's junction_.
  - _Water's n_ (ruling 1): IAPWS R9-97's eq. 1 at 298.15 K and 997.0476 kg m⁻³, every 5 nm over
    380–780 nm, to six figures; the file stays `measured`. The header gives the release's
    uncertainty by range (its Table 2), the check on Daimon and Masumura 2007's 24 °C formula and
    the change from Hale and Querry. `sizeDistributionStop.test.ts`'s held water mode takes T5.b's
