  _QW3_; "Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)" (R08.T8.e), _The hold's four rows_).

Widen R05's ray march to N terms and several sources: each body's list of Design note 7 (its stars
and its planetshine sources), with no source skipped outside the air (since R08.T8.e both of
Design note 7's skips also hold outside it, and the march takes at most two). The march draws any body's
atmosphere other than the ship's local body (`SceneFrame.localBody`) at its `apparentM` from R03's
`sceneAt(model, observer, time, previous)` (Design note 13), with the limb, the terminator and the
planet's shadow in its own air; a `contact` body, which has no position, draws none. The switch to
the sky-view table is by altitude, with a blend band.

A body seen from outside takes Design note 18's spheroid rule with its own quadric constants,
formed in `f64` from the camera's position relative to it, and the closest-approach form beyond
a ÷ 2. At the far limb this task delivers:

- the twin checks at 10⁷, 10⁸ and 10⁹ m, under Design note 18's rule for texels the twin cannot
  resolve, on views narrowed so that the limb's lowest scale height spans at least four texels.
  The 1% cap holds at 10⁷ m. At 10⁸ and 10⁹ m the share is recorded rather than capped, every
  texel stays within 10⁻³ or within its envelope, and the median and largest envelope half-widths
  are recorded per distance;
- the far limb's fidelity under Design note 10's 5%: per distance, the march's limb pixels at the
  output resolution against the twin's mean over each pixel's footprint (8 × 8 sub-rays), on Design
  note 10's limb set. A pixel over 5% is reported to "main" for a ruling: integration across the
  limb, or R07's disc taking over sooner for that body (_ruled 2026-10-21, integration across the
  texel: R08.T8.c, `decision-r08-t8-leans.md` §6.1_).

Tests (no GPU):

- the CPU march just inside the top agrees with the sky-view twin to 1% at the band's edges (_a
  recorded figure since `decision-r08-t8-leans.md` §3; Risks, "Deviations in T8.a, as built"_);
- R05.T12.e's quadrature gate holds for the widened march, at one source and at
  `MAX_SKY_SOURCES`;
- the sky-view table's interpolation across the limb, from cameras at 60–100 km, against the march
  at the same pixels, recorded with the blend band's altitudes;
- the limb falls to zero outside the top;
- a body's atmosphere is drawn at `apparentM`, and only the ship's local body at `geometricM`,
  including when a free camera sits inside another body's Hill sphere;
- the fitted triple's u′v′ error on the limb seen from orbit, by R08.T4.a's colour pipeline (its
  direct beam and singly scattered light, as the channel fit's objective models them), is recorded
  here: views from orbit are not in the channel fit's family, and a limb chord carries about twice
  the horizon's column, whose direct beam is already 0.022 off (R08.T4.a).

Acceptance: `pnpm test` and `just test-render` pass, and by hand an ascent from R05's test planet
to 10⁸ m shows no step at the switch, recorded here.

### R08.T9 Aerial perspective and surface lighting

- **R08.T9.a Aerial perspective.**
  - On the low setting, R05's deferred aerial perspective applies to terrain alone. On the high
    setting it applies to everything opaque (`AERIAL_PERSPECTIVE_SCOPE` in `settings.ts`, the
    projection of R05's `TableSizes.aerialPerspectiveScope`, `"terrain"` and `"scene"`).
  - Beyond the volume's 32 km reach (Hillaire 2020 §5.4, confirmed) the march takes over.
  - `aerialPerspective(view)`, widening R05's `aerialPerspectiveVolume()` (which returns `null` on
    `"terrain"`), exposes the volume and transmittance, and `skyView(view)` the view's summed
    sky-view table, to R11.

  Tests (no GPU):
  - a point at the volume's far edge takes the same in-scattering from volume and march to 2%;
  - the low setting touches terrain alone;
  - `skyView(view)` returns the table `drawFrame` built this frame.

  Acceptance: `pnpm test` passes, and by hand R05's descent shows fog continuous through 32 km,
  recorded here with the pass's time.

- **R08.T9.b Surface lighting.** `irradiance.wgsl` builds the per-planet sky-irradiance table
  (64 × 16 by altitude and sun zenith, Bruneton 2017's layout) with his texel mapping (Design
  note 19) from the transmittance and multiple-scattering tables, one layer a latitude band (Design
  note 17). It is rebuilt with them and has a CPU twin in `tablesCpu.ts`. `surfaceLighting.wgsl` exports
  `atmosphere_sun_transmittance` and `atmosphere_sky_irradiance`, with the latitude and sun azimuth
  arguments of the Provides, for R07's `litBody.wgsl` callers, R10's `terrainLit.wgsl` and R11's lit
  passes. Both are catalogued. `irradiance.wgsl` and `surfaceLighting.wgsl` follow Design note 18.
  Each lookup takes the caller's geodetic height, never a radius. The planet's shadow is
  `groundHitFromHeight`, and no module calls built-in trigonometry. A caller passes a baked or
  interpolated height above the datum (R05 Design note 5) and a cosine against the datum normal,
  never |P| − R. As built, the two names are R07's stubs in `view/shaders/litBody.wgsl` (1 and 0),
  so this task:
  - removes the stubs there, the modules that include `litBody.wgsl` joining
    `surfaceLighting.wgsl` in their place (WGSL resolves every name in a module);
  - binds the body's transmittance and irradiance tables to the disc materials, the smooth mesh and
    the `disc cells` kernel through `view/bodies/draw.ts`'s `DISC_TEXTURES`, at group 2 bindings 6
    and above (0–5 are taken). The `disc cells` kernel, a compute kernel, binds a one-layer table
    through R08.T0's seam;
  - has the callers in `bodyDisc.wgsl` pass the geodetic height and latitude from the spheroid
    normal and the sun's azimuth from local north, in place of R07's zeros, and take the sky term
    per light rather than once at the first light's μ₀;
  - keeps planetshine through the air, as Design note 7 rules (R07 left the choice to this plan).
    Each source's direct term goes through `atmosphere_source_transmittance`, the three-node disc
    rule over `atmosphere_sun_transmittance` at its centre's μ and azimuth, with light slot 0's
    absorber curve. Its sky term is its illuminance times `atmosphere_sky_irradiance` at its own μ,
    on the Lambert share as a star's is. Both terms, a star's and a planetshine source's, are added
    outside R07's below-horizon `continue`, so that a source just set still lights the twilight
    ground;
  - gives `atmosphere_sun_transmittance` the light's absorber-curve slot as a fifth argument,
    `curve : u32`, and `atmosphere_sky_irradiance` the same slot as a fourth. Design note 5's
    curves are per sun, and the shorter forms cannot pick one.
    - Under a medium with an absorber, the irradiance table has one layer per light slot (with
      R08.T6.f's bands, band × slot), each built from that slot's multiple-scattering layer and
      curves, as R08.T7 rules for the multiple-scattering table (`decision-r08-t6b-floor.md` §8).
      A medium with no absorber keeps one.
    - A planetshine source passes slot 0.
    - R10's `terrainLit.wgsl` and R11's lit passes pass both, and take planetshine through the same
      functions;
  - rewrites `view/appearance/litBodyProbe.ts`'s and its smoke check's pins of the stubs' 1, 1
    and 0 against the tables' twin.

  A body without an atmosphere binds R07's one-texel defaults and reads 1 and 0, as the stubs did.

  Tests (no GPU, twin):
  - at the top of the atmosphere the sun's transmittance is 1 and the sky's irradiance is 0;
  - with no scattering terms the irradiance is 0 at every altitude;
  - Earth's surface irradiance, direct plus diffuse at a sun zenith of 0°, lies between the
    direct beam alone and the top's; R08.T13 checks it against the reference;
  - on a Saturn-class figure at equal sun zenith, the pole's diffuse irradiance at the datum is
    below the equator's, by the band tables' column ratio;
  - a planetshine source and a star of equal illuminance and direction, with ρ → 0, light a point
    identically, direct and sky;
  - the three-node rule equals the centre's lookup as ρ → 0 to 10⁻⁶, and at ρ = 9.8° and 10° of
    elevation on Earth's medium it agrees with a 200 × 200 quadrature over the disc in the twin to
    2%;
  - a source 2° below the local horizon gives no direct term and a non-zero sky term;
  - an airless body's planetshine is R07's, unchanged.

  Smoke: the readbacks agree with the twin to 10⁻³. Acceptance: `pnpm test` and
  `just test-render` pass.

  _Built 2026-10-14_ (Risks, "Deviations in T9.b, as built"): the irradiance integrated in the sun's
  frame (two pieces at the horizon, 96 directions, within 0.95% of a dense reference), its rows at
  the root of the height and stored in `f32`, built at its first read after each build; the fit's
  local scale height and the medium's absorbers carried in the body's table for the lit passes;
  seven tables bound to the disc (one-texel defaults where there is no air), a star's sky light
  under its eclipse; and the readbacks within 3 × 10⁻⁶ (the table) and 6.3 × 10⁻⁵ (the lookups) of
  the twin.

### R08.T10 The medium of a body

In two subtasks (split on re-validation, since as built the atmosphere is not yet drawn in the
photorealistic view at all): T10.a assembles and caches the medium, and T10.b draws it in the view.
A third, T10.c, added from a later ruling (`decision-r08-approximate-plate.md`), bounds the trace
broadeners' effect and names `ATMOSPHERE: APPROXIMATE`'s reasons on the plate. A fourth, T10.d,
from that decision's §6 (2026-10-27), answers T10.c's findings: the widthless gases' rule, the
reasons set as sentences, and the aerosol reasons' words.

- **R08.T10.a The medium and its cache.** Described below, with its tests. Acceptance:
  `pnpm --filter hyperion exec vitest run view/atmosphere/assemble view/atmosphere/AtmosphereCache`
  and `pnpm test` pass. _Built 2026-10-26_ (Risks, "Deviations in T10.a, as built", and its
  "Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)" (R08.T10.a)).
- **R08.T10.b In the photorealistic view.** It needs T10.a, T7 and T8.e, and forms each body's
  atmosphere camera with R08.T8.b's `bodyAtmosphereCamera` (`view/atmosphere/bodyCamera.ts`). The
  paragraph "This task also
  draws" below. Tests: `photorealisticPasses`' `atmosphere` entry is built and carries the passes'
  labels; `PhotorealRenderer` submits them after the discs and before R11's slots, and none for a
  view whose bodies have no medium (R05's counting fake, `test/countingRenderEngine.ts`); a
  withheld, unmodelled or approximate body's label reaches `photorealStatements`, after its other
  notes (`atmosphereStatements`, `labels.ts`); a kept scene's body with no atmosphere set, such as
  R07's `TEST GIANT`, carries `ATMOSPHERE: NOT YET MODELLED` (decision-r08-giant-label). From
  T10.a's rulings (`decision-r08-t10a-leans.md`, items 3, 4, 6 and 9) T10.b also hands each body's
  `AtmosphereTables` from `AtmosphereCache` to each view's `HillaireAtmosphere`, which takes them
  in place of building its own and does not dispose them; the forward-lobe tables may then be
  built in the optics worker. It joins the cache's `body_detail` with R10.T16.a's for the detail
  seed, one request a body per trigger. It sets the atmosphere's fault on the label block's fault
  line, in `--status-caution`, after any graphics fault and the terrain's, and forgets the cache's
  failures when `VIEW` is shown again. It feeds `ATMOSPHERE: PENDING`'s debounce each frame. The
  flight records no atmosphere fault. It sets `ATMOSPHERE REJECTED` among the atmosphere's notes
  and `ATMOSPHERE DATA INVALID` on the fault line. The flight records neither. _Built 2026-10-26,
  flown 2026-10-27_ (Risks, "Deviations in T10.b, as built" and its "Deferred findings
  (2026-10-13 rule)" (R08.T10.b); `decision-r08-t10b-depth.md`).
  Acceptance: `pnpm test` and `just test-render` pass, and by hand a flight past every fixture, on
  a kept test scene that carries them (`view/scenes/`), is recorded here, for the fixtures that
  exist: the four of R08.T12.b.1, with R08.T12.b.2's four flown by that task
  (`decision-r08-t10b-ux.md`, item 3), with the moonlit night on the Earth fixture (the Sun beyond
  the twilight limit, a full Moon), whose sky over the stars shows the fainter stars washed out:
  R06's star layer, or with no server `ATMOSPHERE TEST`'s own field, drawn through R06's star
  sprites before the air's composite (`decision-r08-t10b-ux.md`, item 1) (R08.T7's acceptance,
  which its record, "Deviations in T7, as built", leaves to this task, since the smoke's frames
  draw no star layer). R08.T8.e closed
  with its hold missed at four rows (`decision-r08-t8-leans.md` §16; Risks, "Deferred findings
  (2026-10-13 rule)" (R08.T8.e), _The hold's four rows_). The flight's frame times at high on the
  RTX 3080 are recorded beside them. They are no verdict on the frame; R08.T11's measured rows
  are.
- **R08.T10.c The trace broadeners' effect bound, and APPROXIMATE's reasons on the plate.** From
  `decision-r08-approximate-plate.md`, items 1a and 1b (2026-10-27). A line species whose only
  uncertainty is a gas with no width on file, at any share, is no longer `estimated` outright: an
  effect bound decides, in the negligible rule's own terms (`negligible.ts`'s `BroadenerVerdict`),
  and a broadener with a permanent dipole keeps it `estimated` (`absorbers/kDistribution.ts`'s
  `DIPOLAR_BROADENERS`). `ATMOSPHERE: APPROXIMATE` is followed on the plate by each of its
  reasons on a line of its own, naming the bodies it holds for (`labels.ts`'s
  `atmosphereApproximateLines`, from the cache's `AtmosphereViewReport.reasons`), and the guide's
  row says so; two of the guide's rows are reworded (the surface state's `SNOWBALL` clause,
  `CRUST NONE`). Acceptance: `pnpm --filter hyperion exec vitest run` over
  `view/atmosphere/negligible`, `view/atmosphere/absorbers.test`,
  `view/atmosphere/absorbers/kDistribution`, `view/atmosphere/absorbers/lineCurves`,
  `view/atmosphere/assemble`, `view/atmosphere/AtmosphereCache`, `view/atmosphere/labels`,
  `displays/view/viewAtmosphere`, `displays/view/viewRun` and
  `displays/view/ViewDisplayAtmosphere`, and `pnpm test`, pass; the `console-ux` skill's checks
  pass; no kept fixture's labels change and no case-gate figure moves; and no GENERATOR_VERSION,
  PROTOCOL, wire, table, shader or kernel changes. _Built 2026-10-27_ (Risks, "Deviations in
  T10.c, as built", and its "Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)" (R08.T10.c)).
- **R08.T10.d The widthless gases' rule, APPROXIMATE's reasons as sentences, and the aerosol
  reasons' words.** From `decision-r08-approximate-plate.md` §6 (2026-10-27), on T10.c's deferred
  findings, and that decision's §8 (2026-10-27), on T10.d's own. The broadener verdict reads its lines' cell means to (1 + ε) times the body's largest
  broadening pressure, which makes the cap exact (`negligible.ts`). `DIPOLAR_BROADENERS` holds
  every molecule of the registry whose dipole is at least H₂S's, twelve, each with its measured
  value and source. A species' own share takes `self`, else the entry under its own key (H's), and
  a table with neither counts its own species as a widthless broadener of itself, a neutral
  atom's (`SELF_BROADENED_ATOMS`) `estimated` (`absorbers/kDistribution.ts`); so
  `ATMOSPHERE_OPTICS_VERSION` is raised to 2 (`atmosphereInput.ts`). `ATMOSPHERE: APPROXIMATE`'s reasons stand
  `reason` (`labels.ts`) and reach the plate as a `SentenceStatement`, set whole with no letter
  spacing (`displays/view/viewRun.ts`, `LabelStatementLine.tsx`, `styles.css`), and an instrument
  shows the note straight above any reason of its own (`viewRun.ts`'s
  `instrumentPhotorealStatements`). The aerosol reasons cite no paper and give a wavelength in whole
  nm (`aerosol.ts`, `aggregate.ts`, `nonSpherical.ts`). The guide's `ATMOSPHERE: APPROXIMATE`,
  `CRUST` and `UNDIFFERENTIATED` rows, its instruments' rule and its Typography's statement
  bullet are reworded. Acceptance:
  `pnpm --filter hyperion exec vitest run` over `view/atmosphere/negligible`,
  `view/atmosphere/absorbers.test`, `view/atmosphere/absorbers/kDistribution`,
  `view/atmosphere/absorbers/lineCurves`, `view/atmosphere/aerosol`, `view/atmosphere/aggregate`,
  `view/atmosphere/nonSpherical`, `view/atmosphere/sizeDistribution`, `view/atmosphere/assemble`,
  `view/atmosphere/labels`, `displays/view/viewRun`, `displays/view/viewAtmosphere`,
  `displays/view/LabelStatementLine`, `displays/view/InstrumentView`,
  `displays/view/ViewLabelBlock` and `displays/view/ViewDisplayAtmosphere`, and `pnpm typecheck`,
  `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test`, pass; the `console-ux` skill's checks pass on the changed renderer
  files and the guide; no kept fixture's labels change and no case-gate figure moves; no
  GENERATOR_VERSION, PROTOCOL, wire, table, shader, kernel or engine changes; and
  `ATMOSPHERE_OPTICS_VERSION` is 2 (§8, item 1). _Built 2026-10-27_ (Risks, "Deviations in R08.T10.d, as built", and its "Deferred
  findings (2026-10-13 rule)" (R08.T10.d)).

`assemble.ts`, `optics.worker.ts`, `AtmosphereCache.ts` build, from the body's appearance and its
surface section, in a module worker, cached as Design note 14 says. The appearance is the scene's
R07 `WireAppearance` (`heldAppearanceOf`, `view/scene/fromServer.ts`: the figure, the photometry
and the labels), with the record's `mass_kg` and rotation; `BodyGravityInput` (R08.T3.d) takes the
figure's `law` and `momentOfInertiaFactor`, read from the record's `SystemBodyFigure` since
`WireAppearance.figure` (R07's `BodyFigure`) carries only the radii and the pole, so that
`bodyGravity` applies Design note 17's ω_fig; R07's `BodyAppearance` is not built in production.
The surface section comes from `body_detail`, requested through
`toBodyDetailRequest` (`lib/system/bodiesWire.ts`), which nothing in `view/` calls yet.
`AtmosphereCache` requests it when a photorealistic view first draws a body in the disc, mesh or
terrain regime (R07's `litRegimes`, decided in `planLitBodies`; `terrain` is R10.T10.e's
hand-over), or as the camera's local body where terrain draws it (T10.b), again when the scene's
arrival or the granted detail changes, and again when `body_events` reports an event on the body
(P14.T31, once it exists; today it answers `unsupported`). The section's state decides the label.
The build produces:

- the column;
- the molecular, absorber and aerosol terms, an absorber on its record's profile where it carries
  one (R08.T6.h);
- the labels of Design note 12.

This task also draws the atmosphere in the photorealistic view (T10.b), where it is not drawn today:
`PhotorealRenderer.render` (`view/photoreal/renderer.ts`, which hard-codes its passes) gains the
atmosphere's passes after the discs, R07's `photorealisticPasses` slot `"atmosphere"` becomes
built with the labels those passes submit under (R12's `PASS_ROWS` keys on them), and the labels
of Design note 12 join `photorealStatements` (`displays/view/viewRun.ts`) beside `litLabelsOf`
(`displays/view/photorealFrame.ts`). `PhotorealRenderer` hands each body's stars and planetshine
sources, the arrays `planLitBodies` built, to that body's atmosphere (Design note 7's one list).
For the camera's local body, which `planLitBodies` may not light while terrain draws it, the same
two calls are made once a frame. The terrain of a body handed over (R10.T16.c's `FrameTerrain`)
draws in the `bodies` pass before the discs, so the composite covers it on both scopes; each
handed-over body's medium gives its `SurfaceLightingTables` to the terrain through
`TerrainFrameLighting.atmosphere`. Whichever of this task and R10.T16.c lands second binds them and
tests the composite over the terrain. The `body_detail` fetch is shared with R10.T16.a's for the
detail seed.

An airless body (`SurfaceState::Airless`) draws no atmosphere, and its one label is
`EXOSPHERE: NOT YET MODELLED` (`exosphereNotYetModelled`) while the generator computes no exosphere
(below). A body whose surface holds melt carries `SILICATE VAPOUR: NOT YET MODELLED` while its
`silicate_vapour` member is absent (Design note 12). Until the surface section carries P14.T24.a's
figures (R08.T1's P14.T35.e), generated bodies draw no atmosphere and show
`ATMOSPHERE: NOT YET MODELLED`, and so does a giant, whose surface section is `not_applicable`,
until its `envelope` section exists (decision-r08-giant-label). The task runs on the fixtures of
Design note 16: Earth, Earth with ozone, Mars with hand dust, Venus at 92 and at 58 bar, a hand
Titan, and a hand giant. Their media are R08.T12.b's reference cases, built in
`view/atmosphere/reference/cases.ts` (`decision-r08-t12b-scope.md`, ruling 3): `earth` (its
measured ozone), `earth-ozone-slab`, `mars` and `saturn-oblate` from R08.T12.b.1, the thick ones
(Venus, Titan, the giant's deck) from R08.T12.b.2, so that the kept scenes, the CPU twin and the
reference read one medium on one figure. Those that need R08.T5.b's files (Venus's clouds, Mars's
dust, Titan's haze) wait on those files. Their licences were ruled on 2026-10-09
(`decision-r08-licences.md`).

By the composition ruling (decision-composition):

- A generated body's column takes the record's `mean_molecular_mass_g_mol` and
  `heat_capacity_over_r`. Only hand fixtures use T3.a's `gasProperties`.
- The record's `gases` pass to `molecularTerm` unconverted (a type test pins the assignability).
- `atmosphereApproximate` collects the reasons of the optics registry: an estimated or absent
  Rayleigh, an absent absorber, or one with no column free (`noColumnFree`), a stand-in or unknown
  material, or a mode whose size quadrature did not converge (R08.T5.f: `ModeOptics.sizeConvergence`
  with `converged` false, in any channel or bake bin drawn). The reasons are player
  text. Each uses only characters both B612 faces hold,
  and names in words any quantity the literature writes with another symbol (science-r08-mmf.md
  §4.7). Each names a species or material through `substanceName` (P14.T49.f), and a composition
  variant through `variantWords`, never by a key or a variant's identifier
  (decision-substance-names).
- **Negligible absorbers** (`decision-r08-t4b-t12c.md`, follow-ups 3–5).
  - **What is tested:**
    - each listed absorber still in R08.T4.c's `PENDING_ABSORBERS`;
    - each species drawn with estimated optics or past its data's temperatures.
  - **The medium takes:**
    - each entry's 1 nm cell means at the profile's column-weighted temperature: per molecule,
      or per pair for a pair, and for a resonance line's wing per (atom, perturber) pair, as K's
      with H₂ and He. They are interpolated with ln σ linear in 1/T between the nodes and held
      beyond;
    - the profile's largest column, u_max, along the horizontal ray at the medium's lowest level:
      a column, or ∫ n_A n_B ds for a pair or a wing.
  - **The bound.** For each of the body's suns and each channel:
    - Δ_c = Σ_cells |c̄_c| S min(1, Σ_kinds max_entries(k⟨σ⟩_cell) u_max) ÷ Σ_cells c̄_c S;
    - k = 1 for measured data, and k = 100 for estimated data, a temperature past the data's, or
      HITRAN's 500 K nodes above 296 K, which lack hot lines;
    - where a species has a temperate and a hot entry (CO, N₂O, HCN, H₂O), the larger k⟨σ⟩ is
      taken cell by cell at the profile's temperature.
    - a held χ (R08.T4.d's CO₂). Over the cells whose nodes hold χ at the profile's
      temperature, Δ_c,χ = Σ_cells w_c,cell min(1, f₃ ⟨σ⟩_cell u_max) ÷ Σ_cells c̄_c S, with k = 1.
      - f₃ = 1 − (2/π) arctan(σ₁ ÷ γ_L) at the body's largest p_eff.
      - w_c,cell is the largest |c̄_c| S within χ's reach of the cell.
      - The true χ lies in [0, 1], so this bounds any held χ's effect from above.
      - The hold takes no label where Δ_c,χ ≤ 10⁻³ in every channel.
    - CO₂'s fixed-g mix (R08.T4.d). At the body's self share w = x_CO₂ r_self ÷ Σ_j x_j r_j,
      interpolated between the recorded w and held at the end values beyond them, CO₂ is
      `estimated` where the body's u_max reaches a cell's u_mix(w, T), the least over the samples
      bracketing the profile's temperature (at its hold, where held; §17). Elsewhere the mix takes
      no label.
  - **Negligible** means Δ_c ≤ 10⁻³ in every channel. Δ_c bounds the change of the channel's
    light from above, since 1 − e^(−x) ≤ min(1, x).
    - A negligible pending species takes no column and no curve.
    - No negligible species takes a label, and the medium names it `negligible`.
    - Otherwise the species labels the body under Design note 12's τ rule until its task lands.
  - Tests:
    - a Mars-class body's CO, an Earth-class body's N₂O, and Earth's O₂–N₂ and O₂–CO₂ slices
      are negligible;
    - a Uranus-class H₂ column's quadrupole lines are negligible;
    - a Venus-class body's CO₂ is not, until R08.T4.d;
    - an Earth-class body's H₂O continuum below 567 nm is not negligible at k = 100, and a
      Mars-class body's is;
    - a hot giant's K wing grows with its perturber density, and is negligible only where the
      pair column allows;
    - a species whose column is raised past its bound labels the body;
    - an estimated entry needs its hundredfold margin;
    - for a line from a single lower level, the interpolation between nodes equals the
      Boltzmann law to 10⁻⁹;
    - Δ_c bounds the channel change of an `f64` spectral reference from above;
    - an Earth-class body's CO₂ below 295 K takes no label from CO₂–N₂'s held χ (about
      3 × 10⁻⁶ in its strongest cell), and a body whose bound passes 10⁻³ does;
    - a snowball-class body with CO₂ and N₂ near an even share, at a few bar, takes no label
      from the mix, and a column raised past a cell's u_mix does.
- A body in the `Tenuous` state with a drawable haze is drawn in the `thin` regime. One whose gas
  is only an exosphere takes no medium, since its scattering is negligible (vertical τ about
  10⁻¹⁵), but it is labelled `exosphereNotYetModelled` while the generator computes no exosphere
  (P14.T55.c, unscheduled; signed off 2026-10-10 by the sign-off agent, owner's delegation,
  `signoff-2.md`, against decision-composition §9.2's lean of no label).
  - The lean's "below visibility" fails for a Mercury-class body. Its sodium D-line glow above the
    limb is about 0.14–1.4 cd/m², 800 to 8,000 times a dark sky of 22 mag per square arcsecond,
    seen from the night side or with the sunlit ground out of the frame (Cassidy et al. 2015,
    Icarus 248, 547, Figs. 4–5; Zhang et al. 2023, PSJ 4, 70, which find Mercury's sodium tail in
    STEREO's broadband images).
  - The Moon's, about 4 kR of sodium (Potter and Morgan 1988, Science 241, 675), is about three
    times that dark sky, at the edge of a long exposure's reach, and the icy moons' are below it.
  - The generator cannot yet tell them apart, so every generated airless body carries the note,
    and a kept scene's body set airless carries none. The note clears when the generator computes
    the exosphere and the console draws its light or finds it too faint for any view to show.

By the heat-capacity ruling (`science-r08-gases-2.md` §1, 2026-10-10), the client keeps no
thermodynamics of its own. P14.T24.e integrates P14.T49.b's c_p(T) and publishes the adiabat as
nodes, in plan 14's 23 → 24 batch (decision-bump-plan-after-22, 2026-10-14; updated 2026-10-15),
and nothing R08 has built moves until then:

- `TemperatureProfile.radiativeConvective` takes the published nodes, with a T3.a follow-up; the
  existing closed form ∫ T dln p applies per segment.
- `GAS_HEAT_CAPACITY`, `HeatCapacity`, `ofDegrees`, `LINEAR_TRIATOMIC_CP_OVER_R`,
  `GasProperties.heatCapacityOverR` and `dryAdiabatExponent` retire.
- Hand fixtures copy the nodes of the sim golden's Earth, Venus and Titan, or state β as a test
  input.
- Until then C₂H₆'s N = 6 stays, with its 100 K caveat (Risks, "Deviations in T3.b's follow-up,
  as built").

Tests (T10.a):

- a withheld section gives no medium and `atmosphereNotResolved`, and a `not_modelled` one
  `atmosphereNotYetModelled`;
- a request is sent once per body per trigger, and none for a point-regime body;
- an absent inventory gives no aerosol term and `aerosolsNotYetModelled`;
- a giant's record (surface `not_applicable`, no envelope) gives no medium and
  `atmosphereNotYetModelled`;
- a sub-Neptune's record (surface `not_applicable`, envelope `not_modelled`) gives no medium and
  `atmosphereNotYetModelled`, as a giant's does;
- a generated airless body gives no medium and `exosphereNotYetModelled` alone, and a kept scene's
  body set airless gives no medium and no label;
- a body whose request is in flight gives `atmospherePending`, and none on a re-request while its
  previous state is drawn;
- a flyby that brings many bodies into the disc regime does not make `ATMOSPHERE: PENDING` flash
  more than three times a second (the guide's flash threshold; decision-r08-giant-label, §4). If
  it would, the scene's lit bodies are asked for on arrival, or the line is held as R05's terrain
  annunciation holds its own (`view/terrain/annunciation.ts`), the form ruled
  (`decision-r08-t10a-leans.md`, item 9);
- the same inputs give the same key and a changed inventory another;
- a `rotational_and_tidal` record's medium is built at ω_fig = √2.5 ω (its g_ref includes ω²R),
  and a `capped` one builds where its true ω would put γ_e ≤ 0;
- results transfer, and the cache evicts least recently used within its stated size;
- each fixture's optics time is recorded, on a quiet machine;
- a record with an unknown key in each keyed member draws without a fault and carries
  `atmosphereApproximate`; a `Tenuous` Pluto-like record draws its haze;
- the provisional thick line: the measured Earth and the Mars fixture take no
  `atmosphereApproximate` from it, Venus at 58 and 92 bar take it, and an Earth-class column
  raised to τ 1 on its worst channel takes it;
- a generated body's ground is p q per channel from its photometry, clamped to 1;
- a gas envelope sent `ok` gives no medium and `atmosphereNotYetModelled`;
- a build that throws gives no medium, no label, one `console.error` and the fault naming the
  body, and is retried at the body's next trigger and once failures are forgotten; one that
  throws `EngineUnavailable` gives no fault;
- two bodies failing alike give one line naming both, in designation order;
- a `body_detail` answered `too_many_requests`, `queue_full` or `cancelled` raises no line,
  logs nothing, keeps `ATMOSPHERE: PENDING` and is asked again after 2 s, doubling to 32 s;
  any other refusal gives no medium and
  `ATMOSPHERE REJECTED: for <designations>, <the server's reason>, reopen VIEW to retry`, in
  `--text` where the server refused what was asked and in `--status-caution` otherwise, with no
  `console.error`; an answer `toBodyDetail` cannot take, or one of another kind, gives no medium,
  `ATMOSPHERE DATA INVALID: <the check that failed> for <designations>, reopen VIEW to retry` and
  one `console.error`; each of the last two is held, asked afresh at the body's next trigger and once failures are forgotten, and cleared
  by an answer taken;
- a request answered within 250 ms shows no `ATMOSPHERE: PENDING`, and the line comes on at
  most once in any 1.25 s, whatever the replies' timing;
- the cache's bytes are its entries' `rowBytes`, a wanted body is never evicted, and an evicted
  body wanted again sends no request;
- a record absorber layer that straddles the column lays its whole column inside it; one wholly
  above the column's top is dropped with `atmosphereApproximate`, and one wholly below its datum
  with no label;
- a mode of τ 0 or of base equal to top is skipped without a fault;
- every row of `substances.json` has the client table's `absorber` and `rayleigh` flags, both
  ways (`parity.test.ts`).

As ruled before the build (`decision-r08-t10a-leans.md`, 2026-10-26):

- **Thick, before R08.T13.** Until `classifyRegime` exists, a medium whose vertical optical
  depth from the ground to the top over every term but the absorbers (`opticalDepthToTop` at
  μ = 1) reaches `PROVISIONAL_THICK_OPTICAL_DEPTH` (1, `thick/regime.ts`) on its worst channel
  is drawn by the analytic term with `atmosphereApproximate` (Design note 9's routing). It
  covers every medium the cache builds, kept fixtures included. Earth (about 0.3 at 434 nm) and
  Mars take no label from it; Venus at 58 and 92 bar and a Titan-class column do.
- **The ground.** A generated body's ground albedo is its spherical albedo, p q per channel
  from R07's `BodyPhotometry`, clamped to [0, 1]; a kept fixture keeps its own (Risks,
  "Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)" (R08.T10.a), _The ground's albedo_).
- **The tables and the request.** `AtmosphereCache` builds and holds each body's
  `AtmosphereTables` through an injected factory, and asks for `body_detail` through a seam
  shaped as `Pick<RequestClient, "request">`. T10.a changes neither `tables.ts` nor
  `hillaire.ts`; T10.b hands the tables over and joins the fetch with R10.T16.a's.
- **A gas envelope sent `ok`** gives no medium and `atmosphereNotYetModelled` until R08.T16.a
  builds its medium (Design note 12).
- **A build that fails**, by a throw from the assembly or the tables' factory other than
  `EngineUnavailable`, gives no medium and no atmosphere label for the body, one
  `console.error`, and the label block's fault (Design note 12). It is retried at the body's
  next trigger and when `VIEW` is shown again. `EngineUnavailable` raises nothing and is retried
  after the restore. A legal record never reaches it: a mode of τ 0 or of base equal to top is
  skipped (`review-r08-shapes-b.md`, C3), and an absorber layer wholly outside the column is
  dropped (below).
- **A `body_detail` not answered** (`decision-r08-t10a-leans.md`, follow-up to item 6). A
  server too busy refuses nothing: the body is asked again by itself, as the survey's field
  is. Any other refusal is `ATMOSPHERE REJECTED` and an answer the console cannot take
  `ATMOSPHERE DATA INVALID`, each with its reason and `reopen VIEW to retry`, held until the
  body is asked afresh.
- **The registry's flags.** `absorber` and `rayleigh` come from a client table that
  `parity.test.ts` holds to `substances.json` for every row, both ways. A task that appends a
  row or changes a flag updates the table in the same commit.
- **`ATMOSPHERE: PENDING`** is held as the terrain's line is, by one debounce per view over its
  wanted bodies: it shows once a request has stood `ANNUNCIATION_ONSET_MS` (250 ms) and goes
  once none has for `ANNUNCIATION_CLEAR_MS` (1 s).
- **The size.** `ATMOSPHERE_CACHE_BYTES` is 32 MB (decimal), counted by each entry's `rowBytes`
  as built. A body wanted this frame is never evicted, so only the wanted set can take the cache
  past it. Eviction releases the tables and keeps the body's reply for the scene, so a body
  wanted again is rebuilt without a request.
- **Record absorber layers.** One that straddles the column passes as it is: `absorberSpecs`
  clamps it to the column's datum and top and lays its whole column inside. One wholly outside
  the column is dropped before `absorberSpecs`, which refuses it. Wholly above the column's top
  it carries `atmosphereApproximate` under Design note 12's τ rule; wholly below the datum,
  hidden by the ground, it carries none.
- **The negligible-absorber bounds** were written before R08.T4.d–T4.h. T10.a re-derives each
  test's expectation on the tables as built, and records each change with its Δ_c in
  "Deviations in T10.a, as built". A change to a kept fixture's labels goes to "main" first.

Acceptance: T10.a's and T10.b's, above.

### R08.T11 The thin benchmarks

Record, by hand on the development machine's RTX 3080 (the discrete target) and, by the owner, on
the UHD 620 at 720p (low), against
the budget ([Performance budget](../../brainstorming/rendering-and-planets.md#performance-budget)):

- the per-frame atmosphere time, against 2–4 ms low and 0.5–1 ms discrete, at one source, at the
  setting's count (2 + 2 on high, 2 + 1 on low) and at `MAX_SKY_SOURCES`, the last for R07's
  deferred raise. These are estimates, recorded as findings: R05's gate judges terrain and
  atmosphere together (R05 Design note 21, decided 2026-10-06). R05 measured, at one sun and three
  terms on the RTX 3080, about 1.6 ms p50 at full clock, 2.62 / 3.37 ms p50 / p95 at the driver's
  light-load clocks after R05.T12.e, and 3.19, 4.07 and 4.28 ms at the 50th, 95th and 99th
  percentiles on the gate's judged run (1,509 × 821 px; R05's Risks, "The gate's verdict"), the
  figures the brainstorm's budget section has carried since 2026-10-08; R12.T10 replaces the
  estimate;
- the per-planet table time, against about 1 ms and under 0.1 ms;
- the table bytes a planet, against 2 MB, and the per-view bytes on their own line, against
  Design note 11's 0.43 MB, at one, two and four sources;
- the slice and band counts, bytes and per-planet table time of the Jupiter- and Saturn-class
  figures, against Design note 11's 0.57 and 0.72 MB, of an ice giant (2 and 2), and of a giant
  at plan 14's cap (f = 0.2, 9–10 slices and 6–7 bands, Design note 11's worst generated case),
  and any widening of `KAPPA_STEP` or `BAND_STEP`. If the capped giant stays over 2 MB after both
  widenings, it is reported to "main" for a decision agent's ruling (Design note 11);
- R08.T6.i's layer-edge setup, against the lane's count:
  - about 0.7 step (4%) for a ground sky-view ray crossing each edge once;
  - 1.5–2 steps (9–11%) for a two-sided ray-march ray crossing two edges twice;
  - about 80 words of private memory on the edged branch.

  Each pass is timed on an edged medium (the slab Earth) and on Earth. Earth's time is also set
  beside the kernels of R08.T6.h, before T6.i, on both machines, so that the private array's cost
  to occupancy on media with no edge is seen. A cost there beyond the run's noise is raised with

- R08.T6.f's cost per transmittance read (`oblate.wgsl`'s sliced lookup; the operation count in
  "Deviations in T6.f, as built"): each per-frame pass on Earth, on the Saturn-class figure and on
  a sphere, against the kernels before T6.f, on both machines, so that the fit's cost on a body
  of several bands, and any cost of its code on a body of one, is seen.

R08.T8.c's far-limb timings (from 400 km to 10⁸ m on both settings, before and after its kernel;
Risks, "Deviations in T8.c, as built", _Acceptance 7_) are this task's first rows and R08.T8.d's
