    drawn body's low e_q beside it.

- **Deviations in T8.c, as built** (2026-10-22). A new `shaders/farLimb.wgsl` (the footprint),
  `shaders/rayMarch.wgsl` (`marchRay`, and `main`'s blend), `shaders/composite.wgsl`
  (`transmittanceAcrossFromAbove`), `hillaire.ts` (both kernels take `farLimb.wgsl`), `tablesCpu.ts`
  (the twins), `smoke/atmosphere.ts`, `smoke/page.ts`, a new `smoke/writeSlack.ts`,
  `scripts/testRender.sh` and `src/smoke/result.ts`; tests in a new `test/farLimb.ts` (the frames and
  the reference, moved out of `farLimb.test.ts` and widened), `farLimb.test.ts` (rewritten), new
  `farLimbLow.test.ts`, `farLimbFlicker.test.ts` and `smoke/writeSlack.test.ts`, and
  `tablesCpuOblate.test.ts` and `result.test.ts`; two earlier tests follow the kernel:
  `compositeTransmittance.test.ts`'s text check names `transmittanceAcrossFromAbove`, and
  `tablesCpu.test.ts`'s spheroid march from 400 km holds each texel's own ray to its placed steps,
  and the target to it where the texel keeps its centre ray (its 127° frame's air texels all take
  their footprint). No golden, version, wire or table layout moves,
  and no per-frame constant is added: the footprint reads the camera, the ray basis, `view.exact`'s
  quadrics and the body's table, as the march does.
  - _The footprint_ (`decision-r08-t8-leans.md` §6.1). From above the top (the camera's h\* at or
    over the medium's top) a texel whose footprint meets the shell takes the mean over its
    footprint across the limb. A ray's tangent height h is its closest approach's height over the
    datum in space scaled to its sphere, |S o × S d| ÷ |S d| − a. Across the texel h is taken as
    linear, its gradient (g_x, g_y) from h on the rays through the midpoints of the texel's edges.
    _The span_ is |g_x| + |g_y|, the footprint's whole range of h: with the limb along a row it is
    §6.1's angular height × the distance to the tangent point, and with the limb at 45° up to √2
    times that, the range the mean is taken over. The top's cut is the same over the top's quadric
    (a + H ÷ s_e, c + H ÷ s_p). The footprint is projected on ĝ, the screen direction in which h
    rises (a trapezoid, the convolution of boxes |ĝ_x| and |ĝ_y| texels wide; a box where the
    narrower is under 10⁻⁴ texel), and cut where h meets the datum's edge and the top. The ground
    piece takes 2 Gauss–Legendre nodes, the shell piece 8 and space none; each piece is weighted by
    its share (the trapezoid's CDF), each node by the projection's density there, normalised to its
    piece's share. Texels wholly on the face (h + span ÷ 2 ≤ 0), wholly in space, or whose closest
    approach lies behind the camera keep the centre ray. Each node is the march's own ray
    (`marchRay`) through its point, at the scene's depth under its own point (the review's finding:
    the centre's depth cut every shell node at a drawn surface's distance where its edge crossed the
    footprint; `farLimb.test.ts`'s "marches each node at the scene's depth under its own point").
    The space share counts as (0, 0, 0, 1), what the kernel writes for a ray that misses the air.
  - _Tangent heights as a difference of radii._ |S o × S d| ÷ |S d| − a is Design note 18's
    closest-approach form, which the note keeps out of the march's heights within h₀ = a ÷ 2; the
    footprint takes it at every camera above the top, 400 km included. It only weighs and cuts the
    footprint, and f32 rounds it by about ε|o| (0.4 m from 400 km, 6 m from 10⁸ m, 60 m from
    10⁹ m), inside the note's 3 × 10⁻⁷ max(t, h, 1 km), at most 5 × 10⁻⁴ of a texel's span.
  - _s and the blend._ s is the span over the local scale height at the tangent point: the body's
    table's (`oblateScaleHeightAt`, `localScaleHeightM` tabulated) at h\* = s(φ) max(h, 0), φ the
    tangent point's geocentric latitude (taken as geodetic in s(φ)), over s(φ), the table holding H
    in h\* (the review's finding: 0.3% on WGS 84, up to about 15% on a Saturn-class spheroid; every
    CPU figure is on a sphere, s ≡ 1). w_L = clamp((s − 0.6) ÷ 0.4, 0, 1); the output is
    (1 − w_L) × the centre ray + w_L × the mean (WGSL's `mix`, the mean alone at w_L = 1), the
    in-scatter and the march's alpha alike. **Leans accepted by "main" (2026-10-22).** The local
    scale height is the codebase's `localScaleHeightM`, the column's e-folding, which both kernels
    already read from the body's table, so no table is added. It depends on height, where §6.1's s
    figures took Rayleigh's 8.43 km: on R05's Earth 2.37 km at the ground, 3.20 km at 0.1 H,
    14.87 km at 1 H (the ozone layer's column above), 8.43 km at 5 H, and the 1 km floor at the top,
    where H is held to the room left above it; on the measured Earth 2.68 km at 0.1 H and 6.93 km
    at 1 H; the Saturn-class figure 49.7 km throughout. So s shifts by height, and its reach
    supersedes T8.b's "s = 0.55, w_L = 0" at 10⁷ m and the onset at 1.06 and 1.54 × 10⁷ m (below,
    _Deferred findings (R08.T8.b)_): from 10⁷ m on high R05's Earth stands at s 1.37, 0.76, 0.31,
    0.60 and 0.65 on the limb set (w_L 1, 0.40, 0, 0.01, 0.11); the rows reach s = 1 at 8.50, 12.0,
    25.5, 14.2 and 13.5 × 10⁶ m. From 400 km on low a march texel spans 4.14 km of tangent height,
    so its lowest limb rows (s ≈ 1.3–1.75) take the footprint's mean; on high from 400 km the
    datum's row stands at s 0.58. Within about 2 km (high) or 7 km (low) of the top, where H falls to
    the floor, texels blend at any distance, about 10⁻⁵ of the limb's light. The footprint is taken
    only from above the top (also accepted): in the march band the march is blended with the sky
    view, which has no footprint, and from 100 km the horizon's s is about 0.2.
  - _The node schedule._ 8 shell nodes at every span (§6.1's ceiling). On the ruling's frames
    against a 1,024-row reference, 2 nodes under one local scale height put the Saturn-class
    figure's 1 H pixel from 10⁸ m at 10.9% (from 5.0%) and R05's Earth from 10⁸ m at 4.09% (from
    3.22%); 2 under 1 and 4 under 4 the same; so no fewer. Since R08.T8.e
    (`decision-r08-t8-leans.md` §11): the shell piece takes 8 nodes, but where its local scale height
    is held to the room left to the top (top − h\* ≤ 1.01 H at the centre's tangent point) it takes
    2 up to 2 H tall and 4 up to 4 H (`FAR_LIMB_SCHEDULE`, `FAR_LIMB_ROOM_SHARE`,
    `FAR_LIMB_TWO_NODE_SCALE_HEIGHTS`, `FAR_LIMB_FOUR_NODE_SCALE_HEIGHTS`, a 4-node Gauss–Legendre
    rule beside the 2 and the 8; `farLimb.wgsl`'s `farLimbFootprintOf`); the ground piece keeps 2,
    and a NaN takes 8.
    Acceptance 2–5 hold at no wider tolerance, `SATURN_ONSET_MISS` at 0.0502, no record moving at its
    precision ("Deviations in T8.e, as built", _Lever 4_).
  - _What lies behind the limb_ (§6.1). The composite's per-channel transmittance from above the
    top, behind a sky pixel and through each disc, takes the same footprint mean at the output
    pixel's own footprint (`transmittanceAcrossFromAbove`): on high the march's texel's, on low the
    output pixel's, half the texel's, where the in-scatter takes the texel's (the composite runs at
    the output's resolution). The march's alpha for drawn surfaces takes the texel's. Against the
    composite's transmittance converged over the pixel's footprint, R05's Earth's limb set from
    10⁸ and 10⁹ m: worst |ΔT| 0.0013 and 0.0029 across the footprint, 0.21 and 0.47 by the centre
    ray alone.

- **Deviations in T8.d, as built** (2026-10-22). `shaders/source.wgsl`, `scattering.wgsl`,
  `rayMarch.wgsl`, `skyView.wgsl`, `aerialPerspective.wgsl`, `farLimb.wgsl`, `composite.wgsl` and
  `view.wgsl` (`skyPathCount` and `FAR_LIMB_NODES`, unused since, removed); `hillaire.ts` (lever 2)
  and `smoke/atmosphere.ts` (T8.c's timing group reads a frame with the ray march's pass alone);
  `test/atmosphereWgsl.ts` (`wgslFunctions`, `wgslStructs`, `arraysByValueFrom`; `wgslCode` strips
  both kinds of comment in one pass) with a new `test/atmosphereWgsl.test.ts`; tests in
  `hillaire.test.ts` and `marchSteps.test.ts`. Seven commits and this record, landed as a linear
  series on T8.c. No golden, version, wire, table layout or twin moves. SwiftShader's read-backs are
  byte-identical to T8.c's kernel; the RTX 3080's move by one half-float ulp where its compiler
  contracts the new code differently (main's ruling, below).
  - _The cause_ (§8's hypothesis, confirmed). Tint keeps an array value indexed by a loop variable
    in a function-scope variable of its own, stored whole at each call: the SPIR-V (Dawn's
    `dump_shaders` on SwiftShader) shows three OpVariables with whole-array OpStores at
    `viewSourcesAt`'s entry (the sources' directions twice and their angles, 54 floats), one at
    `viewMarchStep`'s (the shares) and one each at `phasedScatteringOf`'s and `lobeOrdersOf`'s (the
    densities), all once a step; and a function-scope array indexed by a variable lives in the
    invocation's local memory. R05.T14's `Medium` by value was the same mechanism.
  - _Lever 1_, in three commits. (1) The sources' directions and angles reach each step by
    pointer, not in `MarchRay` and `SkyRay` by value: on T8.b's kernels the march fell from 19.38 to
    7.46 ms and the sky view from 1.27 to 0.35 ms (high, 400 km, W1). (2) No step holds an array:
    each light slot's share and each term's density a member of its own, selected by a switch
    (`ViewShares`, `TermDensities`), each source's direction read from the view at each step and
    its angle formed there, the counts read in place (7.41 → 7.08 ms, W2). The share's multiply and
    its add stay in one statement (`viewShareAdd`): split across the switch, the RTX 3080's fused
    multiply-add moved one half-float ulp in up to 11 values at 4 and 6 sources (W2's b1–b4). Of
    §8's other variants, the slot loops unrolled to their constant bound cost 5% (7.80 against
    7.45 ms, W1), the source loop's gained nothing (7.79) and the medium by pointer cost 64%
    (12.23 ms); none is taken. (3) On T8.c's footprint (§9 ruling 3): no node array held
    (`farLimbNodeOf` forms each node as it is marched or read), the Gauss–Legendre rules read by
    constant indices, the footprint's helpers taking the view's rays (`FarLimbRays`) rather than
    the view by value, and a bound on the texel's span from the centre ray (|S o| k |Δd|, widened
    1% and 10⁻⁵ |S o| for f32's rounding) that returns the centre ray before the four edge rays
    wherever the span's own test would (the composite 0.37 → 0.28 ms from 400 km, W3). The march's
    entry point calls `marchRay` once, the centre ray and then each node in one loop (below, _One
    march call site_).
  - _Lever 2._ From the march band's upper edge up the composite reads neither the sky view nor the
    aerial perspective, so `drawFrame` leaves both undone there and makes each at its first
    reader's ask (`skyView(view)`, `aerialPerspective(view)`, the smoke's `frameTables`), once a
    frame, on that frame's uniforms; the kernel arm makes all three, and the next frame, a new
    medium, a restore or `dispose()` drops what was left unread. From orbit it saves 0.33 and
    0.21 ms on high and 0.07 and 0.11 ms on low (W2). T8.c's timing group reads a frame with the ray
    march's pass alone, the other two 0.
  - _(b), one round_ (§9 ruling 3, item 4): the march's slot 0 a member of its own, slots 1–3 in
    arrays held by pointer (only absorbing media lit by several stars' lights step them); the
    forward lobes' test taken once a pixel; no pressure-weighted columns for a medium without an
    absorber. From 400 km on high it took the march from 9.38 to 6.84 ms on R05's Earth and from
    12.98 to 10.77 ms on `EARTH_REFERENCE` (W3).

  - _E2 and E3, which move no pixel_ (§10, Ruling 2). A curve's pressure row is found by bisection
    with the scan's own predicate, the rows' ln p ascending as `tables.ts` requires: the same row,
    in about log₂ of the rows' loads (Earth's line slots have 19). And a read comes in two parts,
    what is the same for every light (`common.wgsl`'s `curveNodeOf`, the column's place on the
    grid, and `curveRowsOf`, the pressure rows and their weights) and each light's own texels
    (`curveDepthFrom`); the view's paths cross the same columns, so `viewMarchStep` forms the first
    part once a step and each slot loads only its curve's texels, `ViewMarch` holding slot 0's
    columns and the other slots' depths alone. On SwiftShader the per-frame outputs (the output,
    the march target, the sky view and the aerial volume) are byte-identical to 93396d5f's curve
    read at one source, a binary's two slots and six, on both settings and three media, at T8.c's
    cameras and from 2 km and 40 km (42 of 42), and on the RTX 3080 at full size too (QW2, 42 of
    42). Their payoff is in _QW2_: a binary's two slots gain, one source loses a little.
    `viewAbsorberStep` is gone (`viewMarchStep` forms the step), and with it `curveDepth`'s
    four-row `ys` array, one of T8.d's "Arrays left in locals". _SwiftShader and code size_: the
    first forms, a struct for the read (by value or held by pointer), a matrix with the rows' reads
    unrolled, and E3 calling each slot's read once a slot, crashed SwiftShader's GPU
    process at the first frame (exit 139), as T8.d's two march call sites did, while the bisection
    alone in the old shape passed; the form built keeps each read's rows in one call in a loop, as
    the scan's had, and E3 calls a slot's read from one place in a loop over the slots.

    - For R12.T10, with the census (`.git/rm45-scratch/r08-t8e/census/`) and QW3's split.
  - _Half resolution above the band_ (§16).
    - High's march at `rayMarchScale` 0.5 from the band's upper edge up, read through low's
      depth-nearest pick. It would take about 60–72% off the four rows (to 3.1–4.5 ms;
      estimates).
    - On the hold's 60° frame at 1,920 px, a pixel spans 1.38 km of tangent height from 400 km and
      4.6 km from 10⁷ m, against the limb's 9–10 km e-folding. So pairs of pixels step by about
      25% and 60%, each pixel about 7% and 22% off the full-resolution limb: a seam every second
      row by `decision-r08-t8-leans.md` §5's line. R05 measured low's pick on high's frames at p99
      79.2%.
    - A smoother pick would be a new design, and would still halve the far limb's resolution.
    - Not taken on high. For R12.T10's ladder, as a trade for a rung below high. It would be judged
      by Design note 10's metric per pixel against the full-resolution composite over the limb set
      from 400 km, 10⁷ m and 10⁸ m on the three media, by §5's visibility line, by T8.c's flicker
      sweep, and by the step at the switch.

  - _The bound, re-derived_ (item 12; :4754–4771), each Δ_c the largest over the Sun and the
    2,500 K and 30,000 K Planck suns and the three channels.
    - Earth's O₂–N₂ is not tested: it is measured over 206–346 K. Earth's O₂–CO₂ (held off
      296 K) is 2.9 × 10⁻⁶, its N₂O (drawn, `estimated` everywhere since T4.g) 4.2 × 10⁻⁷ at
      k = 100, and Mars's CO the pending overtones only (its 7–0 band is drawn): 1.4 × 10⁻⁸.
    - Uranus-class H₂ quadrupole lines are drawn, measured at 1 bar, and not tested there. To a
      3.7 bar deck (300 km-amagat) their shape is estimated and they label: 0.10 at k = 100,
      3.3 × 10⁻³ at k = 1. H₂–He is 0.16 at 1 bar (76 K, below the table's 200 K).
    - Venus-class CO₂ stays non-negligible until R08.T4.f, not T4.d: held at 500 K past 10 MPa,
      0.58.
    - Earth's held χ: the strongest cell is 5.0 × 10⁻⁶, not "about 3 × 10⁻⁶" (the full chord and
      the fixture's 330 ppm), f₃ 0.019, Δ_c,χ 3.1 × 10⁻⁸. The body past 10⁻³ is a snowball at
      10 bar, 4.9 × 10⁻³ (3 bar: 4.5 × 10⁻⁴). The mix: w ≈ 0.57, ratio 0.027 at 3 bar and 1.37 at
      150 bar; raising the CO₂ alone takes w to 1, where no u_mix is recorded.
    - The single-lower-level interpolation is the Boltzmann law to 10⁻⁹; the f64 reference test
      holds |1 − T_c| ≤ Δ_c on Earth's held O₂–CO₂ and N₂O lines at 1, 10 and 100 u_max and four
      pressures, under all three suns.
    - No kept fixture's labels change: kept media come prebuilt with their own labels, and only
      the provisional thick line reads them (main, 2026-10-26).
  - _The bound's form._ u_max is the whole grazing chord, both halves, tangent at each level and
    break (Chapman's √(2πR/H) to 0.2%), not the one-sided ray of :4730–4731, and it sits inside
    the sum, one per entry in its own unit (:4733). Entries of one share (a drawn table and its hot
    list) take the larger cell by cell; parts (CO's overtones, a species' lines and its
    cross-sections) add. A hot list holds only above the drawn table's measured range. Cell weights
    are the colour pipeline's own 1 nm rows. Line cell means are the largest over the stored
    pressure rows to the body's largest p_eff. γ_L for f₃ comes from the sidecars' near-wing share
    (`kDistribution.ts` now reads `nearWingShare`), s = (2/π) atan(22γ ÷ (γ² + 75)), each value
    at the top of its two-figure rounding: Earth's 0.090 cm⁻¹, inside §14's 0.075–0.091 (the
    T4.d record's "γ_L = 12.5π × share", :15639–15641, is wrong for CO₂'s χ wing). The air
    partners' 2% trace share is re-implemented to tell which part of H₂O's continuum is estimated.
  - _The assembly._
    - Every gas of `gases` is listed as an absorber layer (:15632's "the bulk gases are listed as
      layers", over :15035's "the gases the registry flags"); one the registry flags no absorber
      (Ar, Ne, Kr, Xe) gives no reason. An inventory absorber of a gas's species replaces its layer.
    - The column is isothermal at the mean surface temperature even where `verticalStructure` is
      sent, until R08.T3.a's follow-up reads P14.T24.e's nodes (:4788–4800).
    - The bound clears reasons, never layers: a key whose every verdict is negligible keeps its
      layer (absorberSpecs gives a wholly pending one no column), drops its `noCrossSections`,
      `estimatedOptics` or `temperatureOutsideTable` reason and is listed in `negligible`. As first
      built a negligible pending part dropped the whole layer, the measured bands and the pairs
      with it (the science check's blocker, fixed before the gate).
    - A key the bound does not clear and no approximation names takes a reason from its verdict
      ("part of its absorption has no data on file, not drawn", or "its absorption estimated, not
      measured" for a held χ or the fixed-g mix).
    - A deck's condensate vapour is cut at the deck's top (its modes' least `topPa`); above it the
      vapour is not drawn and gives "<name>: its vapour above its cloud deck, not drawn" under the
      τ rule (:10920–10922 asked the vapour's column there; a profile would have lost its pairs).
    - The eight terms: the molecular term, then the deepest seven of Thomson (σ_T U), the absorbers
      (`absorberRankingDepth`) and the modes (the inventory's own τ(550), so that the specs-only
      path needs no Mie), earlier first on a tie; the rest are left out with "left out, the
      console can draw no more layers" (of absorbing gas, for a gas or a pair).
    - Record layers and modes (item 11): straddling, passed as they are; wholly above the column's
      top, dropped with a reason; wholly below the datum, dropped silently. A record absorber of
      column 0 or base = top, and a profiled layer whose mixing ratio is 0 throughout the column,
      are skipped (absorberSpecs refuses both); a mode of τ 0 or base = top too.
    - The τ rule's τ above, at 550 nm, counts the molecular term, Thomson and the aerosols, not gas
      absorption. `sizeConvergence` is read in the three channels and at 550 nm; no bake bin is
      drawn yet (:4713's "or bake bin drawn", R08.T14's).
    - Reasons, one a key: a `noColumnFree` or "left out" replaces an estimated reason for the same
      key; a phase reason is prefixed with its substance's name (decision-substance-names §7);
      particles are named with their phase words through `phasedName` ("H2O ice particles",
      "liquid H2SO4 particles").
    - A withheld or unmodelled bulk section under an `ok` surface labels by its own state and
      draws no medium. An airless body that holds melt also carries `SILICATE VAPOUR` (Design
      note 12), so "its one label" (:4691) is stale.
    - Inputs: GM is G × `massMearth` × `EARTH_MASS_KG` (:4658 says `mass_kg`); with no `ok`
      figure section the body is a sphere of its bulk radius with `figureLaw` null; the medium's
      name is the record's designation; more than two lights is a `RangeError`, none is allowed
      (no curve slots); a size distribution sent with shape `aggregate` takes its file's shape.
    - Sign-off 12: 38(c) is built (liquid O₂'s `absorptionStandIn`, a prose member the fit
      ignores, so no table's data hash moves: "liquid O2: its absorption is the gas's O2–O2 pair
      absorption at 203 K carried to the liquid's density; no measurement of the liquid's is
      read"), and 39(c) (`no SO2 ice on file: liquid SO2 at 198 K stands in, a named analogue`;
      an atomic solid reads `no solid Kr on file`, which the sign-off's test names without its
      text). One T5.k test, "seven liquids at τ 0 with no label", now expects liquid O₂'s reason.
  - _The cache._
    - Triggers (:4664–4668): the first want in the disc, mesh or terrain regime, an arrival (an
      opaque token compared by identity), a body's granted level, a body event, and the link's
      return. A changed light set rebuilds from the held reply with no request; a reply whose key
      equals the drawn entry's builds nothing.
    - Answers, classified in one exhaustive switch (`detailAnswerOf`): busy, asked again after 2 s
      doubling to 32 s (`coarseFieldStore.ts`'s constants); `rejected` and `invalid` held;
      `isBulkAssemblyFailure` reads as `answer unreadable`. A problem stands through a light
      change until a trigger.
    - A failed build, a factory throw or a landing that throws is `failed`, one `console.error`;
      `EngineUnavailable` raises nothing and the tables are tried again each frame.
    - Eviction keeps the reply, the assembled medium and its curves, so a body wanted again is
      drawn in that frame with no request and no `PENDING`; only `rowBytes` count. An arrival not
      seen before lets every body no view wants go, so a scene's views share one arrival token.
    - The pool: workers start at the first build. Each light set's curves are split into one share
      a worker, the brightest light's set first and alone, and joined in a worker (0.13–0.23 s on
      Earth, too long for the render thread). Only the channels come back; the bake bins' curves
      (about 1 MB an absorber and sun) are dropped until R08.T14 needs them. Each worker forms
      the specs itself. A join whose worker is lost asks its shares again, at most three times.
      Replies are cloned in the worker and their buffers transferred.

    built; the Titan-class column is `titanClassMethaneMedium`. Beyond the list: six absorber

- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)** (R08.T10.a). Recorded and deferred: each leaves the
  algorithm and every contract as they are.
  - _The ground's albedo_ (`decision-r08-t10a-leans.md`, item 2). A generated body's ground is
    its spherical albedo p q per channel from R07's photometry: the Lambert albedo that gives its
    disc's own integrated light, to which R10 scales its class albedos too (R10 Design note 8).
    It includes the clouds and the air's own reflection, so a cloudy world's ground reads
    bright: about 0.3 on an Earth-class world against the Earth fixture's 0.1, and the deck's
    0.76 on a Venus-class world, which the provisional thick line labels anyway. No cloud-free
    figure is on the wire, since the photometry is the sim's area mix and the server does not
    send its cloud albedo. It is replaced when R11 draws clouds inside the medium, which would
    otherwise count them twice, or when the ground's own albedo is on the wire.
  - _The provisional thick line_ (item 1). τ of at least 1 is the column's optical thickness,
    not a measured boundary. For Rayleigh air, the only scattering a generated body has at 23,
    it falls at about 3.5 Earth columns: inside the fifty times Earth's density Hillaire tested
    to, and past the 3 Earth columns at which R08.T4.a measured the thin path's three-channel
    transmittance 0.0151 off in u′v′. A forward-scattering aerosol under τ 1 that fails the
    metric would go unlabelled until R08.T13; aerosols reach generated bodies only at 24. As
    built the line falls at about 3.9 Earth columns (Earth's τ_R about 0.26 at 433.6 nm). The
    kept fixtures' worst channels: earth 0.394, earth-ozone-slab 0.394, mars 0.508,
    saturn-oblate 0.728; Venus at 58 and 92 bar 27.3 and 43.3.
  - _The cache's size_ (item 10). 32 MB of per-planet rows: about 56 measured Earths with one
    star (570,264 B), or 16 bodies at the 2 MB row. The brainstorm's memory table gives the
    cache no total. For R08.T11 and R12.T10.
  - _Trace broadeners' widths_ (item 12; main, 2026-10-26). A line table that holds no width for
    a trace broadener marks the whole species `estimated`, so generated worlds carry
    `ATMOSPHERE: APPROXIMATE`: Earth-class H₂O by its CO₂ (Δ_c 1.96), Mars-class O₂ by its CO
    (1.35 × 10⁻³), Saturn-class H₂ by its CH₄ (0.060). Lean: the 2% trace-share tolerance the air
    partners already take. Revisited when R08.T10.b or R08.T11 puts generated worlds on screen.
    `MARS_REFERENCE`'s comment ("CO₂, CO and O₂ bands are negligible", `reference/cases.ts:217`)
    no longer holds of the bound; correct it when `cases.ts` is next touched (R08.T12.b.2).
    _Ruled 2026-10-27 (`decision-r08-approximate-plate.md`, item 1a): an effect bound, built in
    R08.T10.c, where `MARS_REFERENCE`'s comment is corrected._
  - _Mars's 214 K_ lies inside CO₂'s estimated 212.5–225 K interval (Δ_c 2.0 × 10⁻³ at k = 100):
    whether k = 100 belongs on a chain-interpolation interval (its error about 4 × 10⁻³) is
    main's.
  - _H₂–He below 200 K_ is held for every cold giant (Saturn-class 0.026, Uranus-class 0.16);
    for R08.T4.f or a colder data set.
  - _The bound's reach_ (the science check). It is per key and per straight path: keys negligible
    on one body add, each up to 10⁻³. On an oblate body the chord is taken on the R_ref sphere,
    about 9% low on a Saturn-class figure, 5% on a Jupiter-class one (until R08.T16.a draws a
    giant's medium). The chord's maximum is sampled at the levels and breaks, 13% low at worst for
    a tent tangent only at its ends and peak, 1.2% for a 1 km tent at Earth's level spacing. The
    held χ's form is §14's as ruled (min(1, ·) at the source cell, ⟨σ⟩ already reduced), which
    may run low by 1.7% on Earth, 5.6% on a snowball at a few bar and up to 5× at Venus's
    pressure. ln σ linear in 1/T runs low for a cell of low-E″ lines: 1.9–2.9% over 200–296 K,
    19–31% over ExoMol's 296–1,000 K. A node held at 0 past the data bounds nothing where hot bands
    appear. None flips a plausible verdict today; each is for the owner's ruling through main.
  - _Atom tables below 10 Pa_ take k = 100 on the whole chord, which is conservative; to be
    restricted to the chord above the 10 Pa level only if a body is labelled by that alone.
  - _The isothermal seam's artefacts._ An Earth-class record with O₂ takes "O2–O2 pairs: their
    absorption held at the nearest temperature on file" at 287.9 K, past the CIA's 287 K. And
    the column is unbound, a `RangeError` and the computation fault, where
    k T_s ln 10⁷ ≥ μ m_u g_ref R_ref (16.1 scale heights at least R_ref): 300 K of H₂ at
    g 0.5 m s⁻² on any body under about 40,000 km. No Solar System fixture comes near it (Titan's
    H is about 20 km). Both go with P14.T24.e's profile.
  - _An aerosol mode outside its optics' range_ (from 24, when the inventory is sent): Mie
    refuses past x = 20,000 and the iron table past its largest size (a solid-iron mode of r_eff
    about 2 µm or more at v_eff 0.3, at 380 nm), and `aerosolTerm`'s throw would raise the
    computation fault, which ruling 6 keeps for bugs. Drop such a mode with a reason before 24's
    inventory reaches the cache. _Closed by R08.T10.b._
  - _Eviction frees no texture_ (item 10). `AtmosphereTables.dispose` stops following restores
    and frees nothing, so an evicted body's textures stay until the engine is disposed. For
    R08.T10.b, with a release in `tables.ts` under `just test-render`. _Closed by R08.T10.b._
  - _Arrival._ Each worker forms a lined body's specs itself, about 0.5 s a worker on Earth, which
    is why the three later shares took about 1.0 s against the first's 0.53 s; sending the specs
    instead would serialise about 3 MB a worker on the render thread. For R08.T11's line-arrival
    budget (5 s a world on the UHD 620).
  - _Liquid methane_ (:12950–12955) was routed here beside 38(c), its sign-off question (does
    38(a) cover a liquid whose red bands are its own measurement?) is open, and nothing is built:
    it stays unlabelled meanwhile.

    `sphereModeInRange`, `nonSpherical.ts`'s `tableReaches` and `particlesInRange` (the routing
    of `opticsOfParticles`; a mineral past `KERNEL_TRANSPARENT_N_MAX` also asks Mie's, since its
    floor's fallback is known only from its optics), `aggregate.ts`'s `aggregateShapeInRange` and
    `aggregateInRange`, routed by shape in `aerosol.ts`'s `aerosolModeInRange` at every wavelength
    the term draws (`AEROSOL_TERM_WAVELENGTHS_NM`: the channels and 550 nm). The shortest is the
    blue channel's 433.625 nm, not 380 nm: a solid-iron mode of r_eff 2 µm at v_eff 0.3 reaches
    19.2 µm against the iron table's 18.1 µm there, and is dropped; one of 1 µm is drawn. Two
    more legal records reach a refusal, and are dropped too: a gamma of v_eff 0.5 or more, which
    the wire takes (`bodiesWire.ts`'s `positive`) and the law refuses; and an aggregate of
    fractal dimension 1, which the wire takes ([1, 2.5]) and the MMF refuses ((1, 2.5]). For P14:
    the wire's checks and the optics' ranges differ there (reported to main). The screen reads the
    term's wavelengths alone: a spectral bake that reads a mode at 380 nm (R08.T14), where the iron
    table ends at 15.9 µm, must screen it there too. The reasons' wording ("outside", not the
    handoff's "past", since a distribution below Mie's smallest size is screened too) passed the
    UX review.
  - _The tables handed over_ (item 3). `HillaireAtmosphere.over(engine, tables, sizes, kernels)`
    takes the cache's `AtmosphereTables` (`HeldTables`), never disposes them, takes its figure and
    gravity from them (`tablesFigureOf`: the body's, or a sphere of `bottomRadiusM`, a new
    getter), and follows the cache's next set (`setTables`); `setMedium` refuses held tables. Its
    gravity is no longer fixed at construction. The per-frame kernels and the composite are the
    view's, made asynchronously with the renderer's other pipelines (`createAtmosphereFrameKernels`)
    and shared by its bodies' atmospheres, since the engine caches no pipeline; the kernels have no
    release, and the composite and its triangle are released with the view. An atmosphere over
    shared kernels refuses a frame after a restore (`AtmosphereRetired`), and its owner makes it
    again. `dispose` now releases the frame's own textures (sky view,
    aerial volume, ray march) and the tables it built. The forward-lobe tables stay where they
    are built; moving them into the optics worker was optional and is not done.
  - _Eviction frees its textures_ (T10.a's deferred finding). `AtmosphereTables.dispose`
    releases the buffer and every texture once, and `setMedium` refuses after it. Each view takes
    a body's tables afresh every frame, so none draws with released ones.
  - _The passes._ `photorealisticPasses`' `atmosphere` slot is built, with
    `PassEntry.labels` (`ATMOSPHERE_PASS_LABELS`: `atmosphere tables`, `atmosphere view`,
    `atmosphere composite`, the constants `ATMOSPHERE_TABLES_PASS`, `ATMOSPHERE_VIEW_PASS` and
    `ATMOSPHERE_COMPOSITE_PASS`). `PhotorealFrame.atmospheres` names each body's tables, its
    `bodyAtmosphereCamera` at the frame's own viewport (not the presented size) and its
    `toBodyFixed` (`atmosphereToBodyFixed`). After the discs, each body's composite is drawn,
    farthest first, into two air targets in turn (`rgba16float`, no depth, so that a composite
    reads the scene's depth), the next over the last; the histogram, bloom and the tone map read
    the last (`frameColours`, a probe for the smoke page). Memory for R08.T11 and R12.T10: two
    full-size air targets a photorealistic view, made at its first air, and one sky view, aerial
    volume and ray-march target a body whose air the view draws, let go when it no longer does.
  - _A composite that throws_ (`decision-r08-t10b-leans.md` §2, ruled on the lane's lean). A throw
    from a view's drawing of a body's atmosphere (`HillaireAtmosphere.over`, `skySources`,
    `drawFrame`), other than a lost device's, is item 6's failure (`decision-r08-t10b-leans.md`
    §2). The renderer reports it to the cache, which holds the body `failed`, logs once, and raises
    `ATMOSPHERE NOT AVAILABLE: computation failed for <designations>, reopen VIEW to retry` on every
    view that draws it larger than a point. It is retried at the next trigger and when `VIEW` is
    shown again. As built: `#drawAtmospheres` catches in one place, `#atmosphereOf` inside its `try`, and
    passes the body, the error and its view's name to `PhotorealFrame.onAtmosphereFailed`, the
    view's `AtmosphereView.reportDrawFailure`, which moves the body to `failed`, cancels its build
    and lets its tables go, with one `console.error` naming the view; a report for a body already
    failed, or from a closed view, does nothing. A lost device's throw is told by its type
    (`EngineUnavailable`, and the new `AtmosphereRetired` that an atmosphere over shared kernels
    throws after a restore; `lostDevice`) and reports nothing. The renderer's `#airFailed` is gone;
    with no handler (the smoke page, a test) it logs the throw itself.
  - _One list of sources_ (Design note 7). `BodyFramePlan.sources` holds the arrays each record
    was shaded from, which the sky takes as they are; `bodyLightSources` gives a body the plan
    holds no record of the same arrays (the camera's local body seen from inside its figure's
    sphere; the renderer gives every such body drawn larger than a point its sources, and draws
    its air where its camera is inside it, or its shell meets the view, below). A star past the
    light slots its tables hold is left out of its sky until the cache builds them for it: the
    cache takes the lights of the view's last plan, a frame behind.
  - _An air body drawn with depth_ (`decision-r08-t10b-depth.md`). A body whose air the frame draws
    (`PhotorealFrame.atmospheres`) and that `planLitBodies` would draw as a disc is drawn as a mesh
    (`BodyFrameOptions.depthBodyShellRadiiM`), and promotes the discs it overlaps, as a mesh body
    does (R07 Design note 2). Without depth the composite reads its pixels as nothing drawn and puts
    the march's bare p q ground over R07's disc. This adds a third case to R07 Design note 1's mesh
    regime. There is no pixel threshold, since a point draws no air and R07's mesh holds down to the
    3 px switch. Its costs are recorded for R08.T11: one smooth mesh per air body; the face's pixels
    at the drawn surface's 36 steps on high, not lever 3's 20–28; and small air bodies' cells shaded
    serially, T9.b's per-tables `disc cells` dispatch deferred.
  - _The scope on low_ (T9.a's question "For R08.T10.b", :7480; ruled, `decision-r08-t10b-leans.md`
    §1). The composite takes the scene target's depth on both settings, so on low it lays the air
    over every air body's face as well as the terrain, not "the terrain alone": without it, an air
    body seen from orbit would show air at its limb over a bare face. T9.a's own lean, kept.
  - _The air beyond an unseen figure_ (`decision-r08-t10b-leans.md` §3): an air body's composite is
    drawn while its shell, a + H ÷ s_e, meets the view, its figure off it or not. Its promotion
    footprint is the shell's circle. As built: `airShellRadiusM` takes the larger semi-axis of the
    march's top shell, (a + H ÷ s_e, c + H ÷ s_p) (`viewExactOf`), a + H ÷ s_e on every oblate body;
    `#drawAtmospheres` draws a body whose shell is not `sphereOutsideView`, its sources those
    `withRecordlessSources` builds; `BodyFrameOptions.depthBodyShellRadiiM` (renamed from
    `depthBodies`, its unit in its name) is now a map of each body's shell radius, its footprint for
    `promoteOverlapping` that circle. The figure's record stays culled at a.
  - _Every view compiles the atmosphere's kernels_ (the four per-frame kernels and the composite)
    with its other pipelines, with air or without: their compile time is for R08.T11, and a failed
    compile fails the photorealistic style as any of its pipelines does.
  - _The surfaces lit through the air._ Each air body's `LitBodyInput.atmosphere` is
    `surfaceLightingTablesOf(tables)`, and a body handed over passes its record's to its terrain
    (`terrainLightingOf`, R10.T16.c's binding point), the composite then laid over the terrain.
  - _The fetch joined_ (item 4). `BodyDetailShare` sits between the link's request client and
    both askers. The cache's asks are its triggers: sent, or joined to a request for the body in
    flight; its reply is kept. The terrain session's `body_detail` joins one in flight or takes
    the latest reply kept (the latest 64 bodies'), at once, so that one request a body serves
    both; every other request, `surface_field`'s bulk with its options among them, passes
    through. `useTerrainSession`'s server stage gains `requests`, the share's; `session.ts`'s
    comments name the share in place of "R08.T10.a's shares".
  - _The frame noted._ Each view's drawer notes its frame with the cache through its own handle
    (`ViewAtmosphereHandle`, opened anew when the stage's cache is remade, closed with the view):
    each lit body at its regime on the view's last photorealistic plan, its lights as `BodyLight`s
    from that plan's sources (the star's scene body, R06's bake spectrum), and a kept scene's
    body with its `ViewBody.atmosphere` (new; absent is `unset`, so R07's `TEST GIANT` and every
    kept body left unset carry `ATMOSPHERE: NOT YET MODELLED`). A wireframe frame notes none
    wanted. The camera's local body where terrain draws it is noted at its plan's regime, not as
    `terrain`, since it is wanted either way. `AtmosphereScene`: the system's place and
    designation, the scene's time, one arrival object a system the stage draws (made anew when
    the scene's system changes; a stage remounts across a system's loss), the grants as
    `SceneSystem.grants`' levels, and the link's state.
  - _The lines_ (item 6, its follow-up and UX review). `photorealStatements` appends the
    atmosphere's notes after the others (`labels.ts`'s `atmosphereNotes`), the `ATMOSPHERE
REJECTED` lines after `ATMOSPHERE: NOT RESOLVED` and before the annunciations; a statement
    may be a request's status (`LabelStatement`, `LabelStatementLine`), the server's own failure in
    `--status-caution`.
    `faultsFor` appends `ATMOSPHERE NOT AVAILABLE` and the `DATA INVALID` lines after the
    graphics fault and the terrain's. An instrument states its own. Each names its bodies by
    designation (`atmosphereShownOf`), published at the readout rate; a problem of a body the
    scene no longer holds says nothing. On the UX review, a `REJECTED` line is a request's status
    (`StatusStatement`, set through `StatusLine` as the survey line's `REJECTED` is): `refused` in
    `--text`, `fault` in `--status-caution`.
  - _The seams narrowed._ `AtmosphereRequests` and R10's `TerrainRequests` take `body_detail` alone
    (`request(body: RequestOf<"body_detail">)`), the one kind either asks of its own, which the
    link's request client takes as it is; the share hands each request back under its own kind,
    with no cast.
  - _Failures forgotten._ The cache lives as long as its engine, which `Activity` disposes when
    `VIEW` is hidden, so `VIEW` shown again makes a cache that holds no failure: the rule is met
    by the cache's lifetime, and `forgetFailures` is not called.
  - _Kept media loading._ `KeptBodyAtmosphere` gains `loading`, pending as a server body's
    asked record is, for a kept scene whose fixtures' optics load lazily.
  - _VIEW's tests_ take `test/silentOpticsWorker.ts`'s workers (`ViewDisplay`'s new
    `opticsWorkers`), which answer nothing, so that no test frame waits on the optics.
  - _The smoke page_ (part 11, `R08.T10.b the air over a drawn ground`; the ruling's §6): an
    Earth from outside its air, 40 px across, drawn twice under one set of tables with its albedo
    halved; the scene's depth above 0 at the disc's centre, (out A − B) ÷ (ground A − B) in (0, 1]
    in every channel, and every texel finite; the ring of pixels at depth 0 recorded. Measured
    (`just test-render --part=11`, both variants, 2026-10-26): the shares 0.789, 0.789 and 0.790
    (r, g, b), 40 of the disc's 1,264 pixels at depth 0; the group 30.2 and 30.4 s, part 11
    101.6 and 102.7 s of its 180 s watchdog, at a 1-minute load of 0.14 when it started. The shares
    are grey: the face seen from above the top takes the march's mean transmittance (T8.b's
    deferred finding, now on every air body's face; `decision-r08-t10b-depth.md` §5). The ruling's
    51 s for part 11 predates T8.c's footprint group, 42.9 s of it here.
  - _The kept scene_ (`view/scenes/atmosphereScene.ts`, `ATMOSPHERE TEST`;
    `decision-r08-t10b-ux.md`). Four of Design note 16's fixtures, R08.T12.b.1's cases as kept
    media: `TEST EARTH` (`earth`), `TEST EARTH O3 SLAB` (`earth-ozone-slab`), `TEST MARS` (`mars`)
    and `TEST SATURN` (`saturn-oblate`), each drawn on its medium's figure and shaded as a grey
    Lambert sphere of its medium's ground albedo (p = A ÷ 1.5), provisional, under
    `BODY PHOTOMETRY: NOT YET MODELLED`, so that the limb's march ground is the disc's.
    R08.T12.b.2's four, `venus-92bar`, `venus-58bar`, `titan-class` and `giant-deck`, do not exist
    yet; that task adds and flies them (ruled, item 3). The media load lazily, once a page, from
    `reference/cases.ts`, started from `VIEW`'s effect when the scene is chosen
    (`SceneOption.prepare`, new), never as the scene is made in render; `loading`
    (`ATMOSPHERE: PENDING`) until they land. A failed load states each body `failed`
    (`KeptBodyAtmosphere`'s new kind), the cache's `loadFailed` problem: `ATMOSPHERE NOT AVAILABLE:
computation failed for TEST EARTH, TEST EARTH O3 SLAB, TEST MARS
and TEST SATURN, relaunch to retry`, which `VIEW` shown again does not clear (ruled, item 4).
    The layout: `TEST EARTH` 1 au out along +x with `TEST MOON` (airless, Lambert p 0.12) 3° off
    its anti-solar point; the other three a quarter of the way round the star, 1.41 au from it,
    10⁹ m apart, each seen at about 60° of phase from the one before and none in another's
    shadow. The first layout chained all four 10⁹ m apart, and the flight of 2026-10-26 found its
    night lit by `TEST SATURN`, 1.7 × 10⁹ m off and 30° from the zenith, at about 127 times the
    Moon (`EV100 4.1` on the `AVG` meter where a full Moon's sky meters about −3); now each other
    body stands 30° below the seat's horizon and gives under 1% of the Moon's light (the test).
    The ship stands 10 m up, so that the hull, pitched 47° up at the moon, clears the ground (its
    stern was 7 m under it at the first 2 m); the seat's eye is 14.6 m up, the star 45° below the
    horizon, beyond the measured Earth's twilight limit (20.2°).
  - _Its stars_ (ruled, item 1). With no server the interim field is empty, and the scene's own
    field stands in (`sceneStarsStandIn`: the scene's stars, no interim field, no sky drawn):
    500 stars spread evenly over the sphere, V spread evenly from 0 to 6, at 10 pc, from a fixed
    seed, drawn through R06's `POINT SPRITES HDR` before the composite. Each view's `STARS` line
    then reads `SCENE TEST FIELD` (`ViewFrameDrawn.sceneStars`, `withSceneStarsLine`) with no count
    line.
  - _The flight_ (`just views-check --hidden --atmosphere`; `atmosphereCheckRun.ts`,
    `atmosphereCheckResults.ts`). Scripted through `VIEW`'s own controls and judged by eye from its
    captures: the seat's night under `AUTO` on `AVG`, once the exposure holds (two readings a second
    apart within 0.1 EV, at most 60 s), then `FREE` on `LIT`, a climb of 5 × 10⁷ m towards
    `TEST MOON` first, so that the first leg leaves the planet upwards, then to 8 equatorial radii
    of each fixture, a long leg flown in stages, each from where the last ended, to a twentieth of
    the range left or the goal, the distance reckoned signed along the leg from the primary's own
    draw times, as the free camera integrates them, a stage that overruns followed by one flown back
    (a frame stall of about 1 s, below, carried one past its fixture). Each capture, a night's or a
    fixture's (`AtmosphereCheckCapture`'s `kind`; the record's version 3, with each stage flown),
    records the frame interval's and the GPU's median and 95th percentile, the exposure's settling,
    the plate's statements and fault lines; the run fails on any fault line, an exposure that never
    settles, or no capture. High then low by default; its record in
    `docs/measurements/atmosphere-flight/`.
  - _The merge of B1_ (P14.T54.b). `modesOf` takes B1's guard on a mode whose sizes or τ the
    generator does not model, then #10's screen, reading the modelled sizes and τ through B1's
    union. The should-fix to make the client's `AerosolMode` itself a union on `kind`, with size
    and τ only on modelled rows, is `lib/system`'s, another lane's: recorded for P14.T54.b's later
    batch, not adopted here.
  - _By hand_ (`just views-check --hidden --atmosphere --setting high`, 2026-10-27, on the RTX
    3080, offscreen, at a 1-minute load of 1.5 when it started;
    `docs/measurements/atmosphere-flight/2026-10-27-effect-high-atmosphere.md`): pass, no fault
    line, 220 s. By eye from its captures: the moonlit night, `EV100 1.0 AUTO` on `AVG`, a dark
    blue-grey sky under the moon's aureole, with the scene's test field, not R06's catalogue (ruled,
    item 1), seen to about V 4 (some 17 of the 30 or so stars outside the plate and the glow);
    `TEST EARTH O3 SLAB` and `TEST EARTH` at 51 Mm and 45° of phase, blue-grey over their grounds;
    `TEST MARS` at 27 Mm and 58°, tan under its dust; `TEST SATURN` at 482 Mm and 59°, grey. No
    limb haze is seen past the datum's stroke (deferred below). Frame times, provisional (a hidden
    run, so no presentation): the interval's median 16.7 ms at every capture, its 95th percentile
    16.7 to 16.8 ms (83.3 ms over the night's 100 draws); the GPU's median and 95th percentile
    1.35 and 1.35 ms at the night, 4.98 and 7.52 ms at the slab, 5.42 and 6.71 ms at Mars, 6.76 and
    9.32 ms at Saturn and 1.53 and 7.25 ms at Earth, beside T8.e's four rows, and no verdict on the
    frame, which is R08.T11's. The flight of 2026-10-26, on the first layout, is superseded: its
    night was lit by `TEST SATURN`.
- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)** (R08.T10.b). Recorded and deferred: each leaves the
  algorithm and every contract as they are.
  - _The limb under the air_: on the limb pixels whose centre ray meets the ground (about 44, 19,
    6 and 2% of a disc's ground pixels at 4, 10, 32 and 100 px), the march's p q Lambert ground
    stands in for R07's law and class map, the colour per channel kept. A point in front of an air
    body's face takes the face's depth, and its air column is laid over it. Both are R08.T16.b's.
    The candidate is a disc-ground input to the composite and the march, through R05.T12.e's gate.
  - _The face's lost lever 3 and the serial cells_ (`decision-r08-t10b-depth.md` §5, §7): for
    R08.T11's measured frame, and to R12.T10 only if its rows miss (lever 3's count for a drawn
    surface on the reference spheroid, through R05.T12.e's gate, and one `disc cells` dispatch
    per set of tables, against T9.b's note that gave it to T10.b). _Taken_
    (`decision-r08-t11-frame.md`): lever 3's count on the face by R08.T11.b, the serial cells by
    R07.T8.e.
  - _The band on each drawn body_ (T8.a's lean: `marchBand.test.ts`'s read, march and blend frames
    on each body T10.b draws) and _each drawn body's low e_q_ beside `LOW_TWIN_WORST` (T8.b): not
    run; figure-matching, for R08.T11's frame or R08.T17.
  - _Several bands on the GPU_ (T8.b's record, :8616, "R08.T10.b checks it on the Saturn-class
    figure"): the flight draws the Saturn-class fixture, by eye only; a measured check is R08.T11's
    or R08.T17's.
  - _The label block's room_ (T2's record, "For R08.T10.b"): every kept scene's body left unset now
    adds `ATMOSPHERE: NOT YET MODELLED` (`PRECISION TEST` had 6 px to spare). Not measured here;
    for R08.T11's frame or R12.
  - _The `APPROXIMATE` row and a mode out of range_ (the UX review): the guide's row names no cloud
    or haze left out for its optics' range, nor when that clears. A clause for the sign-off.
  - _A stall as a body's air is first wanted_: the flight's smokes stall `VIEW` for about 1 s at

    `ATMOSPHERE: APPROXIMATE` stands on every Earth-, Mars- and Saturn-class generated world that
    draws. For main's revisit, as T10.a's record asked.
- **Deviations in T11, as built** (2026-10-27; the RTX 3080's rows; the UHD 620's are the owner's,
  pending). New: `smoke/frameTiming.ts`, `smoke/frameTimingScene.ts` and its test,
  `smoke/frameTimingLedger.ts` (the timing's bookkeeping, GPU-free, since the review) and its test,
  and `view/atmosphere/giantRows.test.ts`. Edited: `smoke/atmosphere.ts` (exports only), `smoke/page.ts`,
  and the smoke main's `result.ts` (with its test) and `main.ts`. The record is in
  `docs/measurements/atmosphere-frame/2026-10-27-effect-frame-timings.md`, with the raw check lines,
  every timed frame's sum included, in the `.txt` beside it. No kernel, table, golden, wire or version
  moves.
  - _The harness, committed._ It is a GPU-timing-only group of the smoke page's part 1,
    `R08.T11 the photorealistic frame's timings`.
    - When it runs: after R08.T8.c's far-limb timings, under `--smoke-gpu-timing=1`. A plain
      `just test-render` never runs it, since SwiftShader has no `timestamp-query`.
    - Why committed, not scratch: the owner's UHD 620 pass runs it too (`settingOutput("low")`
      draws 1280 × 720).
    - Its watchdog: `smokeWatchdogMs` gains `GPU_TIMING_WATCHDOG_MS`, 480 s, for a timing run that
      takes part 1 (3 × the 148 s measured).
    - Its parts:
      - (A) the frame through `PhotorealRenderer`;
      - (B) the atmosphere alone over nothing drawn, on the same tables and `SunState`s;
      - (C) small air bodies;
      - (D) each medium's per-planet tables, cold and warm, with the main thread's split;
      - (E) the first air frame's allocations;
      - (F) its main-thread time and `prepare`'s;
      - (G) the frame without its air.
    - The form: QW2's (`decision-r08-t8-leans.md` §10). Each combination gets 10 warm-up and 30
      timed frames, over two sweeps, the second reversed. Each frame is drawn as soon as frame
      n − 3 has resolved, so the GPU never idles on the page and the timer drops nothing. The
      measure is the frame's GPU pass sum.
    - The scene (the record's header has it whole): high 1920 × 1080, the average meter, EV100 15.
      R05's, the measured and the slab Earth on WGS 84, drawn as R07's mesh. R08.T8.c's five
      far-limb cameras, and T8.c's timed Sun.
    - The sets, each built as scene geometry and checked through `skySourcesWithSkips`:
      - `x1`: the Sun;
      - `x2`: a binary's two light slots, a second Sun-like star at √10 au, 40° off;
      - `x2p`: a star and a giant's planetshine on one slot. The giant is Jupiter-like, 6 R_J off,
        out of view, at 60° of phase, its planetshine 8 × 10⁻³ to 1.4 × 10⁻² of the Sun;
      - `x4`: the setting's count on high, two stars and two giants (`x3` on low).
    - Not drawn: terrain, the sky, the star sprites and the symbology. The terrain's cost from orbit
      stands as R08.T8.e's estimate, 1.5, 1.3 and 1.0 ms from 400 km to 1.54 × 10⁷ m, in the
      mesh's place. The mesh's own `bodies` pass is 1.9–3.5 ms.
  - _QW28._ RTX 3080, hidden, 2026-10-27 03:05 UTC; the 1-minute load 1.33 at the start and 1.12
    at the end; under the heavy-test and GPU locks, CPUQuota 1200%. Clocks: P0 in 1,465 of 1,543
    samples; busy, a median of 1,965 of 2,115 MHz, 5 samples under 90%; at most 66 °C. Every check
    of the group passed. No timed frame was dropped, and every combination drew exactly its set's
    sources. The part's one failure is R07.T16.f's spatial strokes on hardware, which failed alike

      chain, not a fill, and QW29 tests it. Its four pieces of evidence:
      - a limb pixel above 32 px takes 4 × 4 cells, each within two cell widths of the limb shaded
        at up to nine points: on a straight limb about 62 shades a pixel against one inside,
        each over every source with T9.b's reads;
      - V1a leaves 19–60 µs, so the quad costs nothing;
      - small air bodies, which sum their cells in their draws, take 0.49–0.51 ms of `discs` at
        4, 10 and 32 px whatever their pixel count, against 0.008 ms at 4 px bare through the
        `disc cells` pass;
      - R07's T17 record found the in-fragment chain to be arithmetic latency, constant with
        pixel count, and `decision-r07-small-disc-cost.md` §6 names a large limb's cells through
        the pass as the next step.

  (`DRAWN_SURFACE_BAND_M`, `MarchDepthSteps.drawnBandM`, `drawnSurfaceKind`) and its test;

  ground) and its tests; `test/atmosphereGate.ts` (`GateRay.drawnHeightM`, `marchKindOf(ray, rule)`,
  `drawnSurfaceRays`) and its test; `test/marchGate.ts` and the three media's records;
  `reference/twin.test.ts`; `smoke/atmosphere.ts`; the smoke's new part 12 (`smoke/page.ts`,
  `scripts/testRender.sh`, `src/smoke/main.ts`, `result.ts` and its test); and the eight

  `reference/caseGate.json`, re-blessed. No wire, version, golden of the sim or table moves.
  - _The band._ A height over the datum, 25 km (`DRAWN_SURFACE_BAND_M`), not V4's 1% of the hit
    distance: §8 confirmed it, amending §2's start. A drawn surface at or beyond the datum's hit
    counts as in band, since the march ends at the hit there and the segment is the bare ground's.
    R07's face, drawn on its chords, always is (its limb draw writes no depth), so V4's whole saving
    is kept at the four rows. Before the hit the kernel takes the drawn point's height by
    `datumPointOf` from the ground quadric at the surface's distance, near and far forms as a
    step's. The count's depth is the bare ground's, from the datum's hit back along the ray. The
    branch runs only where the setting has the bare ground's rule (`view.marchGround.x` over 0,
    high), so on low the kernel and the twin tell every drawn surface alike.
    - _The limit, recorded_ (§8): plan 14 caps an edifice's rise over its base at 21.9 km at Mars's
      gravity, growing as 1 ÷ g. A summit over 25 km, on a world lighter than Mars or on a base
      more than about 3 km over the datum, keeps the setting's count: no saving there, and no wrong
      picture. Deferred to R12.T10: the band as max(25 km, the body's own edifice cap at its g),

    - So a body in a system with any lit neighbour likely draws x(stars) + 2 on high, the march
      included. The x2p and x4 rows may then be the common frame, not x1 and x2.
    - _Deferred to R08.T11.d_ (main, 2026-10-27), as a candidate lever: a cull of the
      planetshine sources below a brightness that moves no pixel by more than the twin's
      tolerance. `TEST SATURN`'s x2p and x4 rows are for QW30.
- **Deviations in T6.e, as built** (2026-10-13). `tablesCpu.ts`, `oblate.ts` and `hillaire.ts`;
  tests in a new `tablesCpuOblate.test.ts` (inside the acceptance's `view/atmosphere/tablesCpu`
  filter) and in `hillaire.test.ts`. No kernel, no smoke group and no version moves: the twin is
  the oracle T6.f's kernels will be held to.
  - _Names beyond the text._ `tablesCpu.ts`: `TwinBody` (the figure and R08.T3.d's
    `BodyGravity`), `OblateTwinSizes` and `OBLATE_KERNEL_SIZES`, `TwinBand` and `twinBandOf`,
    `OblatePlanetTwin` and `oblatePlanetTwin`; `SlicedFit`, `SliceRead`, `SlicedRay`, `SliceRule`,
    `SlicedSunTransmittance` and `slicedSunTransmittance`, `slicedStoredOpticalDepth`,
    `bandMultiScattering`; `SpheroidOpticalDepth` and `spheroidOpticalDepth` (the brute force);
    `OblateSkyViewRay`, `oblateSkyViewRayTwin`, `oblateSkyViewTexelsTwin`, `oblateSkyViewTwin`,
    `oblateSkyViewReadTwin`, `oblateAerialPerspectiveTwin`, `oblateRayMarchRayAlongTwin`,
    `oblateRayMarchRayTwin`, `oblateRayMarchTexelTwin` and `oblateRayMarchTwin`. `MarchGeometry`
    gains `gravitySpheroid`. Internal: `OblateReader` (the lookups), the marches' `MarchReads`,
    `OblateMarch` and `MarchFrame`, and `scaledTerms`. `oblate.ts`: `gravityRatioSlope` (ds ÷ dφ
    in closed form), `principalRadiiM` and `bandLatitudeRad`; `gravityRatio` keeps each spheroid's
    γ_e and γ_p (the same arithmetic, the same values).
  - _A twin of its own, the body beside the medium._ The medium carries no slicing (T3.d's
    deviations), so T6.e takes the `BodyGravity` beside it, in `TwinBody`, as T3.d left open; T10.a
    may still move it into the medium. The spherical twin is unchanged and stays the kernels' oracle
    for the smoke until T6.f; the oblate functions sit beside it.
  - _The bands in their own frame._ A band at s is the reference medium read at h\* = s h; on
    lengths l\* = s l it is the reference medium with every coefficient, and every absorber column
    per metre, divided by s, on the sphere s √(MN) (Design note 17's scaling, which makes τ ÷ s of a
    table exact where s and R_α are uniform). So each band is "an ordinary build at the band's g(φ)
    and √(MN)", its own transmittance table and multiple-scattering layers, with its rows at h\* and
    the reference medium's top, and Ψ, which the change of length does not move, is read at a
    sample's h\*. A band's latitude is where s is its s (bisection, s being monotonic in sin²φ). A
    body of one band takes R05's build as it is, at s = 1 on R_ref, and with one slice at κ = 1
    shares slice 0's table.
  - _No irradiance table yet._ The text's "multiple scattering and irradiance per band": there is
    no irradiance table in the code before T9.b, so the bands carry the multiple scattering, and
    T9.b adds its irradiance to `TwinBand`, built per band in the same frame.
  - _The fit, for any medium._ The decision measured an isothermal gas of one H. The twin's
    "local scale height" is the stored vertical optical depth above the start in green (slice 0's
    table) over the extinction there, between 1 m and the room to the top: one H for an
    exponential, and the column's own e-folding for any profile. The rest is the decision's rule:
    the start, the analytic slope s μ + h (∂s ÷ ∂φ) √(1 − μ²) cos α ÷ (M + h), and h\* where the ray
    on the start's R_α has risen H ÷ s (one geodetic conversion). A dip of over H ÷ 2 in h\* is
    fitted at its lowest point by the parabola through h\* at the start sphere's tangent point and
    √(2 R_α H ÷ s) either side (three conversions), whose vertex is the lowest h\* and whose
    curvature c gives the radius s² ÷ 2c less it, in place of the decision's golden-section minimum:
    over the deep rays the two give the same worst, 0.905 and 0.905 of the bound through the slices
    (0.78 and 0.77 on the fitted sphere alone; scratch `deep-fit variants`). Every
    dipping ray is read on each slice at the cosine that keeps its lowest h\*, the ground hiding the
    source below the datum; a body of one band reads the start's own sphere (the decision's "may skip
    the fit"); one slice and one band read the slice at h\* and μ. The slices are interpolated
    linearly in ln κ, as written.
  - _Where a march's lookup starts._ The sky view's and the aerial perspective's samples start
    their lookups at the march's own height and normal on R_α, at the sample's own geodetic latitude
    (Vermeille at its body-fixed place), the density's own state; the fit's far points are on the
    true spheroid. The ray march reads every sample at its geodetic height h, not R05's radial
    height, which departs from it by h(1 ÷ cos ψ − 1), ψ the angle between the radius and the
    normal (0.5% of h on Saturn at 45°, 6 × 10⁻⁶ on Earth), since h\* = s h is geodetic (Design note
    17); its layer edges and top are the quadrics through h\* at the equator and the poles,
    (a + e ÷ s_e, c + e ÷ s_p), as R08.T12.d's tracer's shells are. The sky view's and the aerial
    perspective's spheres take the medium's top over the camera's s, and the sky view's layer
    edges cross R_α at e ÷ s at the camera. The sky view's horizon split is each column's R_α, and
    `oblateSkyViewReadTwin` takes it at the direction's own azimuth.
  - _R_α_ is taken as M ÷ (1 − (1 − M ÷ N) sin²α), which is M = N on a sphere to the bit, and √(MN)
    for a vertical ray. With the lookup's start above, a sphere with ω = 0 gives T6.d's sky view,
    aerial perspective and ray march to 10⁻¹² (from 2 m, 2 km and 400 km); its per-planet tables
    are T6.d's to the bit.
  - _`geodeticOf`_ is Vermeille 2002 in Karney 2011's forms, R08.T12.d's Rust operation for
    operation, its signature kept. It round-trips Saturn from the datum to 10 H (H = 49.7 km), WGS 84
    and c ÷ a = 0.2 to under 10⁻⁶ m. R05.T12.c's tests pass unchanged.
  - _The tests' Saturn-class medium_ is the H₂–He air's molecular term (R08.T3.c, the NSSDCA
    fractions, 134 K) on e^(−h\* ÷ H) at the isothermal H = 49.7 km, its top at 16 H, about 10⁻⁷ of
    the datum's density: smooth, so
    that the brute force converges spectrally (Gauss–Legendre's 8 points on 5 km pieces; halving
    them moves it by 1.4 × 10⁻¹⁴, held under 10⁻⁷). Its vertical optical depth is 0.142, 0.285 and
    0.728. A table's or a tent's kinks converge more slowly, which `spheroidOpticalDepth`'s
    documentation states (decision-r08-spheroid §1's "splits at the kinks where it must").
  - _What the bound is held on._ `decision-r08-spheroid.md` §2 measured the lookup with each slice
    integrated exactly. The test does the same: the lookup's sphere and slices, each slice
    integrated along its own read's ray (R05's rule at 8,192 steps), and that meets the bound on
    every ray. The twin's own read through the slices' 256 × 64 tables does not: it misses the
    text's criterion, and Verification's T6.e line, on 5 of the 598 rays, at most 1.244 times. It
    is pinned there (under 1.3, at most 5 rays over) and deferred under the 2026-10-13 rule
    (below); the cure goes to "main" before T6.f builds kernels on the same tables.
  - _The slices' interpolation test_ holds the halfway κ's interpolation against the exact
    integral there, not against a table built at the exact value, whose texels would add their own
    1.44 × 10⁻³; the twin's read of the slices' tables is held to that exact interpolation beside
    it (under 2 × 10⁻³). The march's convergence is checked on every ray of the set.
  - _The bands' bound is held in radiance._ Ψ itself is curved in s high up: between the bands it
    is off linear interpolation in ln s by up to 4% at 12 H and 10% at 15 H (converged in the
    steps: 32 and 128 give the same), where the air holds e⁻¹² of the datum's. So the test holds
    the radiance Ψ adds along views from the datum (zenith, 60° and 80°, the sun at μ_s 1 to
    0.05), Ψ weighted by the scattering through the view's transmittance, against a band built at
    the exact s halfway in ln s: under 0.5%, as the text asks. It also holds the limb from orbit in
    the band's frame, the sun at 0°, 10° and 30° above the tangent point's horizon, in the view's
    plane and across it: under 0.5% to 3 H, and pinned at 10 H, where it is not (below).
  - Figures (the scratch logs are in `.git/rm45-scratch/r08-tables/t6e/`):

- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)** (R08.T6.e). Recorded and deferred: each leaves the
  algorithm and every contract as they are.
  - _The slices' tables on a giant._ Saturn's 64 rows span 16 H, 0.22 H a row at 3 H, so the
    tables' bilinear read adds up to 1.4 × 10⁻³ of τ there, and through the tables 5 of the 598
    rays pass over the component bound, at most 1.244 times (all deep dips from 3 H). R08.T13's
    client-beam check holds the tables in radiance. Cheapest cure, measured: weights linear in √κ
    in place of ln κ, exact for Chapman's √R law at grazing and for a vertical ray, at no cost a
    read: the exact slices' worst goes from 0.905 to 0.782, and the tables' from 1.244 to 1.072 (one
    ray over); log–log interpolation gives the same. Lean: √κ weights in T6.f, with a ruling; rows
    placed by h\* ÷ H on a giant, or a taller table, are contract changes.
  - _Ψ's curvature in s high up_ (4% at 12 H, 10% at 15 H between bands) reaches the limb from
    orbit: the bands' interpolation costs 3.25% of the multiple-scattering radiance at a 10 H
    tangent, against the text's 0.5% (0.19% at 5 H). The single scattering dominates a sunlit limb
    there, so the sky's share is smaller; R08.T13's limb at 10 H and Saturn's case measure it.
    Cures, for later: bands interpolated in ln of each band's own radius s √(MN), or a band more
    where s is steep; R08.T15's deck tables and R08.T16's disc, built per band, may want the same.
  - _The sky view's lookups start on R_α_ and fit their far points on the true spheroid. The two
    heights part by the osculating sphere's third-order error, estimated at metres a thousand
    kilometres out on Saturn and not measured beyond the sphere test; T6.f's readbacks against the
    twin will see it.
  - _The layer edges at the camera's s._ The sky view's crossings take e ÷ s at the camera, not at
    each crossing's own latitude. A medium with edges on a body of several bands is the case;
    none is built yet.

  - _Slices linear in √κ, not ln κ_ (ruled by "main" 2026-10-13, after T6.e's record; a departure
    from Design note 17's "interpolating between slices in ln κ" and from T6.e's text). The twin
    (`OblateReader`'s `#read`) and `oblate.wgsl`'s `slicedRayOn` both weight the two slices about
    κ\* by (√κ\* − √κ_k) ÷ (√κ_{k+1} − √κ_k), exact, to first order in H ÷ R, for Chapman's
    grazing column, which goes as √R, and for a vertical ray. On T6.e's ray set (598 rays that
    clear the ground): the lookup's sphere and slices integrated exactly, worst 0.782 of
    max(0.01, 2 × 10⁻³ τ) (0.905 in ln κ), at 30° north from 1 H at μ −0.035; through the slices'
    256 × 64 tables, worst 1.072 and one ray over (1.244 and 5 in ln κ). `tablesCpuOblate.test.ts`
    pins both (< 0.85; < 1.1 with that one ray named), and holds the interpolation halfway in ln κ
    and halfway in √κ against the exact integral.
  - _The ray left over the bound_ (30° north, h\* 3 H, μ −0.035, a deep dip, τ 0.925, 1.857 and
    4.747; 1.072 of the bound). No cheap cure was found; it is pinned with its figure. More rows do
    not take it under in order: 72 rows put it at 1.116 with a second ray over (45° north from 3 H),
    80 at 0.906, 88 at 1.031, 96 at 0.815 and 128 at 0.876; 512 columns at 1.023. The bilinear
    read's error goes with the phase of the rows about 3 H, not with their count, so a taller table
    would pass by luck, and at 96 rows it costs 50% more in every slice's tables, which on a
    Saturn-class world with the absorber tables is at the 2 MB row already (below). A row mapping
    by h\* ÷ H is the contract change T6.e named, not made.
  - _The body's table is a texture_, `oblateBody` (`rgba32float`, one row of 36 texels, under
    `atmosphere-tables`), in place of a uniform: the composite, a material whose uniforms are its
    `Draw` members, reads it as the kernels do, and a slice's or band's constants are read by
    `textureLoad` at its index, with no dynamically indexed uniform array copied into an
    invocation's memory (R08.T6.b's lesson). Its gravity row is Somigliana's form divided through
    by a and over g_ref, s = (A cos²φ + B sin²φ) ÷ √(cos²φ + K sin²φ) + O with A = s_e − O,
    B = (s_p − O) c ÷ a, K = (c ÷ a)² and O the offset's (`BodyGravity.gravityOffsetMS2` ÷ g_ref),
    taken from `gravityRatio` at the equator and the pole, so that the body's γ_e and γ_p need no
    export; a body with no spheroid has A = B = 0 and O = 1, s ≡ 1 to the bit (`tables.test.ts`
    holds the row to `gravityRatio` from the equator to the pole, and the layout to
    `oblate.wgsl`'s).
  - _A figure with no gravity_ (found by the plan-conformance review). `HillaireAtmosphere` with
    no `gravity` still gives its tables a body on an oblate figure, `bodyOfFigure`: the figure
    with R08.T3.d's gravity for a body with no rotation section (s ≡ 1, one slice and one band),
    so that `oblate.wgsl`'s datum, and the ray march's heights and normals on it, are the figure's
    own, as R05's `radialHeight` and `normalAt` were; a sphere takes none, its tables R05's on
    R_ref = a. The first build packed a sphere of R_ref for a body of none, which put WGS 84's
    heights 0.67% high at the pole and its normals geocentric (the spike and R05.T12.c's and
    R05.T12.e's groups; no twin check runs WGS 84 without gravity). `hillaire.test.ts` holds the
    figure's texel.
  - _The bands' own transmittance tables_ are built into one set of one-layer tables made for the
    build, rebuilt for each band in turn and released after the last band's multiple scattering
    (`#dispatchTables`), so that they cost no per-planet memory: Design note 11 counts the multiple
    scattering per band, not the bands' transmittance. Each band is the reference medium with
    every coefficient ÷ s_b on the sphere s_b √(MN) (T6.e's "bands in their own frame"), through
    `Medium.build`'s coefficient factor. A body of one slice at κ = 1 and one band, Earth's or a
    sphere's, reads the slice's own (`TablesPlan.shared`), as R05's. The kernel arm builds them
    anew in the stored format, and the smoke reads them back through `bandTransmittance(b)`, in
    the stored arm only: it is the slices' kernel, whose kernel arm holds it at the factor 1.
  - _Design note 18's forms, changed as T6.e's contract asked_ (ruled by "main" 2026-10-13).
    - The ray march's top and layer edges are the quadrics through h\* = e at the equator and the
      poles, (a + e ÷ s_e, c + e ÷ s_p), in place of S_t = diag(1, 1, (a + H) ÷ (c + H)): q_t is
      formed in `f64` from them (`viewExactOf`), and an edge's constant from q_g as
      q_g + (k_e − k)(k_e + k) P_z² − e_a (2a + e_a), with
      k_e − k = (c e_a − a e_c) ÷ (c (c + e_c)).
    - `exact.z` is no longer the sky view's β: each column has its own, on its own sphere R_α, taken
      in `f32` in the kernel and in every read by one form (`skyViewColumnOf`): R_α from the
      camera's M and N, formed in `f64` (`view.curvature`), and β = π ÷ 2 − preciseAtan(√(h (2 R_α +
      h)) ÷ R_α), within 5 × 10⁻⁷ rad of `f64`'s atan2 (`precision.test.ts`). The read inverts the
      write to 10⁻³ of a texel on WGS 84 and on the Saturn-class figure, every column on its own
      sphere. `exact.z` now carries the camera's local scale height, for the composite's lookup.
    - A sample's height on the spheroid, the ray march's, is the root of the exact quadratic along
      the similar spheroid's normal (`datumPointOf`), from the ground quadric the march forms, in
      place of R05's radial height (T6.e's twin reads the geodetic height). In `f64` on the
      Saturn-class figure, over 0–90° in 5° steps, it is within 1.6 × 10⁻⁶ of the geodetic height
      at 1,000 km, 2.6 × 10⁻⁷ at 400 km and 1.63 mm at 100 km (1.64 mm at worst, at 43.5°): the
      error goes as h³, so the text's 2 × 10⁻⁶ holds and its 1.2 mm (`decision-r08-f32.md` §8.6,
      its latitudes unstated; about the 60° value) is not reproduced, and `precision.test.ts` pins
      1.7 mm. The root is the text's. Its latitude is the datum's normal at the root's foot, within
      3.2 × 10⁻⁵ rad of the geodetic latitude at 1,000 km and 3.2 × 10⁻⁷ at 100 km, which moves s
      by under 9 × 10⁻⁶ (8.8 × 10⁻⁶ at 45°); the text named no latitude. Emulated in `f32` it keeps
      10⁻⁶ · max(t, |h|, 1 km) of its own form from −400 m to 400 km, and the far bound from 1.5a
      to 10⁹ m, on the four figures (`precision.test.ts`).
    - The sky view's and the aerial perspective's samples take their latitude from the datum point
      of their body-fixed place, its quadric by the near form from q_g; a body of one slice and
      one band with no spheroid takes none (`oblateNeedsLatitude`).
    - The fit's distances are written in forms chosen not to cancel in `f32`: x₁'s root as
      rise (2 reach + rise) ÷ (reach μ + √(…)) for a rising ray, the fitted radius's numerator with
      (h\*₀ − h\*₁)(h\*₀ + h\*₁), and the dip as (r + h) μ² ÷ (1 + √(1 − μ²)). `precision.test.ts`
      emulates the datum height and the column's β only; the fit's forms are held by the smoke's
      kernel arm (deferred, below).

- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)** (R08.T6.f). Recorded and deferred: each leaves the
  algorithm and every contract as they are.
  - _A Saturn-class world's per-planet tables reach 2 MB_ (1,999,424 B at one light slot, above).
    The absorber-column and pressure-column tables take every slice whatever the medium's
    absorbers, though the kernels read the first only with two absorbers or more and the second
    with one or more; a medium without them could bind one-texel tables, as the fifth pressure
    channel's does, saving up to 1.31 MB here, back near Design note 11's 0.72 MB. For R08.T11's
    budget, which holds Design note 11's row.
  - _The split's rounding from above the air_ (above): the kernel cannot tell R05.T12.e's split at
    its rounding, so from above the air the sky view's twilight texels may differ from the twin by
    a step's worth, 1–4% on the Saturn-class limb. The smoke counts them apart; the cure is the
    kernels' split taken from a form that does not cancel (the sides' difference from the shell's
    heights, (top − h)(2R + top + h) over their sum) or the camera held further inside the shell,
    either a change to R05.T12.e's steps for every march.
  - _The fit's `f32` forms are not emulated_ in `precision.test.ts` (the datum height and the
    column's β are): x₁'s root, the dip, the fitted radius, the parabola, the ground decision,
    `lowestOnSphereM`, `cosineToLowestOf`, `quadricAlong`, the sky view's lifted quadric, the edge
    constant with e_a ≠ e_c, and `gravityRatioAt` and `gravityRatioSlopeAt`. The smoke's kernel
    arm holds them against the twin (to 6.5 × 10⁻⁴, above).
  - _The kernels' cost on SwiftShader._ R05.T12.e's group, one slice and one band, grew from 43 s
    to 56.8 s, more than its added operations account for. A likely reading, not measured:
    SwiftShader runs its lanes in step and need not skip a branch none of them takes, so every
    body would pay for the bands' fit, where a real GPU's branch on the body's uniform counts skips
    it. R08.T11 times the kernels on both. If the smoke's parts grow again, the cure is kernels
    specialised by the body's slice and band counts (an `override` constant, which R01's
    `createCompute` does not yet take).
  - _The ray left over the bound_ (1.072, above). R08.T13's client-beam check holds the tables in
    radiance; a row mapping by h\* ÷ H on a giant, if it ever is, is a contract change.
  - _The composite's sliced read has no twin of its own_: its transmittance to space (the disc's)
    is checked only finite and in range in the smoke, its lookup the kernels' form from the camera.
    R08.T13's client-beam check sees it.
  - _T6.e's lookups that start on R_α_ (T6.e's deferred findings) are the kernels' too, so the
    readbacks, which agree with the twin, do not see them; R08.T13's limb at 10 H and Saturn's case
    measure them against the tracer. So do the layer edges at the camera's s in the sky view (no
    medium with edges on a body of several bands is built).
  - _The spike's Earth has no gravity_ until R08.T10.a gives each body its `BodyGravity`: its sky
    keeps s ≡ 1, which moves Earth's air by under 0.3% at the equator (T6.e's figures).
  - _`--captures` meets part 1's watchdog_ under load: part 1's groups took about 95 s and the
    captures after them ran past 180 s at a load of 15–20, so no frame was saved. The captures
    could run in a part of their own, or under a longer watchdog of their own.
  - _The UX guide's `APPROXIMATE` row_ (`docs/frontend/ux-guidelines.md`) still names the strongly
    flattened body, which no body is now drawn as; keeping it as conditional wording or dropping it
    is the sign-off agent's, through "main".
  - _`SkyViewTable.sphere`_ keeps the sphere's scalar reading nested, not as top-level fields, as
    ruling 2's "a scalar reading for them if that keeps callers simple" allows; "main" may settle
    it with R11's re-validation.
