  - _The irradiance's quadrature_ (`irradianceQuadrature.ts`; the task named Bruneton's layout and
    mapping, not how to integrate when each direction is a march). E = ∫ L μ_v dω over the sky above
    the horizon, L each direction's per-frame march (each term's phase, shadowed by the ground, the
    forward lobes' higher orders, Hillaire's multiple scattering), in the band's frame over its own
    tables. The directions stand in the sun's frame, γ from the sun integrated in u = √(γ ÷ π), the
    phase tables' coordinate, so that a forward peak is resolved, on two pieces split where the
    rings meet the horizon (γ_a = |π ÷ 2 − θ_s|, wholly lit rings and cut ones), Gauss–Legendre on
    each, and each cut ring only over its arc above the horizon, so that no node straddles μ_v's
    kink; ψ counts twice by the symmetry about the sun's vertical plane. 2 × 8 × 6 = 96 directions,
    32 steps each, placed and cut at the layer edges as the multiple-scattering kernel's; one
    workgroup a texel, one invocation a direction, summed in order by the first. Measured against
    24 × 24 nodes and 128 steps at ten texels (the ground to 2/3 of the top, suns from the zenith
    to 6° down): worst 0.82% on Earth's medium, 0.95% on Earth's with a Henyey–Greenstein g = 0.85
    aerosol, 0.63% on the Saturn-class air; 4 arc nodes left 1.0% and 6 matched 8; the steps carry
    most of what is left near the ground (48 steps take Earth's zenith sun from −0.82% to −0.35%).
    Σ w is π to 2 × 10⁻³ for every sun (`surfaceLighting.test.ts`). On the Mars mode's tabulated
    dust with its lobes' higher orders (`forwardLobe.test.ts`'s dusty Mars at τ(550) 0.45 and 2,
    against 32 × 32 nodes and 128 steps, the science check's ask) the worst is 0.87%, a sun 1° up in
    blue; 16 ring nodes would take the zenith sun's 0.55% to 0.1%.
  - _The sky alone._ The table holds the sky's diffuse irradiance, Bruneton's irradiance texture's
    content: the sun's direct beam is each pass's own term through `atmosphere_sun_transmittance`,
    and the ground's light reaches a horizontal surface only as Hillaire's multiple scattering
    carries it (the lower hemisphere is the ground itself). In the thin limit it is a spherical
    single-scattering integral, held to an independent quadrature to 1%: 0.968 of the
    plane-parallel τ ÷ 2 for a Rayleigh air of τ = 10⁻⁴ on Earth's radius, the horizon's slant
    column being bounded (Chapman's grazing √(πR ÷ 2H)).
  - _The height axis_ (the science check's finding). The rows stand at x_r = √(h\* ÷ H), not
    Bruneton's (r − R) ÷ (R_top − R): his rows are 6.7 km apart on Earth, where the aerosol's scale
    height is 1.2 km, and a read between the first two came out 28%, 58% and 116% high at 0.5, 1 and
    2 km (680 nm, thin). Earth's rows now stand at 0, 0.44, 1.8, 4 and 7.1 km and on; a 1.2 km
    haze's sky reads within −7% to +8% of its falloff from 100 m to 2 km (`surfaceLighting.test.ts`
    holds 10% at 0.5, 1 and 2 km). The rows' heights come from heights alone, as Design note 18
    asks; R07's disc reads row 0 and is unchanged by it. The texel mapping is Design note 19's.
  - _Stored in `rgba32float`, so no kernel arm_ (the science check's finding). Per unit of the Sun's
    illuminance Earth's sky gives about 2.7 × 10⁻⁵, 3.1 × 10⁻⁶ and 6 × 10⁻⁸ at −6°, −8° and −12°
    (horizontal illuminances of 3.4, 0.4 and 0.008 lx over 1.27 × 10⁵ lx: the estimates from
    typical clear-sky illuminances of `decision-r08-t6b-floor.md` §6 and "The per-view tables'
    range at twilight", below, not measured), some 450, 53 and 1 of the half float's 2⁻²⁴ steps, so
    the twilight ground the sky term lights turned coarse past −9°, one step at −12° and black just
    beyond. In `f32` a layer is 16 KB; it is written as a storage texture (core in WebGPU) and read
    by `textureLoad`, as before. The stored table is the kernel's own output, so the smoke holds it
    to its twin with no floor, and `buildKernelArm` builds the transmittance and multiple
    scattering alone, as at T6.f.
  - _Built at its first read after each build_ (`AtmosphereTables.irradiance()`, which
    `surfaceLightingTablesOf` calls). The task's "rebuilt with them" is kept as rebuilt from them:
    a build leaves the irradiance to be built, and the first read builds it (a band's own
    transmittance made again for it on a body of several bands), its kernel made at the first.
    Tables whose air lights no surface, a body seen only as a point and every smoke group before
    T9.b's, never pay for it: built with the tables, it took part 2 of the smoke from T6.f's
    103 s to 145 s (at a load of 16), over the ~130 s the parts are held to.
  - _The local scale height on a body of several bands_ (T6.f's "For T9.b": the lit passes declare no
    medium). The body's table carries `medium.ts`'s `localScaleHeightM` (the composite's form, from
    each term's column) at 64 heights h\* evenly from the datum to the top, read linearly
    (`oblateScaleHeightAt`), and the medium's absorber count and line-slot mask, which the lookups'
    curves need: one texel past the bands and 16 more, `OBLATE_BODY_TEXELS` 36 → 53. The layout
    only grows at its end, so the per-frame kernels and the composite read it as before. The
    tabulation is the medium as given, with its forward deltas (the composite's own); the fit only
    places its second point by it. `localScaleHeightM` and `FIT_SCALE_FLOOR_M` moved from
    `hillaire.ts` to `medium.ts` so that `tables.ts` packs it with no cycle of imports;
    `hillaire.ts` re-exports both.
  - _`scattering.wgsl`_ holds `source.wgsl`'s medium at a sample, phases and forward lobes, moved
    unchanged but for π (`preciseTrig.wgsl`'s `TRIG_PI`, the same `f32` as `view.wgsl`'s
    `PI_VIEW`), so that the irradiance kernel, which declares no view, takes them; the per-frame
    kernels compose it before `source.wgsl`.
  - _Seven tables, not two._ The task's "transmittance and irradiance tables" are, as built since
    T6.c, T4.d and T6.f, the body's table, the four transmittance tables (slices), the lights'
    curves and the irradiance: `bodyDisc.wgsl` declares them at group 2 bindings 6 to 12, read by
    `textureLoad` (`unfilterable-float`), and `surfaceLighting.wgsl` reads them by name. A body
    without an atmosphere binds one one-texel `rgba32float` texture of zeros in all seven
    (`createAirlessTables`): the body table's a of 0 makes the lookups return 1, 0 and 1 before any
    other read, so R07's light is unchanged to the bit (R07's disc smoke, and the probe's exact
    checks).
  - _The angles in the signatures._ The Provides' latitude and azimuth arguments are kept as
    angles: `bodyDisc.wgsl` forms them with `preciseAtan2` from the spheroid normal, the pole and the
    source's direction, and `surfaceLighting.wgsl` turns them back into direction cosines with
    `preciseSinCos`, about 5 × 10⁻⁷ each way. The lit point stands at longitude 0, its foot
    (N cos φ, 0, N (1 − e²) sin φ), its quadric 2hN + h²(cos²φ + k² sin²φ) from the height.
  - _Light slots._ Star j of a disc takes light slot j's curves and irradiance layer, a planetshine
    source slot 0, each held to the medium's slots; R08.T10.a builds a body's curves in
    `lightsAt`'s order.
  - _The three-node rule's value_ is the irradiance-weighted mean transmittance of the disc's part
    above the horizon, Σ w μ T ÷ Σ w μ, which multiplies the caller's own irradiance factor
    (`planetshine_irradiance`'s): the centre's lookup as ρ → 0 (10⁻⁶), within 2% of a 200 × 200
    quadrature over a 9.8° disc 10° up on Earth's medium, and 0 for a source wholly below the local
    horizon, even from a height whose ground does not hide its centre.
  - _The sky term_ is the source's illuminance (a planetshine source's carried to the point by the
    inverse square, as its direct term is) times the sky's irradiance at its own μ₀, on the
    surface's mean A, R07's "Lambert share's flat term". A star's shares the point's eclipse and
    ring shadow (the science check's finding, where this was first deferred): the air above the
    point is taken to lie in the shadow with it, as an umbra's air does, so that a moon in its
    planet's shadow keeps no daylight sky. The eclipse is formed before the horizon's `continue`,
    and skipped where the star is down and the sky gives nothing (every airless disc), so R07's
    light is unchanged to the bit. A planetshine source's sky is not shadowed, as its direct term
    is not (Design note 7).
  - _The disc's height is 0_, the datum: R07's disc is the figure at zero height, with no terrain.
  - _Catalogued_: `irradiance.wgsl` as `IRRADIANCE_KERNEL` among the atmosphere's table kernels;
    `surfaceLighting.wgsl`, a library with no entry point, through every module that composes it
    (the disc materials, the smooth mesh, the `disc cells` kernel and the lit-body probe).
  - _The disc cells pass_ binds the one-texel defaults: a disc with an atmosphere sums its own cells
    in its draws (`drawnThroughCells`), as a class map's disc does. _Superseded by R07.T8.e
    (`decision-r08-t11-frame.md` §2): the pass binds each record's tables, one dispatch a set of
    textures (plan 07's "Deviations in R07.T8.e and R07.T8.f, as built")._
  - _R07's shading called from one place_ (found by the smoke). With the lookups in it, SwiftShader,
    which inlines every call, lost its device compiling the disc's materials, whose `shade` was
    inlined six times (two `pixel_cells` sites in `disc_pixel`, three `add_sample` sites in
    `cell_sum`), and the disc-cells kernel took 4.7 s to compile with three. `cell_sum` now gathers
    its points first (`cell_samples`) and `disc_pixel` calls `pixel_cells` once, each draw's own
    count, the arithmetic and the order of every sum R07's; the kernel compiles in 1.7 s and R07's
    disc checks pass unchanged.
  - _The probe_ (`litBodyProbe.ts`): its `stubs` case is `hooks` (R11's ring-shadow stub, 1, and R08's
    two lookups at fixed arguments), and an `atmosphere` case evaluates any of the three lookups;
    the kernel composes `SURFACE_LIGHTING_WGSL` and declares the tables at group 0 bindings 5 to 11.
    `smoke/litBody.ts` binds the defaults and holds them to R07's 1, 1 and 0 exactly; R08.T9.b's
    group binds a body's stored tables (`probeSurfaceLighting`).
  - _The twin on demand._ T6.e's note had T9.b add the irradiance to `TwinBand`; it is built apart
    (`oblateIrradianceTwin`, `irradianceTwin`), since a table costs 4–9 s in the twin and the tests
    and groups that never read it should not pay for it.
  - _The tests' Saturn-class ratio._ The pole's diffuse irradiance at the datum under a zenith sun
    is 0.786, 0.813 and 0.900 of the equator's (r, g, b; ground albedo 0.3), against the bands'
    vertical columns' 0.754 (s_e ÷ s_p): thin, the sky's light goes as the column, and it saturates
    towards 1 as τ grows (0.16, 0.33, 0.84 at the equator). The test holds each between the
    columns' ratio and 1, in order of depth, red within 5% of the columns'. The task's "by the band
    tables' column ratio" is read as the thin limit the ratio tends to; the twin's reads above
    are the figure's.
  - _The unit tests' twin_ runs on small tables beneath (transmittance 64 × 16 at 128 steps,
    multiple scattering 16 × 16), so its figures are the quadrature's and the lookups', not the
    kernel sizes' (the smoke's twin is at the kernels' sizes).
  - _The smoke_ (`just test-render`, both variants): part 6 (new) holds `R08.T9.b surface lighting
on Earth` and `… on a Saturn-class figure`: every band and light slot's irradiance layer, as
    stored, against its twin over the GPU's own band tables and multiple scattering, and the three
    lookups at 216, 144 and 216 points (heights to 30 km on Earth and 300 km on the Saturn-class
    figure, latitudes 0°, 35°, 60° and 89°, sources from the zenith to 2° down, radii to 9.8°)
    through the probe with the stored tables bound, against `surfaceLightingTwin` over the GPU's
    slices and irradiance. Worst, against the twin: the irradiance 3 × 10⁻⁶ on Earth and in each
    of the Saturn-class figure's four bands; the lookups, sun, sky and wide source, 7 × 10⁻⁶,
    2 × 10⁻⁶ and 8 × 10⁻⁶ on Earth, 6.3 × 10⁻⁵ (the sun's, its fitted lookup), 2 × 10⁻⁶ and
    1.0 × 10⁻⁵ on the Saturn-class figure.
  - _The parts' times_ (2026-10-14, before the gate, at a load of 4 to 10; default / no
    subgroups): parts 2 to 5 took 97.6/98.2, 101.0/100.0, 92.5/95.1 and 104.0/105.0 s (T6.f's
    gate: 101–112 s at a load of 9–17). The lit materials, larger with `surfaceLighting.wgsl`, cost
    part 1 some 13 s of SwiftShader's compiling (its catalogue, R07.T9's meshes, R07.T8.b's class
    map), and a first gate at a load of 34 took it to 157 s against the 180 s watchdog, so
    R05.T12.c's frames (32–36 s) moved to part 6: part 1 then took 65.3/64.9 s and part 6 59.8/62.0 s (at a
    load of 5), R08.T9.b's groups 8.6–9.3 s (Earth) and 19.1–19.6 s (the Saturn-class figure).
    With the irradiance built with every set of tables, part 2 had taken 145 s at a load of 16
    (above).

- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)** (R08.T9.b). Recorded and deferred: each leaves the
  algorithm and every contract as they are.
  - _The irradiance's quadrature_ leaves up to 0.95% against a dense reference (8 × 6 nodes, 32
    steps), most of it the steps near the ground; R08.T13 checks the surface's irradiance against
    the reference, and 48 steps would take it to about 0.5% at 1.5 times the kernel's cost.
  - _A lobe narrower than the dust's._ The science check's Gaussian stand-ins for a phase peaked
    within a few degrees (2°, 3.5°, 5° wide) erred by −21% to +12% with the sun's height, the nodes
    aliasing on the peak, and Henyey–Greenstein g = 0.95 by −2.5%; the fixtures' tabulated phases
    are within 0.95%. If a medium brings such a lobe (large ice crystals), splitting the whole
    rings' piece at the lobe's reach, u = √(1 ÷ 6), took the 3.5° and 5° lobes to 0.6% and 0.5%.
  - _The sky between μ_s texels near the horizon_ (Bruneton's layout, which the task names): with
    2 ÷ 63 in μ_s a texel (1.8° there) and the twilight sky falling about 8 times in 2°, a linear
    read is up to about 50% high between texels; a column axis dense near μ_s = 0 would answer it.
  - _The rows above a haze._ The root axis leaves a pure 1.2 km haze's sky up to 39% high between
    the 1.8 and 4 km rows (at 3.2 km) and up to 100% between the 4 and 7.1 km rows (at 6.1 km),
    where it is 7% and 0.6% of the ground's (the science check, interpolating e^(−h ÷ 1.2 km) as the
    rows do, which matches the measured 37%, 55% and 61% at 3, 5 and 8 km); a Rayleigh air's sky
    dilutes it. R10's and R11's re-validation may ask more rows.
  - _Design note 7's figures for the rule_ hold along the vertical diameter. On the whole disc (the
    science check) the three nodes are +0.5% at 10° (the test's case, within its 2%), −3.5% at 5°
    (within the note's 4%) and +0.8% at 20° and τ = 1, where the note's "under 0.1%" is the
    diameter's.
  - _A partly set wide source._ The rule's top node is (√2 ÷ 2) ρ above the centre, so a source
    whose upper 0.29 ρ alone is up returns 0: about 2.9° of Jupiter's disc from Io.
  - _The ground's light under the sky_: Hillaire's multiple scattering takes the ground's one
    Lambertian bounce of the direct sun, so the light the ground and sky pass between them is
    missing: the sky's irradiance would be its one bounce's E₀ ÷ (1 − A S̄), S̄ the air's spherical
    albedo seen from below (the science check's estimate, about 0.18 at 440 nm on Earth's medium:
    some 2% at A = 0.1 in blue, 10–20% over snow); R08.T13 should hold a bright-ground case.
  - _A narrow umbra's sky._ A star's sky light takes the point's eclipse, right where the shadow is
    much wider than the air's reach (a moon in its planet's shadow, a ring's shadow). Under an umbra
    a few hundred kilometres wide (the Moon's on Earth, at most about 270 km), the air outside it
    lights the sky in totality to about twilight's levels, and the model gives none.
  - _A disc with an atmosphere skips the cells pass_, so a small disc with air shades its cells
    serially in its draws, as before R07.T8.d; one cells dispatch per set of tables is R08.T10.b's
    to add when bodies are drawn with air.
  - _The sky on a lunar-Lambert surface_ reflects on the mean A as a flat (Lambertian) term, R07's
    choice; the Lommel–Seeliger share's diffuse response is not modelled.
  - _The memory._ Each band's irradiance layer adds 16 KB a light slot, and the body's table
    272 B (36 → 53 texels): the Saturn-class figure's tables are 2,065,232 B at one slot, over
    R08.T6.f's 1,999,424 B; R08.T11's budget item.
  - _No disc is drawn with a body's tables yet._ No caller passes `LitBodyInput.atmosphere`: the
    smoke draws airless discs and holds the lookups through the probe. R08.T10.b passes
    `surfaceLightingTablesOf(tables)` each frame, adds one cells dispatch per set of tables, and
    is where a disc with air is first drawn and checked.
  - _A tilted surface._ The lookups take the datum normal's μ; Bruneton's (1 + n · up) ÷ 2 for a
    tilted normal, and R10's horizon, are the callers' (R10's `terrain_sky_factor`).
  - _The scale heights from the medium as given_ (with its forward deltas, the composite's), where
    the kernels read slice 0's delta-free column; the two part by under 10⁻³ of H on a medium with
    no forward delta.
  - _The cost on SwiftShader_: the irradiance's build is about 1.4 s a layer there, paid now only
    by the tables a lit pass reads (the parts' times above).

- **The per-view tables' range at twilight and by moonlight** (found 2026-10-10,
  `decision-r08-t6b-floor.md` §6; scheduled in T7; built and recorded by R08.T7, "Deviations in T7,
  as built").
  - _The finding._ R05's sky view, aerial volume and ray march store radiance per unit of the
    sun's illuminance in `rgba16float`, with no scale.
    - From typical clear-sky illuminances (estimated, not measured), Earth's mean twilight sky is
      about 8.5 × 10⁻⁶ sr⁻¹ at −6°, 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ at −8° and 2 × 10⁻⁸ at −12°. That is 143, 17 and
      0.3 of the half float's 2⁻²⁴ steps.
    - So the stored sky is banded from about −6° to −8° and black by nautical twilight, whatever
      the kernels compute. The multiple-scattering table's night side is the same (Earth's texel
      (13, 3) is 11 steps).
    - A moonlit sky kept per unit of the Sun's illuminance would be under one step.
  - _Why no check sees it._ The twin bound's floor passes such a table by construction.
    Verification records it as format-limited, and R08.T7's twilights and moonlit night, by hand,
    would show it.
  - _Lean, adopted 2026-10-10 and written into R08.T7's task._
    - The per-view tables are written per unit of a per-frame scale formed in `f64` (the drawn
      sources' sky scale, or the pre-exposure, as the composite's output is). The composite
      divides it out where `skyScale` multiplies today.
    - R08.T7 records its twilight and moonlit tables' largest values against 2⁻¹⁴.
    - The per-planet multiple-scattering table needs its own answer.
    - R08.T6.g's kernel arm already holds the kernels at every scale.
  - _Built by R08.T7_ (2026-10-13): the per-view tables are written per unit of the pre-exposure.
    At the metered exposure every table's largest lies far above 2⁻¹⁴, and the sky's least above
    the horizon at 149–329 × 2⁻¹⁴. The multiple-scattering table's answer is with "main" ("Deferred
    findings (2026-10-13 rule)", R08.T7).

- **Plan 14 produces no CH₄, O₂ or giant composition** (Design note 16). Titan-class haze, ozone and
  giants are fixture-only until P14.T24.c, d and f land. Biotic O₂ has no owner.
- **The stratosphere is provisional** (Design note 3). The skin is isothermal, with no ozone or
  haze heating, until R&C 2012's term follows P14.T24.c. Until P14.T24.e lands the isothermal seam
  stands, 3× wrong in scale height at Venus's cloud tops; the gate cannot catch it, because the
  reference traces the same column.
- **The medium ends at a hard top** (`decision-r08-t8-leans.md` §7, 2026-10-22). A column ends at
  p_s × 10⁻⁷ (Design note 3). R05's Earth ends at 100 km, at e^(−11.86) of its ground's density
  (Hillaire's and Bruneton's top). The air is cut there, not thinned, and nothing above it
  scatters. So the light of a real atmosphere's tail is missing in two places. One is the glow of
  the air over a camera near the top, which falls as √(top − h) to nothing at the top. The other
  is the limb's light at tangent heights near and over the top. By day it is about 10⁻⁶ of the
  limb's brightest. It shows at the camera's last light within about a scale height of the top,
  and on the deep-twilight limb, as 10⁻⁴ to a few 10⁻³ cd/m². That is the order of the airglow
  this plan does not draw. A thermosphere above the render column is the flight model's (Scope).
  There are two candidate fixes, for when that model arrives, or if a frame shows the cut by day
  or with the Sun more than 3° over the camera's visible horizon:
  - a tail: a top at p_s × 10⁻¹⁰, 6.9 scale heights higher, puts the cut about 10³ times fainter,
    below the night sky's own light;
  - a taper over the last one or two scale heights: the fade spreads over kilometres and the edge
    softens, at the cost of real air.

  Either moves the medium on which every R05 and R08 gate, table and reference is measured, and
  the march band (a share of the top, `decision-r08-t8-leans.md` §1). It is a medium task with
  its own re-measure, and no task owns it yet.

- **The bake's cost is an operation count, not a measurement.** If R08.T14 exceeds `BAKE_CEILING_S`,
  the fallback is a family of tables computed at development time. The research lean is that a
  family over (τ, ω, g, H/R) cannot represent a layered Venus, so it would need its own gate and
  probably a coarser claim.
- **Titan limb and low sun** may fail the pseudo-spherical gate by up to 8% (Loughman et al. 2004).
  The fallback for the failing geometries is a spherical Monte Carlo in the worker, with its noise
  and minutes of time.
- **H₂'s cross-section** (medium confidence): Peck and Huang's refractivity runs 6–7% above
  Dalgarno and Williams, a 6–7% difference in a giant's Rayleigh depth. Ford and Browne 1973 or a
  modern polarisability anisotropy would settle it. _Checked by R08.T3.b (2026-10-09):_ with Raj,
  Hamaguchi and Witek 2018's ab initio anisotropy in the King factor and the real-gas N, the
  module's H₂ runs 7.0% above Dalgarno and Williams (6.9% with the ideal N). Raj et al.'s own ᾱ
  gives a cross-section within 0.4% of the module's at 532 nm (a science check). Ford and Browne
  1973, or Raj et al.'s mean polarisability set against Peck and Huang, would test the
  refractivity itself.
- **Scalar radiance: decided 2026-10-09** (`decision-r08-vector.md` item 2). The error is
  corrected, not accepted.
  - **Measured:** R08.T12.a found −11.8% to +10.7% on Natraj's τ 0.5 case. The ruling's sweep
    found up to −18.7% and +11.9% at τ 0.5–1, and −5.2% to +4.6% in Earth's blue with aerosol.
  - **The correction:** R08.T14.e's 8-stream vector-minus-scalar table, read by R08.T14.f.
    From R08.T14.f on, every gate compares with the vector reference (Design note 10,
    Polarisation). Until then, the drawn sky carries the scalar error.
  - **Stated approximations:**
    - terms without a published matrix are total depolarisers;
    - planetshine is unpolarised;
    - Lambertian ground and decks depolarise;
    - the correction is plane-parallel with the pseudo-spherical beam, so its residual at
      twilight and the limb is the gate's to find;
    - fluxes and the surface irradiance are not corrected (under about 1%).
  - **Its costs**, which R08.T14.e–f measure: a sub-second bake a band, 0.20–0.39 MB a band,
    and three reads per sample per source.
- **Data licences: decided 2026-10-09** (delegated, `decision-r08-licences.md`, after
  `decisions-r05.md` item 4). No raw table is committed; the values R08 uses are committed
  reduced, with their citations in `NOTICE`:
  - methane from NASA PSG's conversion of Karkoschka and Tomasko 2010 (Elsevier's own image table
    is not used);
  - H₂SO₄, Mars dust and tholin from ARIA's, NASA Ames's and HITRAN's copies.

  NH₄SH takes a stated stand-in under `ATMOSPHERE: APPROXIMATE`. Benchmarks are committed as
  asserted values only. Serdyuchenko's data files (terms unstated) were ruled on 2026-10-02
  (`decisions-r05.md` item 4): no raw table, and R08.T4.b's reduced 1 nm table with its citation.
  The CIE matching functions (CC BY-SA 4.0) are read from R06's committed, checksum-verified
  copy. Values derived from them are committed with the CIE's citation, and `colourMatching.json`,
  their re-expression in Rec. 709, ships as adapted material under CC BY-SA 4.0 (decided
  2026-10-10, `decision-r08-cmf-licence.md`). `NOTICE` must ship in the app once packaging
  exists (`decisions-r05.md` item 4's packaging ask). GPL source may be read for a numerical method
  stated in full in the implementing file's doc, never ported: none of its statements, structure,
  names or comments enter the repository (`decision-r08-cmf-licence.md` §6, after
  decision-composition row 17).

- **Atomic line data: decided 2026-10-11** (`decision-r08-cmf-licence.md` §7).
  - NIST's Atomic Spectra Database is SRD 78. It is copyright under the Standard Reference Data
    Act (15 U.S.C. §290e) with "All rights reserved", and "None of our SRD may be reproduced …
    without prior permission".
  - That copyright covers ASD's compilation, not the facts in it (_Feist_; 17 U.S.C. §103(b)), so
    values derived from it would be lawful. But decision-composition §5's rule for NIST SRD
    (JANAF, CCCBDB, the WebBook) governs, and an open source exists. So ASD is a finding aid and
    a cross-check only, with at most a few values per species asserted in tests.
  - The T4.c bounds and T4.e's lines come from R. L. Kurucz's line lists, which state no terms:
    reduced values with citation, no raw file.
  - Where Kurucz lacks a line, the primary paper's value is used, cited to it.
  - A spectrum held by no source but ASD may take an ASD-derived bound, as a derived value with
    citation, listed here as a stated exception. Listed (R08.T4.c; accepted,
    `decision-r08-cmf-licence.md` §9.1): Ti⁺'s
    15 forbidden [Ti II] lines in the range, which Kurucz lacks and whose primary papers (Deb et
    al. 2009; Hartman et al. 2005) are closed, at ASD's values with citation, Ti⁺'s entry marked
    `estimated`. They lead its largest cell only at 300 K; from 1,000 K Kurucz's permitted lines
    lead. Listed (R08.T4.h, §4.1 of its brief, ruled 2026-10-19): Zn⁺'s transition probabilities
    for 7 of the 17 Zn II lines ASD lists over 350–800 nm (5p–7s, 5p–5d, 4d ²D₃/₂–4f and
    4d ²D₅/₂–4f ²F₇/₂), at ASD's values with citation, since Kurucz's `gf3001.all` holds no Zn II
    line in the range and their primary paper (Mayo, Ortiz and Campos 2006) is closed. Zn⁺'s
    entry is `estimated` on the bound its four lines without a found A take.
- **H₂–H₂ collision-induced absorption: decided 2026-10-11** (`decision-r08-cmf-licence.md` §8).
  - Borysow 2002's tables (A&A 390, 779), 60–1,000 K to about 16,500 cm⁻¹, are used as reduced
    values with citation: 1 nm cell means in `crossSections.json`. The raw files are not
    committed.
  - Her page reads "All rights reserved" but offers the tables for use, asking for a citation.
  - No open source reaches the range: HITRAN's H₂–H₂ ends at 10,000 cm⁻¹. So decision-composition
    §5's stricter NIST rule, which needs an open alternative, does not apply.
  - The article prints no table and there is no CDS deposit.
  - The same holds for Borysow, Jørgensen and Fu 2001's 1,000–7,000 K table, which T4.c uses
    above 1,000 K.
  - Below each table's end (607 nm to 350 K, 589 nm to 1,000 K and 501 nm above) the pair is 0,
    as a stated approximation.
- **H₂O's visible continuum: decided 2026-10-12** (`decision-r08-t4d-kdist.md` §6).
  - MT_CKD's netCDF and code are granted "for scientific and research purposes only", and "may
    not be incorporated into … commercial software or data offered for sale without the express
    written consent of AER". That is a non-commercial licence reaching modified versions, so
    MT_CKD is not an input in any form.
  - The continuum is CKD's, from LOWTRAN 7's tables. It is `measured` from 567 nm with air over
    260–296 K. Its residuals against the visible measurements:
    - 1.25 times Tikhomirov et al. 2006's (2.2 ± 0.7) × 10⁻²⁶ cm² at 694 nm, inside 1σ;
    - "good agreement" in the 720 nm band (Sierk et al. 2004, as Daniel et al. 2004 report it);
    - "same order of magnitude" at 590 and 650 nm (Lotter 2006).
  - No visible window has been measured.
  - Below 567 nm the continuum is CKD's ratio carried onto HITRAN2024's lines, `estimated`. Earth
    therefore carries `ATMOSPHERE: APPROXIMATE` under R08.T10.a until a measurement or a published
    model covers 380–567 nm.
  - CKD_2.4.1 (Sierk's comparison) is taken to equal CKD_2.4 in the visible. RRTMG_SW confirms
    CKD_2.4's equality with LOWTRAN's tables over 12,850–16,000 cm⁻¹.
- **Venus's ultraviolet absorber is an empirical stand-in** (science-r08-unowned-absorbers).
  - Its identity is unknown: FeCl₃, S₂O/OSSO, Sₓ and organics each fail a constraint. So every
    case-1 deck's mode 2 carries `acid_uv_absorber`, Venus's absorption fitted to its 365 nm
    albedo and g′/r′ colour, and is labelled.
  - **Not modelled:**
    - its markings (Lee et al. 2022 see more than 20% peak-to-peak at 365 nm);
    - its factor-2 decadal change and its latitude dependence (Lee et al. 2019);
    - its 283 nm side;
    - any dependence on a world's chemistry.
  - The absorbed-energy share is recorded, not matched.
- **Trace heavy elements are not carried** (science-r08-unowned-absorbers). Li, Sc, Co, Sr, Y and
  Ba lie outside plan 14's `Element`.
  - At a 0.1 bar upper-bound column their lines change an ultra-hot dayside's transmitted sunlight
    by up to Δu′v′ 1.7 × 10⁻³ and 3% in luminance together.
  - At a 10 mbar photosphere the change is 2.3 × 10⁻⁴ and 0.6%.
  - They are P14.T55.l.
  - Lava worlds' vapour waits on P14.T55.b.

- **Stars beyond the body's two** (decided 2026-10-09, `decision-r08-design.md` item 3). The sky
  takes the body's own list (Design note 7), so it agrees with the surfaces by construction. A
  third or fourth star past `STAR_CUT_RELATIVE` lights neither: it is unseen by day, and it is a
  night under a visible star while the two brightest are set. Two corrections to R07 are deferred
  (main's deferred list, for R12's audit):
  - `MAX_BODY_LIGHTS` per setting, 4 on high and 2 on low, which this plan's kernels already hold
    (`MAX_SKY_SOURCES` = 6);
  - for the camera's local body inside its air, Design note 7's twilight limit applied before the
    cap, so that a set star yields its slot to one that is up.

  Whether a dropped star that is up needs an annunciation is for R12's audit.

- **Planetshine's approximations** (Design note 7; decided 2026-10-09, `decision-r08-design.md`
  item 2). A planetshine source lights surfaces and the sky as a star does. Five things are not
  modelled:
  - the neighbour's own band depletion: a giant's methane seen through a Titan-class air's
    methane, where light slot 0's curve reads the absorption somewhat too deep;
  - its disc in the sky's phase function (a point at its centre, under 0.8% for Rayleigh at
    ρ = 9.8°);
  - a partly set source's sky, lit or shadowed by its centre;
  - the inverse square across the body in the march (±0.9% at Io);
  - R07's own stated errors (the crescent's centroid, the far-field E).

  The low setting's sky may take three sources (2 + 1) in a multiple system's twilight with a moon
  up. R08.T11 records it, and if the budget misses there, the low sky drops planetshine while a
  star lies within the twilight limit, recorded.

- **Which star's absorber curve the shared tables are built with: decided 2026-10-10**
  (`decision-r08-t6b-floor.md` §8; `decision-r08-design.md`, adjacent finding 3).
  - R08.T6.c builds the multiple-scattering table with light slot 0's curves, which is exact while
    one sun is drawn.
  - From R08.T7, under a medium with an absorber, the multiple-scattering and irradiance tables have
    one layer per light slot, each built with its own star's curves. Each sun's transmittance,
    view-path absorber depth and disc take its own curves. Planetshine takes slot 0's.
  - The error avoided is the companion's. Its curves differ from a K5 primary's by 2.2% (red, 10 ×
    300 DU of ozone) to 8.3% (30 ×) for an M3 companion, and by 3.9% to 15.5% from a G2 primary's.
    This matters where it lights the sky alone: a circumbinary world's companion after the primary
    sets, or an S-type companion at night.
  - Cost: 8 KB and under 0.1 ms a layer, per planet, never per frame.
  - _Built by R08.T7_ (2026-10-13) for the multiple-scattering table, the transmittances, the view
    paths and the discs; the irradiance table's layers are R08.T9.b's.
- **`atmosphere_sun_transmittance`'s fifth argument** (`decision-r08-design.md` item 2 and
  adjacent finding 1). R08.T9.b gives it `curve : u32`, the light's absorber-curve slot, and adds
  `atmosphere_source_transmittance` for planetshine (Provides, "Tables and passes"). R10's plan
  still names the four-argument form (its Consumes, for R10.T10.b's `terrainLit.wgsl`), as R11's
  does. R10's re-validation must pick up the fifth argument, `curve`.
  `atmosphere_sky_irradiance` gains the same `curve : u32` as a fourth argument
  (`decision-r08-t6b-floor.md` §8), which R10's and R11's re-validations pick up with it.
- **Refraction and scintillation are not drawn.** On Venus, refraction near the surface raises the
  horizon; R06 leaves scintillation to this plan, and the brainstorm asks for neither. If the
  realism ruling wants them, they are later tasks. R10 asks this plan for the sun's refracted
  apparent elevation for its shadow test (R10 Design note 10). The ask stays open until refraction
  is drawn; until then R10 reads the geometric elevation.
- **Io's sodium cloud and eclipse glows are not drawn** (`signoff-2.md`, "For main", 2026-10-10).
  An Io is `Tenuous` under P14.T53.c, not airless, so it is drawn with its gases and is outside
  the `EXOSPHERE: NOT YET MODELLED` note (Design note 12). Its sodium cloud and its eclipse glows,
  which Galileo's broadband solid-state imager recorded above 300 kR (Geissler et al. 1999,
  Science 285, 870), are another light the console does not draw: no medium term carries a line's
  resonance or emission light. No note names them today; whether a `Tenuous` body's unmodelled
  light takes one is open, for "main", and a resonance term is a later task's, with P14.T55.c's
  exosphere by species.
- **The metric's floor** (decided, decision-backlog-1, 2026-10-09).
  - The gate is |ΔL| ≤ max(0.05·L_ref, 3 × 10⁻⁴·L_max(image)) + 4σ_ref, with σ_ref ≤ T ÷ 8
    (Design note 10).
  - It replaces max(0.05·L_ref, 3σ_ref, 10⁻³·L_max(case)), which had three faults:
    - its floor took over from the 5% below 2% of the case's brightest, not 10⁻³ as this bullet
      said;
    - over the whole case, a twilight image's sky fell under the noon image's floor;
    - its 3σ term gave no noise allowance where the 5% governed.
  - The 5% is in radiance, so that it holds at every exposure. Through AgX at the automatic
    exposure it is at most about one just-noticeable difference (0.96 ΔL*).
  - The 2% aggregates stand.
  - A regime whose table cannot reach the gate stays `ATMOSPHERE: APPROXIMATE`. The gate is not
    loosened for it.
  - _The guide row_ (`docs/frontend/ux-guidelines.md`, `ATMOSPHERE: APPROXIMATE`) names the
    check's figure, decision-backlog-1 §2.6 (f)'s clause "agreement within 5% in radiance wherever
    in the view a difference could be seen", applied in the composition ruling's docs pass
    (2026-10-09).
    The row had been signed off by then and carries no draft trailer, so §2.6 (f)'s trailer is not
    added: the figure stands signed off by decision-backlog-1, under the owner's delegation.
- **Licences no longer block the cloudy gates** (decided 2026-10-09, `decision-r08-licences.md`).
  The Venus-class cloudy case, Mars and the Titan-class haze gate as R08.T5.b's files land, and
  are drawn `ATMOSPHERE: APPROXIMATE` only until their gates pass. NH₄SH alone stays ungated: a
  stand-in index, the label, and no committed case, until visible optical constants are
  published. If a source is withdrawn, the earlier lean stands, with its own physics check: a
  published parameterisation cited without copying the table, that is a constant index with a
  published Cauchy slope, or a Henyey–Greenstein pair fitted in the paper.
- **Non-spherical optics** (researched 2026-10-10, science-r08-nonspherical.md).
  - **Minerals.** TAMUdust2020's hexahedra reproduce a Martian analogue's measured matrix in
    shape and sign, but they run 20–37% low at side and back angles (Martikainen et al. 2025).
    Spheres misplace that light by factors of 2–3, and Henyey–Greenstein by 2–4.
  - **Other ices.** They are drawn on water ice's roughened table. Their g is expected to run
    high by up to 0.056 (NH₃; van Diedenhoven et al. 2014, eq. 16), and they stay labelled until
    their phase functions are measured. NH₄SH's n of 1.638 lies past the fit's 1.18–1.43, where
    eq. (16) would put its g about 0.10 high (Δg ≈ −0.10), the largest of all; it is left
    unestimated as an extrapolation
    (R08.T5.c's science check).
  - **Enstatite** (Frattin et al. 2019) is the one weakly absorbing crystalline silicate measured.
    On its own index and sizes, the hexahedra's residual at side and back angles is recorded in
    R08.T5.c's as-built notes. A residual above a factor of 1.5 that survives the iron-matched
    index is a known limit of smooth, homogeneous hexahedra for transparent silicates, and not a
    tuning target. The class's sphericity stays 0.71.
  - **Transparent high-index grains** larger than the floor rule allows keep the
    Henyey–Greenstein fallback.
  - **Downloads.** The kernels are a one-off 7.9 GB and 27 GB, offline.
  - **Owner access items:** Tomasko et al. 1999's phase-function parameters, Wolff et al. 2010's
    ultraviolet indices, Howett et al. 2007's full text, and Clancy et al. 2003.
  - **Signed off 2026-10-10** (`signoff-2.md` item 5; science-r08-nonspherical.md §5, items 1
    and 2; built as T5.c's two constants, `decision-r08-aerosol-labels.md` item 2):
    - a validated model with known residuals, such as the hexahedra above, stays unlabelled
      (`model`) with its residuals recorded here, as Mie does for spheres;
    - every analogue is labelled, CH₄ ice's (estimated Δg −0.007) included, with no exemption by
      estimated bias.
  - **For plan 14** (science-r08-nonspherical.md §6.4, for "main" to route):
    - P14.T24.c: iron's shape class follows its phase. A liquid droplet is a `sphere`, and a solid
      grain a `nonSphericalMineral` (Visscher et al. 2010).
    - P14.T49.e: κ_ext for `nonSphericalMineral` and `crystal` modes is read from R08.T5.c's
      tables' C_ext, not from sphere Mie, so that the sim's mass extinction and the client's
      optics agree.
    - P14.T24.c (science-r08-mmf.md §2.5): a mode's r_eff and v_eff are the moments of the
      volume-to-area radius r = 3V ÷ 4A, A the orientation-averaged projected area, for every
      shape class, so r_eff = (3 ÷ 4)⟨V⟩ ÷ ⟨A⟩ and τ(550) = (3 ÷ 4) Q̄_ext(550) M ÷ (ρ r_eff). A
      size from visible scattering is converted on the way in at equal projected area
      (r = Ψ^(3/2) r_A), and one fixed by mass or absorption at equal V/A.
  - _The MMF past x₀ ≈ 0.5_ (science-r08-mmf.md). The mean field's pair correlation has no
    contact peak, so for monomers above x₀ ≈ 0.5 it overestimates C_ext and C_sca near x₀ ≈ 0.6,
    most for D_f ≈ 1.9 (Rannou, Botet and Tazaki 2024, Icarus 424, 116247). In their Titan case ω
    is about 0.04 high at 400 nm, and the backscatter tail is off at short wavelengths
    (Seignovert et al. 2017).
    - This covers the Titan-like aggregate from 380 to about 630 nm, within Tazaki and Tanaka's
      stated 20–25% in opacity. Its blue is an `analogue` by Design note 6.
    - The published repair (MFT-M+, a Dirac contact peak) has no reference implementation in
      optool and is not adopted.
    - The DISR phase functions (Tomasko et al. 2008; Doose et al. 2016) are closed and specific to
      Titan. They are an owner access item, for an optional test only.
  - _The MMF below D_f 1.9_ (R08.T5.c's science check; ruled 2026-10-10,
    `decision-r08-aerosol-labels.md` item 1). Tazaki and Tanaka 2018 compare the MMF with
    T-matrix results at D_f 1.9 and 3.0 only. Those are test points, not a stated range: the
    model's stated condition is (9)'s phase shift, which `aggregate.ts` applies at every D_f it
    accepts (1 < D_f ≤ 2.5), as optool does above 1. Below D_f 2 the multiple scattering a mean
    field can miss does not grow with N (Berry and Percival 1986; Tazaki et al. 2016 §4.1.4;
    Tazaki and Tanaka's Appendix C), and (9)'s aggregate term falls as the aggregate grows.
    Tazaki 2021's geometric cross-section holds within 5% for linear chains under the Gaussian
    cut-off.
    - One optical check exists below 1.9, against the discrete dipole approximation for soot over
      0.2–15 µm (Lodge, Wakeford and Leinhardt 2024, MNRAS, DOI 10.1093/mnras/stad3743, Table 2).
      On a linear branched aggregate of D_f 1.81 the MMF's g is within 4.5% on average, against
      15.4% for a compact cluster of D_f 2.53, and its cross-sections within 24–27%, as at D_f 2.5
      (19–26%).
    - So such a mode is a `model` inside (9)'s gate and unlabelled. Its residuals are recorded
      here, as the hexahedra's are (`signoff-2.md`, item 5a).
    - No optical comparison exists below D_f 1.8. The contact-peak error above (x₀ ≈ 0.5) applies
      there as at D_f 2.
    - _Caveats_ (the science check of the commit that applied the ruling, 2026-10-10; added beside
      the ruled text, for "main"):
      - Lodge et al.'s errors are means in log λ (MNRAS 527, 11113), with Botet et al. 1995's
        fractal-dimension cut-off, not the Gaussian. Their monomers (R_mie 0.5 µm over N 76,
        a₀ ≈ 0.12 µm, x₀ ≈ 1.4 at 540 nm) put the visible part of the comparison past (9)'s gate.
      - Where single scattering dominates, well inside the gate, the mean field coincides with
        Rayleigh–Gans–Debye theory (Tazaki and Tanaka's Appendix C). That limit agrees with an
        exact volume-integral method to 10% or better in scattering and absorption for soot-like
        aggregates of D_f 1.7–1.8 (m 1.57 + 0.57i, N 16–256, ka 0.1–0.4; Farias et al. 1995,
        J. Heat Transfer 117, 152, and 1996a, J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transfer 55, 357, as
        reviewed by C. M. Sorensen, Aerosol Sci. Technol. 35 (2001) 648–687). "No optical
        comparison" above means none of the MMF itself.
      - An aggregate whose monomers fail Tazaki and Tanaka's condition (7), with |m − 1| ≥ 2, is
        an `analogue` even inside (9)'s gate (science-r08-mmf.md §4). Soot and tholin meet (7).
        Metallic iron fails it at every visible wavelength, and chromium and graphite's E ⊥ c
        component would fail it as monomers.
- **M-dwarf suns.** A curve of growth weighted by a 15-sample spectrum is adequate for FGK, A and B
  stars, but not for M dwarfs. Their TiO bands at 590–630 and 705–760 nm overlap Chappuis and
  methane's 727 nm band, so the weight correlates with σ (Design note 5). This is a recorded
  limitation. The lean is that R06 supply a model spectrum at 1 nm for M stars (for example
  PHOENIX, Husser et al. 2013, A&A 553, A6). The ask is made and open (the roadmap's between-plans
  table; R06's Risks), outside R06's scope and waiting on the stellar libraries' licence ruling;
  until then the 15-bin interpolation stands for M stars and the limitation is recorded with them.
- **Titan's skin temperature.** Design note 3's Titan check takes T_skin = 64 K. A T_eq of
  83.5 K, from a Bond albedo of 0.265, would give T_skin 70 K and a tropopause at 0.40 bar,
  outside P14.T24.e's test. Where plan 14's Titan T_eq comes from is to be re-checked when
  P14.T24.e is built. _Checked by R08.T1 (2026-10-09), computed:_ plan 14's Titan is a snowball,
  Bond albedo 0.50, placed at 9.583 au with e 0.0565 (its Solar System table), so its T_eq is
  about 75.6 K and T_skin 63.6 K, which puts the tropopause near 0.24 bar inside the test. A change
  of the snowball's albedo moves it, and P14.T24.e's test says so.
- **The summed sky-view** (Design note 7) is a research lean of medium confidence, not checked
  against Hillaire's parameterisation. R08.T7 tests it, and the per-sun fallback costs 0.43 MB a
  sun a view. _Checked by R08.T7_ (2026-10-13) against R05's sun-relative per-source tables
  within 10° of each source: within 2.0 × 10⁻³ on both settings ("Deviations in T7, as built").
- **The forward delta in the direct beam** (decided 2026-10-10, `decision-r08-aerosol-labels.md`
  item 3; Design note 6). The client draws the light of a table's forward delta at the source.
  - Its total is the delta's scattering depth f_c τ_sca, sized to the source's g by R08.T5.c:
    about 4% of the scattering for cirrus of r_eff 30 µm, 12% for dust of r_eff 30 µm, and up to
    about 40% for crystals near a table's largest size.
  - Physically it lies within the files' first angle (0.05° for Yang et al., 0.08° for
    TAMUdust2020), inside the disc of a Sun-like star out to about 3–6 au and just beyond it
    farther out. There the console draws it into the star's point, a displacement of about 2.6
    pixels at the default 60° on a 1,920-pixel-wide view and up to about 31 at 10° on a
    3,840-pixel-wide one, far finer than the sky-view's own 1.9° (2.8° on low).
  - It is the tables' angular resolution, not a substitute, so it carries no label.
  - R08.T12.b writes its cases from the full medium, delta included, so the reference keeps it as
    scattering. The two differ only in the direct beam (the client's e^(−τ + f_c τ_sca) against
    Beer–Lambert) and within 0.08° of a sun, which R08.T13's comparisons leave out or add back.
  - Restoring the aureole's shape (Fraunhofer diffraction of the mode's projected areas) would be
    a separate pass. It is not planned.
- **The reference in `hyperion-fit`** is a new kind of output for that crate. If plan 15's owners
  prefer, it moves to a sibling offline tool, and nothing else changes.
- **Knowledge.** Until a sensors plan builds the body-level overlay, the server grants the detail
  level asked, so `ATMOSPHERE: NOT RESOLVED` is exercised only by tests and by requests that ask for
  less.
- **CPU budgets on the desktop, decided 2026-09-30 by a delegated decision** (the hardware
  decisions, item 3). `BAKE_CEILING_S`, 5 s a world, stays the UHD 620 laptop's figure, the
  minimum specification. The development machine (Ryzen 7 3700X) records its own bake time beside
  it and fails only if it is over the laptop's ceiling; no separate desktop ceiling is set.
- **The asks R08.T1 wrote into plan 14** (2026-10-09, at `62c196c3`). P14.T24.c–f sit under
  plan 14's Phase E and P14.T35.e under Phase H, each marked drafted for the owner. **Accepted
  with amendments** 2026-10-10 by the sign-off agent under the owner's delegation (`signoff-3.md`,
  items 1.1–1.8); the client is built to them. They were reconciled
  with R09.T0.a's five asks (plan 14's Phase K, P14.T48.a–e), and the reconciliation is in plan
  14's Risks too ("The rendering plans' asks of the surface section"). What departs from T1's
  bullets:
  - _One record section, one wire task._ P14.T48.e (R09's) defines the record's surface section;
    T24.e and T24.c add their members to it. P14.T35.e is "The surface section and the gas envelope
    on the wire": the whole section mirrored member for member, which R10 and R11 also read, not
    only the atmosphere's fields. Its members for T24.c–e and T24.d are declared
    from the start and absent until their tasks land (plan 14's T34 rule), which this plan reads as
    not modelled: `AEROSOLS AND ABSORBERS: NOT YET MODELLED` and the isothermal seam.
  - _Field by field, where the two plans' asks met:_
    - T_s and p_s are P14.T24.a's, read by T24.e's profile and by T48.c's crater screening. The
      wire's vertical structure carries β and T_skin alone, so R08.T3.a's `radiativeConvective`
      takes `surfaceK` and `surfacePa` from the conditions.
    - The gravity is the bulk section's, which T24.a and T48.c both read; nothing repeats it.
    - The gases are T24.a's mole fractions, a list largest first summing to 1 to 10⁻⁹, which
      R08.T3.c's refusal assumes; T24.f fills CH₄ and O₂ and defines no field. Methane as an
      absorber is its gas fraction, so R08.T10.a builds methane's absorber term from that fraction
      and the column, and ozone's from T24.c's absorbers. That still draws methane only from plan
      14's inventory (Design note 12).
    - The condensing species is P14.T48.d's condensable, which T24.e's α reads (water 0.6, methane
      0.77, CO₂ or none 0.8), so the picture's lapse rate and R09's climate model agree.
    - T24.c's decks lie on T13.c's one saturation curve per species, with the vapour set at the
      ground by a surface relative humidity (from memory, for the builder), and each deck gives
      its vapour's cold-trap fraction above it, which R08.T10.a reads for the vapour's column there.
    - T24.c's dust reads plan 14's own figures, never R09's coarse wind, which reads the section (a
      cycle otherwise); R10's `Dust` class still follows R09's winds locally.
  - _The order:_ T24.f; then T24.a–b with P14.T48.a–e; then T35.e; then T24.e, then T24.c; T24.d
    beside any of them.
  - _The gas envelope_ (decision-r08-giant-label, finding F1). T24.d serves every body in the
    gas-envelope state, giants and sub-Neptunes alike (every sub-Neptune is one by construction),
    and such a body's surface section is `not_applicable` (P14.T48.e as reconciled). Design note
    13's "Giants inside 10⁹ m" and R08.T16 are written for giants alone. Once P14.T24.d lands they
    read every gas-envelope body, a sub-Neptune's visible atmosphere being its envelope and its
    deck the surface; the labels hold either way (that ruling). The envelope's profile is the
    `Envelope` variant of plan 14's `VerticalStructure`, so R08.T16.a gives `TemperatureProfile` a
    matching variant. T24.d gains H₂O for its deck; H₂S is the envelope's own species.
  - _Findings for this plan._ Plan 14 tracked no sulphur. A science agent has since drafted
    P14.T24.g (`science-r08-sulphur-co2ice.md`, 2026-10-09; amended 2026-10-10, `signoff-3.md`
    item 1.6).
    - It gives a runaway-greenhouse world a sulphuric-acid deck of four modes. On plan 14's Venus
      the deck lies at 1.34–0.04 bar with τ(550) 33, so this plan classifies it `cloudDeck` and
      R11's boundary leaves it here.
    - It gives a temperate world a stratospheric sulphate layer of τ about 0.003.
    - It adds SO₂ as an absorber. This plan draws no SO₂ term until a cross-section is ruled: its
      weak band near the violet edge is from memory, check at build.
    - A deck's modes carry their deck, and Design note 9's per-body rule sums them.

    CO₂ ice now has a derived index file in R08.T5.b: Warren 1986's real index as a Cauchy fit,
    and Hansen 2005's k. The Titan check of Design note 3 holds on plan 14's albedo (the Titan
    bullet above).

  - _Marked "from memory" in plan 14_, for the builder: the surface relative humidity, Ackerman and
    Marley's closed form, Mars's background dust, Niemann et al.'s 5.65%, the protosolar He/H₂, a
    sub-Neptune's metallicity, Sudarsky's class temperatures and Venus's trace of O₂.
