- **Deviations in T12.a, as built** (2026-10-09; `crates/hyperion-fit/src/atmosphere/`, the
  `atmosphere-reference` command in `cli.rs`, `RunFitError` in `lib.rs`).
  - _Signatures._ `trace_reference` returns `Result<ReferenceRadiances, TraceReferenceError>`: the
    thread pool can fail (`ThreadPool`), the Stokes mode refuses a term it has no matrix for
    (`StokesNeedsRayleigh`, a Cornette–Shanks term), and `samples` is capped at `MAX_SAMPLES` = 2⁵³
    so that every count is an exact `f64` (`TooManySamples`). `RunFitError` gains
    `AtmosphereCase` (exit 1), `AtmosphereReference` (exit 2 for `StokesNeedsRayleigh` and
    `TooManySamples`, bad command lines; 1 otherwise) and `WriteReference { path, source }` (exit
    1). The command's arguments are a clap `Args` struct, `AtmosphereReferenceArgs`, in a tuple
    variant; `--samples` defaults to 100,000 per geometry, aggregate and wavelength, and
    `--threads` resolves as `orbits`'s does. The fit crate's `clippy.toml` gains `LeVeque` in
    `doc-valid-idents` (Chan, Golub and LeVeque 1979, the moments' merge).
  - _The case format (`CASE_FORMAT` 1) is T12.a's reader's_ (`case.rs`'s module documentation), so
    T12.b's "builds the case format" now reads as the client's writer of it. Names are the client's
    camel case and unknown fields are refused, inside the tagged kinds too. Terms are the client's
    `MediumTerm` with every per-channel array one entry per traced wavelength, without `absorber` or
    `spectral`; there may be any number of them, each from data, so the medium names no species.
    Densities: `exponential`, `tent` and `tabulated`, the last linear in relative density between
    nodes and constant beyond the end nodes, a negative height reading as the ground; **T3.a's
    `densityAt` for `tabulated` must follow the same rule**, or the gate counts the difference as
    the client's error. Phases: `rayleigh` (ρ per wavelength), `cornette-shanks` (`asymmetry`),
    `isotropic` (added, for the Stokes test and the benchmarks) and `none`. Suns are spectral
    irradiances normal to the beam at the top. A geometry is an observer (height, latitude), a view
    (zenith, azimuth from north towards east), one direction per sun, an optional `maxDistanceM`
    (a black target, for aerial perspective) and an optional cone; aggregates are a latitude and
    sun directions; an optional `seed` defaults to 0. Cones of 0°–10° are accepted, 0° for the
    analytic tests and point benchmarks; Design note 10's 0.5°–1° is the cases' to choose. At most
    65,536 wavelengths, and fewer than 2³² geometries and aggregates each, which the draws' keys
    pack.
  - _The tabulated phase function is not read yet._ R08.T12.c adds the one its benchmarks need
    (Garcia and Siewert's Legendre series; Kokhanovsky's and IPRT's tables) before it runs, since it
    precedes T12.b; T12.b then reads T5's `PhaseTable` (u = √(θ/π)) through it.
  - _Output (`REFERENCE_FORMAT` 1)._ One `samples`, `seed` and `polarisation` for the whole
    reference, not samples per geometry. Each geometry adds `sunOpticalDepth` per sun and
    wavelength (`null` where the ground hides the sun), the direct beam for Design note 10's
    Beer–Lambert check, and in the Stokes mode Q and U with their errors. Each aggregate gives
    `incidentTop`, `directGround`, `diffuseGround` and `upwellingTop` (the last two with errors):
    the downwelling flux is direct plus diffuse, the plane albedo upwelling over incident. Q and U
    are in the frame e₁ in the view's vertical plane, e₂ = k × e₁ for the light's direction k;
    Natraj et al. 2009 tabulate −Q and −U of these at the same relative azimuth (their Q = Iᵣ − Iₗ).
    `to_json` is `serde_json`'s pretty form, which `prettier --check` would reflow: T12.b formats
    the committed references for it or lists them in `.prettierignore`.
  - _The estimator._ Absorption is a weight (quadrature, so an absorbing-only medium gives
    Beer–Lambert exactly); free paths by delta tracking against per-shell majorants, so T12.d
    changes only the shells and the majorant (and, as built, where the detector and the aggregates
    stand and the ground's normal: "Deviations in T12.d, as built"); the first collision on the
    view ray is forced;
    next-event estimation to every sun integrates the transmittance by 8-point Gauss–Legendre per
    shell; the ground is Lambertian; Russian roulette below 0.1 of each branch's starting weight
    (an absolute threshold left a 10 H limb's multiple scattering at 8% noise, against 0.3%
    now). Shells split at every profile kink and every scale height, to 36 H.
  - _Reproducibility._ `Draws` is reused from `tasks/displaced_forms/births.rs`, not copied, with
    the case's seed XORed with `ATMOSPHERE_STREAM` so that its streams are its own; a sample's key
    is (wavelength, geometry or aggregate by its own index, sample), so adding a geometry leaves
    the others' draws alone (tested). Blocks of 1,024 samples run through `map_reduce_chunks` with
    chunk 1. `atmosphere_reference_bits_are_pinned` pins two values to the bit: an edit to `Draws`
    (P15's to make), `Gl16Panel`, `bisect` or the Gauss–Legendre tables shows there before it moves
    a committed reference. Moving `Draws` to a shared module is plan 15's change, later.
  - _Tests_ beyond the three named: single scattering in a thin slab (to 10⁻⁴), Rayleigh's degree
    and plane of polarisation, energy conservation over black and white ground, a grazing optical
    depth against a fine quadrature (10⁻¹⁰), two suns adding, case validation, phase normalisation
    and sampling, shell walks, moments, frames and cones, and the command line. The
    Stokes-equals-scalar test holds I to 10⁻¹² relative, not bit for bit: the Stokes mode mixes the
    terms' matrices, which rounds differently from the scalar mixture.
  - _Cost, provisional_ (shared load 8–9 on 16 threads, the dev profile at `opt-level` 2, 4 threads
    under a 400% CPU quota): about 9 µs a path on the τ = 0.5 Rayleigh slab and 107 µs on an
    Earth-like case of three terms (Rayleigh, a Cornette–Shanks aerosol and an ozone tent; about 50
    shells), where the quadrature of each sun's transmittance dominates. A twilight ground view
    (sun at 95°) is noisy, about 4–7% at 2 × 10⁴ samples, since few forced collisions see the sun.
    Under Design note 10's metric (decision-backlog-1) that image is held to its own brightest
    radiance, and σ_ref ≤ T ÷ 8 binds at every geometry, so T12.b traces such views until it holds
    and budgets their samples. (This note first cited the superseded floor, 10⁻² L_max of the case,
    under which σ_ref ≤ 1% did not bind.)
  - _Citations, decided 2026-10-09_ (`decision-r08-vector.md` item 3).
    - Hansen and Travis 1974's matrix is eq. (2.15), with Δ and Δ′ in eq. (2.16), p. 541; their
      δ is the code's ρ.
    - Witt 1977's Henyey–Greenstein inverse CDF is eq. (19). The "eq. 13" cited is the forced
      first collision's.
    - Cornette and Shanks 1992's number is unreadable (every copy is paywalled), so it is cited
      by DOI without one, beside Draine 2003's eq. (5) at α = 1.
    - R08.T12.c's commit corrects `optics.rs` and `case.rs`.
- **The scalar against the vector Rayleigh radiance, measured in R08.T12.a** (2026-10-09; a
  finding, for a decision agent's sign-off through "main"). The case: Natraj, Li and Yung 2009
  (ApJ 691, 1909), τ = 0.5, μ₀ = 0.2, A = 0, ρ = 0, πF₀ = π, diffuse radiance only, as a
  plane-parallel slab (1 km of uniform Rayleigh scatterer on a sphere of radius 10¹² m, a pencil
  detector), at the top (upwelling) and bottom (downwelling) for μ = 0.1, 0.2, 0.52, 0.84 and 1 and
  relative azimuth 0°, 90° and 180°: 26 geometries, 10⁶ samples each, seed 0, 4 threads, 58 s per
  mode at load 8–9. The case's generator is in the lane's handoff for T12.c.
  - The Stokes mode reproduces Natraj's Tables 1–2 (read from the paper by the science check) within
    3σ at all 26 geometries (largest 2.98σ, χ² = 28.1 for 26; independent runs at seed 1 and before
    the review's re-keying gave largest 2.12σ and 1.81σ), σ ≤ 0.17%, and the degree of
    polarisation to about 0.001.
  - Scalar minus vector, on the same paths: −11.8% at the bottom, μ = 0.1, towards the sun's
    azimuth, −10.8% at μ = 0.1 away from it, and −10.4% and −8.7% at μ = 0.2; +10.0% at the top's
    nadir and +10.7% at the bottom's zenith; at 90° in azimuth within 0.4% for μ ≤ 0.2, +2.0% to
    +2.5% at μ = 0.52 and +6.6% to +7.2% at μ = 0.84. An independent scalar adding–doubling by the
    science check gives −11.79% to +10.75%, and the literature has errors "as large as 10%" for pure
    Rayleigh (Lacis et al. 1998, GRL 25, 135; Kotchenova et al. 2006, Appl. Opt. 45, 6762).
  - _Decided 2026-10-09 (`decision-r08-vector.md`)._
    - The error is corrected, not accepted: R08.T14.e–f, with the gates against the vector
      reference from R08.T14.f on (item 2).
    - The Stokes mode gains tabulated block-diagonal matrices (a₁–a₄, b₁, b₂), the Stokes vector
      (I, Q, U, V), a `depolarising` mark and the scalar I of the same paths, in R08.T12.c (item
      1).
    - The equation numbers are settled under "Deviations in T12.a, as built" (item 3).
- **Closed set, for the composition audit (R08.T12.a).** The tracer's medium is open: any number of
  terms, each a density, spectral coefficients and a phase function from data, so it references
  whatever composition the client's optics write. Closed, each small and stated: the phase
  function kinds (Rayleigh, Cornette–Shanks, isotropic, none, and from R08.T12.c a table on
  u = √(Θ ÷ π) and a Legendre series, so that any Mie, literature or aggregate phase function is
  referenced through the table); the Stokes mode's kinds (Rayleigh, isotropic, none and a table
  with its matrix; a term without one is traced only if marked `depolarising`, as a total
  depolariser, R08.T12.c and `decision-r08-vector.md`);
  the ground (Lambertian only: no BRDF, ocean or glint, which are R11's); and the shells: the
  sphere, or an oblate level spheroid of revolution under every figure law (0 < c ≤ a, spinning
  below breakup; R08.T12.d), with no prolate or triaxial figure, which the generator does not make.
  Ruled by decision-composition: these are physics classes and stay closed.
- **Deviations in T12.d, as built** (2026-10-09; `crates/hyperion-fit/src/atmosphere/spheroid.rs`,
  new, and `case.rs`, `geometry.rs`, `transport.rs`, `mod.rs`).
  - _The case's spheroid._ `Shells::Spheroid` keeps the Provides' Rust fields and adds a fifth,
    `gravity_offset_m_s2`. Its JSON is the client's `bodyGravity` result field for field
    (`oblate.ts`, with R08.T3.d's figure-law follow-up, 533bbfbc): kind `spheroid` with
    `equatorialRadiusM`, `polarRadiusM`, `gmM3S2`, `angularVelocityRadS` and `gravityOffsetMS2`, the
    last optional and 0 by default. So ω's key is `angularVelocityRadS` (`omegaRadS` is refused,
    tested), ω is Design note 17's ω_fig, and the offset is the client's `gravityOffsetMS2`. The
    plan's "rotational figures; a tidal case would take ω_fig and ω²R" is built for every law:
    g(φ) = γ(φ) + the offset, g_ref = √(g_e g_p) of that g, s = g ÷ g_ref, held to the client's
    printed g_ref and s for one figure under `rotational_and_tidal`, `capped` and `rotational` to
    10⁻¹², beside WGS 84's γ_e and γ_p to 10⁻⁹ and the client's γ for WGS 84, Saturn and Jupiter
    to 10⁻¹². `LevelSpheroid::new` returns `BuildLevelSpheroidError` (radii, GM, spin, past
    breakup, offset, a gravity that is not finite), which the case maps to its field, and the
    validated figure is kept in `AtmosphereCase` for the grid (`case::Figure`). `CASE_FORMAT` stays
    1: no case is committed.
  - _Heights and latitudes._ On a spheroid `topHeightM` and every profile height are
    gravity-scaled heights h\*; an observer's height is geodetic, and every latitude (an
    observer's and an aggregate's) is geodetic, the frame's up the datum's normal. So T12.b's
    writer places a limb at n H at the geodetic height n H ÷ s(φ). A body traced on one sphere
    takes R05's `tableRadiusM`, (2a + c) ÷ 3, as `radiusM`.
  - _Vermeille, in Karney's form._ Outside the evolute (8r³ + e⁴pq > 0) u = r + ½R + 2r² ÷ R,
    R = ∛((√(e⁴pq) + √(8r³ + e⁴pq))²): Karney 2011's u = r + T + r² ÷ T (arXiv:1102.1215, App. B),
    the same root as Vermeille's for either sign of r, with no division by r and none of his form's
    cancellation where r < 0. Inside it (only above the poles of a body with c ÷ a < 1 ÷ √2, which
    `FLATTENING_CAP` 0.2 never reaches) u is the cubic's largest root by Viète's trigonometric
    form; any root gives the same k. Held to a brute-force foot point (10⁻¹² in latitude, 10⁻⁹ a in
    height) and round-tripped for c ÷ a from 1 to 0.2 (10⁻¹³ a). h\* is computed with √(D² + z²)
    cancelled from Somigliana's part of h·s (the same value to 10⁻¹³). R08.T6.e's closed form may
    port this form.
  - _The shells_ are quadrics (a + Hₖ ÷ sₑ, c + Hₖ ÷ sₚ) through h\* = Hₖ at the equator and the
    poles, at T12.a's split heights, the datum the ground. Between, they depart from h\* = Hₖ by up
    to 1.7% of Hₖ on Saturn (at 46.5°), 0.5% on Jupiter and 4 × 10⁻⁶ on Earth (computed), always
    outward. The top is the quadric through h\* = `topHeightM`, so the medium reaches up to 1.7%
    past it, each profile read there as past its top: T12.b puts the top where that is negligible
    (an exponential at 40 H; T3.a's column, whose last level holds 10⁻⁷ of the ground's density,
    adds about 2 × 10⁻⁵ of a limb's optical depth there).
  - _The majorant is per shell_, as T12.a's estimator has it, not per path. Each shell's bounds of
    h\* come from a 1,025-latitude scan of s hₖ(φ) along the datum's normals, widened by the
    largest step between neighbouring latitudes (some 300 times the most the scan can miss on
    Saturn, computed), and each profile's maximum over them gives the majorant, the density at the
    lowest h\* a shell can hold for an exponential. A looser majorant costs null collisions, not
    bias (tested on a grid of the meridian half-plane).
  - _Beyond the shells and the majorant_, the figure sets the detector's origin, the aggregates'
    ground and top points, the ground's normal at a reflection and the aggregates' vertical.
    `ShellGrid` is an enum over `SphereShells` (T12.a's struct, its arithmetic unchanged, so
    `atmosphere_reference_bits_are_pinned` stands as T12.a pinned it) and `SpheroidShells`; a
    distance clamped at zero no longer goes through `max`, which may return either zero at −0 and
    so differ between targets (the determinism audit), with the same bits wherever the distance is
    not a signed zero. `atmosphere_spheroid_reference_bits_are_pinned` pins four values of a
    Saturn-class sample case: a ground view, the top flux, a view from orbit (the entry through the
    top) and a pole's direct beam, which no draw touches.
  - _Beer–Lambert on a spheroid._ A profile's kink lies on a surface of constant h\*, which the
    quadrics leave, so a piece's 8-point rule can straddle one. On Saturn's grazing chords
    (horizontal from 100 m at the equator north and east and at the pole, and tangent at 1 H and
    3 H), against an independent `f64` quadrature (bisection for the foot point, TR8350.2's form of
    Somigliana from the client's printed γ_e and γ_p): an exponential agrees to 4 × 10⁻¹⁰ and
    T3.a's column (1,024 levels even in ln p, each a slight kink) to 3 × 10⁻⁹, both held to the
    task's 10⁻⁶; a tent, whose kinks are sharp, to 1.4 × 10⁻⁶, held to 10⁻⁵. So `saturn-oblate` on
    T3.a's column meets Design note 10's 10⁻⁶ direct beam in the reference with room to spare; a
    sharp-kinked profile on a strongly flattened body would want each piece split where the ray
    crosses a kink's h\*, which is not built.
  - _a = c against the sphere_, on the Earth-like sample case (`case::tests::sample_case`), since
    T12.b's `earth` case comes later. The fast test (1,500 samples) holds the same draws to 10⁻⁹
    (4 × 10⁻¹³ measured: the paths are the sphere's), far inside the task's 3σ, and independent
    draws (seed 1) to 4σ on each of the 8 stochastic values, a family-wise α of 5 × 10⁻⁴ under the
    sim-determinism rule's α = 10⁻³ (3σ would be 2%). The Testing section's slow comparison is
    `atmosphere_spheroid_with_a_equal_to_c_follows_the_spheres_paths` (`#[ignore]`, 104 s on 4
    threads in the slow-test profile, run by `just test-slow atmosphere_spheroid`), the same draws
    to 10⁻⁹ at 10⁵ samples, rare paths included. At 10⁵ independent samples one of the 8 values stood at 3.2σ, the two
    runs' noise alone, since the paths are the same.
  - _Tests_ beyond the three named: the client's printed gravities, rotational and under every
    figure law; a still sphere's GM ÷ R²; the series' join with the closed form; out-of-range
    figures refused, by variant and by the case's field; the geodetic round trip and the
    foot-point search; h\* = h·s; the shells' heights at the equator and the poles, their h\*
    bounds, walks, grazing passes, entry from orbit and the ground's vertical; majorants bounding
    the coefficient; views down from orbit at 0°, 45° and 90° through the vertical column and the
    sun's slant one (10⁻⁶); a flattened plane-parallel slab's single scattering at τ ÷ s (10⁻⁴),
    its energy conservation and its direct beam e^(−τ ÷ s μ₀) (10⁻⁶); one and four threads
    identical on the spheroid.
  - _Cost, provisional:_ 312 µs a path on the a = c Earth-like sample case against the sphere's
    117 µs, and 354 µs on the Saturn-class sample case (three terms, 38 shells), one thread, load
    average 7.7, the dev profile at `opt-level` 2; h\* costs 79 ns, where the sphere's height is a
    square root. The quiet-machine run is pending.
  - _Scope._ Oblate spheroids of revolution, 0 < c ≤ a, spinning below breakup, under every figure
    law through ω_fig and the offset. Prolate and triaxial figures are refused: the generator makes
    none (its synchronous 4 : 1 : 3 figure is drawn as its spheroid), a triaxial body's geodetic
    conversion has no closed form in radicals (a sextic: Diaz-Toca, Marín and Necula 2020,
    arXiv:1909.06452), and Somigliana's is a level ellipsoid of revolution's. `oblate.ts`'s caveats
    (winds, the 1-bar surface, T(p) by latitude, the sectoral tide) hold here unchanged.
  - _Decided 2026-10-10 (`decision-r08-spheroid.md`)._
    - _The direct beam on spheroid cases._ Both of Design note 10's beam checks apply to every
      case, sphere or spheroid:
      - the reference's `sunOpticalDepth` against the client's own `f64` quadrature, to
        10⁻⁶·max(1, τ) (R08.T6.e's brute-force spheroid march on `saturn-oblate`; T12.d's test
        holds the tracer to 10⁻⁶ of an independent one);
      - the client's beam in radiance, under the metric.

      R08.T6.e's 0.5% at grazing was not consistent with the 5%: an error Δτ moves the beam by
      e^(−Δτ) − 1 whatever τ is. Its bound becomes max(0.01, 2 × 10⁻³ τ). A lookup at the
      sample's s and R_α alone misses that by up to 5.3× at 30–75° along the meridian, which
      Design note 17's _The ray's own gradient_ takes up.

    - _"Geopotential height"._ Reworded in Design note 17 and `oblate.ts`; nothing computed
      changes. h\* is the level spheroid's geopotential height to first order. The column's
      R_ref Φ ÷ (R_ref − Φ) already restores the h² ÷ R term, the science check's 0.08 H at 10 H
      on Saturn. What is left is the monopole's free-air gradient against the level spheroid's:
      0.036 H at Saturn's equator and 0.011 H at its pole at 10 H, and 0.001 H on Earth.
- **Deviations in T12.c, as built** (2026-10-10; `crates/hyperion-fit/src/atmosphere/`: `case.rs`,
  `optics.rs`, `transport.rs`, `reference.rs`, `mod.rs` and the new `benchmarks.rs`; `cli.rs` and
  `lib.rs`; the new `crates/hyperion-fit/data/iprt_phase_a/`; `NOTICE`; the crate's
  `Cargo.toml` takes `hyperion-testkit` as a dev-dependency, for its α and χ² helpers, with
  `Cargo.lock`; `.config/nextest.toml`'s slow profile gives each benchmark four threads,
  `threads-required = 4`, as it traces on four).
  - _The case format_ (`CASE_FORMAT` stays 1: no case is committed). Phases gain `tabulated`,
    `{ u, a1, asymmetry, matrix? }`: one u = √(Θ ÷ π) grid a term, from exactly 0 to exactly 1 as
    the client's `PhaseTable` has it, a₁ per traced wavelength (named `a1` where the client's table
    says `values`), the source's mean cosine per wavelength, and optionally all five of `a2`,
    `a3`, `a4`, `b1` and `b2`, linear in u as `phaseAt` reads them. And `legendre`,
    `{ coefficients }` per wavelength, p = (1 ÷ 4π) Σ βₗ Pₗ. A term gains `depolarising`
    (false by default), refused on a term with a matrix (Rayleigh, isotropic, none, a table with
    its matrix).
  - _Load checks._ |a₂|, |a₃|, |a₄|, |b₁|, |b₂| ≤ a₁ (1 + 10⁻⁹, for rounding); a table's integral
    over the sphere, read linearly in u (16-point Gauss–Legendre an interval), within 10⁻⁴ of 1
    and its mean cosine within 10⁻⁴ of `asymmetry`. The tracer then divides the table by its
    integral, so that what it draws from and what its next-event estimates weigh are the same
    function. A series' β₀ stands within 10⁻⁴ of 1 (the series is divided by it), and the series
    must be positive at each of the 4,097 entries of its proposal table.
  - _Finding for R08.T5.c and T12.b._ Read linearly in u, a 256-entry table sampled at its entries
    integrates to more than 1: 6.5 × 10⁻⁵ over at g 0.7, 1.1 × 10⁻⁴ at 0.8, 2.3 × 10⁻⁴ at 0.9
    and 4.8 × 10⁻⁴ at 0.95 (Henyey–Greenstein; a quarter of that on 512 entries), while the mean
    cosine stays within 1.3 × 10⁻⁵. So T5.c's builder normalises its entries under the linear-in-u
    rule, as the client's `PhaseTable` documentation already asks, or the 10⁻⁴ check refuses a
    forward aerosol's table. And the case's `asymmetry` is the source's mean cosine, which the
    client's `PhaseTable` does not carry: T12.b's writer takes it from T5's Mie g, not from the
    table, or the check proves nothing.
  - _Sampling._ A table is drawn from exactly: an interval by the inverse of its cumulative
    distribution, then a direction uniform in 1 − cos Θ within it, kept with probability a₁ ÷ the
    interval's larger end. A draw of ξ = 1, which `Draws::uniform` returns once in 2⁵³ (its
    `k + 0.5` rounds up at the top), lands in the last interval of positive probability, so a table
    that ends in zeros cannot hang the rejection (the determinism audit). A series is drawn from its proposal table, 4,097 entries even in u, and
    weighted by the series over the proposal. The draws of Rayleigh, Cornette–Shanks and isotropic
    terms are unchanged.
  - _The Stokes vector_ is (I, Q, U, V), the path's matrix 4 × 4 and the scattering matrix
    block-diagonal. Rayleigh's a₄ carries Δ′ (Hansen and Travis's eq. 2.16) and its b₂ is 0. V's
    sign is the case's b₂'s. `StokesNeedsRayleigh` is renamed `StokesNeedsMatrix` (exit code 2, as
    before).
  - _The scalar radiance of the same paths._ In the Stokes mode every sample scores the scalar
    estimate beside I. `StokesRadiance` gains `v`, `scalar_radiance` and their errors and the
    error of I − scalar; `FluxAggregate` gains `scalar: Option<ScalarFlux>`, the diffuse ground and
    upwelling top fluxes of the same paths, each with its error and its difference's, for R08.T13's
    scalar gates. The Stokes run's scalar radiance is the scalar mode's bit for bit (tested).
    `REFERENCE_FORMAT` stays 1: no reference is committed.
  - _Directions drawn towards the suns_ (unbiased variance reduction, which the task allows for the
    forward peak). Without it, IPRT A4's spheroids (g 0.84) converged from below: at 20,000
    samples the upwelling radiances stood 3–5% under PSTAR's, σ 1–6%, since the rare path that
    points at the sun after a wide first scattering scores some 1,000 times the rest (P1 557 in the
    peak against about 0.1 sideways). Built: the detector directional importance sampling of Buras
    and Mayer 2011 (JQSRT 112, 434) with the case's suns as the detector. At a vertex whose phase
    mixture's forward value passes `FORWARD_PEAK_PER_SR` = 1 sr⁻¹, `SUNWARD_FRACTION` = 0.2 of the
    new directions are drawn from the mixture about a sun, every path weighted by the phase function
    over both branches' density (at most 1.25 for an exact draw; a Legendre series' proposal can
    take it higher), and the roulette's threshold scales with that weight. Each term's forward value
    is computed once a medium, not at every vertex.
    With both, the bias went and σ fell to 0.4–0.9% at 20,000 samples. Pure Rayleigh, and media
    below the threshold, draw as before, so Natraj's T12.a run is unchanged. The draws do not depend
    on the suns' irradiance. `atmosphere_reference_bits_are_pinned`'s ground view moved, since its
    Cornette–Shanks aerosol is forward-peaked (0.039731668489903935 to 0.04009082837728386); its top
    flux and T12.d's spheroid pins did not.
  - _Statistics (a technical correction to "each to 3σ")._ Over a benchmark of N values a 3σ bound
    on each fails by chance with probability 1 − 0.9973ᴺ (19% at N 78), far above the testkit's
    α = 10⁻³. So each benchmark holds every value to the two-sided Bonferroni bound at α ÷ 2 over
    its N values (4.4σ–4.8σ here) and each Stokes component's χ² over its independent geometries
    to α ÷ 2 over the components; σ ≤ 0.3% of the geometry's I is asserted at every value, and the
    count past 3σ and the largest |z| are printed and recorded below. The benchmarks' own errors
    enter σ in quadrature: Natraj's last printed digit, Kokhanovsky's six correct digits, and
    PSTAR's largest difference from IPOL (its U and V negated) in each component at the rows used,
    relative to I: 1.1 × 10⁻⁶ in A1, up to 6.9 × 10⁻⁶ in A2, and in A4 1.8 × 10⁻⁴ in I and
    3 × 10⁻⁶ in Q and U; A4's V is held to its difference from MYSTIC's, 1.4 × 10⁻⁶. _Upheld
    2026-10-10 (`decision-r08-t4b-t12c.md`):_ Design note 10's _Statistics_ states it for every
    agreement test in R08, beside the metric's tolerance tests.
  - _Conventions found._ The tracer's (Q, U) is Natraj and Hovenier 2012's (Hovenier's), and the
    negative of Natraj, Li and Yung 2009's: the two papers' τ = 1 tables carry Q and U of opposite
    signs to each other.
    Kokhanovsky et al. tabulate −Q, their Q the tracer's, and their U is −U of the tracer's; their
    radiances are π I ÷ (μ₀F₀). IPRT's files disagree in U: IPOL's and SHDOM's carry one sign,
    PSTAR's and MYSTIC's (the organisers') the other, in U and V alike. PSTAR's (Q, U, V) is
    (Q, −U, −V) of the tracer's, one difference of handedness, as IPOL's V, PSTAR's negated to
    5 × 10⁻⁹ of I in A4, confirms. With U and V negated, IPOL agrees with PSTAR to 1.1 × 10⁻⁶ of I
    in A1; A4's V reaches 1.6 × 10⁻⁴ of I, and PSTAR's and MYSTIC's agree to 1.4 × 10⁻⁶. PSTAR's
    values (as printed, seven digits) are the ones asserted.
    Relative azimuths map directly in every benchmark.
  - _The benchmarks run_ (module `atmosphere::benchmarks`, run by
    `just test-slow atmosphere::benchmarks`; all seven pass, 112 s of wall time four at a time on
    16 threads; each at seed 0, run one at a time on 4 threads under a 400% CPU quota at load
    7–25 for the figures below). Of 739 values, 3 stand past 3σ, against 2.0 expected by chance:

    | Benchmark                                     | Values | Samples   | Largest \|z\| (where)                     | Past 3σ | Bound | Largest σ ÷ I | χ² p: I, Q, U, V        | Time  |
    | --------------------------------------------- | ------ | --------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------- | ----- | ------------- | ----------------------- | ----- |
    | Natraj et al. 2009, τ 0.5, μ₀ 0.2, A 0        | 78     | 5 × 10⁵   | 3.68 (top, μ 0.2, φ 180°, I)              | 1       | 4.51  | 0.24%         | 0.017, 0.22, 0.86       | 25 s  |
    | Natraj et al. 2009, τ 1, μ₀ 0.6, A 0.8        | 78     | 4 × 10⁵   | 2.63 (bottom, μ 0.2, φ 60°, U)            | 0       | 4.51  | 0.18%         | 0.74, 0.44, 0.30        | 31 s  |
    | Natraj and Hovenier 2012, τ 2, μ₀ 0.5, A 0.25 | 60     | 1.5 × 10⁶ | 2.56 (bottom, μ 0.9, φ 90°, I)            | 0       | 4.46  | 0.27%         | 0.017, 0.39, 0.22       | 110 s |
    | Kokhanovsky et al. 2010, molecular            | 42     | 2.5 × 10⁵ | 2.75 (reflected, VZA 0°, φ 180°, Q)       | 0       | 4.38  | 0.20%         | 0.93, 0.14, 0.46        | 8 s   |
    | IPRT A1 (PSTAR)                               | 246    | 2 × 10⁵   | 3.02 (ρ 0.03, bottom, sza 30°, vza 0°, I) | 1       | 4.75  | 0.19%         | 0.16, 0.11, 0.15        | 35 s  |
    | IPRT A2 (PSTAR)                               | 99     | 10⁵       | 2.69 (top, vza 120°, vaa 0°, U)           | 0       | 4.56  | 0.15%         | 0.96, 0.62, 0.47        | 7 s   |
    | IPRT A4 (PSTAR)                               | 136    | 4 × 10⁵   | 3.09 (bottom, vza 0°, vaa 90°, Q)         | 1       | 4.63  | 0.20%         | 0.99, 0.21, 0.69, 0.997 | 35 s  |

    Every value meets σ ≤ 0.3% of I, so no case needed the task's allowance for a σ it cannot
    reach. The two I components at p 0.017 are chance as far as can be told: Natraj 2009's is
    carried by its one value at 3.68σ (P ≈ 2% that the largest of 78 reaches it), and T12.a
    traced the same Rayleigh paths at 10⁶ samples with none past 3σ. Each summary also prints
    the χ² the run would give against the benchmark's values with the sign flipped: 1.5 × 10⁶ to
    5.5 × 10⁷ for Q and U in every benchmark, and 13,124 for A4's 34 values of V, against 15.4 as
    used. So every convention above is determined by the run, V's included; A4's V χ² stands
    below its expectation, so its σ, if anything, is overstated. Two runs at seed 0 gave the same
    values to the last digit.

  - _Thick Rayleigh is τ 2._ Design note 10's thick case (Natraj and Hovenier 2012) runs at τ 2,

    geometry (below, "Thick transmitted light"), and thicker tables wait on a variance reduction
    for deep transmission.

  - _Thick transmitted light (for T12.b)._ The backward estimator's transmitted diffuse radiance
    at μ₀ 0.5 has a coefficient of variation of about 3 at τ 2 and 7 at τ 4 (σ ÷ I of 2.1% and
    5% at 20,000 samples), since a path from the bottom must climb to within about τ 0.5 of the
    top before its next-event estimates count. So Natraj and Hovenier's τ 4 would need some
    5 × 10⁶ samples a geometry; the benchmark runs τ 2 at 1.5 × 10⁶. The Venus- and Titan-class
    surface views will need far more, or a variance reduction for deep transmission (not built).

- **Deviations in T12.e, as built** (2026-10-10;
  `apps/hyperion/src/renderer/src/test/mieMatrices.ts` and `mieMatrices.test.ts`;
  `crates/hyperion-fit/src/atmosphere/benchmarks.rs` and the new `sphere_matrices/`; four new files
  in `crates/hyperion-fit/data/iprt_phase_a/`, with its `PROVENANCE.toml` and `README.md`;
  `NOTICE`; `.prettierignore`. Rulings: `decision-r08-t4b-t12c.md`, follow-up, 1–7).
  - _The writer_ is test code beside `bless.ts` (`test/mieMatrices.ts`), since only the benchmarks
    read it: `SPHERE_CASES`, `SphereCase`, `RadiusDistribution` (`logNormal` by mode radius and s,
    the σ of ln r; `gamma` by libRadtran's α), `RadiusRule` (`gaussLegendre`, `libRadtran`),
    `radiusNodes`, `sphereCaseOptics`, `tableIntegral`, `tableValue`, `tabulatedPhase`,
    `sphereMatrixFile`, `linearInUMoments` (the tracer's integral of a table, in TypeScript),
    `evenU`, `cosinesOf`, `sampledEntries` and `SIGNIFICANT_DIGITS` (10). Each sphere's matrix is
    T5.b's `sphereScatteringMatrix` of T5.a's `mieSphere`, weighted by n(r) dr × x² Q_sca, and ω and
    g are the same sums', not the table's. T5.b's `sphereModeOptics` is not used: it takes an
    effective radius and variance and its own interval, where each benchmark states its own
    distribution, its own cut and, for IPRT, its own quadrature. A matrix with T5.c's
    `forwardPeak` (a delta the case format cannot carry) is refused.
  - _Its files_ are `crates/hyperion-fit/src/atmosphere/sphere_matrices/<case>.json`, one a case
    (the tracer `include_str!`s them, the vitest imports them): the case's definition, its node
    count, ω, g, the linear-in-u integral divided out, and the `tabulated` phase with all five
    elements beside a₁, 513 or 1,025 entries even in u. 54–108 kB each, under the 500 kB hook,
    listed in `.prettierignore` since `bless.ts` writes and compares them byte for byte.
  - _The vitest_ checks IPRT A3's file whole in every run (69 radii, milliseconds), the others
    whole only under a bless or by hand (`HYPERION_SLOW_TESTS=1`, with the file's vitest; no recipe
    sets it for this file, and the two Kokhanovsky cases take 59 s and 148 s), and otherwise every
    64th entry, ω, g and the node count exactly (8 s): Mie at one cosine does not depend on the
    others asked for, and the sums run in the same order. Beside it, every written table's
    integral is 1 to 10⁻⁹ and its mean cosine the Mie g's to 10⁻⁴ under the tracer's rule, with
    each |a₂ … b₂| ≤ a₁(1 + 10⁻⁹); T12.c's load checks themselves run in Rust
    (`sphere_matrix_tables_make_valid_cases_and_hold_the_tracers_normalisation`). The files were
    blessed before T5.c's refactor of `mieSphere` (`mieCoefficients`, `mieAmplitudes`) and are
    the same bits after it, whole.
  - _Kokhanovsky et al.'s sums._ Their matrices came from Mishchenko's `spher.f`, whose quadrature
    they do not state. The writer converges their stated integral (0.005 µm to a_end, eq. (10))
    by T5.b's composite rule, refined 5 times for the aerosol (60,080 nodes) and 3 times for the
    cloud (49,184). Non-absorbing spheres' resonances converge slowly: the aerosol's a₁ moves by
    ≤ 6.6 × 10⁻⁴ between levels 5 and 6, the cloud's by ≤ 9 × 10⁻³ (150°–176°) between levels 2
    and 3. g is 0.792762 against their 0.79275 and 0.861060 against their 0.86114, held to 2 × 10⁻⁴.
  - _IPRT's sums_ (found here). IPRT's spheres are runs of libRadtran's Mie tool, whose netCDF
    copies (`waso.mie.cdf`, `watercloud.mie.cdf`, read with a stdlib reader) record what the wiki
    and Emde et al. do not all state:
    - A3: index 1.422 − 0.002649i at 350 nm (the wiki's A3 page says 500 nm; Emde et al. §3.2.3
      and both files say 350), a log-normal of mode radius 0.0262 µm and σ_g 2.24 (the file records
      2.0, but only Emde et al.'s 2.24 reproduces the matrix), cut at `n_r_max` 5 × the radius
      parameter on libRadtran's grid (`dx_max` 0.03);
    - A5: a gamma distribution of α 7 and r_eff 10 µm (Emde et al.'s "width of 0.1" is v_eff),
      index 1.3258698 − 1.250319 × 10⁻⁷i, `dx_max` 0.003.

    The writer repeats the size sampling of libRadtran's Mie tool, radii from 0.02 r to n_r_max r
    in steps of Δx = max(dx_max, dx_max √x) and the trapezoid in r, as a method stated in its doc,
    not as code (ruled 2026-10-10, `decision-r08-cmf-licence.md` §6). A numerical method and its
    parameters are not expression, and nothing of `src/mie.c` is copied or translated, so
    decision-composition row 17's "ported" does not reach it. The √x step is F. Evans's, from
    SHDOM's Mie tables, which libRadtran credits. A3's distribution is cut where its integrand
    is still large, so the exact integral to 5 r is not IPRT's matrix (g 0.5544 against 0.5498);
    A5's water resonances leave T5.b's rule 0.3% of a₁ from IPRT's at 50,240 nodes, where
    libRadtran's sum gives 1.6 × 10⁻⁴. The vitest holds the writer to IPRT's own matrices
    (`a3_sphere_matrix.txt`, all 68 angles, 10⁻⁵ of P1, 3.6 × 10⁻⁶ measured; `a5_cloud_matrix.txt`,
    every fifth of 450 angles, 3 × 10⁻⁴, 1.6 × 10⁻⁴ measured) and both ω to the files' six digits.

  - _T5.b's b₂ sign: confirmed._ A3's V gives χ² 21.2 for 34 values, against 112,247 with the sign
    flipped, under T12.c's PSTAR handedness, which A4's own matrix fixed independently of T5.b; and
    the writer's b₂ is IPRT's P4, sign included, at all 68 angles. Kokhanovsky et al.'s printed V is

  - _σ must fall as N^−½_ (ruling 7). Every benchmark in `atmosphere::benchmarks`, T12.c's seven
    included, now traces its case twice, at N and N ÷ 4 samples (each sample draws from its own
    counter-based stream, so the second is exactly the run's first quarter), and asserts only the
    values whose σ at N is within 25% (`SIGMA_SCALING_TOLERANCE`) of half their σ at N ÷ 4. Any
    other is named in the summary and not asserted, and the set each benchmark leaves out is pinned
    in `EXPECTED_UNSCALED`, so that a value that starts or stops scaling fails the benchmark; a σ
    that is not finite fails it, as does a benchmark left with nothing to assert
    (`a_standard_error_scales_only_within_a_quarter_of_n_to_the_minus_half` tests the check).
    T12.c's seven trace the same seeds and counts, so their full runs are unchanged to the bit;
    they take 25% longer. T12.d's a = c test and the tracer's other statistical unit tests do not
    carry the check yet (for "main"). No looser σ cap is admitted for an agreement test, T12.c's
    allowance is withdrawn (its text, above), and no as-built case used it.

  - _The τ 5 clouds_ (ruling 7: option (a); R08.T12.f's starting point). Neither is asserted, their
    slow tests are not committed, and Kokhanovsky et al.'s cloud values stay out of the commit
    until a test asserts them. Committed: both written matrices (`kokhanovsky-cloud.json`,
    `iprt-a5.json`), A5's 62 selected rows and its matrix, and their fast load and matrix tests.
    Measured, at the counts and seed the tests would use:
    - IPRT A5, 6 × 10⁵ samples a geometry, 62 geometries, about 200 s on 4 threads at load 33: the
      per-value bound held (largest |z| 4.56 against 4.75) but the χ² of I was 113 for 62
      (p ≈ 4 × 10⁻⁵); traced ÷ expected averaged 0.9962, up from 0.9877 at 5 × 10⁴ (median 0.994,
      37 of 58 values low), σ/I 1.3% at the median and 6.9% at worst. Q, U and V hold (χ² 62, 60
      and 70 for 62), and their flipped χ² decide the signs (90,295, 11,916).
    - Kokhanovsky et al.'s cloud, 10⁶ samples, 36 geometries, about 200 s: σ/I 1.5% at the median
      and 40% at its worst (transmitted, VZA 89°, φ 90°); traced ÷ expected 1.020 on average,
      carried by one spike.
    - _Why_ (diagnosed with temporary instrumentation, not committed): the heavy tail is next-event
      estimates at vertices just under the cloud's top whose arrival direction lies within about 1°
      of the sun (cos Θ > 0.9998, p up to 500 sr⁻¹) at weights 0.1–1.6. The path's direction
      diffuses into the sun's forward peak by small scatterings, and T12.c's sunward draws do not
      reduce the weight, since each step's old and new directions lie in the same peak. It is not
      the polarisation: the scalar σ of the same paths is the same. At reflected VZA 0°, φ 90°, σ/I
      fell from 3.9% to 2.8% over 2 × 10⁵ to 8 × 10⁵ samples, a factor 0.71 where N^−½ gives 0.5.
    - _The cloud's matrix_ moved a₁ by up to 9 × 10⁻³ at 150°–176° from level 2 to level 3, its
      committed level; R08.T12.f shows level 3 against level 4 before it asserts the cloud.
    - _Tried and reverted:_ a sunward fraction proportional to the best-lit sun's transmittance from
      the vertex below e⁻¹ (unbiased, and bit-identical on every T12.c case), meant to stop the
      weights' growth by 1 ÷ 0.8 a vertex deep in the cloud. It gave no clear gain at 8 × 10⁵
      samples (σ/I 2.0% against 2.8% at reflected VZA 0°, φ 90°, but 1.15% against 0.88% at
      transmitted VZA 20°, φ 90°), so T12.c's tracer is unchanged.

- **Deviations in T12.f, as built** (2026-10-12; `crates/hyperion-fit/src/atmosphere/`:
  `transport.rs`, `mod.rs`, `benchmarks.rs`; `crates/hyperion-fit/data/iprt_phase_a/README.md`).
  - _The method_ is Buras and Mayer 2011's VROOM (JQSRT 112, 434; their DLR copy,
    <https://elib.dlr.de/65843/1/buras2011.pdf>, SHA-256 `27857d27…cf364`), ported from the
    paper's text (§2.2–2.6) with its parameter set (§2.6), in `transport.rs`'s module
    documentation and constants:
    - the n-tuple local estimate (§2.3): a mother path estimates its first `MOTHER_ORDERS` (4)
      orders, natural from its order 4 on, and clones made at its orders 4 + 11i estimate the
      rest in blocks (`CLONE_SCATTERINGS` 12, `ESTIMATES_PER_CLONE` 11), each order once
      (`atmosphere_vroom_estimates_every_order_exactly_once`);
    - sunward draws (DDIS, §2.2) at every clone vertex and at the mother's orders 1–3, those whose
      next estimate is its own, as the paper's Fig. 8 and §2.4 have it (its §2.6 says the first
      n_firstCP), at `VROOM_SUNWARD_FRACTION` 0.1;
    - prediction-based splitting and roulette (§2.4: `SPLIT_ABOVE` 3, `MOST_COPIES` 5,000,
      `ROULETTE_BELOW` 1/3, `LEAST_SURVIVAL` 0.2, the weight never lifted past the sample's
      first-flight weight), the prediction in the paper's units (`PAPER_PHASE_SCALE`, 4π).

    Not built: circumsolar virtual importance sampling (§2.5), for a detector that looks into or
    near a sun through a thin peaked medium. Its trigger, w_redspl > 10, holds within some 7°–8° of
    the sun in these clouds; no benchmark looks within 15° of a sun. The near-sun pilot (`decision-r08-t12f.md`
    ruling 2; through the `atmosphere-reference` command at seeds 1000 and 1001, not committed):
    slabs of τ 0.5 and ω 1 over a black ground, seen from the ground at 3°, 5°, 8° and 12° from a
    sun 60° (above, below and in its almucantar) and 85° (above and in its almucantar) from the
    zenith, 20 views, at 1.6 × 10⁶, 4 × 10⁵ and 10⁵ samples a view:
    - (i) the 1,024-entry Henyey–Greenstein g 0.9 table (forward 15 sr⁻¹, w_redspl > 10 within
      15° of the sun): against the ruling's adding-doubling values, largest |z| 1.87 (bound z_20
      4.21), χ² 14.9 for 20 (p 0.78), Σz ÷ √n −0.43; σ ÷ I at worst 0.174% at 1.6 × 10⁶ (0.35%
      at 4 × 10⁵); every σ ratio to N^(−1/2) from 0.989 to 1.007 at both steps; 87 s.
    - (ii) A5's matrix (forward 283 sr⁻¹, w_redspl > 10 within 8.2°): σ ÷ I at worst 0.221% at
      1.6 × 10⁶ (85° sun, 3° in azimuth); every σ ratio from 0.981 to 1.013; 86 s.
    - The outcome under the ruling's rule, stated before the run: neither fails, so §2.5 stays
      unbuilt, and R08.T12.b's item near a sun guards its own media.
      Iwabuchi 2006 (J. Atmos. Sci. 63, 2324) was weighed from its abstract and Buras and Mayer's
      account of it (its text is behind a 403 here): its truncation approximation alters the phase
      function and biases by an amount the run cannot state (Buras and Mayer §1), and the task
      admits a biasing technique only with its bias measured below 10⁻³ of I, which the benchmarks'
      own 0.2% spreads cannot show; its modified local estimate, a roulette of the estimate's ray,
      saves time, not variance (ibid. §2.6); its collision forcing for optically thin media and its
      numerical diffusion were weighed from the abstract only.

  - _Choices beyond the paper_, each unbiased, any splitting or roulette rule being so:
    - splitting and the prediction-based roulette play at the guided vertices alone, with the
      sunward draws, so on the mother at its orders 1–3 (as Fig. 8 has the draws), where §2.6
      plays the roulette at every vertex: not on the natural mother past its order 3, whose
      weight changes by losses alone (the cap would keep a full-weight mother out of it anyway);
      both read the prediction after its division by w_redspl;
    - the sunward branch draws from the vertex's own phase mixture (R08.T12.c's), where eq. 10
      takes the largest of the scene's phase functions; the two agree in a medium of one term,
      every benchmark's, and in a layered one (T12.b's haze over a deck) a sunward draw at a haze
      vertex does not bound the next cloud vertex's estimate, which the splitting does;
    - the prediction is 4π times the largest of the case's terms' phase functions at the new
      direction's cosine with a sun, the largest over the suns, in place of the paper's
      C_ddis·max normalised: no irradiance enters it, so the draws stay independent of it;
    - W is relative to the sample's first-flight weight (the forced collision's 1 − e^(−τ), or
      the ground seen directly), which its clones and copies inherit, not to 1, so that a thin
      limb's small first weight is not split or rouletted for being small;
    - the least prediction of w_redspl (eq. 12) includes the first flight's direction;
    - the existing roulette's threshold divides with a split, so that copies are not rouletted
      for being copies.
  - _Where it runs:_ `Estimator::ByMedium`, what every reference runs, takes VROOM at a wavelength
    where some term that scatters has a forward phase value above `FORWARD_PEAK_PER_SR`
    (1 sr⁻¹), and R08.T12.c's estimator elsewhere, so that Rayleigh's sky and every Rayleigh
    benchmark (Natraj ×3, Kokhanovsky's molecular case, IPRT A1 and A2) run the same paths to
    the bit. `Estimator::SunwardDraws` and `Estimator::Vroom` force either; the tests' switch,
    through the crate-private `trace_reference_with` (`trace_reference`'s signature is
    unchanged). `Medium::new` takes the estimator. The reference format does not record which
    estimator ran: it is a function of the case.
  - _Bit pins_: `atmosphere_reference_bits_are_pinned`,
    `atmosphere_stokes_reference_bits_are_pinned` and
    `atmosphere_spheroid_reference_bits_are_pinned` now pin both: R08.T12.c's estimator at
    its old values to the bit, and the default, whose values moved because the sample case's
    Cornette–Shanks aerosol (forward 4.1 sr⁻¹), `polarising_case`'s table and the Saturn case's
    haze turn VROOM on. `atmosphere_rayleigh_alone_keeps_the_sunward_draws_paths` holds a
    Rayleigh-only case to R08.T12.c's bits under the default, and
    `atmosphere_vroom_runs_where_a_scattering_term_is_forward_peaked` the selection (a peaked term
    that does not scatter at a wavelength leaves it off there). The thread test gains a thick
    peaked slab (τ 5 at g 0.9), so that clones and splits are traced on one and four threads.

  - _The check of VROOM against the sunward draws_
    (`vroom_agrees_with_the_sunward_draws_where_they_converge`): the task's Henyey–Greenstein slab
    of g 0.9 and τ 2 (sun 50°, black ground). The sunward draws do not converge there everywhere:

    VROOM at 7 × 10⁵ and the sunward draws at 1.6 × 10⁶ samples, each at its own seed (0 and 1),
    every σ some 0.25% of I at most; z takes both σ, and both are held to 0.3% of I. The pilots:
    - over the 57 views at 4 × 10⁵ each, χ² 69.1 for 57, but Σz ÷ √n = +2.73 over the 50 that
      scale (VROOM about 0.13% above). The excess lay in the 28 best-converged views themselves

  - _One tally._ The ten tests share `Agreement` in `mod.rs`'s tests, which `optics.rs`'s tests use
    too. It does three things:
    - it asserts every σ a test reads through `assert_sigma_scales` (`benchmarks::sigma_scales`,
      25%);
    - it holds each value to `benchmarks::bonferroni_bound` times its σ, or to 4σ at 8 values or
      fewer, beside the test's own slack;
    - it prints the σ ratios and the largest |z| past the slack.

    `bonferroni_bound` is new. It is the rule that `assert_agreement` and the energy check wrote
    inline, −Φ⁻¹(α ÷ 4N) by `math::normal_quantile` at the testkit's α, and both now call it. The
    fast `the_bonferroni_bound_is_design_note_10s` pins it to the printed z_8, z_12, z_24, z_48,
    z_78 and z_246. IPRT A2 and the energy check were traced again by name and give T12.f's figures
    to the digit (largest |z| 2.69 and 1.34).

    The tracer's tests trace again at N ÷ 4, which is the run's first quarter
    (`trace_and_quarter`). `optics.rs`'s `sampled_mean` returns `Sampled`, which keeps the σ of the
    same draws' first quarter.

    Design note 10's false-failure count assumes; one seed would have given `earth` and
    `earth-ozone-slab` the same paths but at the slab's edges (the plan-conformance check).
    - `earth`: `EARTH_REFERENCE` (its measured ozone under `EARTH_REFERENCE_CURVES`) on a sphere of
      `tableRadiusM(WGS 84)`, 6,371,008.77 m. Vertical τ 0.172, 0.228 and 0.394: Rayleigh 0.051,
      0.102 and 0.258, the aerosol 0.081, 0.101 and 0.136, the ozone's curve at its vertical
      column 0.039, 0.025 and 0.

  - _The format's two additions_ (`CASE_FORMAT` and `REFERENCE_FORMAT` stay 1: none was committed
    before). A term's optional `absorber`: its `kind`, `"column"`, its `numberDensityPerM3`, and its
    `curves`, one a sun, each `{ logColumns, opticalDepth }`; it is carried only by a term of no
    scattering, absorption or phase, and `pair` and a curve of several pressure rows are refused
    until T12.b.2. And
    an optional `samples` on each geometry and aggregate, the command's `--samples` the default; the
    reference records each one's `samples`, `quarterSamples` (⌊N ÷ 4⌋) and the σ of its first quarter
    (of the vector and the scalar radiance, and of both fluxes of an aggregate). A sample's key is
    unchanged.
  - _The estimator_ (`transport.rs`, `absorber.rs`): each path carries each absorber's column,
    molecules m⁻², from the detector (the forced collision's piece, the ground seen directly, every
    later flight, by the 8-point rule per shell piece; clones and copies inherit it), and each
    next-event score towards sun s takes the sun leg's column beside its transmittance and
    multiplies by T_s(u_path + u_leg), read by the client's rule; `sunOpticalDepth` and
    `directGround` add −ln T of the beam's own column. The draws do not depend on it, and a case with
    no absorber traces bit for bit as before: the three pins are unchanged. Each score being one
    whole path, it is exact for a band mean where every other term's extinction, absorption and phase
    and the ground are grey within the channel under the sun's and the response's weight, the curve
    is one row, and several absorbers' spectra are uncorrelated (the multiplication property; the
    science check). Tests: an e^(−σu) curve against the same σ as absorption to 10⁻¹² (Beer–Lambert,
    and Rayleigh over a black ground, in both modes); a √u curve on a two-leg path, T(u₁ + u₂) to
    10⁻⁸ where T(u₁)T(u₂) is 51% and 76% lower at its two wavelengths; per-geometry counts changing
    their own draws alone, the first quarter's σ the trace's at N ÷ 4 to the bit across blocks; one
    and four threads with an absorber and uneven counts; the refusals.
  - _The shared values_ (`absorber_curves.json`, 80 kB, written by `absorberCurves.test.ts`): the
    tracer's read against the client's `absorberTransmittance` on Earth's two ozone curves and a
    saturated synthetic one (a step from τ 0 in green, the floor in red), 0 to 10⁵ times past the last
    node: largest relative difference 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁶, held to 10⁻¹².
  - _A faster lookup, the same bits_ (`optics.rs`'s `ProfileLookup`; accepted by main, 2026-10-21): a
    tabulated profile's node is found from an even grid of buckets and a step or two, the node
    `partition_point` finds and so the same interpolation (held to `at` to the bit by
    `atmosphere_a_profiles_lookup_reads_it_to_the_bit`). Smoke traces of all four cases, one geometry
    and aggregate in eight at 64 samples with `--stokes`, are byte for byte the same with and without
    it, and Earth's runs some 15% faster.
  - _`gate.ts`_: Design note 10's metric with its named constants (0.05, F = 3 × 10⁻⁴, 4 and 8; 0.02
    and 0.0025 for the aggregates; 16 for a sanity range; 25% for the N^(−1/2) check), the images
    and their floors, the refusals (`noisy`, σ > T ÷ 8, with the count it would need; `unscaled`,
    σ beyond 25% of σ_q √(N_q ÷ N)), the cone average (uniform in solid angle, as the tracer draws),
    the beam's two checks, the aggregates' and sanity ranges' tests, and the diagnostics: Δu′v′, ΔE*ab
    through `toneCurve` at the AVG exposure, IPRT's relative RMS and L_max ÷ mean. Its test confirms
    Design note 10's figure: 5% of a grey is at most 0.92 ΔE*ab (at the metered mean) anywhere from
    10⁻⁴ to 10³ times it, held under its 0.96. `reference/references.ts` reads the references as its
    readings, vector or scalar, and holds the client's own beam quadrature, converged below 10⁻⁷.
    `gate()` reports a refused geometry, not holds it; from R08.T14.d a refused geometry does not
    pass, which that task takes from the refusals.

- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)** (R08.T12.b.1). Recorded and deferred: each leaves the
  algorithm and every contract as they are.
  - _The legs apart_: `tablesCpu.ts` takes T_view(u_view) T_sun(u_sun) where the reference takes
    T(u_view + u_sun) (ruling 4): T13's to measure (ozone's red about +1.5% at 2 × 10 × 300 DU).
  - _Earth's limb, a deviation to revisit_: `localScaleHeightM` is the green extinction's e-folding,
    2.10 km on Earth against the air's 8.45 km, so its limbs stand at 0.21–21 km and none higher (the
    science check, the TypeScript review). Main kept ruling 7 as traced (2026-10-21), and an extra
    `limb` image for `earth` at the air's scale height, tangent to about 85 km, is T12.b.2's.
  - _The slab's limb_: `earth-ozone-slab`'s limbs at 0.21–21 km leave only the 10 H ray tangent
    inside the slab (18.6–38.5 km), none at its base or top, where R08.T13's layer-edge checks at the
    limb look (the plan-conformance check). Traced as built; main, 2026-10-22: T12.b.2 adds the higher
    `limb` image (tangents to about 85 km) to `earth-ozone-slab` as well as `earth`, and tangents at
    the slab's base and top.
  - _The twilight images_: with the sun 5° below the horizon a ground view needs up to 5.4 × 10⁷
    samples on Earth and 3.1 × 10⁸ on Saturn (the final traces) for σ ≤ T ÷ 8, since few forced
    collisions see the sun; those capped are refused. A variance reduction for a view whose lit air
    is far along its ray is not built.
  - _The aggregates under a low sun_: `earth`'s `flux-s80` misses its cap (σ_F ÷ F up to
    3.9 × 10⁻³), and Mars's fluxes are heavy-tailed, the dust's forward delta caught only by the rare
    hemisphere ray within 0.08° of the sun (`flux-s80` would need 1.2 × 10⁷ by the pilot).
  - _Earth's cost_: R08.T3.a's column puts a shell boundary at each of its ~980 levels below the top,
    so each estimate's transmittance crosses some thousand shells at eight points each, about 4 ms of
    CPU a sample at a wavelength.
  - _The depth-to-space walk_ is repeated, with the absorbers' columns, in
    `depth_and_columns_to_space_from` and `beam_optical_depth`, so that a case with no absorber keeps
    its bits by the old code: a later change to one must be made to both (the Rust review). A fused
    walk that took the depths and the columns at the same nodes would save the second height of
    each node on an absorber case's sun legs (the Rust review; not measured).
  - _`TooManySamples`_ also names an overflow of the run's blocks past 2⁶⁴, as `u64::MAX` samples.
  - §2.5 (circumsolar virtual importance sampling) stays unbuilt (ruling 8), main's deferred item:
    three near-sun geometries of `mars` are refused, `ground-s90-v75-a0`, `ground-s90-v85-a0` and
    `ground-s95-v85-a0`, each falling as N^(−1/2) and short of its cap only by the budget's 10.9 min;
    no near-sun geometry failed to scale, in the pilots or the final trace.
  - _Heavy tails away from the sun_: `mars`'s `disc-p30` (red) and green `flux-s0`, and
    `saturn-oblate`'s `equator-s60-v85-a0` (blue), caught a rare heavy path, so their σ does not fall
    as N^(−1/2) from the first quarter (4.6, 0.54 and 0.70 of its prediction); all three refused.
- **Deviations in T13.a, as built** (2026-10-27; `crates/hyperion-fit/src/atmosphere/`: `sweep.rs`,
  `metric.rs`, `metric_verdicts.json` and `sweep_smoke.case.json` (new), `mod.rs`, `transport.rs`;
  `cli.rs`, `lib.rs`; `tests/atmosphere_sweep.rs` (new); `view/atmosphere/reference/`: `twin.ts`,
  `twin.test.ts`, `sweepCases.test.ts`, `metricVerdicts.test.ts` and the eight
  `ms-sweep-w*.case.json` (new), `geometries.ts`; `test/atmosphereSweep.ts` (new); `.prettierignore`.
  Rulings: `decision-r08-t13-scope.md`, rulings 1–8 and 12, "#107's twin ground" and "#107's floor
  misses", 2026-10-27).
  - _The sweep case_ (`SWEEP_FORMAT` 1, `sweep.rs`'s module documentation): the template (radius,
    H, top, ground albedo, 550 nm, the sun's irradiance 1, the 0.5° cone, ρ), ω, the fifteen τ with
    their roles (`tauRoles`) and β₀ (`extinctionPerM`, β₀ H (1 − e^(−12.5)) = τ to 10⁻¹²), the u
    grid once (`phaseU`, `PHASE_TABLE_U`), the 54 geometries with their image, `kind` and
    `groundConeShare`, the aggregate, N_p, the seeds, the floor scan's grounds
    (`scanGroundAlbedos`), and per column its g, its phase (`rayleigh`, or `tabulated` with `a1`),
    its points and twin rows by τ candidate, and its scan points and twin rows by scan ground.
  - _The CLI_: `atmosphere-sweep <case> --out <file> --work <dir>` with
    `--cpu-per-vertex-us X` and `--vroom-cpu-per-vertex-us Y`, and optionally
    `--point-cap-cpu-h 24`, `--threads N`, `--max-points N` and `--pilot-only --points I,J,…`; and
    `--smoke --out <file> [--threads N]`. Both CPU figures are required, with no default
    (reading 2). `--max-points` is added: it stops after N points, for
    the resumption test and a planned stop. Exit 2 for a missing argument or an unknown `--points`
    index, 1 for any other failure.
  - _The counts_: T12.e's rule rounded up to whole blocks of 1,024 (`BLOCK_SAMPLES`), the geometry
    cap rounded down to whole blocks, both at least N_p. The aggregate's target is 0.0025 F, F
    direct plus diffuse; its miss is recorded, never a stop.
  - _The work directory_: `<work>/<case>-<16 hex digits>/point-NNNN.json`, written beside and
    renamed. The key is the SHA-256 of `SWEEP_FORMAT`, the case's SHA-256 (its line ends read as
    LF), the binary's SHA-256, the mode and the settings; the binary's hash stands for the crate's
    version (reading 4). A kept point of another τ, ground or index is refused as stale.
  - _The output_: the head (`format`, `kind`, `case`, `caseSha256`, `binarySha256`, `settings`,
    `pilotSamples`, `geometries`), then a cell or a point a line, numbers to seven significant
    figures. A cell: ω, g, A, VROOM, `kind`, `tauStar`, its walk's points, `floorMisses`,
    `listedRefusals`, `scanPoints`, `fixedMisses`, `groundMisses` (each with the least albedo it
    fails over), `unsortedMisses` and `albedoStar`, the misses by name. A point: its index, τ, ω,
    g, A, VROOM, `pilotSeed`, `class` (`pass`, `drift`, `reach` or `scan`), the projection, CPU and
    wall time, and its final trace's seed, samples, L, σ and first quarter's σ by geometry, the
    twin echoed, the failing and refused geometries by index into the head's `geometries` (names
    would put a file walked to τ 8 past the 450 kB line), and the aggregate; a capped point its
    pilot instead. N_q is ⌊N ÷ 4⌋, not written. `cpuS` is Linux's alone (`/proc/self/stat`,
    `USER_HZ` 100), else `null`.
  - _The floor scan_ ("#107's floor misses", items 1 and 2): each column's τ 1/32 again over grey
    grounds of 0, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5 and 0.8, after its walk, under the walk's counts and
    caps and never cut: 350 points, indices 750 + 7 × (ω row × 7 + g column) + ground, the bright
    column's 1,093 + ground, seeded as the walk's. The walk is ruling 5's: its floor misses set no
    τ*. `sort_floor` then sorts each geometry that fails at the floor τ over any ground, the walk's
    own included: fixed if it fails over the black ground, ground if it passes there, unsorted if
    it is refused or not traced there; A* is the least albedo of a ground miss, else 1. The bright
    column's scan repeats (1, 0)'s on its own seeds. `classifyRegime`'s ground line and
    `ThickBoundary`'s `albedoStar` are c2's (item 3, in the split note).
  - _Main's readings as applied_:
    1. (1, 0.75) at τ 8 (point 74) is the pilot's fourteenth point.
    2. Vertices are counted in `Scratch` beside the draws (`trace_counted`), once a `visit` past the
       stage check; the projection is the pilot's counted vertices a sample times the given CPU a
       vertex, by estimator. The three pinned-bits tests pass with their values untouched.
    3. Masked when outputs are compared: `cpuS`, `wallS`, `cpuPerVertexUs` and `cpuPerSampleUs`; a
       resumed point keeps its first run's.
    4. Index ω row × 105 + g column × 15 + τ candidate, the bright column 735 + τ candidate, the

    5. The default compare: τ 1 of `ms-sweep-w1000`'s g 0 and g 0.75 columns and of the bright

    6. All three τ* scenarios are projected, the scan with each.
    7. τ is vertical, ground to top, at 550 nm; both pipelines read the file's β₀.
    8. The bright file is `ms-sweep-w1000-a800.case.json`.
    9. The twin reads `TABLE_SIZES.high`.
  - _The near-sun listing_: "within 15°" is read inclusively, to 10⁻¹² in cosine:

- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)** (R08.T13.a). Recorded and deferred: each leaves the
  algorithm and every contract as they are.
  - _The tracer is cheaper than the model_: 8.79 µs a vertex under R08.T12.c's estimator and 4.00
    under VROOM (5.57 and 2.66 on a cooler machine), against §3.7's 30–60, and part b 0.71–0.98
    CPU-days against the ruling's 6–14. VROOM's split paths count as vertices, so its figure is not
    the other's.
  - _The ground misses_: at (0.9, 0.75), τ 1/32, the twin reads 1.98 and 1.48 times the reference at
    `ground-s30-v60-a180` and `ground-s60-v60-a90` over the 0.3 ground (σ ÷ L 0.6%), but 1.04 × 10⁻³
    over a black one, the single scattering: Hillaire's ground bounce scattered isotropically, where
    a g 0.75 phase sends back about a quarter of it. The smoke sorts both as ground misses, A* 0.02.
    The scan's pilot, provisional at its own σ: A* 1 in every g 0 column, 0.2 at g 0.3, 0.1 at g 0.5,
    0.02–0.05 at g 0.65 and 0.02 from g 0.75; so a VROOM medium over any ground but black routes
    thick by the ground line, Mars's 0.25 among them (item 4), and Earth's 0.1 stays thin by it at
    ḡ 0.3 or less.
  - _Fixed misses over the black ground_ (the scan's pilot, provisional): none at g ≤ 0.5; from
    g 0.65, in most columns, the disc at phases 0° to 60°, and at g 0.85 and 0.9 a few views at 75°
    to 85° (`ground-s30-v85-a0` the most) and one limb, 0 to 5 geometries a column. c1 meets the
    disc on `mars`.
  - _Provisional verdicts_ (the pilot's own σ, 1–10% of L; they set nothing): the twin leaves the
    metric at τ ½–1 in most columns; at (1, 0), τ 1, 36 of 54 geometries, the ground views reading
    0.42–0.89 of the reference, and over the bright ground all 54 (0.24–0.81). Earth's (0.99, 0.3) and
    Mars's (0.95, 0.65) cells fail 26 and 23 geometries at τ ½, so their τ* may fall below their
    worst channels' 0.394 and 0.508; Earth classified thick is to be raised (item 4).
  - _The aerial read is mirrored_: `twin.ts` repeats `aerialRead.wgsl`'s slice mapping and first
    slice's fade, which no CPU read exports; a change to one must be made to both.
  - _The pilot's σ at 2,048 samples_ may understate a heavy tail at depth (T12.c's coefficient of
    variation 3–7 at τ 2–4); the final trace's `noisy` refusal then stops the column as `reach`, and
    part b may cost more than its projection.
  - _The output's margin_: an ω file projects to about 390 kB, 436 kB at the worst, under the 450 kB
    line but not far; a file past it is split by halves of g (ruling 8), part b's to do.
  - _The hashed files' line ends_: a case's SHA-256 is taken over its text with CRLF read as LF, so a
    checkout that writes CRLF keeps its work directory; a `.gitattributes` rule keeping the sweep
    cases LF is outside the lane.
  - _ρ's citation_: `rayleigh.ts` cites Sneep and Ubachs 2005, eq. 7, for ρ = 6(F_K − 1) ÷ (3 + 7F_K);
    the paper was not read (the science check), and the formula is Bodhaine et al. 1999's eqs. 1 and
    22 inverted, which it reproduces.
- **Deviations in T13.c1, as built** (2026-10-27; `view/atmosphere/reference/`: `twin.ts` and
  `twin.test.ts`, `caseGate.ts`, `caseGate.test.ts` and `caseGate.json` (new); `.prettierignore`.
  Rulings: `decision-r08-t13-scope.md`, rulings 1, 10 and 12, "#107's twin ground" and "#107's floor
  misses", 2026-10-27).
  - _The twin's additions_ (`reference/twin.ts`). The sphere's default path makes the same calls in
    the same order: `twin.test.ts`'s earlier tests and `sweepCases.test.ts`'s default compare pass
    unchanged, so the eight sweep cases stay current.
    - `TwinFigure` is `cases.ts`'s `CaseFigure`. A `spheroid` builds `oblatePlanetTwin` on its level
      spheroid and gravity and reads it as `tablesCpuOblate.test.ts` drives it:
      `oblateSkyViewTexelsTwin` and `oblateSkyViewReadTwin` on the ground,
      `oblateRayMarchTargetTexelTwin` from orbit, `oblateAerialPerspectiveTwin`, and the lit ground by
      `surfaceLightingTwin` over `oblateIrradianceTwin`'s bands at the point's geodetic latitude,
      normal and sun azimuth. New: `spheroidGroundDistanceM`, `figureGroundDistanceM`, `twinDatum`;
      `groundConeShare` takes either figure. A spheroid of a sphere's radii reads the sphere within
      10⁻⁶ (a test).
    - `TwinOptions` gains `slicing` (`body`, or `single`: one slice at κ 1 and one band at s 1, read
      by the `single` fit), `transmittanceSteps` (`split`, or `equal`: R05's 256 equal steps, the
      transmittance built from the medium with its layer edges dropped) and `marchSteps` (`pieces`,
      or `placed`: every march, the multiple-scattering and sky-irradiance tables' and the per-frame
      ones', on the medium with its edges dropped, the multiple scattering placed by R05.T12.e's
      rule). On a medium with no layer edge both steps' options read the default to the bit (a
      test); on one with edges they are built on one slice and one band alone, a `RangeError`
      otherwise, which no case meets. Both drop every tabulated term's edges, not the slab's alone,
      as R05's tables had none.
    - `ReferenceTwin` gains `oblate` and `transmittanceAlong`: the composite's transmittance along a
      direction from the observer (`compositeTransmittanceTwin`, `oblateCompositeTransmittanceTwin`
      on the spheroid), towards the sun the drawn beam, and along a limb its line of sight.
    - _No drawn surface for a ground observer_: no ground view of the four cases has a cone that meets
      the ground (85° and the 0.5° cone stay above the horizon at 1 m; the record's `attribution`
      lists none), so none is built, and the twin refuses a ground view that would need one
      (`RangeError`, a test).
    - `tablesCpu.ts` and the other read-only modules are untouched, and no `export` is added.
  - _The harness_ (`reference/caseGate.ts`, with no runtime import outside `view/atmosphere/` and
    none from `test/`, for R08.T14.f). Every value read from a twin (`TwinValueSpec`: a radiance, a
    surface share, a beam, a line of sight, a per-channel drawn surface, the downwelling irradiance)
    is kept at seven significant figures, and the record is a pure function of the cases, their
    references and those values (`caseGateRecord`), so its verdicts are the recorded values'. The
    record's head names the references' radiance it reads (`RecordHead.radiance`): `scalar` here,
    `vector` for R08.T14.f. Seven twins: each case's own (`caseTwin`: its medium, figure and
    curves, its `sunIlluminanceLx` as the irradiance, `TABLE_SIZES.high`), `saturn-oblate`'s of one
    slice and one band, read at its nine limbs alone, where the check looks, and `earth-ozone-slab`'s
    of equal steps and of R05.T12.e's placement, read at the slab's runs' geometries alone.
  - _The record_ (`caseGate.json`, 233,644 B, through `bless.ts`'s `expectCommittedTable` from a `{}`
    placeholder, in `.prettierignore`): a head (its writer, the twin's settings, `gate.ts`'s
    constants, every table's columns); each case's headline, tally and images, and a geometry a line
    (image, kind, cone share, and per channel L_twin, surface share, L_ref, σ_ref, T, verdict and
    |ΔL| ÷ (T + 4σ_ref)); the runs below; and last the twin's values the geometry lines do not hold,
    a key a line. Under a bless or `HYPERION_SLOW_TESTS=1` every value is computed. By default the
    record is computed from its own values and held byte for byte, and 15 values of three twins,
    `earth-ozone-slab`'s (each draw, a beam, a line of sight, a per-channel surface), `mars`'s (its
    tabulated dust) and `saturn-oblate`'s, are recomputed and held equal to them, as
    `sweepCases.test.ts` holds the sweep's. A case's `headline` is `pass` where no comparison
    misses; refused comparisons are counted beside it and pass nothing. The
    hard checks are ruling 12's blockers (a twin value non-finite or negative: none), the record's
    currency and its coverage of every geometry; every verdict is recorded, none asserted.

- **Deviations in T0, as built** (2026-10-09; in `view/engine/webgpu/`, `compute.ts`,
  `kernelResources.ts`, `resources.ts`, `drawing.ts` and their tests; `smoke/work.ts` and
  `smoke/page.ts`). R01's seam as the task gives it. What differs:
  - _The type table is all of WebGPU's §6.2.1 list._ Beyond the task's, `texture_1d` and
    `texture_storage_1d` give `1d`, and `texture_depth_multisampled_2d` gives `2d`.
    `texture_external` binds an external texture, not a view, and gives `undefined`, as buffers and
    samplers do. `TextureSpec` has no 1D texture, so a `1d` declaration refuses every texture.
  - _A name with no declared dimension._ A texture given under a name the kernel does not declare,
    or declares as a buffer, a sampler or a type the table does not read, is viewed at its own
    dimension (a cube's storage as the six-layer `2d-array`), unchecked, as before T0. It is refused
    where it was before: `kernelBindGroupEntries` throws for an undeclared name inside the
    dispatch's encoding, so `engine.test.ts`'s "leave out a dispatch whose encoding threw" still
    exercises the timer's rollback, and WebGPU refuses a kind mismatch.
  - _"Before any GPU call."_ `resolveKernelResources` looks up and checks every sampled and storage
    texture before it makes or writes a uniform buffer or makes a view, and `dispatch` calls it
    before it encodes. A mismatch now throws from `dispatch` itself, before any writer is recorded,
    where before the call returned and WebGPU refused the submission. No caller mismatches today
    (`tables.ts`, `hillaire.ts`, the sky's `bake.ts` and the post kernels checked by review). The
    message also names the texture, as "kernel K declares B as D, but T is O", where O is `cube`
    for a cube bound as storage.

    Creation" (`"2d-array"` asks only that the texture be `2d`, whatever its layer count). Its
    unit test moves with it from `drawing.test.ts` to `resources.test.ts`.
  - _Tests beyond the task:_ `kernelBindings` over the whole table; a refusal leaves no uniform
    buffer, queue write or view; a cube refused where `texture_storage_2d` is declared; a texture
    under a name declared as a uniform keeps its own dimension.

  Provides names them, with additions. `Dispersion` gains `compressibility` (Z at the reference
  state), `dataFile` (the refractiveindex.info file, or `undefined`) and `measuredNm` (the fitted
  span). `Gas` is derived from `GASES`, and each species is one entry in each of `GAS_DISPERSION`,
  `GAS_KING_FACTOR` (`KingFactor { factor, source }`; `kingFactor` reads it) and
  `GAS_MOLAR_MASS_G_PER_MOL` (below, "Species"). The module also exports
  `RAYLEIGH_WAVELENGTH_RANGE_NM` (300–1,000 nm vacuum; outside it a `RangeError`, a unit error),
  `BOLTZMANN_J_PER_K`, `referenceNumberDensityPerM3`,
  `crossSectionFromDispersionM2(dispersion, kingFactorAt, wavelengthNm)` (F_K passed as a function
  of the wavelength, so that it is taken where n is), and the Earth check's `DRY_AIR_DISPERSION`
  and `dryAirKingFactor`. Two science-checker agents checked Design note 4's table against the
  primary sources, and their key figures were recomputed; a third reviewed the result. Main
  adopted every lean below on 2026-10-09. Design note 4 stands as written; these corrections
  supersede it. _Superseded 2026-10-09:_ Design note 4's table is now T3.b's as built, with these
  corrections (lane docs-consistency, bringing the plans in line with the signed-off brainstorm):
  - **CH₄** takes He, Fang, Shoshanim, Brown and Rudich, Atmos. Chem. Phys. 21 (2021) 14927,
    eq. 10: 10⁸(n − 1) = 3,603.09 + 4.403 62 × 10¹⁴ ÷ (1.1741 × 10¹⁰ − ν²), at 288.15 K, fitted
    over 264–671 nm, with F_K = 1. Sneep and Ubachs 2005's eq. 18 is a fit to Hohm 1993's
    polarisabilities. It runs 13% high in n − 1 against Loria 1909, Rollefson and Havens 1940 and
    the static polarisability, and Wilmouth and Sayres 2019 measured 22% below it. He et al.'s
    formula matches Loria to 0.5% over 529–658 nm.
  - **O₂** takes refractiveindex.info's 1.181 494 × 10⁻⁴ + 9.708 931 × 10⁻³ ÷ (75.4 − λ⁻²), at
    20 °C, cited to Křen, Appl. Opt. 50 (2011) 6484, which refits Zhang et al.'s data. Zhang, Lu
    and Wang 2008's own eq. 20, 15,532.45 + 456,402.97 ÷ (50 − λ⁻²), holds only over 740–860 nm.
    The tests hold the formula to Zhang's eq. 20 within 0.1% over 740–860 nm, to Bates's O₂
    (Sneep and Ubachs, eq. 23) within 0.2% over 300–546 nm, and to Peck and Reeder's dry air
    within 0.1% through the mixture. _Open:_ Křen's comment was not read (Optica, closed). Reading
    it would settle the coefficients and the 20 °C state.
  - **N₂** takes Peck and Khanna's own 15 °C form, 6,497.378 + 3,073,864.9 ÷ (144 − λ⁻²) (their
    abstract), from 468 nm. Sneep and Ubachs's eq. 10, 6,498.2 + …, is their 0 °C form scaled as an
    ideal gas and runs 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ higher. Below 468 nm the module takes Bates 1984's ultraviolet
    branch (Sneep and Ubachs, eq. 11), which joins it to 4 × 10⁻⁷.
  - **CO₂** takes Bideau-Mehu et al. 1973 at 0 °C, as Sneep and Ubachs's eq. 13 corrects it.
    Their printed last numerator, 0.121 814 5 × 10⁻⁴, is 10⁴ too small: only 0.121 814 5
    reproduces their Table 2's 13.29, and it is what refractiveindex.info's 0 °C copy carries.
    Their printed prefactor, 1.1427 × 10⁶, is 10³ too large.
  - **King factors.** "Hohm 1993" (Mol. Phys. 78, 929) is the hydrocarbon mean-polarisability
    paper. The anisotropies are in Hohm 1994 (Chem. Phys. 179, 533), which was not read.
    - H₂ takes 1.0312 + 3.09 × 10⁻⁴ λ⁻² (1.0322 at 550 nm). This is 1 + (2/9)(γ ÷ ᾱ)² for the
      v = 0, J = 0 averages of Raj, Hamaguchi and Witek 2018's ab initio α∥ and α⊥ (J. Chem.
      Phys. 148, 104308; data public), fitted over 380–800 nm. With it, the module's H₂ runs
      7.0% above Dalgarno and Williams 1962 (6.9% with the ideal N); Design note 4's "6.5% low"
      is the same gap seen from the other side.
    - H₂O's 1.001 is now cited: Murphy 1977, ρ = (3.0 ± 1.4) × 10⁻⁴ for linear polarisation,
      which gives F_K = 1.0010 ± 0.0005.
    - _Open:_ NH₃ takes F_K = 1, provisional and probably about 1% low. Reading Hohm 1994 or

      Keir 1995's measurement.
  - **The real gas.** N_ref = p ÷ (Z k_B T), with Z = p ÷ (ρRT) from the NIST Chemistry

    NH₃, 1.36% for CO₂ and Xe, 0.55% for Kr and at most 0.15% for the rest (_superseded
    2026-10-10_ by T3.b's follow-up: NH₃ 0.37%, and the rest within 0.21%). Air takes CIPM-2007's
    0.999 592. He et al.'s CH₄ and N₂O take Z = 1, because their n is defined through the ideal N.
