  - _Split out._ NH₃ (C2018's 243.7M transitions need a super-line reduction) and N₂O's TYM part
    went to the new R08.T4.g (chain §§9–11). Both are `PENDING_ABSORBERS` entries naming it.
    N₂O's bound (§11, ruling 3) is TYM's 296 K cells over 380–712 nm, 2.21 × 10⁻³² m² at 713 nm
    (T4.c's 1.29 × 10⁻³² bound for TYM's part below 713.4 nm plus its excess there), and TYM's
    excess over HITRAN2024's cells from 714 nm, taken in decimal arithmetic so that no cell rounds
    a step high. At the helium Rayleigh caps TYM's cells over 380–712 nm reach τ 72 (706 nm) and
    64 (669 nm), and 0.48 at 600 nm (the 713 nm cell's bound, τ 142), which is why the part stays
    pending rather than dropped. The "τ ≈ 26 at 600 nm" first reported was wrong.
  - _Pending entries._ A species leaves R08.T4.d's list when its table is committed, a test
    holding the two together, and every T4.d species has. Two entries are new:
    - Hot CO₂ in R08.T4.f, at HITRAN's 500 K row and `estimated`, since T4.d's table is held at
      500 K.
    - A gap found and closed: CO's 8–0 to 13–0 bands. HITRAN2024 holds none; Li et al. 2015
      (ApJS 216, 15) list them to Δv = 11, but those are dropped (its 9–0 exceeds its 8–0); 12–0
      and 13–0 are in no list. They are an overtone-ladder estimate below HITRAN2024's 7–0, owned
      by R08.T4.f. The largest cell is 3.03 × 10⁻³⁵ m² at 609 nm (the 8–0 R head, 608.5 nm), and
      a window anywhere holds at most 4.45 × 10⁻³⁵, under T4.c's 5.1 × 10⁻³⁵.

    Bounds and listings gain an optional `part`, so that one task holds two entries for a key
    (CO's `overtones` beside its hot list), keyed by key, task and part.

  - _The species, as fetched._
    - The ladder species, C₂H₂, C₂H₄, C₂H₆, CH₃OH and PH₃, all take the overtone-ladder estimate:
      no measured visible band intensity was read, the papers found being closed (the plan's first
      route). Their anchors are HITRAN2024's: C₂H₂'s 3ν₃ moved to 15,600 cm⁻¹ at 10⁻², C₂H₄'s ν₉ to
      14,300 cm⁻¹ and C₂H₆'s ν₇ to 13,800 cm⁻¹ at 10⁻⁴, CH₃OH's ν₈ to 13,600 cm⁻¹ at 10⁻³, and
      PH₃'s ν₁ + ν₃ to 13,700 cm⁻¹ at 10⁻⁵. Each table's basis is `estimated` at every node.
    - HCN: HITRAN2024's 1,918 lines reach 568.6 nm (17,585.79 cm⁻¹). ExoMol's Harris list,
      T4.f's hot entry, reaches no further (its first cell 569 nm), so T4.d takes HITRAN2024
      alone.
    - Karman et al. 2018's sets replace T4.c's single temperatures in the 1 nm bins they cover
      whole: O₂–O₂'s B (675.4–703.9 nm) and A (746.2–781.1 nm) bands and O₂–N₂'s A band. A pair
      table has one measured range, so O₂–O₂ is `measured` over 206–287 K and its A and B bands
      `estimated` at 287–346 K, while 203–206 K, `measured` in T4.c, is now `estimated`. O₂–N₂ is
      `measured` over 206–346 K. The bins outside Karman's coverage keep their one temperature,
      held.
    - Ranges: H₂O runs from 150 K; CO₂, N₂O and HCN from 100 K; O₂, CO, H₂ and the five ladder
      species from 50 K. All run to 500 K and are `measured` only to 296 K, HITRAN's 500 K values
      lacking hot lines (follow-up 5). The ladder species are not cut at their own saturation, so
      their estimated intervals at 50–75 K lie where none can be a gas.
    - Caps: only O₂ (§4.1's derivation) and CO₂ (Span and Wagner 1996) take the saturation cap.
      Every other species is gated to the 400 p_eff ÷ (m g) and Rayleigh caps, which gates more
      columns, not fewer.
  - _Storage._ Binary as ruled (§9): "HYKD" parts under 500 kB, and a JSON sidecar per species
    listing them with their SHA-256; `?url` in the worker, `?inline` in tests. O₂–O₂'s widened
    sets moved to `oxygenPairs.json` (165 kB), since `crossSections.json` (405 kB with H₂O's
    continuum) has no room left under the hook. Neither the loader nor a test checks a part's
    recorded bytes and SHA-256; the sidecars list them. Bytes are under _Figures_.
  - _CO₂'s χ_ (§§12–13, superseding §10's Perrin and Hartmann 1989 sets and their 193 K hold).
    - The sets are SpeCT's (Chaverot et al. 2025, A&A 702, A137; CC BY 4.0) under its Eq. 11
      shape, `wingShape: "quantumAsymmetric"` (`chiWingFactor`): beyond σ₁, x ÷ (1 − e^(−x)) with
      x = c₂(ν − ν₀) ÷ T, times ν(1 − e^(−c₂ν/T)) ÷ (ν₀(1 − e^(−c₂ν₀/T))). The wing is therefore
      signed in ν − ν₀, and `lineShape` and the cell spectrum take the offset and the centre. The
      beyond-cut-off share averages the two sides at the cell's centre.
    - CO₂–N₂'s B₂ α is the coded 0.00167, not Table 2's printed 0.0167 (option (a)). The source
      record names the misprint and its evidence: SpeCT's `fcts.f90` (commit e7c4579c08) is a
      finding aid, one number read and nothing copied or run.
    - Holds: CO₂–CO₂ outside 218–751 K, CO₂–N₂ outside 295–773 K. Cousin et al. 1985 is not in
      SpeCT's compilation, so the 295 K hold stays. `CHI_HELD_BELOW_K` is gone; `chiSlopes`
      clamps to each set's own `measuredRangeK`.
    - The reach is 293 cm⁻¹ by the rule (χ < 10⁻³ at every temperature over 100–500 K), tested;
      §10's 247 cm⁻¹ (itself not §8's 246) is superseded.
    - The science check against SpeCT's lab compilation (Zenodo 15564294) with HITRAN2024's lines:
      CO₂–CO₂ +0.04 in mean ln(model ÷ lab) (rms 0.11) at 295 K against Perrin and Hartmann's
      −0.71 (rms 1.10), and SpeCT's set without the Eq. 11 shape −0.42 (rms 0.50). CO₂–N₂'s
      coded set ties with Perrin and Hartmann's, rms 0.417 against 0.375 over Perrin et al.
      1989's six temperatures and Burch et al.'s ν3 (the printed set's 0.526), within the lab
      sets' own 0.15–0.45 disagreement. At 296 K the printed 0.0167 errs −0.70 on Perrin et al.'s
      data and −0.43 on Burch et al.'s, the coded +0.04 and +0.33.
    - The fixed-g mix (§16). The first passes' 50/50 test failed the tier, 1.0 × 10⁻² at 715 nm, 250
      K and 1 MPa, at a node, so no refinement could cure it, and the merge refused. As ruled, the
      reduction now tests the mix at w = 0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 0.95 and records each cell's
      u_mix(w, T) in the sidecar's `mixing`, by share and by each of the 29 tested temperatures,
      beside each share's worst error, and the merge no longer refuses on it. A sample inside an
      `estimated` interval sets none (§17): there the chain's own interpolation erred, not the mix,
      and the least over every node had judged Venus by a 218.75 K state it never has.
      `kDistribution.ts`'s `mixLimitColumnM2(table, cell, w, T)` gives u_mix at a body's w and
      temperature for R08.T10.a: at each share the least over the samples bracketing T (the end
      sample's where held), then ln u linear in w between the shares, the end values held beyond,
      and the recorded column where a neighbour records none. CO₂'s record:
      three of its 187 cells hold a u_mix within the cap, none at w = 0.95, so that Venus (w ≈ 0.97,
      read at its 500 K hold) takes no label from the mix. 715 nm: from 2.8 × 10²⁸ cm⁻² at w = 0.5
      and 500 K (3.48 × 10²⁸ at 0.25, 4.15 × 10²⁸ at 0.75, 9.16 × 10²⁸ at 0.05), 7–9 × 10²⁸ at
      244–262 K. 660 nm: 1.96–4.7 × 10²⁹ over 287.5–450 K at w = 0.25–0.75. 722 nm: 1.86–4.9 ×
      10²⁹ over 212.5–300 K at w = 0.25–0.75. Each share's worst error over every tested state:
      5.2, 12.2, 10.3, 5.45 and 3.95 × 10⁻³. The sidecar is 180 kB with the record.
    - How the record was made. The full per-temperature rerun was killed by the machine's freeze
      at 05:10. The seven cells to which §16's first run (all 187 cells, the least over every node)
      gave a finite u_mix, 654, 660, 708, 709, 714, 715 and 722 nm, were rerun alone with the
      per-temperature record: their 16-bit codes, weights, offset and step are the first run's
      byte for byte (`cmp`, all seven identical; memory peak 1.20 GB). They were spliced into the
      first run's partials, and the other 180 cells, none at every share there, took none at every
      tested temperature, since the first run's record is the least over them. The merged parts
      are the first run's byte for byte.
  - _Held χ_ (§14). The sidecar stores `chiHeld[t][v]`, whether node t's variant v holds its
    set's coefficients, and `kDistributionAt` returns it for the variants the mix takes. The
    reduction marks no held node `estimated`: whether a hold is visible is R08.T10.a's test on
    the body's own column (T10.a's text carries it). T4.d's `chiVisible` rule, which had labelled
    Earth's CO₂ `estimated` over the gated columns, was removed.
  - _Width exponents_ (§13, ruling 4). HITRAN2024's n_self, n_H2, n_He, n_CO2 and n_H2O are
    parsed (fields 9–17). Each sidecar's `broadeningExponents` holds n̄_j − n̄_air, each n̄ the
    S γ-weighted mean over the lines that give γ_j, with n_air standing in where a line gives no
    n_j. An offset under 10⁻⁶ (`EXPONENT_OFFSET_FLOOR`) is 0: it moves (296 ÷ T)^Δn by under
    2 × 10⁻⁶ over 50–500 K, and H₂'s γ_H2 and n_H2, HITRAN2024's γ_air and n_air to their printed
    digits, leave −7.5 × 10⁻¹². `broadeningFactor(table, mixture, T)` folds them in as
    p_eff = p Σ_j x_j r_j (296 ÷ T)^(n̄_j − n̄_air), the first-order form; the second-order
    remainder, ½(σ²_j − σ²_air) ln²(296 ÷ T) with σ² the S γ-weighted variance of n, is not
    taken. The merge's `--lines` recomputes the ratios and exponents from the line list
    (`withLineBroadening`), and the merge refuses partials whose records are missing or differ.
  - _The 16-bit test_ is gated within each node's cap and recorded beyond it
    (`worstQuantisationBeyondCapError`). Run past the cap, it had refused H₂'s first merge, where
    112 G = 1 cells quantised at 2–5 × 10⁻⁴ only on columns no path holds; H₂ was rerun.
  - _The continuum._ CKD from LOWTRAN 7 (§6): ratios 5.884 foreign and 9.891 self below 567 nm, and
    the self ratio 1.522 of 260 to 296 K. The RRTMG band-24 check gives 1.1781 × 10⁻²⁵ and 1.3876 ×
    10⁻²⁶ cm². Its foreign part is `H2O+air`, an air partner standing for every other listed gas
    weighted by its broadening ratio. It is `measured` as air with N₂ and O₂ and with other gases up
    to 2% of its partner molecules (`AIR_TRACE_SHARE`, §15, ruling 1; Earth's 0.93% Ar among them).
    Beyond that the pair is `estimated` as a whole, a pair's provenance being one label, where the
    ruling's text marks the excess share. The basis holds on the drawn CKD: 2% of its foreign part's
    9.1 × 10⁻³ in red through 38 air masses is 1.8 × 10⁻⁴, about 4 × 10⁻⁴ along a horizontal ray
    (the ruling's 5.7 × 10⁻³ is MT_CKD's, §6.5). The limit is a relative one, stated: it scales with
    the foreign τ, so a humid world whose foreign part passes τ 0.05 in a channel passes 10⁻³ at 2%.
    The continuum's source record says so. A test pins the lines' pedestal to exactly the species
    with a CKD pair, H₂O. Ar itself reports `noCrossSections`: it is in neither the cross-sections
    nor `NO_VISIBLE_ABSORPTION`, for the transparency list (to "main").
  - _Earth's column budget._ Five: O₃, O₂'s lines, O₂–O₂ with O₂–N₂, H₂O's lines, and H₂O's
    continuum. An `AbsorberLayer` is one constant-mixing layer, and the self and foreign pairs'
    overlaps coincide wherever the listed partners span H₂O's layer, so they form one pair
    profile from the start; both pair densities go as ρ² there, and the fold is exact on every
    path, with no fold step coded. The plan's 20% at grazing incidence is that of a water profile
    with its own scale height, which the layer model does not represent until plan 14 publishes
    structure (for R08.T10.a).
  - _The end-to-end test._ Paths run from 1 air mass to the horizon, which is 35 air masses
    without refraction (35.2 by the science check's integration; Kasten and Young 1989's 38.09
    includes refraction), from the ground and from 3 km: 16 paths. The worst channel is
    9.77 × 10⁻⁴ and the worst Δu′v′ 5.13 × 10⁻⁵. The Curtis–Godson error (the path homogeneous at
    its absorber-weighted p and T) is 6.75 × 10⁻⁴.
  - _The rows._
    - A curve's rows run from its table's first node, 10 Pa ÷ f, to the second node past the
      layer's base, so that a p̄ at the base reads a centred stencil. None is cut at the layer's
      top: H₂O's 300 hPa top keeps 12 rows it never reads (10 Pa to 5.6 kPa), which the
      bytes below count. No row is
      cut at a deck: a `cloudDeck` body's rows stop there once its layers are clamped to the deck
      (R08.T10.a, R08.T14).
    - A profile's rows are the nodes of its line species with the largest column
      (`dominantLines`). Another line species on the profile reads its σ between its own nodes at
      each row, then τ between the rows: on O₂'s and H₂O's committed reference cells with the rows
      half a node off their own, the chain errs at most 5.7 × 10⁻⁴ (`lineReferences.test.ts`),
      under the chain's 2 × 10⁻³.
  - _The read between rows._ Earth's O₂ and H₂O curves read at their rows and midway between them,
    at each column node and midway between nodes, keep τ in [0, −ln 10⁻⁶]. The largest fall of τ
    along u at a fixed p̄ is 1.62 × 10⁻⁵ (H₂O; O₂'s 6.4 × 10⁻⁸), gated under the chain's 2 × 10⁻³: a
    fall δ raises T by at most T δ ≤ δ. It is measured on Earth's rows, to 0.32 MPa; the deep rows
    (1–13.3 MPa), where T at fixed u is not monotone in p, are measured on a Venus-class body's CO₂
    (`deepLines.test.ts`, rows to 9.9 MPa, 13.3 MPa of broadening pressure): τ stays in [0, −ln
    10⁻⁶] and never falls along u at the samples.
  - _Arrival_ (§15, ruling 3: a budget line of its own in R08.T11, 5 s a world on the UHD 620
    host, not sharing `BAKE_CEILING_S`).
    - `absorberCurvesBySun` takes the lines' cell exponentials, and each grid point's, once for
      every sun, channel and bin; `absorberCurve` and `absorberCurves` stay one sun's.
    - The curves split by cell across the optics workers: `absorberCurveSums` sums a share's line
      cells (index modulo the share count; share 0 also the points without lines), each share
      carrying its bins' logarithms where its sums underflow, and `absorberCurvesFromSums` joins
      them, equal to the whole within 10⁻¹² in τ (relative where τ passes 1); it refuses a split
      missing a share, or none at all. The workers take the brightest sun's curves first, alone, and
      the others' after; the pool itself is R08.T10.a's.
    - A cell whose largest σ times the curve's top column, 10³ U, is at most 0.02
      (`LINEAR_CELL_DEPTH`) takes its mean σ̄ in that row, one exponential a column: within (σ_max
      u)² ÷ 8, under 4.95 × 10⁻⁵, of its own sum per species (Popoviciu's inequality), so inside the
      ruling's 2 × 10⁻⁴ for a cell of up to four species. Earth's figures above are unchanged by it
      to three figures.
    - A bin whose every cell's sum underflows takes the cells' sums as logarithms
      (`lineCellLog`), so that its depth stays finite and its read is not NaN, as the bins' were
      before lines (the science check's second round; a regression test holds it).
    - Measured on the development machine (Ryzen 7 3700X, 16 threads) at a load average of 15–25
      from other lanes' runs, in a vitest worker, three runs each: Earth's specs 0.66–0.80 s; the
      curves of its four profiles under four suns, channels and bins, 2.2–2.8 s on one worker; split
      four ways, the slowest share 1.0–1.4 s and the join 0.13–0.23 s; the brightest sun's alone
      first 1.5–2.0 s. H₂O's lines are about three quarters of it. §2.4 estimated 0.6 s, about four
      times low for the whole (about three times, H₂O like for like). The four-way split ran 2.0–2.2
      times faster here, against §15's projected 3–4 times, each share also reading every row's σ
      and its suns' optics. R08.T11 times line arrival on the UHD 620 host, and a thick world's
      curves plus bake.
  - _Not measurable._ H₂O's curve on a CO₂ background: HITRAN2024 gives no γ_CO2, γ_H2 or γ_He
    for H₂O's visible lines, so the background error is 0 by construction, recorded. O₂, CO and
    N₂O do have γ_CO2, and a `background-error` run on one of them would give the p_eff mapping's
    spread once; not run.
  - _The Rayleigh cap._ 5.1 × 10²⁸ cm⁻² at 380 nm from helium's dispersion (§10, ruling 4),
    after Mansfield and Peck 1969, checked below 480 nm against Kurucz 1970's helium after
    Dalgarno 1962 to 0.33%, and tested to half the figure's last digit.
  - _The GPU read_ (T6.c's read sites, widened after T6.d).
    - The pressure profile is `AtmosphereMedium.pressureBar`, p(h) in bar, over 10⁵ Pa
      (`ABSORBER_PRESSURE_REFERENCE_PA`, `medium.ts`), from `column.ts`'s `columnPressureBar`.
      It is one more density-table layer, after the terms', and the medium uniform's `z` flags
      it. A path's p̄ is the Curtis–Godson one (Curtis 1952, QJRMS 78, 638; Godson 1953, QJRMS 79,
      367), each slot's own: 10⁵ Pa × w ÷ x, w = Σ (p ÷ 10⁵ Pa)(u ÷ U).
    - The line slots (`lineSlotMask`, a bitmask in the medium uniform's `w` and the composite's
      `Draw.shell.z`) each take one pressure channel, in slot order (§15, ruling 2): `absorberSpecs`
      puts every species mixed through one layer in one profile, so the well-mixed line species, the
      bulk's, are one slot, and on Earth channel 0 is O₂'s, its pressure-weighted column the bulk's.
      Channels 0–3 stand in `absorberPressureColumns`, one `rgba16float` table of the
      transmittance's size; channel 4, for a medium of five line slots alone, in
      `lastAbsorberPressureColumn`, which is one texel otherwise and is written only then
      (`lastPressureColumnSize`, the kernels' `PRESSURE_CHANNELS_A_TABLE`); the tables make it anew,
      before releasing the old, when a medium's line slots change its size. The twin and the kernels
      name them `pressureColumns` (the TypeScript review: a unit in each name, since the read path
      also carries pressures in Pa and their logarithms). They are bound in every kernel that reads
      the absorber columns (transmittance's outputs 6 and 7, multiple scattering's 7 and 8, the
      sky-view's and aerial perspective's 10 and 11, the march's 11 and 12, and the composite's
      group 2, 9 and 10).
    - Bytes: one 131 kB table where Design note 11 counted one (its "128 KB" was KiB). Earth's
      per-planet tables come to about 1.17 MB on Design note 11's 0.40 MB, with the curves texture's
      0.64 MB at four suns (19 rows a line slot, 1 + 4 × 41 rows of 241 texels), or 1.31 MB counting
      the absorber-column and irradiance tables that 0.40 MB leaves out. A thin Saturn-class world's
      five slices take about 655 kB of pressure columns with up to four line slots (1.31 MB with
      five).
    - `rgba16float` holds a Venus-class grazing chord's w, about 3 × 10³, under its 65,504; a
      high, thin path's w is subnormal where x p̄ is under 6.1 Pa (on Earth's vertical rays above
      about 31 km) and rounds to 0 under about 3 × 10⁻³ Pa, at pressures where a visible line's
      Lorentz width no longer matters. The read floors p̄ at 10⁻³ Pa
      (`ABSORBER_PRESSURE_FLOOR_PA`), so that a 0 reads at the first row rather than at ln 0.
    - The curves texture's row 0 is a header: texel k is [first row, rows, the read's top ln p, 0]
      for absorber slot k, and texel `ABSORBER_SLOTS` holds the block of rows a light. Light s's
      row q for slot k sits at row 1 + s·block + first + q, each texel τ in `rgb` and the row's
      ln p in `a`. `curveDepth` is `absorbers.ts`'s read: 4-point Lagrange in ln p̄ on τ, linear
      on 2–3 rows, then clamped; it finds its row by a scan of the rows' ln p, one load a row,
      which R08.T11's low-setting figure may replace by computing it from the fixed spacing.
      `tablesCpuLines.test.ts` holds the twin to it within 10⁻¹², and the table and a marched ray
      to the `f64` oracle (`opticalDepth.ts`'s `absorberPressuresPa`) within 10⁻³, on a medium
      whose line slot (slot 1, its pair in slot 0) reads channel 0 and on one of five line slots.
    - With pressure rows a march step's absorber depth, the whole path's new depth less its old,
      may fall a little below 0 where the path's p̄ moves. It is not clamped, so that the path's
      sum stays the curve's own depth.
    - The smoke (`smoke/atmosphere.ts`) adds `lineAbsorberMedium` and `fiveLineSlotMedium` at
      the "tables" scope alone, for the 180 s watchdog, with checks of their pressure-column
      tables. Every check passes on both variants: the pressure-column table at 0.49 × 10⁻³ and
      multiple scattering in both arms. The group takes 13.6 s; the whole page took 243 and 234 s
      under a load of 17–21, in a run with `src/smoke/main.ts`'s watchdog raised to 285 s for the
      timing and its source reverted, past the 180 s watchdog with or without the group, which
      the perf-smoke lane fixes centrally ("main").
  - _Readers._ `absorberTransmittance`, `absorberBinTransmittance`, `channelTransmittance` and
    the twin's `curveOpticalDepth` take a required `pressurePa: number | undefined` (the
    TypeScript review), and refuse an absorber with lines read with none. `packAbsorberCurves`
    refuses rows that are not ascending, differ between light slots, stand on a slot without
    lines (or one row on a slot with them), or lack a pressure profile, each in its own words.
    Units are named throughout: `intensitiesCm`, `airHalfWidthsPerCmAtm`,
    `selfHalfWidthsPerCmAtm`, `foreignHalfWidthsPerCmAtm`, `MOLAR_GAS_CONSTANT_J_PER_MOL_K`, and
    the continuum's `self296Cm3`, `self260Cm3` and `foreign296Cm3`.

  - _Acceptance._ The command selects `absorbers.test.ts` and
    `absorbers/{earthLines,kDistribution,lineCurves,lineReferences,transparency,hMinus,heliumMinus}.test.ts`.
    `tablesCpuLines.test.ts`, `tables.test.ts`, `tablesCpu.test.ts`, `hillaire.test.ts` and
    `src/tools/{kDistributions,kDistributionsReduce,molecularLines,waterContinuum,atmosphereData}.test.ts`
    run under `pnpm test`.
  - _For R08.T10.a._
    - CO₂'s fixed-g mix labels by `mixLimitColumnM2` at the body's w, `Broadening.selfShare`,
      and its profile's temperature (§§16–17).
    - The optics worker passes `loadKDistributions`' tables and `bulkMoleFractions` to
      `absorberSpecs`; without the tables a line species reports `noCrossSections`. The bulk
      gases are listed as layers spanning the column, since `H2O+air`'s partners are the other
      listed gases. It runs the curve shares on its pool (`absorberCurveSums`).
    - `PairCrossSection` does not carry `estimatedBelowNm`, so the k = 100 margin applies below
      567 nm only if T10.a reads the table's field.
    - f₃ needs γ_L at the body's largest p_eff. The sidecars give it only through
      `beyondCutoffShare` (γ_L = 12.5π × share, to two figures, the largest over the cells),
      which `readKDistribution` does not read.
    - The Mars-class half of T4.d's Earth-like test is T10.a's (`decision-r08-t4d-kdist.md`
      §6.7), with its line in T10.a's Tests from "main".
  - _For "main"_ (§6.7 and §15): R08.T4.b's ranking bullet gains "after H₂O's two continuum pairs

- **Deviations in T4.g, as built** (2026-10-14). New `src/tools/superLines.ts`, `exomolLines.ts`
  and `exomolCli.ts`, with `superLines.test.ts`, `exomolLines.test.ts` and `exomolCli.test.ts`;
  `atmosphereData.ts`'s new subcommands (`exomol-bands`, `exomol-bins`, `exomol-k-distributions`,
  `exomol-k-distributions-merge`, `exomol-cell-references`); `kDistributions.ts`'s spectrum source,
  `kDistributionsCli.ts`'s shared cell reduction and table source, and `lineReferences.ts`'s shared
  cell reference; the data `absorbers/exomol/kDistributions/NH3.json` and `NH3-<n>.bin`,
  `N2O.json` and `N2O-<n>.bin`, `exomol/lineReferencesNH3.json`, `lineReferencesN2O.json` and
  `n2oMerge.json`, `exomol/bounds.json` rewritten, `absorbers/kDistributions/N2O.json` and
  `N2O-1.bin` removed; `absorbers/transparency.ts` and its test, a new
  `absorbers/exomolLines.test.ts`, `lineReferences.test.ts`; `exomol/README.md`, `NOTICE`,
  `.prettierignore`. The scope is `decision-r08-t4d-kdist-chain.md` §§9–11 on T4.d's machinery.
  - _The spectrum source._ `reduceGridCell` and `belowGridError` take a `NodeSpectra`, one node's
    sorted spectrum for a mix of the policy's variants, in place of a `LineSpecies`: T4.d's is
    `lineByLine(species, policy)`, T4.g's `superLineSpectra` and N₂O's `mergedSpectra`, so that one
    reduction and one set of tests reads them all. `cellNodeOf` builds a node's shares from any
    spectrum. `runKDistributions`' cell work is `reducePartialCell`, and `runCellReferences`' is
    `cellReference`, shared by the ExoMol commands; `mergePartials` takes a `TableSource` (its
    inputs' checksums, and a sidecar description where it is not T4.d's), T4.d's made by
    `lineTableSource(source)`, so that its sidecars are written as before. T4.d's tests take
    `lineByLine` and `lineTableSource` at their call sites and pass unchanged.
  - _Super-lines_ (`superLines.ts`). Each line's S(T) is shared linearly between the two nodes of a
    wavenumber grid about it (Hockney and Eastwood 1981), whose step is a twelfth of the Doppler
    half-width at 13,100 cm⁻¹ at that temperature, finer than the plan's tenth of the narrowest
    Voigt half-width. At a node the bins over the cell and 25 cm⁻¹ each side are coarsened by a
    whole factor while the step stays under a tenth of the node's narrowest Voigt half-width and a
    600th of the cut-off (0.042 cm⁻¹, within the second ruling's 0.17 cm⁻¹; below), and convolved
    with the Voigt profile cut off at 25 cm⁻¹ by a radix-2 FFT written in the tool (Cooley and Tukey
    1965). Four things the plan leaves open are settled so:
    - the binning's own smoothing (a triangle of one step, about 10⁻³ of a Doppler core's width) is
      divided out of the bins' transform, as particle-mesh codes divide by their assignment
      function; without it the 10 Pa curve of growth erred 2.3 × 10⁻⁴ against line by line;
    - the Doppler width grows 0.1–0.2% across a cell, so the profile is convolved at both edges'
      widths and blended linearly in ν, both kernels in one complex transform and both outputs in
      another;
    - the result is read at the cell's T4.d points (a quarter of the narrowest half-width, at
      least 512) by 4-point Lagrange interpolation on its own grid, ten or more steps a half-width;
    - the cut-off falls at 25 cm⁻¹ in the profile's integral whatever the step: the kernel's last
      sample takes the share of its step within the cut-off. Rounded to a whole step, as first
      built, the cut-off moved by up to a step, near 0.8 cm⁻¹ at 10 MPa where a line's wing at
      25 cm⁻¹ is a tenth of its peak, and so jumped from one pressure node to the next: N₂O's first
      pass failed the chain test at node temperatures 277 times (to 1.85 × 10⁻² at 701 nm, 200 K
      and 8.66 MPa), which no refinement reaches. With the share, the 701 nm cell's worst fell to
      4.3 × 10⁻³ and its failures from 86 to 5. Both tables were reduced again with it.

    Against T4.d's own line-by-line spectrum of the same 3,000 toy lines (`superLines.test.ts`),
    the curves of growth agree within 1.1 × 10⁻⁵ at 10 Pa and 150 K and 1.6–7.6 × 10⁻⁶ at 10 kPa to
    3 MPa, 1–2 orders under the node tier; the test holds 3 × 10⁻⁵.

  - _Streaming and the cache_ (`exomolLines.ts`). The `.bz2` files stream through the system's
    `bzip2 -dc` (it must be on the PATH: Linux and macOS ship it; on Windows Git for Windows or MSYS2
    provides it), three at a time, every line binned at every temperature of the pass. The bins go
    to a cache outside the repository, one file a temperature and set, with a record of each pass
    (Q(T), the direct-sum cell means, the `.broad` sums, the band survey's sums); a refinement pass
    bins only its new nodes and midpoints. Nothing of the lists, the bins or the record is
    committed. `main` returns a promise for the streaming subcommands, which the script awaits.
  - _Intensities._ ExoMol's formula, S = g_u A ÷ (8π c ν²) e^(−c₂E″/T)(1 − e^(−c₂ν/T)) ÷ Q(T)
    (Yurchenko, Al-Refaie and Tennyson 2018, ExoCross's Eq. 1, on the 2016 format paper's files),
    each times HITRAN's natural abundance of the isotopologue (¹⁴NH₃ 0.995 872, ¹⁴N₂¹⁶O 0.990 333),
    so that each table is per molecule of the
    species as T4.d's are; the minor isotopologues, in neither list, are not drawn. Q(T) is summed
    from each states file: C2018's Q(296) is 1,725.287 (TIPS 1,725.2); TYM's 4,984.898 (its own
    `.pf` 4,984.8954, TIPS 4,984.9). TYM's transition files hold three columns, so ν is E′ − E″
    from its states, whose file holds 2,078,676 states (its `def.json` counts 1,759,068); the
    states are read as the file holds them. Binned over 13,100–20,000 cm⁻¹: C2018's 244,642,280 of
    the 246,563,337 lines its seven files hold (the plan's 243.7M counted from 13,149 cm⁻¹), TYM's
    605,489,714 of 623,071,063 (its 1.36 billion span all 21 files).
  - _Widths._ Every line takes its list's default air width from its `def.json`, in cm⁻¹ bar⁻¹ at
    296 K as the 2016 format paper and both `def.json`s state it (chain §10.5): C2018's 0.053
    (0.0537 cm⁻¹ atm⁻¹) and TYM's 0.07 (0.0709 cm⁻¹ atm⁻¹), both with n = 0.5. `exomol-bins` reads
    them, each `.broad` gas's default and the isotopologue's mass from the checksummed `def.json`
    (`parseDefinition`) and keeps them in the cache's record for the later commands; none is typed
    into the tool. The lines' broadening being `estimated`, every node's shape is: `measuredShapeTo`
    is −1 at every
    temperature, so a layer of either species is `estimated` by its optics wherever it is drawn
    (`absorberSpecs`'s rule), as the plan asks for NH₃ and the brief for TYM.
    - NH₃'s H₂ and He widths come from ExoMol's `.broad` files by code, read from the files
      themselves (they hold a0, m0 and m1; C2018's `def.json` lists a4, a1 and a0): m1 by |m| and
      K″, else m0 by |m|, else a0 by J″, else the `def.json`'s default, m = −J″ (P), J″ + 1 (R) and
      J″ (Q) as the 2024 release paper defines it. Their ratios to the default air width, S-weighted
      at 296 K over every line, are r_H2 1.473 and r_He 0.555, and their exponents' offsets +0.127
      and −0.127. NH₃'s self-broadening has no file, so the client takes it as air, `estimated`.
    - N₂O's ratios and exponents are HITRAN2024's, from its 184 lines alone, as T4.d's; TYM's
      added bands enter them not at all, since TYM gives no width but its default.
  - _NH₃'s range._ T_min by the criterion (§3.1: Δ_c < 10⁻³ at k = 100 over a pure vapour's
    40 p_sat ÷ (m g) at 0.5 m s⁻²), with p_sat from Fray and Schmitt 2009's sublimation fit (Eq. 4,
    Table 5, NH3-1; 15–195.41 K, its measurements 162–195 K and the colder values a thermodynamic
    extension) and the cell means read from the table itself through the client's chain: 104.1 K
    for the Sun, 104.1 K for a 2,500 K and 103.9 K for a 30,000 K Planck sun, red leading. The
    nodes run down from 300 K in 50 K steps to the first at or below it, 100 K, where the Sun's Δ_c
    is 2.2 × 10⁻⁴ (`exomolLines.test.ts`). The cap's saturation is a new `SaturationCurve` kind,
    `sublimationFit`: Fray and Schmitt's fit to their triple point (195.41 K, 6,116 Pa from the fit
    itself), Clausius–Clapeyron above it at ΔH_vap 25.57 kJ mol⁻¹ (ΔH_sub 31.22 from the fit's
    slope there, less ΔH_fus 5.653 after Overstreet and Giauque 1937, which NIST's WebBook does not
    list), which overstates p_sat upward (1.47 against 1.06 MPa at 300 K) and so only widens the
    cap.
  - _Cell 499 nm is not reduced._ Both lists end at 20,000 cm⁻¹ (500 nm), and the 499 nm cell holds
    only the cut-off wings of their last 5 cm⁻¹ of lines, the lines beyond the list's end that would
    reach it being absent. On NH₃'s first pass it failed the chain test at node temperatures
    (6.7 × 10⁻³ at 250 K and 8.7 MPa), which no refinement reaches. Its mean at 300 K is
    4.0 × 10⁻⁴⁰ m² at 10 Pa and 2.2 × 10⁻³⁴ at 1.3 MPa (τ 0.33 at its Rayleigh cap, 1.52 × 10²⁹
    cm⁻²), three orders and more under the 501 nm cell's 2.7 × 10⁻³¹, and is a wing of lines whose
    neighbours past the list's end are missing. The tables run 500–760 nm; below 500 nm neither
    list holds a line, as the pending rows had it.
  - _N₂O's bands_ (§11). TYM's states label two of HITRAN2024's four upper levels otherwise (no
    TYM state is 1 0 0 6 or 2 4 0 4) and give one label to two levels (6 0 0 3 at 13,295.8 and
    14,153.4 cm⁻¹; 2 0 0 5 at 12,891.1 and 12,894.7), so matching by label alone would draw two
    bands twice. `exomol-bands` therefore surveys TYM's lines first, at 296 K, over each HITRAN
    band's window (its lines' span ± 2 cm⁻¹) and at or above its weakest line (HITRAN's cut-off
    there, 1.0–1.06 × 10⁻²⁸ cm), by TYM's own bands. A same-label band within the tolerances
    (intensity-weighted centres within 2 cm⁻¹, strengths within a factor of 3) is matched; failing
    that, TYM's dominant band in the window that agrees is taken, `doubtful`; HITRAN2024's is kept
    either way and TYM's binned apart, filtered by its states' Herzberg quanta before binning. Each
    window held one TYM band above the cut-off:

    | HITRAN2024 band | Lines | Centre, cm⁻¹ | S(296), cm   | TYM band | Lines | Offset, cm⁻¹ | Ratio | Kept, verdict                |
    | --------------- | ----- | ------------ | ------------ | -------- | ----- | ------------ | ----- | ---------------------------- |
    | 1 0 0 6         | 87    | 14,000.29    | 5.19 × 10⁻²⁶ | 7 0 0 3  | 87    | +0.14        | 1.049 | HITRAN2024, doubtful (label) |
    | 6 0 0 3         | 41    | 13,290.47    | 5.74 × 10⁻²⁷ | 6 0 0 3  | 42    | +0.12        | 1.106 | HITRAN2024, matched          |
    | 2 0 0 5         | 25    | 13,109.72    | 4.14 × 10⁻²⁷ | 7 0 0 2  | 22    | +0.08        | 0.776 | HITRAN2024, doubtful (label) |
    | 2 4 0 4         | 31    | 13,364.94    | 3.75 × 10⁻²⁷ | 7 2 0 2  | 28    | +0.89        | 0.919 | HITRAN2024, doubtful (label) |

    All four are from 0 0 0 0 and of ¹⁴N₂¹⁶O; HITRAN2024's 2 0 0 5 lines in its request are the
    band's tail above 13,100 cm⁻¹. TYM's lines of the four bands under HITRAN's cut-off go with
    them. From 714 nm each cell takes HITRAN2024's four bands line by line, as T4.d, and TYM's
    other bands as super-lines, on the finer of the two parts' point counts; below it every TYM
    band. Over 714–760 nm each cell's mean equals HITRAN2024's plus TYM's added bands' to
    1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ (`exomol/n2oMerge.json`: 47 cells at the ten temperature nodes and 1 kPa, 0.1 and
    1 MPa, 1,410 rows; the test holds 10⁻⁹). Each cell names TYM's added bands whose 296 K strength
    reaches HITRAN2024's cut-off (its weakest line, 1.0 × 10⁻²⁸ cm), 14–22 a cell, and counts the
    weaker ones (193,535–301,640 a cell); none names a band from both lists, nor any of the four
    TYM bands binned apart. Listing every band, as first written, made the record 280 MB.

  - _N₂O's chain gate_ (the issue's ruling, 2026-10-14). On its 25 K pass N₂O's table failed the
    chain test at node temperatures, between pressure rows, 7 times in two cells, at 6.49 or
    8.66 MPa and columns within 14% of the helium Rayleigh cap, which no refinement reaches. The
    ruling took neither recording them (the tier holds at `estimated` nodes) nor more pressure
    nodes, and found the gate wrong for N₂O on two counts:
    - N₂O condenses below 309.52 K, so it takes the condensing cap (chain §§4 and 8):
      `N2O_SATURATION`, a derivation from the triple point as O₂'s. The triple point is 182.33 K
      and 87.84 kPa and the critical point 309.52 K (Lemmon and Span 2006's equation of state, as
      REFPROP 10 and NIST's WebBook give it); ΔH_fus 1,563.0 and ΔH_vap 3,958 cal mol⁻¹ (Blue and
      Giauque 1935, as Hoge 1945 quotes them; 4.1840 J a calorie), so ΔH_sub 23.10 kJ mol⁻¹. p_sat
      is 0.31 Pa at 100 K, 3.3 kPa at 150 K, 46 kPa at 175 K and 0.70 MPa at 225 K, the caps
      3.4 × 10²³, 3.6 × 10²⁷, 5.1 × 10²⁸ and 7.6 × 10²⁹ cm⁻². Below the triple point it overstates
      p_sat (+12% at 150 K, 1.3–2.4 times at 100 K, against REFPROP's sublimation fit after Bell
      2018 and a heat-capacity estimate); above it, it understates by up to 1.3% to 222 K and
      overstates beyond (+8.3% at 300 K, against Lemmon and Span's), each but the 1.3% widening the
      cap.
    - The between-node test's columns also stop at the species' own Rayleigh column, −ln 10⁻⁶ ÷
      σ_R,s at the cell's centre (`chainColumnCm2`; `reduceGridCell` takes this chain cap beside
      its node cap). σ_R,s is the client's `rayleighCrossSectionM2` for a `measured` gas: an
      ExoMol table names its species' cross-section (`nitrousOxideRayleighCm2`,
      `ammoniaRayleighCm2`, held to the client's within 10⁻¹² by `kDistributions.test.ts`, which
      loads the client's module at run time since the node project's compiler does not reach the
      renderer's). u_R,N₂O is 1.96 × 10²⁷ cm⁻² at 668 nm and 2.38 × 10²⁷ at 701 nm, against
      helium's 4.94 and 5.99 × 10²⁹: the ruling's 2.15 and 2.62 × 10²⁷ were 10% above the columns
      the client's cross-section gives, by which N₂O scatters 252 times as much as helium there,
      not 229. The node tier, the bisection, G = 1, the 16-bit test and the mixing record keep the
      gated column.
    - The seven, each beyond the corrected gate, N₂O's own Rayleigh depth τ_R = u σ_R,N₂O:

      | Cell   | T, K | p, MPa | u, cm⁻²     | Error       | u ÷ u_R,N₂O | τ_R   | u ÷ condensing cap |
      | ------ | ---- | ------ | ----------- | ----------- | ----------- | ----- | ------------------ |
      | 668 nm | 100  | 8.66   | 4.53 × 10²⁹ | 7.44 × 10⁻³ | 231         | 3,198 | 1.3 × 10⁶          |
      | 668 nm | 100  | 6.49   | 4.54 × 10²⁹ | 3.35 × 10⁻³ | 232         | 3,205 | 1.3 × 10⁶          |
      | 668 nm | 150  | 8.66   | 4.28 × 10²⁹ | 2.96 × 10⁻³ | 219         | 3,022 | 119                |
      | 668 nm | 175  | 8.66   | 4.62 × 10²⁹ | 3.21 × 10⁻³ | 236         | 3,262 | 9.1                |
      | 668 nm | 225  | 6.49   | 4.65 × 10²⁹ | 2.27 × 10⁻³ | 238         | 3,283 | does not bind      |
      | 701 nm | 175  | 8.66   | 5.93 × 10²⁹ | 2.66 × 10⁻³ | 249         | 3,438 | 11.7               |
      | 701 nm | 300  | 8.66   | 5.83 × 10²⁹ | 2.28 × 10⁻³ | 245         | 3,380 | does not bind      |

      On the corrected gate, and with the step bound (below), N₂O ran again from the protocol's
      50 K nodes: one failure, 2.55 × 10⁻³ at 715 nm, 175 K, 0.133 MPa and
      2.45 × 10²⁷ cm⁻² (inside u_R,N₂O there, 2.57 × 10²⁷), asked for 175 K, on which every
      interval passes (worst chain 1.27 × 10⁻³ at 715 nm, 225 K, 0.133 MPa and 2.34 × 10²⁷ cm⁻²);
      no failure lies at a node's temperature.

    - NH₃'s gate: its table, as first reduced, passed on the wider gate (helium's Rayleigh cap
      and its saturation), worst chain 9.20 × 10⁻⁴, so the ruling did not ask it to run again; it
      was reduced again for the step bound (below), on the corrected gate, its table source in the
      tool naming ammonia's cross-section: u_R,NH₃ is 1.30 × 10²⁷ cm⁻² at 500 nm, 3.72 × 10²⁷ at
      645 nm and 7.29 × 10²⁷ at 760 nm, so the gate binds for NH₃ wherever its pressure and
      condensing caps pass those columns, at the warmer nodes and higher pressures.
    - _The diagnostic_ (ruling item 5, not gated), at 668 nm, 100 K, 8.66 MPa and 4.527 × 10²⁹
      cm⁻² on the 25 K pass's gate: T there is 0.6454 (τ 0.438, far from the floor); the four
      rows' node errors at that column are 4.4, 5.0, 4.2 and 7.3 × 10⁻⁵ (5.62, 7.50, 10 and
      13.3 MPa); the exact curve's own cubic error is 7.45 × 10⁻³, the chain's 7.44 × 10⁻³. So the
      super-line spectra were not smooth in p. With the coarse step held fixed across the
      stencil's rows and midpoint (0.68, 0.34 or 0.17 cm⁻¹), the exact curve's cubic misses by
      5.2–6.3 × 10⁻⁶ there and by at most 2.3 × 10⁻⁵ over 10²⁰–3 × 10³⁰ cm⁻², as the ruling's
      synthetic cells do. (A twentieth of the half-width, tried before the ruling, still grows
      with p, and left the failures.)
  - _The super-lines' step bound_ (the issue's second ruling). The cause: the coarse step was a
    tenth of each node's narrowest half-width, so it grew with p (1.04 cm⁻¹ at 8.66 MPa and
    100 K), and each line's wing, which stops at the 25 cm⁻¹ cut-off at 7–29% of its peak at
    5.6–13.3 MPa (N₂O at 100 K), puts a step into the summed spectrum there that the grid resolved
    only to its own step, so the spectrum's error moved with the step from row to row. Against a
    converged step
    the spectra as first built erred in T at that column by 5.3 × 10⁻³, 3.9 × 10⁻³, 1.1 × 10⁻²
    and 2.1 × 10⁻² on the four rows at 100 K, by 0.3–4.3 × 10⁻³ at 300 K, where helium's cap
    gates such columns, and by under 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ at 0.75–1.78 MPa. The step is now bounded in cm⁻¹
    as well, under a 600th of the cut-off (`SUPER_LINE_STEPS_PER_CUTOFF`, 0.042 cm⁻¹), within the
    ruling's "at most 0.17 cm⁻¹" and the plan's "finer than a tenth"; it binds above about
    0.35–0.8 MPa for N₂O (100–500 K) and 0.45–0.8 MPa for NH₃ (100–300 K), and is then the same at
    every pressure. A 150th, the ruling's figure, failed its own check, the rows within about
    3 × 10⁻⁵ of a converged step at the worst state:

    | Step, cm⁻¹                                      | 0.33    | 0.17    | 0.083   | 0.042   | 0.021   | 0.010   |
    | ----------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------- |
    | T at 4.53 × 10²⁹ cm⁻² (668 nm, 100 K, 8.66 MPa) | 0.65722 | 0.65869 | 0.65930 | 0.65954 | 0.65951 | 0.65958 |

    A 600th's rows and midpoint lie 2.3–5.8 × 10⁻⁵ from a step four times finer at that column,
    the exact curve's cubic 5 × 10⁻⁶ there. That meets the check to the spectra's own floor, not
    under it: the 0.021 and 0.010 cm⁻¹ steps themselves differ by 7 × 10⁻⁵ there, so no step shows
    3 × 10⁻⁵ against a finer one at that column (posted on the issue). A 150th's rows lay 4.2–8.7 ×
    10⁻⁴ away there, and within 1 × 10⁻⁴ of a converged step at 300 K and 10–13 MPa, where helium's
    cap gates such columns. The FFT grows to 2,048 points at the high-pressure nodes, at no cost
    measured. `superLines.test.ts` pins the bound, and in a toy cell lit by a band's cut-off wings
    holds
    super-lines to line by line within 5 × 10⁻⁵ (2.9 and 3.0 × 10⁻⁵ at 8.66 and 13.3 MPa, against
    1.3 and 1.4 × 10⁻⁴ bounded by the half-width alone; 4.4 × 10⁻⁵ at 0.1 MPa, where the
    half-width binds). Both tables were reduced again with it from the protocol's start, the
    50 K nodes. R08.T4.f's hot lists take the same bound.

  - _The committed references._ `exomol/lineReferencesNH3.json` (550 and 645 nm) and
    `lineReferencesN2O.json` (700 and 716 nm) hold each cell's curves from the spectrum the
    reduction read, their midpoints' columns stopping at the chain test's cap (`cellReference`
    takes both caps), in their `lineByLine` field: super-lines, and for N₂O from 714 nm the merged
    spectrum. No line-by-line
    pass over 244.6M or 605.5M lines is made; super-lines are held to line by line on
    `superLines.test.ts`'s 3,000 toy lines.
  - _Pending entries._ NH₃'s and N₂O's R08.T4.g entries and their rows in `exomol/bounds.json` are
    gone. Hot NH₃ is R08.T4.f's (CoYuTe, Coles, Yurchenko and Tennyson 2019), a new entry at C2018's
    300 K row, `estimated`: its direct-sum cell means at 300 K, rounded up to three figures (the

- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)** (R08.T4.g). Recorded and deferred: each leaves the
  algorithm and every contract as they are.
  - _ExoMol's width unit._ The 2016 format paper and both `def.json`s give the default and `.broad`
    widths in cm⁻¹ bar⁻¹; the 2024 release paper's §4 (Eq. 6) gives γ₀ in cm⁻¹ atm⁻¹. Per bar is
    taken (chain §10.5); per atm would move every width 1.3%.
  - _C2018's `.broad` files beyond their quanta._ Past |m| = 15 and J″ = 14 a line takes the
    `def.json`'s default (0.0801 cm⁻¹ bar⁻¹ for H₂), 70% above m0's last row (0.0472 at |m| = 15),
    a jump ExoMol's files make; at 296 K such lines hold under 10⁻⁵ of the S.
  - _The lists' `def.json`s are stale._ C2018's lists `.broad` codes its files do not hold, and
    TYM's counts 1,759,068 states where its states file holds 2,078,676; the files are read as they
    are.
  - _Stored rounding residue._ T4.d's two-grid sum leaves σ of 10⁻¹⁷ of a node's largest where a
    line's wing cancels, which the 16-bit codes store, so that a table's bytes depend on the libm
    (the setup check); flooring σ under 10⁻¹⁵ of the node's largest to 0 would make them
    reproducible across Node versions.
  - _T4.d's sources keep helium's chain cap._ The tool holds σ_R,s for N₂O and NH₃, the measured
    gases it reduces from T4.g on; T4.d's `LINE_SOURCES` (O₂, H₂O, CO₂, CO, N₂O, HCN and H₂) keep
    helium's, as their tables were gated. A task that reduces one of them again gives its source
    the species' cross-section first (HCN, unmeasured, keeps helium's), held to the client's by the
    same test.
  - _The condensing cap's mass._ The cap is 400 p_sat ÷ (m g) with m the species' own mass
    (chain §§4 and 8). A species at its saturation pressure in a lighter background holds
    p_sat ÷ (m̄ g), m̄ the mean molecular mass: in H₂ and He (m̄ ≈ 2.3 Da) a saturated N₂O column is
    19 times p_sat ÷ (m g) and NH₃'s 7.4 times, so the tenfold supersaturation spares N₂O there by
    under a factor of 2. None of N₂O's seven failures moves, each lying 219–249 times past its own
    Rayleigh column. Whether the cap should take m̄'s least plausible value is for the rule's owner.
  - _Fray and Schmitt for N₂O._ Their 2009 compilation lists N₂O; its fit was not readable here,
    so N₂O takes the derivation from the triple point, which overstates p_sat below 150 K (up to
    2.4 times at 100 K) and so only widens the cap.
  - _TYM's default width against HITRAN's._ HITRAN2024's 184 N₂O lines average γ_air 0.0776
    cm⁻¹ atm⁻¹ with n 0.737, S-weighted (0.0681–0.0962), against TYM's default 0.0709 with n 0.5:
    9% narrower at 296 K and about 30% at 100 K. Taking HITRAN's means for TYM's lines, or its
    J-dependence, would be a change of the estimate, for R08.T4.f's hot N₂O to weigh.
- **Deviations in T19, as built** (2026-10-16; `view/atmosphere/parity.test.ts`, new; `rayleigh.ts`
  and `rayleigh.test.ts`; `channels.json` and `channels.ts`; `absorbers/transparency.test.ts` and
  `materials/materials.test.ts`). Rulings: decision-composition §1.1 and §1.9, science-r08-gases-2
  §1.4, decision-bump-plan-after-22 and P14.T49.b's rows and flags as built (plan 14's record).
  - _The check._ `parity.test.ts` reads the fixture as a JSON import, and of each row only its key,
    its molar mass and its three flags, never `heat_capacity_over_r`, which P14.T54.a renames
    (`heat_capacity_over_r_298k`). It fails if:
    1. a `rayleigh` row's `rayleighOf(key).provenance` is `none` (one test a row);
    2. an `absorber` row has no cross-sections (`crossSectionAt`, H⁻'s closed form included), no
       committed line table (`committedLineSpecies()`, R08.T4.d's and T4.g's), no
       `PENDING_ABSORBERS` entry with its cell means and no `NO_VISIBLE_ABSORPTION` entry with its
       evidence. The task's text predates the line tables; they are counted, as
       `transparency.test.ts`'s check counted them;
    3. an `aerosol_material` row resolves to no file of its own (`resolveMaterial(key).file`, as
       R08.T5.d's test had it): a stated stand-in is a file of provenance `standIn` whose text says
       what stands in, which is also checked, and the generic stand-in alone fails. The reverse,
       which T5.b's text gives T19: every key of `MATERIAL_FILES` is a row of the fixture;
    4. `GAS_MOLAR_MASS_G_PER_MOL` differs from the fixture's `molar_mass_g_per_mol` by more than
       10⁻¹² g mol⁻¹ for a key in both (each of `GASES`). There is no c_p row (science-r08-gases-2
       §1.4, which supersedes decision-composition §1.9's c_p ÷ R).

      in the asserted object beside the members found.

      generated type fails the type check rather than leaving the hold to outlive its member.

  - _At 5622cb95, before the rows below:_ condition 1 checked 43 rows and failed seven, `Al`, `V`,
    `Mn`, `Ni`, `Zn`, `HCl` and `Cr`; condition 2 checked 35 and failed none (H⁻ through the closed

  - _The seven rows_, which P14.T49.b's record assigns to "R08.T19's extension", by T3.c's rule,
    appended to `ESTIMATED_RAYLEIGH` after FeH in the registry's order (Al, V, Mn, Ni, Zn, HCl,
    Cr), so that "keep the registry's order" holds. `ESTIMATED_RAYLEIGH` goes from 20 to 27, and
    `GASES` stays 16.
    - _The six atoms_ take `polarisability` rows from Schwerdtfeger and Nagle's 2018 table (the
      CTCP copy last updated 27 November 2018, read through the Wayback Machine's 2019-01-22
      snapshot), each the table's recommended value, computed: Al 57.8 ± 1.0, V 87 ± 10, Mn 68 ± 9,
      Ni 49 ± 3, Zn 38.67 ± 0.30 and Cr 83 ± 12 a.u. Each basis names the calculation the value
      rests on and the measurements beside it (Al's 46 ± 2 and 55.3 ± 5.5, V's 68.2 ± 5.4, Cr's
      60 ± 24, Zn's 38.8 ± 0.8).
    - _Oscillators_, as Mg's and Fe's rows have them, at the strongest resonance line below 300 nm
      (NIST ASD, vacuum): Mn 279.56 nm (its triplet carries 72% of α(0)), Ni 232.07 nm and Zn
      213.92 nm (84%). Al's, V's and Cr's strong lines lie above 300 nm (Al 308–396, V 305–386, Cr
      358–429 nm), so they take the static rule.
    - _Uncertainty factors_: the sum over each atom's lines from its ground level (NIST ASD, every f
      from the line's A and statistical weights), with the rest of α(0) static or dispersed at the
      ionisation energy, against the estimate over 440–680 nm, the King factor the rule leaves out,
      and (1 + δα ÷ α)², rounded up to two figures:
      - Al 6.2: its ²P₃/₂ level, 112 cm⁻¹ up, holds most of the atoms, and the thermal mixture puts
        the true σ 1.3–4.1 times the estimate; its open 3p shell's anisotropic scattering (F_K
        about 1.2 for ²P₁/₂ and 1.8 for ²P₃/₂ at 440 nm) raises that to 1.4–6.0;
      - Mn 2.3 (1.03–1.79), Zn 1.1 (0.93–0.98), with F_K within 0.01% of 1 for Mn and 1 for Zn;
      - Ni 2.2: the thermal mixture of its a³F and 3d⁹4s a³D levels (205–1,713 cm⁻¹ up, about
        two-fifths of the atoms above 1,000 K), the a³D levels given the ground level's rest, puts
        the true σ 1.3–1.9 times the estimate, against 0.90–0.98 for the ground level alone. Its
        anisotropic share is not bounded: NIST ASD lacks the partner of its 232.0 nm line's
        multiplet, so a line sum would not hold it;
      - Cr 62 (2.1–46, its F_K 1.011 at 440 nm from its resolved fine structure);
      - V `undefined`: its ground-level lines at 457.85, 483.38 and 485.28 nm lie inside the span,
        as Na's and Ti's do.
    - _A reading._ The brief's "`undefined` where the atom's lines from its ground term lie in or
      near that span" is read as the existing rows have it: `undefined` where a line lies inside
      440–680 nm (V, as Na and Ti), and a factor from the sum over lines where they lie outside it
      (Al, Cr and Mn, as K's 13 and Ca's 180). Mn's 539.6 and 543.4 nm intercombination lines
      (f = 5.2 and 2.7 × 10⁻⁵) lie inside it; its bound fails only within 0.07 and 0.04 nm of
      them, so `uncertaintyFactor`'s doc excepts a line too weak to move σ beyond 0.1 nm of its
      centre, and Mn's basis names them.
    - _The science check_ (the `science-checker` agent, 2026-10-16) confirmed every α, its
      uncertainty and its label against the table, each cited calculation and measurement, each
      wavelength and f against NIST ASD, the oscillator choices and HCl's row against the paper.
      It corrected three factors, which stand as above: Al's from 4.1 (its ground level alone),
      Ni's from 2.0 (its rest static only) and Cr's from 61 (its F_K left out). Al's anisotropic
      F_K, from a sum of the rank-1 and rank-2 polarisability over ASD's lines with the rest taken
      isotropic, is its own calculation, to about ±30% in F_K − 1, and was checked here only in
      size: a single J = 3/2 → 1/2 line scatters six times its isotropic part.
    - _NIST ASD's printed f_ for Zn I's lines is ten times what their A and weights give (213.9 nm:
      10.35 against 1.47; 307.7 nm: 1.6 × 10⁻³ against 1.6 × 10⁻⁴), and 3.6 times at 110.8 nm. The
      rows use the f from A.
    - _HCl_ takes a `dispersion` row, as SO₂'s Cuthbertson row does: C. and M. Cuthbertson 1914,
      re-read in archive.org's public-domain scan (item philtrans08506476). Its formula, p. 12, is
      (μ − 1)D ÷ (d₀76) = 4.6425 × 10²⁷ ÷ (10,664 × 10²⁷ − n²) with n = 3 × 10¹⁰ ÷ λ (p. 6, stated
      with chlorine's formula), that is n − 1 = 0.051 583 ÷ (118.49 − λ⁻²), the materials tool's
      `HCL_REFRACTIVITY`; the paper reduces every gas to hydrogen's number density at 0 °C and
      76 cm (p. 5; HCl's own correction on p. 11), so Z is H₂'s there,
      `GAS_DISPERSION.H2.compressibility`, 1.000 624. Its wavelengths are air wavelengths, read as
      vacuum (2 × 10⁻⁵ of n − 1), as NH₃'s row from the same paper reads them, over Table V's
      4799.9–6707.85 Å. F_K = 1 (`noKingFactor`), and `uncertaintyFactor` 1.03: the
      scatter between measurements, Mascart's D-line 1.000 444 (as the paper quotes it) lying 1.2%
      below the Cuthbertsons' own unreduced index there, 2.4% in σ, and an unread King factor that
      a near-isotropic hydride holds to perhaps 1.002–1.005.
    - _HCl's tests_: the row is the printed formula with n = 3 × 10¹⁰ ÷ λ to 2 × 10⁻⁵ over
      480–670 nm, and reproduces Table V's 44,803 × 10⁻⁸ at 5460.7 Å to 5 × 10⁻⁵, the figure the
      tool's test holds its copy to. Table V's other calculated values stray from the printed
      formula by up to 1.9 × 10⁻⁴ (44,994 at 5085.8 Å against 45,002.7, its difference column's −13
      agreeing with the print), so only the one is asserted.
  - _The channel fit._ HCl, an estimated molecule, joins `CHANNEL_FIT_GASES` (27 gases to 28). The

    and Fe's (T4.a's record). `CHANNEL_FIT_GASES`' remarks name the six with their figures and HCl
    with its own, beyond the brief's "only if HCl's membership needs a sentence": the remarks named

  - _HCl from HITRAN2024_ (decision-r08-t4ef-storage §4; T4.f's bullet "any molecule P14.T52.a
    lists with a visible band system", its source HITRAN, since ExoMol holds only HCl's `.broad`

    their digits (5–0 5.36 × 10⁻²⁵, 6–0 3.96 × 10⁻²⁵, 7–0 1.08 × 10⁻²⁵, 8–0 2.19 × 10⁻²⁶ cm, none
    above 20,231.25 cm⁻¹).
    - _The science check's verdict._ HITRAN2024's 5–0, 6–0 and 7–0 band strengths reproduce Gelfand
      et al.'s measured overtone intensities (J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transfer 26 (1981) 303)
      corrected for isotopic abundance by HITRAN2024's factor 1.3 (Gordon et al. 2026, §2.15), which
      rests on Vasilchenko et al.'s 5–0 cavity ring-down measurements (J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat.
      Transfer 296 (2023) 108460); Reddy (J. Mol. Spectrosc. 82 (1980) 127) confirms the flat 5–0/6–0
      step (1.37–1.38 against HITRAN's 1.36), so the shape is measured, not the extrapolation
      artefact of Li2015's CO, and the three bands are kept, `measured`. The 8–0 band, never
      measured, is Li et al.'s dipole moment function (J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transfer 121
      (2013) 78) carried a quantum past its data and left without the 1.3 (HITRAN's code "estimate");
      it is smooth (7–0/8–0 3.8 within one dipole function), so it is kept, `estimated`, probably
      25% low. HITRAN holds no 9–0 to 11–0 since HITRAN2016 (§2.15 there), though they lie in the
      range. No band was dropped.
    - _A cut, as built._ A table has one basis, so the 8–0 band (132 lines from 19,058.48 cm⁻¹, with
      its 9–1 hot band) leaves the table for an `overtones` part, `estimated`, R08.T4.f, in
      `bounds.json`, as CO's is (follow-up 3, ruling 2): HITRAN's 8–0 lines unchanged, and the
      overtone ladder below them (follow-up 3, ruling 3, CO's construction) for 9–0, 10–0 and 11–0,
      each line moved by E(v) − E(8) of H³⁵Cl's levels (20,196.056, 22,251.585, 24,197.664 and
      26,030.666 cm⁻¹, E′ = ν + E″ of the hot bands' P(1) lines in HITRAN's `.par` records; Huber
      and Herzberg's three constants put them 66–240 cm⁻¹ higher there) and divided by 10 for each
      quantum, at the table's 50 K grid with 296 K for 300 K (`hcl-overtones`). Its largest cells at
      296 K: 1.50 × 10⁻³² m² (8–0, 494–525 nm), 2.16 × 10⁻³³ (9–0, 449–474 nm), 1.85 × 10⁻³⁴ (10–0,
      413–434 nm), 1.75 × 10⁻³⁵ (11–0, 384–402 nm); 12–0 lies above 380 nm's 26,316 cm⁻¹. The
      table takes the 3,255 lines below 19,029.5 cm⁻¹ (the 525/526 nm cells' edge,
      `HCL_TABLE_BELOW_PER_CM`, a new optional `LineSource.tableBelowPerCm` that `readLineList`
      applies): the cut falls in the 34 cm⁻¹ gap after the last line below it, 19,024.33 cm⁻¹.
    - _Its range._ T_min by §3.1's criterion through the client's chain from the table: 93.62 K for
      the Sun, 93.57 K for a 2,500 K and 93.39 K for a 30,000 K Planck sun (`hclLines.test.ts`), so
      the nodes run down from 500 K in 50 K steps to 50 K. p_sat is `HCL_SATURATION`, from the triple
      point: 159.07 K (Thol et al. 2018's equation of state, as CoolProp gives it) and 13.800 kPa
      (Henderson et al. 1986, as NIST's WebBook gives it), ΔH_sub 19.7 kJ mol⁻¹ (Ser and Larher 1990,
      the WebBook's) and ΔH_vap 17.227 kJ mol⁻¹ at the triple point (Thol et al.); 2.1 Pa at 100 K and
      103.4 kPa at the boiling point. The curve widens the cap below about 103 K and above about
      175 K and narrows it by at most 4% between, where ΔH_sub falls towards the triple point (the
      science check's), inside the cap's factor of 10. HCl condenses below its critical point,
      324.68 K, so it takes the condensing cap, as N₂O does. It is not in `GASES`, so its
      between-node test stops at helium's Rayleigh column, not its own as T4.g's ruling has the
      ExoMol species': helium's is about 165 times the deeper ((n − 1)² ratio), so the test covers
      more columns, not fewer. `measured` to 296 K and held and `estimated` above 500 K.
    - _Its grid._ A sample of every tenth cell on the 50 K grid failed the chain test at 125 and
      175 K (in 5 of 26 cells, 7.0 × 10⁻³ at worst), so the full reduction ran on the grid refined
      there, 12 nodes, with no failure left; the merge exited 0.

      528 km-amagat gives τ ≈ 5 × 10⁻⁶. So the correction changes the form of HCl's answer and is

  - _Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)_ (R08.T4.h). Each leaves the algorithm and every contract
    as they are.
    - _Kurucz does hold Zn II's lines_, in `atoms/3001/gf3001.pos` (2012), not `gfall/`: 255 over
      350–800 nm, the 17 ASD lists among them, the three 6.0 eV lines at log gf −2.40, −3.12 and
      −2.24. R08.T4.e may take Zn⁺'s lines from it in place of the bound; Kisielius et al.'s
      calculation is 6.5–7.3 times lower for the same three.
    - _HCl's 8–0 band is probably 25% low_, HITRAN2024's 1.3 having reached only 4–0 to 7–0; the
      `overtones` part keeps HITRAN's value, `estimated`, whose hundredfold margin covers it.
    - _Above 500 K_ HCl's table is held at its 500 K node, `estimated`, as T4.d's are; no hot HCl list
      reaches the range (HITEMP holds none; ExoMol only `.broad` files), so it has no hot entry.
    - _The ladder's shifts_ take H³⁵Cl's levels for every isotopologue's 8–0 lines.
    - _The ladder's factor._ HITRAN's own HCl bands step 3.7–4.9 times a quantum from 6–0 to 8–0
      (3.8 within one dipole function), so the ruled factor of 10 may put 9–0 to 11–0 2–10 times
      low; their cells stay under 3 × 10⁻³³ m², inside the `estimated` hundredfold margin.
    - _HCl's size on bodies, corrected._ The brief's sub-Neptune column (about 10 km-amagat, τ ≈
      10⁻⁵) matches the column above 0.1 bar; at 10 bar it is about 500 km-amagat and τ(744 nm) ≈ 6 ×
      10⁻⁴ (the HCl record above). Not visible vertically; R08.T10.a's test decides grazing paths.
    - _Unsöld's widths near the limit._ The 0.1 eV floor on a level's binding only widens a line; a
      dedicated (ABO) width is R08.T4.e's.

    ruled 4,600, and 4,300 (4,600, 4,200); Si⁺ 4,700, ruled 4,600, and 4,300 (4,600, 4,400). E1's

    3,800 (3,400), Ni⁺ 4,600 ruled (4,000). Na, K, Mg, Al, Ca, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe and Ni have none:

    (MNRAS 312, 813, Table 4) give A = 6.446 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹ (log gf about −9.72), above Kurucz's,

    100 times the reference column its share reaches 10⁻³ (1.6 × 10⁻³ from 1,000 K, on the flat
    part of its curve of growth).
  - _H I's widths_ (decision-r08-t4e-budget §8). By H atoms, Hα, Hβ and Hγ take Barklem, Piskunov
    and O'Mara 2000b's Table 3 p–d component (Hα σ 1,180 a₀², α 0.677; Hβ 2,320, 0.455; Hγ 4,208,
    0.380; their impact limits 35.0, 13.2 and 7.7 Å, beyond the 25 cm⁻¹ shape), converted as ABO's
    are (`aboWidth`, at the H–H reduced mass), the members above Hγ Hγ's, a lower bound; by H₂ and
    He Unsöld's, as before (`selfBroadeningSource`, `hydrogenLineSet`). They enter only H's
    broadening ratio: the table's axis is H₂'s pressure. Stark broadening (the brief's §3.1) is a
    Lorentzian of Stehlé and Hutcheon 1999's half width (A&AS 140, 93; CDS VI/98A: H3–H10, 10¹⁰–
    10¹⁵ cm⁻³, 2,500–10,000 K, ln w linear in ln n_e, linear in T; H10's for the members above,
    whose 25 cm⁻¹ shapes reach no cell) at the node's n_e from the solar-abundance Saha balance at
    its T and p (`balmerStark.ts`): 6 × 10⁹–1 × 10¹⁵ cm⁻³ at 3,300–5,000 K and 10 Pa–10 MPa. Near
    1 kPa above 4,300 K it is 35–50% of Hα's Lorentz width; at 10 Pa under the radiative; at
    0.1 MPa and above about 10% of the van der Waals. The table is `estimated` (n_e is no axis, and
    a Lorentzian overstates the quasi-static ion wing, ∝ Δλ^(−5/2) beyond a few half widths). In
    LTE; a non-LTE thermosphere is not modelled. H's bound–free from n ≥ 3 is stated negligible
    beside H⁻ below 5,000 K, as the plan has it.

  - _The Rydberg bound on Unsöld's widths_ (decision-r08-t4e-unsold, main, 2026-10-20), a deviation
    from T4.h as built that settles its deferred finding "Unsöld's widths near the limit".
    `vanDerWaalsWidthPerS` takes, per perturber p of H, H₂ and He before the sum, Γ_p =
    min(Γ_Unsöld,p, Γ_R,p), Γ_R,p = 2 v̄ N_p (σ_pol + σ_F) in atomic units (`rydbergWidthM3PerS`):
    σ_pol = 3.59 (α_p ÷ v̄)^(2/3), the polarisation width's asymptote (Alekseev and Sobel'man 1966,
    Sov. Phys. JETP 22, 882, eq. (34), a full width by their eq. (2); Omont 1977, J. Physique 38,
    1343, eq. (4.3); 3.59, not Omont's (4.15) Anderson estimate of 3.18, reproduces his Table III);
    σ_F the Fermi term over b₁ < b < 2n*² (Omont's (4.9), (4.11)–(4.17)), b₁ = (α_p ÷ v̄)^(1/3),
    b₂ = ½ (0.53 L_p ÷ (n*³ v̄))², σ_F = 0 where 2n*² ≤ b₁, 2π b₂ (2n*² − b₁) where b₂ ≤ b₁
    (4.17a), π (4 b₂ n*² − b₂² − b₁²) where b₁ < b₂ < 2n*² (4.17b), π (4n*⁴ − b₁²) where b₂ ≥ 2n*²;
    v̄ = √(8kT ÷ πμ), as Unsöld's width takes it. Both papers were read in full by main and the
    equations checked on the page images; this build's science check read Omont (HAL), Alekseev
    and Sobel'man (the JETP archive), Lei et al. 2025 and Osorio et al. 2015 again and reproduced
    every test value to 3 × 10⁻⁵.
    - _Where it applies_ (`takesRydbergBound`), all four together: a neutral atom; a line on
      Unsöld's width (no Kurucz damping field; the tables give it only lines with no ABO width, and
      ABO's tables stop below n* 6); the upper level's own n*, √(Ry ÷ (I − E_u)) unfloored, at least
      6 (Omont §4.2: n* < 6 "are not proper Rydberg states"); and that n* at least 0.1 from an
      integer (a level by the high-l manifold is widened by l-mixing, which the elastic model leaves
      out: Na 8d–11d + He is 2–3 times Γ_R). At or above the limit Γ_R is 2 v̄ N σ_pol. Γ_Unsöld
      keeps T4.h's 0.1 eV floor, whose doc now says that it narrows Unsöld's width below its value
      at the true n*. H I's levels are all hydrogenic, so only its 364.70 nm series-limit entry,
      above Barklem and Collet's limit, takes the bound: its n* from their 13.5984 eV (to 0.1 meV)
      and the infinite-mass Rydberg drifts past 0.1 from the integer from n 42 (`hydrogenic`; main
      confirmed it as physics, the drift being arithmetic). Every other stage takes its limit as
      Barklem and Collet give it, to their four decimals, at which the near-hydrogenic test is stable
      to n* ≈ 40. The lower level is left out, as Omont's model does (its
      Unsöld C₆ in the phase would lower Γ_R 35–50%).
    - _Parameters_ (`PERTURBER_SCATTERING_LENGTHS_A0`): α_p T4.h's (H 4.5, H₂ 5.429, He 1.387 a₀³);
      L_He 1.19 a₀ (O'Malley 1963, Phys. Rev. 130, 1020, its abstract read; Omont's Table I and Lei
      et al.'s Table III give it from Massey and Burhop 1969); L_H₂ 1.61 a₀ (Randell et al. 1994, J.
      Phys. B 27, 2369, as Lei et al. 2025 take it; within Thompson et al. 1987's 1.64 ± 0.07 from Rb
      Rydberg shifts, abstract read, and above Chang 1981's 1.27, not read; the spread moves Γ_R 5%
      at n* 10.8 and 30–38% at n* 6); L_H = √((a_s² + 3a_t²) ÷ 4) = 3.353 a₀, a_s 5.965 and a_t 1.7686
      (Schwartz 1961, Phys. Rev. 124, 1468, not open at write; Osorio et al. 2015 §3.3.2 give 5.965
      and 1.769), the spin weights Alekseev and Sobel'man's eqs. (20)–(22).

  - _The condensing cap in the chain test_ (residual protocol item (ii), decision-r08-t4e-unsold
    §5; `CellReductionSource.chainSaturation`, `POTASSIUM_SATURATION`, a `SaturationCurve` of kind
    `antoine`): at a temperature where liquid K is fitted, the between-node test's columns also stop
    at 400 p_sat(T) ÷ (m g), g = 0.5 m s⁻², errors beyond it recorded, not gated; the node tier, the
    bisection, G = 1 and the 16-bit test keep their wider columns, so no g-point moves. p_sat is NIST
    Chemistry WebBook's Antoine fit for liquid K, log₁₀(p ÷ 1 bar) = 4.45718 − 4,691.58 ÷ (T +
    24.195) over 679.4–1,033 K, NIST's coefficients from Fiock and Rodebush 1926 (J. Am. Chem. Soc.
    48, 2522), read 2026-10-20, used from K's 650 K node, extrapolated 29 K below the fit (main:
    it can't matter at that margin), to 1,033 K, with no cap outside them; Alcock, Itkin and
    Horrigan 1984 (the ruling's example) was not open. Its caps: 3.9 × 10²⁶ cm⁻² at 650 K, 6.9 ×
    10²⁶ at 675 K, 1.2 × 10²⁷ at 700 K, 1.9 × 10²⁷ at 725 K and 3.1 × 10²⁷ at 750 K. It moved out of
    the gate 697 nm's one failure (650 K, 0.75 MPa, 4.0 × 10²⁹ cm⁻², about 1,000 times past its
    cap; 4p₃/₂–4d on ABO's width) and 581 nm's at 675, 700 and 725 K (3.3 × 10²⁸, 1.2 × 10²⁸ and

  - _The residual protocol's item (i), the refinement economy_ (decision-r08-t4e-unsold §5, from
    this lane's note): a failure between temperature nodes is not bisected, nor `estimated`, where a
    bracketing node fails at the same pressure between the same rows with no alternate to keep; it
    is reported with that node's failure, which the merge refuses (`sortFailures`). On K's second
    pass on Unsöld's widths it would have spared 255 of the 268 interval failures (the pass asked
    for 30 → 56 nodes).
  - _The broadening axis_ (§3): the reference broadener is H₂; each table's `broadening` holds every
    gas's width ratio to H₂ at its middle node, N₂, O₂, Ar and air among them (the client would
    otherwise take them at ratio 1, as it takes air for a molecular table, here H₂'s width,
    unlabelled), by Unsöld's scaling from the line's H width (N₂ 1.710,
    O₂ 1.562 and Ar 1.664 Å³, NIST CCCBDB's experimental list from Olney et al. 1997, Chem. Phys.
    223, 59, read 2026-10-20; air by US Standard Atmosphere 1976's Table 3, 0.780 84 N₂, 0.209 476
    O₂ and 0.009 34 Ar, normalised over them), the exponent offsets 0, each gas's width sharing its
    line's exponent. He and H to H₂: Na 0.464 and 1.736, K 0.454 and 1.198, Fe 0.453 and 1.196, H
    0.549 and 2.198, Zn 0.476 and 1.137, Mg⁺ 0.482 and 1.129, Si⁺ 0.481 and 1.130, Mg 0.472 and
    1.154, Cr 0.456 and 1.190. No ratio is under 0.40, so no cap widens. H₂'s and He's
    polarisabilities are Lorentz–Lorenz on the client's dispersions, the air gases' Olney et
    al.'s: Lorentz–Lorenz on the client's N₂, O₂ and Ar would differ by 1.7%, 0.4% and −1.3%, and
    Olney's H₂ lies 2.2% under T4.h's, moving the ratios by 0.7% or less (the science check's
    figures).

      `ratio ?? 1`), `estimated`: for an atom's table that is H₂'s width, 1.4–1.5 times the
      table's `air` ratio, where the brief's §4 has such a gas "taken as air". A deviation, left as
      built: taking the table's `air` ratio instead changes the curves' read, which is main's
      question (this lane's report).
  - _E3's alternates, as built._ The merge keeps a thinned table's dropped alternate where the
    between-node test fails at a node's temperature between two stored nodes that hold one, or in an
    interval at its finest step (`sortFailures`' `keepPressuresPa`, `droppedNodesAbout`), and asks
    for them as `refine-pressures:`; where any failure at a node's temperature asks for one, the pass
    keeps those alone and refines no interval, since a dropped node also fails between temperature
    nodes at its pressure. Keeping both at once, as first built, refined every interval of Na's
    425 nm sample (30 → 53 nodes) where the alternates alone sufficed (30). On a table of every
    standard pressure nothing changes.

    lines at each pressure; for the atoms the grid at 10 Pa (their own below) serves every higher
    pressure. On each pressure's own grid a saturated wing's 25 cm⁻¹ cut-off moved by up to a step
    between pressures and the exact depth jittered by up to 1% (Mg I's 385 nm cell at 3,600 K and
    2 × 10²⁵ cm⁻²: 2.384 at 31.6 kPa, 2.372 at 42.2 kPa, 2.409 at 56.2 kPa), which the chain test
