  - _Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)_ (R08.T4.e). Each leaves the algorithm and every contract
    as they are.
    - _The 10 Pa hold fails the 1 Pa check_ in most atomic cells (Na's 5.9 × 10⁻², Fe I 527 nm's
      2.2 × 10⁻² in the first projection), so the atomic tables are `estimated` below 10 Pa; a node
      below 10 Pa would be a layout change.
    - _Deb and Hibbert's table 9_ holds computed wavelengths (190 lines in 360–780 nm); it bites
      only if Fe⁺ is drawn, as it is not.
    - _J/A+A/657/A121's_ open H–H Balmer-α profile could inform Hα's self-broadening.
    - _[O I] near 10⁻³ at 100 times the reference column._
    - _Storey and Zeippen's A for [O I] 630 nm_ lies 10% above Kurucz's; the statement stays on
      Kurucz's list.
    - _K's H₂ width_ is Barklem et al.'s ABO width scaled by Unsöld's rule, which for Na D ran
      1.25–1.74 times Allard et al.'s ab initio widths; K's core and its `K+H2` estimate may be as wide.
      Allard et al. 2016's K–H₂ paper gives K's impact widths (not read).
    - _Allard et al. 2019's Eq. 8_ (D2's width, T^0.39) lies 1.5–1.7 times above their own tables'
      widths, which match their Fig. 6's label (T^0.32) within 2.5%; A&A refused the fetch, so the
      published version was not read.
    - _D1's blue far wing_ by H₂ is not deposited (2–5% of D2's blue wing by the impact estimate).
    - _The Stark Lorentzian_ overstates the quasi-static ion wing of H I's Balmer lines: against
      Stehlé and Hutcheon's Stark-only profiles it is within 1–15% to about three half widths,
      1.4–2.5 times above at 300–3,000 half widths (10¹⁰ cm⁻³) and about 11 times at 25 cm⁻¹
      (3 × 10¹² cm⁻³), the profile's tail going as Δλ^(−5/2) (the science check's figures).
    - _The line-by-line grid jitter_ that the atoms' fixed grid removes may also act, more weakly, in
      T4.d's and T4.g's tables, whose grids follow each pressure's lines.
    - _Ions' near-limit widths_ keep Unsöld's (Mg⁺ 24, Si⁺ 71 lines from within 0.6 eV of the
      limit), no ion source read (decision-r08-t4e-unsold §8).
    - _Near-hydrogenic levels_ keep Unsöld's width, and l-mixing is not modelled: Na nd + He is
      0.5–0.9 of Unsöld's width and 2–3 times Γ_R. Above n* ≈ 15–20 the exception keeps Unsöld's
      floored width, about 9 times γ_p in H₂ (H's Balmer members from n 15, and Mg's highest
      near-hydrogenic levels), where l-mixing cross-sections fall and widths tend to γ_p (Omont §4.1
      finds n > 30 agreeing with γ_p on principal series); an upper end near n* 15 is one route, not
      ruled.
    - _Below n\* 6_ Unsöld's width is kept, though the measured widths there exceed it 2–4 times.
    - _The bound's own approximations_, which all err wide: it is extrapolated from n* 6 to about
      10; the Fermi part leaves the impact regime at the tables' high pressures (collision duration
      times width 0.6–2.8 at 0.42 MPa for n* ≤ 8); the lower level is left out (35–50%); H's
      zero-energy L is used (up to 30%); L(H₂) spans 1.27–1.64 a₀; the mean speed stands in for the
      Maxwell average (−13% to +8%).
    - _H₂'s molecular channels_ (ion–quadrupole, rotational excitation) are not modelled: Na's 1935
      series-end width in H₂ is 2–3 times Γ_R. _The H ion-pair channel_ is not modelled either.
    - _Pressure shifts are left out_, as for every atomic line: Fermi's shift less the polarisation
      shift is +3.5–4.8 × 10⁻⁸ rad cm³ s⁻¹ per H₂ at 1,000 K, +5.7–7.8 cm⁻¹ at 0.42 MPa, above these
      lines' bounded half widths (Ny and Ch'en 1938 measure +3.2–3.7 × 10⁻⁸ for H₂).
    - _At 10 MPa_ the highest members stop being distinct lines: Alekseev and Sobel'man's χ_i
      reaches 0.3–0.6, and Fermi's merging limit falls to n* ≈ 11.
    - _The 4-a-decade grid below 1 MPa_ limits atoms whose lines from n* 4–6 are a fifth to a tenth of
      the cut-off wide; the midpoint rule covers it table by table.
    - _The air gases' widths of the bounded lines_ are scaled from the line's bounded H width by
      Unsöld's α^(2/5) rule, while H₂'s takes its own bound from its scattering length; not
      quantified (the science check's), these lines being from n* 6 and weak in the strength-weighted
      ratios.
    - _The estimated pairs_ (`Na+He`, `K+H2`, `K+He`) may lie below their true wings near the
      lines: Na–H₂'s open tables run 2–12 times their impact estimate in D2's blue wing at
      200–2,000 cm⁻¹.
    - _Kurucz's Zn II in `gf3001.pos`_ (T4.h's finding) stays deferred.
- **Deviations in T14.a, as built** (2026-10-21; `thick/discreteOrdinates.ts` and
  `thick/linearAlgebra.ts`, with their tests; decision-r08-t14a-scope).
  - _The signature._ The entry point is
    `solveDiscreteOrdinates(problem: DiscreteOrdinatesProblem): DiscreteOrdinatesSolution`.
    - In: `layers` from the top down, each an `OrdinateLayer` with `opticalDepth`,
      `singleScatteringAlbedo` and `moments`; `groundAlbedo` (Lambertian); `beamCosines` (μ₀, all
      on one factorisation a mode); `userCosines` in (0, 1], each solved upward and downward;
      `maxMode` M ≤ NSTR − 1; optional `streams` (NSTR, even, ≥ 2; `DISCRETE_ORDINATE_STREAMS` =
      16 by default, counting both hemispheres) and `beamPaths` (the seam, below).
    - Out: `quadrature` (`DoubleGaussQuadrature`: `streams`, `nodes` μ_i ascending, `weights`
      summing to 1 a hemisphere), `interfaceDepths` (L + 1), `userCosines`, and per beam a
      `BeamSolution` `{ beamCosine, modes, fluxes }`. Each of `modes` (m = 0 … M) is a
      `ModeIntensities` of I^m at every interface: `quadratureUp`, `quadratureDown` ((L + 1) × N)
      and `userUp`, `userDown` ((L + 1) × U), interface-major `Float64Array`s. `fluxes`
      (`InterfaceFluxes`, m = 0) holds `direct`, `diffuseDown`, `diffuseUp` and `meanIntensity`,
      the last with the direct beam's T ÷ 4π.
    - The beam's flux normal to itself is 1, and I = Σ_m I^m cos(mΔφ). Δφ is the azimuth of the
      stream's direction of travel less the beam's: a downward stream at Δφ = 0 is the forward one,
      and for an observer Δφ is the azimuth looked toward less the sun's. `intensityAtAzimuth`
      sums the modes.
    - Separable, for T14.e's vector mode and T15's deck: `doubleGaussQuadrature(streams)`,
      `normalizedAssociatedLegendre(m, maxDegree, μ)`, `homogeneousSolution(layer, m, quadrature)`,
      and the stack, generic in n (the streams a hemisphere, times the Stokes components):
      `factorLayerStack(faces, n, reflection)`, which takes each layer's 2n solutions at its two
      faces (`LayerFaces`) and the ground's n × n reflection R (I⁺ = R I⁻ + S), then
      `layerStackRightHandSide` and `solveLayerStack`. `linearAlgebra.ts` exports `choleskyLower`,
      `solveLower`, `solveLowerTransposed`, `symmetricEigen` (cyclic Jacobi) and `bandMatrix`,
      `bandIndex`, `factorBand` and `solveBand` (banded LU with partial pivoting). Nothing vector is
      built.
  - _The eigenproblem._ Stamnes and Swanson's reduced (α − β)(α + β) is made symmetric through
    the Cholesky factor L of −P, its odd-parity half: Lᵀ(−Q)L, by cyclic Jacobi (Golub and Van
    Loan §§8.5, 8.7; LAPACK Users' Guide Table 2.13, type 3), in place of a nonsymmetric
    eigensolver. −P is the factor taken because at ω = 1 −Q holds the conservative null. Its k²
    are real by construction. G⁺ − G⁻ is taken as k(α − β)⁻¹X, which stays finite as k → 0. The
    beam's particular solution uses the same eigenvectors, so a beam costs no factorisation.
  - _Raw forward-peaked moments are refused_ (the science check's finding, 2026-10-21). The
    double-Gauss rule integrates Λ_l Λ_l′ exactly only to l + l′ = 2N − 1, so the discrete
    scattering operator of a phase function's own χ₀ … χ_{NSTR−1} need not be a contraction.
    Henyey–Greenstein's χ_l = g^l fail from g 0.9436 at 16 streams and ω 1 (0.9444 at ω 0.99,
    0.9522 at ω 0.9, 0.99 at 32 streams): −P is not definite or a k² is negative, and the
    discrete system itself breaks down there, so the solver refuses them with a `RangeError`
    naming delta-M as the cure. Their delta-M truncations (f = χ_NSTR) passed for g 0.85–0.999 at
    ω 1 and 0.5 and NSTR 4–32, and a test holds g 0.95: refused raw, solved and conserving energy
    truncated. T14.b must truncate before it solves.
  - _ω = 1 is the conservative solution, no dither._ At m = 0 the null pair is replaced by I = 1
    and I = t ± u_i, u = −(α − β)⁻¹1. A co-albedo at or below
    `DISCRETE_ORDINATE_CONSERVATIVE_CO_ALBEDO` = 10⁻¹² is solved as conservative. With that bound
    set to 0, k₀² held to 0.2% down to 10⁻¹² at 16, 32 and 64 streams and reached rounding at
    10⁻¹⁵; the rule drops at most about 9 × 10⁻¹⁰ of absorption, on a slab of τ 1,000. As a
    check that the null vector is there, a conservative layer's smallest k² must lie within 10⁻⁸
    of its largest k² from 0 (measured: at most 7 × 10⁻¹⁶ absolute).
  - _A μ₀ at an eigenvalue's reciprocal._ Where a layer's slant factor λ lies within
    `RESONANCE_HALF_WIDTH` = 10⁻⁵ of one of its k_n, relatively, that mode is solved at
    λ(1 ∓ 2 × 10⁻⁵) in the flagged layers and the two averaged: two more back-solves on the same
    factorisation. Measured, the value at μ₀ = 1 ÷ k_n is within 2.4 × 10⁻⁸ of the mean of
    μ₀(1 ± 10⁻⁴)'s, and energy at ω = 1 holds there to 6 × 10⁻¹⁰ (4 × 10⁻¹⁴ elsewhere; 4 × 10⁻⁸
    at a half-width of 10⁻⁴, 1.2 × 10⁻⁹ at 3 × 10⁻⁶). A user cosine at μ₀ or at a 1 ÷ k_n needs
    nothing: the source's integrals are divided differences of exponentials, taken stably.
  - _The seam is built_ (ruling 4): it cost nothing past the particular solution's algebra, which
    takes λ as a parameter anyway. `beamPaths[b]` is a `BeamPath`: its `topTransmission` is T_p
    at each layer's top, and its `slantFactor` λ_p, the slant optical depth per unit vertical
    optical depth inside the layer. `planeParallelBeam(layers, μ₀)` fills the default,
    e^{−τ_p ÷ μ₀} and 1 ÷ μ₀. Inside layer p the beam is T_p e^{−λ_p t}; at the ground it is
    T_L e^{−λ_L τ_L}. The scattering geometry is the beam's one μ₀ in every layer, as the
    pseudo-spherical approximation takes it. A pseudo-spherical caller (T14.b, Dahlback and
    Stamnes 1991) supplies, per μ₀ and layer, T_p from the slant path to the layer's top and λ_p
    from the layer's slant optical depth. The direct flux reported at interface p is μ₀ T_p, so
    T_{p+1} = T_p e^{−λ_p τ_p} is the caller's to keep; the solver does not check it.
  - _Moments._ χ₀ … χ_{NSTR−1} enter the solve, missing ones as 0; later ones are ignored, their
    truncation (delta-M) being T14.b's. χ₀ must be within 10⁻¹² of 1, and is taken as 1.
  - _For T14.b's J_ms._ The solver returns intensities; the source function at a view cosine is
    J^m(τ, μ_v) = (ω ÷ 2) Σ_l (2l + 1) χ_l Λ_l(μ_v) Σ_j w_j Λ_l(μ_j) (I⁺_j + (−1)^{l+m} I⁻_j), plus
    the beam's term, from the quadrature intensities at an interface. The module computes it
    privately (`userSource`); T14.b may export it, or rebuild it with its own phase function, the
    single-scattering term taken out for J_ms. User cosines are refused at μ = 0, where the
    formal integration divides by μ but J is finite.
  - _The checks as held._ Each is deterministic, so no α applies. The two files hold 62 tests,
    about 0.5 s in all, the slowest 0.22 s. The cases:
    - (a) energy at ω 1 on 1 and 64 layers at τ 10⁻³, 0.1, 1, 10, 64 and 1,000, for
      Henyey–Greenstein g 0.85 (cut at l = 15) and Rayleigh, μ₀ 0.1, 0.5 and 1, over black and
      white grounds;
    - (b) τ 50, isotropic, ω 0.5 and 0.9, μ and μ₀ 0.1–1, at user and quadrature angles;
    - (c) τ 10⁻⁶, ω 0.9, Rayleigh and g 0.5 cut at l = 15, modes 0–15 summed at Δφ 0°, 60°, 120°
      and 180°;
    - (d) τ 2, ω 0.9, g 0.5, A 0.2, modes 0–3; (e) three layers, A 0.3, five μ₀, modes 0–4;
    - (f) as (a)'s g 0.85 at τ 1,000, modes 0–1; (g) and (h) τ 1, ω 0.9, g 0.75, (h) at A 0.3.

  - _Timing (ruling 8), recorded and never asserted; provisional._ One solve of 16 streams, 64
    layers, 32 μ₀, m = 0–1 and 16 user angles took 54 ms, the median of 12 (53–57 ms, the first
    57 ms).
    - It ran on one of this laptop's 8 threads (an i7-8665U, governor `powersave`, energy
      preference `balance_performance`), at a 1-minute load of 3.4, with #65's 4-thread trace
      beside it.
    - Being under load, it is provisional by the roadmap's rule (README, "Measurements on a quiet
      machine"), to be repeated on a quiet machine, as T14.b's bake timing will be.
    - DN9's operation count puts a bake at 0.1–1 s; T14.b measures one against `BAKE_CEILING_S`.
    - For scale, at the same load: 64 streams with all 64 modes on 8 layers and 2 μ₀ took 2–3.4 s
      a solve. The banded LU dominates there (512 unknowns, bandwidth 95, about 9 × 10⁶
      operations a mode), and T14.e's 8-stream vector mode at 64 layers is of that order a mode.
  - _PythonicDISORT 1.8_ (MIT; Python 3.14, numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1), run once by hand and
    never asserted.
    - How it was run: after the solver was written, with only its documented interface read. Each
      case was over a black ground, with its I₀ = 1 the beam's flux normal to itself, compared at
      its double-Gauss nodes (the solver's own), with all modes and the fluxes.
    - (b), τ 50, isotropic, μ₀ 0.5: F↑(0) 0.2539692487 at ω 0.9 and 0.08007210895 at ω 0.5 in
      both, to 2 × 10⁻¹⁵ and 3 × 10⁻¹⁵. The node intensities at the top agree to 8 × 10⁻¹⁴ and
      3 × 10⁻¹⁴.
    - (c), τ 10⁻⁶, ω 0.9, at Δφ 0°, 60°, 120° and 180°: Rayleigh at μ₀ 0.3 agrees to 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰
      in flux and 7.7 × 10⁻¹⁰ in intensity, and g 0.5 at μ₀ 0.7 to 1.3 × 10⁻⁹ and 7.9 × 10⁻⁹,
      which is rounding at that τ in either solver.
    - (i), all 24 cases: at ω 0.9, fluxes agree to 1.9 × 10⁻¹³ and node intensities to 3 × 10⁻¹⁰.
      It refuses ω = 1. At 1 − 10⁻⁶ they agree to 3.6 × 10⁻⁹ and 7.8 × 10⁻⁷, and at 1 − 10⁻⁹ to
      7.9 × 10⁻⁶ and 1.8 × 10⁻⁴ (32 streams).
    - Why the gap near ω = 1 is read as PythonicDISORT's conditioning there: it warned of complex
      eigenvalues in every case. This solver's values at 1 − 10⁻⁶, 1 − 10⁻⁹ and 1 lie on a line
      in the co-albedo; PythonicDISORT's at 1 − 10⁻⁹ move the other way. Both balance energy there.

    radiative transfer", Transport Theory Stat. Phys. 14(4) (1985) 437–483,

    asserted only at 10⁻³ to their published digits, at the streams those digits need (recorded
    then).
  - _`DELTA_M_STREAMS`, for T14.b._ `aerosol.ts`'s `DELTA_M_STREAMS` = 16 counts a hemisphere
    (2M = 32 moments kept, f = χ₃₂). `DISCRETE_ORDINATE_STREAMS` = 16 counts both, so a 16-stream
    solve reads χ₀ … χ₁₅, and its delta-M is `deltaMTruncation(table, channel, 8)` (f = χ₁₆), not
    that function's default. T14.b sets its count. Nothing here changes `aerosol.ts`.
  - _Sources._
    - Read: Stamnes et al. 1988 (by the research agent, its eqs. 4–8e); the LAPACK Users' Guide's
      "Generalized Symmetric Definite Eigenproblems" (Table 2.13); Chandrasekhar 1947 (Bull. Amer.
      Math. Soc. 53, 641, eqs. 125 and 168, in place of _Radiative Transfer_, not read).
    - The DISORT methodology report (Stamnes et al. 2000, v1.1, a document, not code) was read by
      the research agent for the conventions only.
    - Cited, not re-read: Golub and Van Loan's 4th edition, its sections placed by the book's
      contents alone (§3.1 triangular systems, §4.2 Cholesky, §4.3 banded systems, §8.5 Jacobi,
      §8.7 the symmetric-definite problems), each method held by its own test; Abramowitz and
      Stegun §8.5 and _Numerical Recipes_ §6.7 for the Legendre recurrence, whose normalised form
      was derived here and is held to P_l and the addition theorem.
    - Checked by their DOI or Crossref records alone: Stamnes and Swanson 1981, Stamnes and Conklin
      1984, Dahlback and Stamnes 1991 and Demmel and Veselić 1992 (cited for Jacobi's relative
      accuracy).
    - The H-function's 1 ÷ H form and α₀ were checked against the 1947 form numerically (its
      residual is asserted), not against the book.
    - The science check re-derived items 1–10 of the module and its tests and confirmed them with
      an independent full 2N × 2N solve. Its one finding, that raw forward-peaked moments can fail
      the contraction, is recorded above.
  - _Departures from the brief._
    - `linearAlgebra.ts` is a module of its own, with its own test (ruling 6 allows one), and the
      acceptance ran as the brief's `vitest run view/atmosphere/thick/`, which covers it.
    - The interface refines ruling 4's lean:
      - one list of user cosines, each solved both ways;
      - the outputs as flat arrays;
      - the stack taking a general reflection matrix R and source S, for T15's deck. The solver
        itself fills only the Lambertian ones: its ground's beam source and its ground term at the
        user cosines are Lambertian and m = 0 alone, which T15 widens.
      - a `StreamDirection` type (`"up"` or `"down"`) for `intensityAtAzimuth`.
    - Jacobi on the symmetric reduction, not a nonsymmetric QR: still a text's method (ruling 5),
      and it keeps the small k² that ω near 1 needs.
    - PythonicDISORT ran at ω 1 − 10⁻⁹ where the cases ask ω 1, since it refuses 1.
- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)** (R08.T14.a). Recorded and deferred: each leaves the
  algorithm and every contract as they are.
  - _Two Legendre recurrences in `atm/`._ `aerosol.ts`'s private `legendre` and this module's
    `normalizedAssociatedLegendre`, whose m = 0 is P_l, compute the same polynomials. One could
    serve both, but `aerosol.ts` lies outside this task's paths.
  - _PythonicDISORT near ω = 1._ As a cross-check it is reliable at ω ≤ 1 − 10⁻⁶, and not at
    1 − 10⁻⁹ (its warnings; the record above). T14.b's and T14.e's by-hand checks against it
    should stay at or below 1 − 10⁻⁶.
  - _The boundary solve's cost at many streams._ The stack is block-bidiagonal, layer by layer, so
    a block elimination would cost less than the general banded LU, whose bandwidth 3N − 1 grows
    with the streams (2–3.4 s a 64-stream, 64-mode solve of 8 layers). At 16 streams it is not
    needed (54 ms for the ruling's solve); T14.e's vector mode may want it.
- **Deviations in T14.b, as built** (2026-10-26; `thick/bake.ts`, `thick/spectralColumn.ts`,
  `thick/expSum.ts`, `thick/sphericalBeam.ts` and `thick/binConversion.ts`, each with its test,
  `thick/deltaM.test.ts`, `thick/bakeJob.test.ts`, `thick/bakeFixtures.ts` and
  `thick/bake.bench.ts`; `opticsJobs.ts`, `opticsMessages.ts`, `optics.worker.ts`'s docs and
  `tsconfig.worker.json`; decision-r08-t14a-scope).
  - _The signatures._ Two calls in place of the sketch's `(medium: AtmosphereMedium, band)`:
    - `prepareBake(column, lights, grid?, options?): PreparedBake`, with `column: SpectralColumn`,
      `lights: ReadonlyArray<ThickBakeLight>`, `grid = THICK_BAKE_GRID` and
      `options = EXP_SUM_OPTIONS`;
    - then `bakeMultipleScattering(prepared: PreparedBake, body: ThickBakeBody, band: number)`,
      which gives an `MsSourceTable`.
    - The medium's terms are three-channel, so the sketch could not be spectral; the bins' optics
      (Mie) and the fits do not depend on the band, so they are prepared once for every band.
    - A `ThickBakeLight` is `{ spectrum, absorbers }`, one `AbsorberBinCurves` an absorber term in
      the column's order. A `ThickBakeBody` is the assembly's `{ figure, gravity }` with R_ref as
      `bottomRadiusM`. `thickBakeBands(body)` gives `tablesPlanOf`'s bands, held equal by a test,
      since the worker may not import the tables.
    - `thick/bake.ts` also exports `BAKE_CEILING_S` (5), `THICK_BAKE_STREAMS` (16),
      `THICK_BAKE_MODES` (2), `THICK_BAKE_MAX_TERMS_PER_BIN` (64), `THICK_BAKE_GRID`, `deltaMLayer`
      and `bakeBinSolve` (one solve and its source, for the tests).
  - _The spectral column_ (`thick/spectralColumn.ts`).
    - `SpectralColumn` is `{ name, topHeightM, groundAlbedo, terms, pressureBar? }`. Each
      `SpectralTerm` is the drawn term's `name` and `density` with a `SpectralSource`: `molecular`
      (the gas fractions and n_s), `thomson` (n_e), `aerosol` (the mode's `AerosolParticles` and
      σ_ext(550) at relative density 1) or `absorber` (its amount at relative density 1).
    - `spectralOptics(column, wavelengths)` takes `molecularMixture`, σ_T, and `aerosolModeOptics`
      with `aerosolPhaseTable` (the mode's optics in all three of its channels, channel 0 read)
      and `aerosolTerm`'s scale in its own order of operations. At `CHANNEL_WAVELENGTHS_NM` every
      coefficient, ρ and table entry is the drawn term's to the bit.
    - No rule of `assemble.ts` is repeated: the term selection, `MEDIUM_TERM_LIMIT`, the modes'
      guards and names and the deck's cuts stay the assembly's, and the column takes the terms it
      drew.
    - _The hand-off for T14.c._ `DrawnMedium` gains `sources: ReadonlyArray<SpectralSource>`, one a
      medium term in order: n_s from the column, n_e and an aerosol's σ_ext(550) as `thomsonTerm`
      and `aerosolTerm` form them, the particles as `particlesOf` forms them, and an absorber
      term's amount from the term. `spectralColumnOf(medium, sources)` lays them beside the terms.
      None can be read from the assembly's exports without repeating its rules: the fixtures read
      n_s from the drawn term's green coefficient over σ_mix there, which holds only to rounding.
    - _Also for T14.c._ A kept scene's medium is handed to the cache whole and never assembled, so
      it has no record for a request's `input`: T14.c gives kept scenes their own path. A bake whose
      worker is lost, or whose k-tables fail to load, reaches the pool as the worker's error, not
      `thick-bake-failed`: T14.c shows `ATMOSPHERE: APPROXIMATE` for those too.
  - _The table_ (`MsSourceTable`, one a band, an `MsSourceSlot` a light).
    - A slot's `values` are a `Float32Array`, `[altitude][μ₀][μ_v][m][RGB]` row-major: 33
      altitudes, every second interface of the solve's 64 layers in h\* from the ground
      (`altitudesM`, per body); 32 μ₀ at (s + ½) ÷ 32; 16 travel cosines at ±(v + ½) ÷ 8, the
      downward half first, so that an observer looking at elevation e reads −sin e; m = 0 and 1.
      The cosines are cells' centres, which a texture's filter with clamped edges reads directly.
    - 405,504 B a band and light as `f32` and 270,336 B as `rgba16float`, Design note 9's 0.26 MB
      at 33 altitudes for its 32. The solve is `f64`.
    - Each light slot holds its own table, since μ₀ and the curves of growth are a sun's. Two suns
      double Design note 11's J_ms row: a four-band Saturn-class world's comes to 2.16 MB, for
      R08.T11 and T14.c's `TABLE_SIZES`.
    - Stored is E, the emission of orders two and up per unit of true length at h\*, per
      steradian, per unit of the star's irradiance normal to its beam at the top: m⁻¹ sr⁻¹, which
      the kernels multiply by the star's colour in place of σ_s·Ψ_ms·p_u. E = E⁰ + E¹ cos Δφ, Δφ the
      azimuth looked toward less the sun's.
  - _The layers._ 64, evenly in ξ = ½(1 − τ(h) ÷ τ(0)) + ½ h ÷ top, τ the vertical extinction
    above h at 570 nm without the gases. The table's rows step 2.8–13 km below the Venus-class
    cloud, 1.4–3.7 km through it (about 67–94 km on the isothermal seam's column) and 17 km above
    it, and 1.3–24 km on the Titan-class column. Each layer's terms are their exact ∫ρ dh over it,
    mixed by their scattering; E takes the medium's own optics at each altitude.
  - _The beam_ (`thick/sphericalBeam.ts`).
    - T_p = e^(−τ_s), τ_s the slant depth from the chords through the band's homogeneous shells of
      R_b + h\* (R_b = s_b √(MN), or R_ref for one band), and λ_p the average secant
      (τ_s(p + 1) − τ_s(p)) ÷ τ_p, so that T_{p+1} = T_p e^(−λ_p τ_p).
    - μ₀'s domain is (0, 1]. A ray with μ₀ > 0 climbs from its point, so the beam is defined at
      every height and no entry is 0 for want of it. μ₀ ≤ 0, twilight's lit upper air included,
      lies outside the table: T14.c and T14.d judge it. (Loughman et al. 2004's 8% at 60 km
      tangent height is a figure for Earth's limb, which Design note 9 takes as its warning for
      Titan: the science check, 2026-10-26.)
    - Where τ_s falls downward (a thin layer under a thick one at a grazing sun) λ is floored at
      10⁻⁶ and the beam catches up below: 5,406 layers of the Venus-class fixture's 34 × 32 beams,
      withholding at most 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁶ of the beam, and none on the Titan-class.
  - _Delta-M and Nakajima and Tanaka's corrections_ (derived here).
    - 16 streams in all. On each layer's mixed moments f = max(χ₁₆, f_c, 0), f_c the forward
      delta's share (R08.T5.c), and τ′, ω′ and χ′ as Wiscombe's.
    - The kernels march with σ_ext − f_c σ_s and add the exact single scattering of their own beam
      T_k, in place of TMS (which scatters the delta-M beam T′ by the exact phase function), so the
      table holds no single scattering.
    - For the kernels' extinction to carry delta-M's transport, E = σ_s[(f − f_c) I′_d(Ω) +
      (1 − f) ∫ p′ I′_d dΩ′ + (1 − f) p′(Θ₀)(T′ − T_k)]: the truncated lobe's re-emission of the
      diffuse field into its own direction, the smooth part's, and the aureole (the light delta-M
      counts as beam) scattered once more.
    - IMS is left out: the aureole scattered again inside the lobe, σ_s (f − f_c)(T′ − T_k), stays
      within the lobe of the sun, and no table of m ≤ 1 and 16 cosines holds it. Its share of a
      point's light, (f − f_c)(T′ − T_k) ÷ [(1 − f_c)(4π Ī′_d + T′ − T_k)], is at most 1.2% on the
      Venus-class fixture and 5.0% on the Titan-class (`doubleForwardShare`). The science check
      re-derived E and found it consistent, this term the only one missing.
  - _The exponential sums_ (`thick/expSum.ts`).
    - The method: the weights by non-negative least squares (Lawson and Hanson) at fixed k on a
      grid of 8 a decade, kU from 10^−4.5 to 10⁵ and 0, their sum held to 1; terms dropped one at a
      time while the largest |ΔT| over the curve's nodes stays within 2 × 10⁻³, at most 8 kept; a
      drop that misses on the grid's k alone polished by a joint Levenberg–Marquardt of the
      weights and ln k.
    - The rows: the weights fitted at the row nearest the column's Curtis–Godson pressure and
      shared; each row's k fitted alone, from its neighbour's. Each layer reads k at its own
      Curtis–Godson pressure, ln k linear in ln p, p held as the curves' read holds it.
    - The overlap is random, the product of the absorbers' sums, the weakest taken as one term
      past 64 solves a bin.
    - Under the Sun, the terms by bin and the largest |ΔT|:
      - Titan-class CH₄ (one row): 1 2 4 3 4 3 4 3 3 4 4 3 3 3 3, 47 solves, 1.7 × 10⁻³ (bin 13);
      - Venus-class CO₂ (30 rows): 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 2 3 5 5 2 7 2, 34 solves; 3.9 × 10⁻² over every
        row (bin 13, at the rows below 0.1 bar, which hold under 0.1% of the gas), and 1.2 × 10⁻²
        over the rows its bulk reads (the fullest layers holding 99%, `readFitError`). The k order
        crosses at 3, 2 and 8 of its rows in bins 10, 11 and 13 (`crossedRows`; none on Titan).
  - _The conversion and the ground_ (`thick/binConversion.ts`).
    - X_c = Σ_b W_cb X_b ÷ C_c, W_cb the star's c̄ S Δλ over bin b's 1 nm rows
      (⌊15 (λ − 380) ÷ 380⌋, 760 nm in the last) and C_c its colour; a flat X converts to itself.
    - The guard: a channel whose star colour is at most 10⁻⁶ of its largest takes the spectrum's
      mean over the bins, Σ S_b X_b ÷ Σ S_b, also the identity on a flat X.
    - The ground: each bin's albedo linear in wavelength between the channels' wavelengths, and
      the nearer channel's outside them.
  - _The job._ `thick-bake` is `{ id, input, slots, bands, column, body }`. The worker forms the
    specs (`absorberSpecsOf`), matches each absorber term to the spec of its name, forms the lights'
    bin curves (`absorberCurvesBySun`), prepares once and bakes each band asked. It answers
    `thick-baked` `{ id, tables }`, every buffer transferred, or `thick-bake-failed`
    `{ id, bands, message }` for any throw of a bake, never `failed`. The other kinds are unchanged.
  - _The tests' figures._
    - Delta-M: the worst flux gap from the whole 64-stream solve is 1.8 × 10⁻⁴ (Henyey–Greenstein
      g 0.85, χ₁₆ 0.074) and 1.9 × 10⁻⁴ (`sulphuric-acid-75`, r_eff 1.05 µm, at 550 nm, χ₁₆ 0.118),
      relative to the flux or to 1% of μ₀ (a black ground's upward flux there is 0); with the same
      moments cut at l = 15, delta-M off, 4.8 × 10⁻³ and 3.1 × 10⁻³. Both are held to 1%.
    - The conversion: 1.3 × 10⁻¹⁵. The bands: τ₁ ÷ τ₂ = s₂ ÷ s₁ to 4.4 × 10⁻¹⁶ (Uranus, s 0.975
      and 1.026 on spheres of 24,352 and 26,826 km), the geometry `tablesPlanOf`'s. The column
      against the medium: 0, to the bit.
    - The source's consistency: 2π ∫ E⁰ dμ_v at the Gauss nodes against
      σ_s[(1 − f_c) 4π Ī′_d + (1 − f)(T′ − T_k)] from the solver's mean intensity, 1.9 × 10⁻¹⁴.
    - E⁰ ≥ 0 at every point of both fixtures. E¹ is a signed coefficient, and E⁰ + E¹ cos Δφ dips
      below 0 by up to 4.4% of E⁰ on the Venus-class fixture and 49% on the Titan-class (a finding
      below).
    - A direct quadrature of σ_s ∫ p I_d dΩ′ over the solver's own field on a Rayleigh column, at
      Δφ 0, π ÷ 2 and π, holds E⁰ + E¹ cos Δφ to 10⁻¹², and E¹ is 0 at an overhead sun.
  - _Timing_, provisional: the laptop's 8 threads, the benchmark on one at `nice 10`, at a 1-minute
    load of 3.4–4.5 with #107's three-process sweep beside it, a mean of 3 each. Vitest's module
    runner also flagged its export getters in the solver's hot loop, which a bundled worker does
    not pay. The Titan-class row was timed with the haze at τ 3, before the science check set it
    to 8.1; at 8.1 its terms and solves are the same.

    | Fixture                 | Solves | Preparation | A band | A solve | One band | Four bands |
    | ----------------------- | ------ | ----------- | ------ | ------- | -------- | ---------- |
    | Venus-class, H₂SO₄ τ 30 | 34     | 9.0 s       | 2.98 s | 88 ms   | 12.6 s   | 21.5 s     |
    | Titan-class, tholin     | 47     | 0.50 s      | 4.55 s | 97 ms   | 5.1 s    | 18.7 s     |
    - The preparation holds the column's optics in the 15 bins, 5.6 s and 0.05 s. The bin curves
      under the Sun, 0.58 s and 0.04 s, are formed before it and counted in "One band".
    - "Four bands" is the bin curves and the preparation once and four bands, as one request takes
      them; four whole bakes would be 50 s and 20 s.
    - A first run of the benchmark at a load of 4.9–6.0, #107's four processes beside it, took
      16.6 s and 4.45 s (Venus-class) and 0.75 s and 4.45 s (Titan-class). Under `vitest run`, the
      module runner's export getters unflagged, a Venus-class band took 1.8 s at a load of 0.8
      (6.1 s to prepare), and a Titan-class band at τ 8.1 took 2.4 s at a load of 3.3: 47–51 ms a
      solve, as T14.a's 54 ms.
    - Against `BAKE_CEILING_S` = 5 s: a Titan-class band is about at it on this laptop, a four-band
      Saturn-class body three to four times over it, and the Venus-class over it on Mie alone (15
      bins of the cloud's matrix at 256 angles). To be repeated on a quiet machine.

  - _The fixtures_ (`thick/bakeFixtures.ts`, the science check's corrections, 2026-10-26).
    - The Venus-class column is `venus92Detail`'s air as the assembly draws it, its CO₂ on the
      committed line tables, with a cloud of `sulphuric-acid-75` droplets: r_eff 1.05 µm and v_eff
      0.07 (Hansen and Hovenier 1974), from 1 bar (50.4 km in VIRA, Seiff et al. 1985) to 0.04 bar
      (69.6 km), the measured base at 47.9 km and about 1.37 bar (Tomasko et al. 1980) left out,
      and τ(550) 30, a test's choice inside the clouds' measured 25 at 0.63 µm (Tomasko et
      al. 1980) and the probes' 25–40 (the brainstorm).
    - The Titan-class column is `titanClassMethaneMedium`'s air with a tholin haze of aggregates,
      3,000 monomers of 0.05 µm at D_f 2 (`aerosol.test.ts`'s, after Tomasko et al. 2008, not
      read; Hörst 2017 quotes 4,000 of 0.04 µm), well mixed, at τ(550) 8.1: the column DISR
      measured (Tomasko et al. 2008, Fig. 47, as Bazzon, Schmid and Buenzli 2014, A&A 572, A6,
      fit it), as `hyperion-sim`'s Titan haze takes it. The first build's 3 was a third of it.

  - _Sources._ Read: T14.a's solver and its record, and `aerosol.ts`, `absorbers.ts`,
    `rayleigh.ts`, `oblate.ts`, `spectralColour.ts`, `assemble.ts` and `tables.ts`'s
    `tablesPlanOf`. Cited, not re-read: Wiscombe 1977; Nakajima and Tanaka 1988, for TMS's and
    IMS's roles (the source table's form is derived here); Dahlback and Stamnes 1991, by its DOI
    record and the solver's seam; Lacis and Oinas 1991; Wiscombe and Evans 1977; Lawson and Hanson
    1974; Levenberg 1944 and Marquardt 1963; Golub and Van Loan, §5.3. Read by the science
    check: the DISORT report v1.1 (delta-M, eqs. 54 and 68a), Hansen and Hovenier 1974's and
    Tomasko et al. 1980's abstracts, VIRA as EPIC transcribes it, Bazzon et al. 2014 and Hörst
    2017 (arXiv), and Loughman et al. 2004's abstract; Dahlback and Stamnes 1991 and Tomasko et al.
    2008 could not be reached.
  - _Departures from the brief._
    - The band-independent work is `prepareBake`, the band's bake `bakeMultipleScattering`.
    - IMS is measured (`doubleForwardShare`) rather than shown negligible, and held to 2% and 6%
      against the 1.2% and 5.0% measured. The fits are held to 2 × 10⁻³ (Titan-class), and to 0.04
      over every row and 0.013 over the bulk's rows (Venus-class).
    - Beside the brief's error over every row, the error over the rows the bulk reads is recorded.
    - "Not negative" is read as E⁰ ≥ 0: E¹ is a signed coefficient, and the sum's dips below 0 are
      recorded above and deferred below.
    - The fixtures sit in `thick/bakeFixtures.ts`, outside `test/`, which this lane may not edit.
- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)** (R08.T14.b). Recorded and deferred: each leaves the
  algorithm and every contract as they are.
  - _Mie's share of the bake._ The Venus-class cloud's optics in 15 bins are most of its
    preparation, and the matrix at 256 angles is about 80% of each call (33 ms without angles, 164
    ms with them, at 550 nm). A Mie that gives the Legendre moments from its expansion
    coefficients, or a worker that keeps a body's bin optics, would cut it several times;
    `sizeDistribution.ts` lies outside this task's files.
  - _CO₂'s low-pressure rows._ With the weights shared, the rows below 0.1 bar miss by up to 3.9%
    in T. The layers there hold under 0.1% of the gas; weights fitted over the bulk's rows together
    would cut it.
  - _m ≤ 1 dips below 0._ E⁰ + E¹ cos Δφ falls below 0 by up to 49% of E⁰ (Titan-class) on the far
    side of a forward-peaked point. T14.c's read clamps it at 0 (lean), and T14.d's gate judges
    whether m = 1 suffices.
  - _The altitudes are per body._ The table's altitudes follow the column's optical depth, so
    T14.c reads them through a lookup, as the oblate body's table carries its scale heights.
  - _One request for every band._ The preparation is per request, so T14.c asks for a body's bands
    in one request; split over workers, each would repeat its Mie.
  - _IMS on Titan._ Up to 5.0% of a point's light, within the haze's lobe of the sun, is left out;
    T14.d's gate near the sun judges it.
  - _The k order across rows._ CO₂'s fits cross at 13 of their rows in three bins. Correlated-k
    takes each term as one g interval at every pressure; an ordered fit (each k the last one's plus
    a positive step) would hold it, its error recorded beside this one's.
  - _Half floats._ E is about 10⁻⁷–10⁻⁶ m⁻¹ sr⁻¹ near an Earth-like ground and far less aloft,
    under `rgba16float`'s least normal (6.1 × 10⁻⁵): T14.c stores it with a scale a table or an
    altitude, or in km⁻¹ (the science check).
  - _Design note 9's Titan bullet._ It gives Loughman et al. 2004's 8% at 60 km tangent height as
    Titan's; the paper's comparison is of Earth's limb (the science check, 2026-10-26). The warning
    stands for Titan, its figure Earth's.
  - _The fixtures' home._ `thick/bakeFixtures.ts` is a test fixture outside `test/`, which this lane
    may not edit; it moves to `test/` with the next task that may, as `view/clouds/slabFixtures.ts`
    waits to.
  - _A Cholesky that does not throw._ `expSum.ts` keeps its own `definiteSolve` for the fit's damped
    steps, where a matrix that is not positive definite is an outcome, since `linearAlgebra.ts`'s
    `choleskyLower` throws; T14.a's module could give both the non-throwing form.
- **Composition (decision-composition, 2026-10-09).** Every species and material is a plan-14
  registry key. The client's tables are keyed by those strings, with measured, estimated, derived
  or stand-in provenance, and the labelled fallback never drops a species. R08.T19 holds the client
  to the sim's fixture.
  - `Gas` (13; 16 since T3.b's follow-up) remains the set with measured dispersions, never a wire
    type.
  - The 15 bake bins' inadequacy for M dwarfs' TiO bands stays a recorded limitation, since TiO
    in the star overlaps TiO in the planet.
- **Deviations in T10.c, as built** (2026-10-27; `decision-r08-approximate-plate.md`, items 1a
  and 1b). Edited in `view/atmosphere/`: `absorbers/kDistribution.ts`, `absorbers.ts`,
  `negligible.ts`, `assemble.ts`, `thick/regime.ts`, `AtmosphereCache.ts`, `labels.ts` and
  `reference/cases.ts` (a comment alone); in `displays/view/`: `viewAtmosphere.ts` and
  `viewRun.ts`; their tests; and the guide. No table, shader or kernel changes, so the gate ran no
  `just test-render`, and no GENERATOR_VERSION, PROTOCOL or wire change.
  - _The split._ `broadeningFactor`'s `Broadening` gains `widthlessShare`, ε: the gases the table
    holds no width for, other than N₂, O₂ and Ar and the five of `DIPOLAR_BROADENERS` (H₂O, NH₃,
    SO₂, HCN and H₂S, a constant beside `AIR_GASES`), each its normalised mole fraction times its
    r of 1, over Σ x r at the temperature. `estimated` stays for a dipolar gas with no width and
    for a two-variant table's every partner but its own and air's gases, whose gases with no
    width add nothing to ε. `SpeciesLinesData.widthlessShare` carries it, and the gases with no
    width no longer set `optics` by themselves.
  - _The bound's form_ (a deviation: the exact form of the same bound,
    `decision-r08-approximate-plate.md` §1; accepted on the issue, 2026-10-27, and kept as built).
    Δ_c,γ = min(1, −ln(1 − ε)) Δ_c(k = 1), in place of the ruling's ε Δ_c(k = 1), which is its
    first-order term. The ruling's derivative bound holds per unit of ln s, for s the factor
    between the true broadening pressure and the one drawn, s ∈ [1 − ε, 1 + ε]. And T lies within
    Δ_c(k = 1) of 1 at every width, which gives the cap, reached at ε = 1 − 1/e, about 0.63.
    −ln(1 − ε) lies above ε by about ε ÷ 2 of itself: under 3 × 10⁻⁴ for Earth and Mars, 0.28% for
    Saturn, and 39% at ε 0.5. `BroadenerVerdict`
    (`test: "broadener"`, the key, `widthlessShare`, `widthFactor`, `amount`, `temperatureK`,
    `lineChanges` for Δ_c(k = 1), `changes` for Δ_c,γ, `largestChange`, `negligible`) runs for
    each drawn line species whose `linesRule` is `measured` and whose ε is above 0. It takes the
    lines' own cell means, chord and suns at k = 1, and stands after `fixedGMix` in a key's tests.
  - _Its figures_, each the largest over the Sun and the 2,500 K and 30,000 K Planck suns and the
    three channels:

    | Case                                          | ε           | Δ_c(k = 1)  | Δ_c,γ       | Largest       |
    | --------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------- | ----------- | ------------- |
    | Earth-class H₂O, CO₂ at 330 ppm (`earthBody`) | 3.25 × 10⁻⁴ | 0.512       | 1.66 × 10⁻⁴ | red, 30,000 K |
    | Mars-class O₂, CO at 0.06% (`marsBody`)       | 5.2 × 10⁻⁴  | 1.35 × 10⁻⁵ | 7.1 × 10⁻⁹  | red, 2,500 K  |
    | Saturn-class H₂, CH₄ at 4,500 ppm, 134 K      | 5.5 × 10⁻³  | 1.22 × 10⁻³ | 6.7 × 10⁻⁶  | red, 30,000 K |

    Against the ruling's figures, each is within a factor of three. Mars's ε is the fixture's
    0.06% CO, not "about 7 × 10⁻⁴". Saturn's ε takes each width's temperature exponent at 134 K
    (Σ x r 0.82). Saturn's Δ_c(k = 1) is that of the `saturn-oblate` column, 1.22 × 10⁻³, against
    the 6.0 × 10⁻⁴ that T10.a's record implies. T10.a's 0.060 has no committed test, so the column
    behind it is not known.

    With Earth's CO₂ raised, H₂O labels between 6.0 and 6.1 times the 330 ppm, about 2,000 ppm
    (Δ_c,γ 9.97 × 10⁻⁴ and 1.014 × 10⁻³, at ε 1.95 × 10⁻³ and 1.98 × 10⁻³). NH₃ at 1 ppb labels
    Earth's H₂O at k = 100, 1.96 as before. The Mars-class H₂O, in 95% CO₂ (ε 0.95), takes the
    cap: Δ_c,γ = Δ_c(k = 1) = 2.8 × 10⁻⁴, negligible.

- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)** (R08.T10.c). Recorded and deferred: each leaves the
  algorithm and every contract as they are.
  - _The widths' range_ (for the science check). R08.T10.c's bound takes each gas with no width
    on file at a ratio to air in [0, 2] at the profile's temperature, `AIR_TRACE_SHARE`'s doc's
    range for a partner's efficiency. It does so for every gas without a dipole, on every table:
    the atoms' tables too, whose ratios are to H₂'s width. No measured ratio has been checked
    against the range. The committed molecular tables' intensity-weighted ratios to air for the
    foreign gases without a dipole they list lie in 0.34–1.58 (HCl's He, CO₂'s H₂). The cases
    lean on CO₂'s widths of H₂O's lines (Earth's case) and CH₄'s of H₂'s quadrupole lines, for
    which the science check found no measurement. H₂'s ratios are to its own narrow width, so one
    above 2 is plausible. No verdict rests on it: with s to 1 + (R − 1)ε for a ratio up to R,
    Earth's H₂O stays negligible for R up to 7.0, and Saturn's H₂ for R up to about 230. Only the
    raised-CO₂ crossing leans on the range. From ε of
    1 − 1/e, about 0.63, the cap holds and the range no longer matters.
    _Ruled 2026-10-27 (§6): a science check, due before R08.T16.a; not a client change._
  - _The shape's limits._ `speciesLines`' measured-shape and 10 MPa tests read the broadening
    pressure as drawn. A body within ε of either limit could cross it unseen. At the three ruled
    cases' ε (at most 5.5 × 10⁻³) this is negligible. The Mars-class H₂O (ε 0.95) could be
    broadened at up to 1.95 times the drawn pressure, about 1.2 kPa on Mars's 636 Pa datum, far
    below the 1 bar to which Earth's H₂O lines are drawn measured.
  - _The cell means_ (the science check). Δ_c(k = 1) takes the lines' cell means over the stored
    rows to the body's largest p_eff, with the first row past it. The integral and the cap both
    take ⟨σ⟩ at every width to (1 + ε) p_eff. A cell's mean is its lines' strength within it, but
    wings from the cells beside it, which the 1 nm cells' 17 cm⁻¹ at 760 nm lets in under the
    25 cm⁻¹ cut-off, grow with the width. The first row past reaches between 1 and 1.78 times the
    largest p_eff (1.33 above 1 MPa): for the Mars-class H₂O 1.57, not 1.95. There, a cell of
    such wings alone could run 1.24 times low, 2.8 × 10⁻⁴ at most 3.5 × 10⁻⁴; at the three ruled
    cases' ε it is nothing. Reading the means at (1 + ε) times the largest p_eff would close it.
    The amendment of 2026-10-27 keeps the bound as built, so this is the owner's.
    _Ruled 2026-10-27 (`decision-r08-approximate-plate.md` §6): built in R08.T10.d._
  - _The dipolar list_ (the science check, for the owner). The ruling names five gases. The
    registry also holds HCl, CH₃OH, SiO, H₂SO₄, TiO, VO and FeH, whose dipoles are as strong as
    H₂S's or stronger (NIST CCCBDB, by the science check). The bound weighs them as it stands;
    some of their kind's self widths pass twice air's (HCl's 2.909, CH₃OH's 4 in the committed
    tables).
    _Ruled 2026-10-27 (`decision-r08-approximate-plate.md` §6): built in R08.T10.d._
  - _NH₃'s own width_ (the science check, for the owner; from before this task). NH₃'s table lists

    question on the issue). An atom's own share takes r 1, H₂'s, inside [0, 2]; but its resonance
    lines are broadened by its own kind far more: resonance-broadening theory, which Weller et al.
    2011 (J. Phys. B 44, 195006) test on Rb D1, gives Na D's self-broadening 44–129 times its H₂
    widths over 500–3,000 K (Allard et al. 2019, A&A 628, A120), or half that if their width is a
    half width, and K's D lines and Cr's and Fe's resonance lines are alike (Lewis 1980, Phys. Rep.
    58, 1). The first check's 34–66, which read Weller et al.'s figures as Na's, lies inside it.
    No verdict rests on it yet: the neutral atoms' tables are never `measured` below their grid
    and H's basis is `estimated`, so no neutral atom's lines reach the bound; the ions' visible
    lines (Mg⁺, Si⁺) are not resonance lines. Lean: an atom's own share `estimated`,
    as a dipolar gas's is, until a `self` width is on file.
    _Ruled 2026-10-27 (decision-r08-approximate-plate §8): built in R08.T10.d._
  - _Polar salts' vapour_ (the science check, low confidence). The registry files NaCl and KCl as
    `mineral`, so `DIPOLAR_BROADENERS`' rule, which reads molecules, leaves them out, though their
    vapours' dipoles are 8.971 D and 10.239 D (NIST CCCBDB). Were a server to send either as a
    bulk gas, the bound would weigh it.
  - _NH₃'s shape._ NH₃'s table marks no node's line shape measured, so the own-width rule cannot
    show on NH₃ until a table records a measured shape for it.
  - _A reason's head in the guide_ (the UX review, for the owner). The `ATMOSPHERE: APPROXIMATE`
    row, verbatim from the ruling, sets each reason "as a sentence with no letter spacing", but
    does not say "its head included", which the ruling does. The Typography bullet still sets "a
    label block's statement that names a thing and then says what it is in a sentence" as
    `TEST PLANET: provisional, …`, its head tracked, which `H2O: its absorption estimated, …` fits.
    The code follows the ruling. The row could add "its head included", or the bullet an exception
    that points to the row.
    _Ruled 2026-10-27 (decision-r08-approximate-plate §8): built in R08.T10.d._
